Gérôme drew on archaeological sources to render every harness, obelisk, and statue with the meticulous polish that made him a star of Salon history painting.

A late landscape recalling the village of Achères near the forest of Saint-Germain, painted in the final year of Gérôme's life. The academic precision of his Orientalist canvases is here loosened into a quieter, more atmospheric record of the Île-de-France countryside.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-jean-louis-t: Four thoroughbreds stretched into the rocking-horse 'flying gallop' pose then conventional in sporting art, set against a low storm-bruised English sky. Géricault painted it in London, where his fascination with horseflesh and equestrian sport reshaped his late Romantic style.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-ndl-dc-25865: Sun setting over the rooftops of Ichinokura at Ikegami, from Hasui's series Twenty Views of Tōkyō. The shin-hanga print uses long horizontal bands of graded orange and indigo to fix a single, melancholic moment of urban dusk.

A wet street in the Akashi-chō district after rain, lamplight pooling on the pavement. Hasui, working with the publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō, was the master of these reflective night and weather scenes that defined the shin-hanga revival of Japanese woodblock printing.

A cliff-bound view of Ryūga Island off the Oga Peninsula in Akita, from Hasui's third Souvenirs of Travel set. Pine-fringed rocks rise from a deep cobalt sea, printed with the multiple bokashi gradations that gave shin-hanga its photographic depth.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-nihon-fukei-: An early Hasui woodblock from Selected Views of Japan, showing thatched roofs at Kazusa village in former Hizen Province on the Kyūshū coast. The print already shows the publisher Watanabe's house style: precise architecture, soft skies, and water rendered in layered indigo wash.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-ondergesneeu: A bleak field at Auvers with a discarded harrow under fresh snow, freely after a black-and-white print by Jean-François Millet. Van Gogh translated Millet's earthbound peasant subjects into his own thicker, colour-saturated impasto throughout his last year.

A bleak field at Auvers with a discarded harrow under fresh snow, freely after a black-and-white print by Jean-François Millet. Van Gogh translated Millet's earthbound peasant subjects into his own thicker, colour-saturated impasto throughout his last year.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-pieter-brueg: Returning hunters and their lean dogs trudge across a snowy ridge above frozen ponds where villagers skate, the panel that anchors Bruegel's celebrated cycle of the months commissioned by the Antwerp merchant Niclaes Jonghelinck. Now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna, it set the template for European winter landscape painting.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-saint-franci: The saint swoons into the arms of an angel after receiving the stigmata on Mount La Verna, a nocturnal vision lit by a single raking source. It is generally taken to be Caravaggio's earliest religious commission of consequence, painted for his patron Cardinal Francesco Maria del Monte in Rome.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-saint-jerome: The aged hermit-scholar bends over his Vulgate translation, his bald head and the skull on the table almost mirrored across the strong diagonal of his outstretched arm. Painted in Rome for Cardinal Scipione Borghese, the work is now in the Galleria Borghese.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-the-big-wave: A page from Hokusai's later, more contemplative woodblock series One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji, in which a curling wave frames the distant sacred peak. Printed in monochrome ink with discreet grey gradations, it reprises in book form the motif of his earlier Great Wave.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-the-langlois: A small Provençal drawbridge over the Arles canal, with washerwomen at the bank and a horse-drawn cart crossing above. The subject obsessed Van Gogh in spring 1888, who returned to it in several oils, watercolours, and drawings for its echo of the Dutch canals of his childhood.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-the-taking-o: Judas's kiss seals Christ's arrest as armoured soldiers surge in from the right, their polished steel catching the lantern held by a self-portrait of the painter at the edge of the scene. Lost for nearly two centuries, the canvas was rediscovered in a Jesuit residence in Dublin in 1990 and is now on long-term loan to the National Gallery of Ireland.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-thumbnail: An unattributed image from the collection. Without a reliable title, artist, or date, no descriptive label can be drawn from the historical record.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-van-dyck-sir: A posthumous portrait of Venetia Stanley, Lady Digby, propped on her pillows in the dawn following her sudden death in 1633. Commissioned by the grieving Sir Kenelm Digby and now at Dulwich Picture Gallery, the picture is unusually intimate among Van Dyck's English court portraits.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-van-gogh-ack: A Provençal field worked by oxen and ploughman, painted while Van Gogh was a voluntary patient at the asylum of Saint-Paul-de-Mausole near Saint-Rémy. The furrows roll across the canvas in his characteristic ribbon-like impasto, an homage to the peasant labour Millet had pictured a generation earlier.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-van-gogh-the: Gnarled olives churn in the foreground while the limestone Alpilles rise behind under a clouded sky, painted from the grounds of Saint-Paul asylum. Now at MoMA, it belongs to the group of about fifteen olive-grove canvases Van Gogh devoted to the trees during his Saint-Rémy year.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-vincent-van-: A still life of grapes, lemons, pears, and apples banked across the table, painted in Paris under the influence of Adolphe Monticelli's heavy paint and the Impressionists' fruit studies. Now at the Art Institute of Chicago, it shows Van Gogh testing a brighter, complementary-colour palette.

A thatched cottage screened by trees in Auvers-sur-Oise, where Van Gogh spent his last seventy days under the care of Dr Paul Gachet. The brisk diagonal strokes and pale, cool palette belong to the prolific summer 1890 burst that produced more than seventy canvases.

Two harvesters nap in the shade of a haystack at noon, freely copied from a Millet print Van Gogh kept in his Saint-Rémy studio. He translated Millet's grey original into a pairing of complementary blue shadows and golden yellow stubble.

A walled vineyard outside Auvers descends toward red-roofed cottages and the church tower beyond. Painted weeks before Van Gogh's death, the canvas balances his late, agitated brushwork with an unusually orderly Northern French motif.

Beached fishing smacks on the Mediterranean sand at Les Saintes-Maries-de-la-Mer, their masts and rigging picked out in clean primary colour. Made on a five-day excursion from Arles in June 1888, the picture marks Van Gogh's first encounter with the sea in the South of France.

A reaper bends to his work amid sun-bleached fields under a churning sky, painted in the final months of Van Gogh's life at Auvers-sur-Oise. Thick parallel strokes of yellow and ochre carry the artist's recurring theme of the harvester as a figure of mortality and quiet acceptance.
collection-of-beauty-2560px-william-holm: A goat staggers across the salt flats of the Dead Sea, its horns bound with the red wool of the Yom Kippur ritual. Hunt painted the scene on site in 1854, hauling his easel to the shore of Oosdoom in pursuit of the Pre-Raphaelite ideal of truth to nature, sharpened by Christian symbolism.
collection-of-beauty-26-the-oi-river-bet: Porters ford the broad shallows of the Oi River, with Fuji's cone framed beyond. Hiroshige drew the design for the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji issued by Tsutaya Kichizo, deploying the bokashi gradient technique to suggest mist rising off the water.
collection-of-beauty-2895-1-modigliani-0: A reclining female nude with elongated neck and almond-shaped eyes, set against a deep red ground. Painted around 1918 and held at the Honolulu Museum of Art under accession 2895.1, the canvas belongs to the series of nudes that drew police censure when shown at Berthe Weill's Paris gallery in late 1917.
collection-of-beauty-bogatyy-kirgizskiy-: A wealthy Kyrgyz hunter on horseback with a hooded falcon on his gloved fist, dressed in a heavy embroidered robe. Vereshchagin painted the subject in 1871 from observations made on his Central Asian travels for the Turkestan series.
collection-of-beauty-31-the-otsuki-plain: Travellers cross the open plain of Otsuki with Fuji set against a pale sky, plate 31 of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. Hiroshige favoured such low horizons to let the mountain dominate, balanced by the human-scale activity of road and field.
collection-of-beauty-32-dog-eye-pass: Hiroshige's view from Inume Pass in Kai Province looks down on a sea of cloud broken by Fuji's summit, plate 32 of his Thirty-six Views series. The composition compresses foreground rocks and distant peak into a single graphic plane, a hallmark of late-Edo landscape design.
collection-of-beauty-33-kogane-plain: A wide view across the Kogane plain in Shimosa, with Fuji blue on the horizon and grasses sketched in the foreground. From Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the print uses the bokashi gradation to soften sky and distance.
collection-of-beauty-34-kuroto-bay: Boats drift in Kuroto Bay with Fuji visible across the water, plate 34 of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The flat blue expanses and economical drawing of sails reflect the woodblock vocabulary that would soon enthral European Japonisme.
collection-of-beauty-3415-maria-magdalen: The Magdalene rests her cheek on her hand in the conventional pose of melancholia, jar of ointment beside her. Painted during Gentileschi's Roman years, the work fuses Caravaggesque chiaroscuro with the artist's signature interest in solitary, introspective female protagonists.
collection-of-beauty-35390682010-4609909: A landscape catalogued as Wildenstein 1449 in Monet's oeuvre. The artist's standard practice in such canvases is to dissolve form into broken touches of complementary colour, recording transient light with a saturated, high-keyed palette.
collection-of-beauty-36-the-hoda-coast: The closing print of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji shows the rocky Hoda coast in Awa Province, Fuji floating across Edo Bay. Crisp keyblock outlines and indigo seas give the design the graphic clarity that defined his late style.
collection-of-beauty-4344-vis-print-1476: An oil sketch on oak panel of an elderly woman, made as preparatory study for figures populating Rubens's larger religious and mythological compositions. The loose, economical handling typifies the head-studies the Antwerp workshop produced from life models.
collection-of-beauty-500px-gipsen-vrouwe: A plaster cast of a female torso set against a warm ground, one of a series of academic still-lifes Van Gogh painted in Paris while studying at Cormon's atelier. The handling shows him working through colour theory on a deliberately neutral subject.
collection-of-beauty-500px-kuniyoshi-uta: A hawk poised in profile, its plumage detailed in the layered keyblock and colour blocks of an ukiyo-e print. Hawks were a favoured subject of late Edo print designers, the bird's predatory stillness suiting the medium's graphic economy.

A tiger paces against a wind-blown ground, its striped coat picked out in dense keyblock lines. Kuniyoshi, never having seen a live tiger, drew on imported Chinese painting models and his own taste for muscular animal subjects in the warrior-print tradition.
collection-of-beauty-ayvazovskiy-gayvazo: A rainbow arches above a shipwreck and lifeboat tossed in heavy seas, survivors pulling at the oars while the sky breaks open behind them. Painted in 1873 and now in the State Tretyakov Gallery, the canvas is one of Aivazovsky's signature meditations on rescue at sea, salvation hinging on a sliver of coloured light.
collection-of-beauty-kirgizskie-kibitki-: Kyrgyz felt tents (kibitki) pitched along the Chu river, which marks the border between present-day Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. Vereshchagin recorded the encampment on his Central Asian travels of 1869 to 1870, the source material for his Turkestan series.
collection-of-beauty-kitayskaya-palatka: A Chinese tent standing in a Central Asian landscape, recorded as Kitayskaya palatka. The study comes from Vereshchagin's Turkestan travels of 1869 to 1870 across the Russian Empire's newly conquered frontier in Central Asia.
collection-of-beauty-valentin-a-serov-ku: Two boys lead a dappled horse into shallow water under a high summer sky, the animal's reflection broken across the surface. Serov painted the canvas in 1905, oil on canvas, now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg. The plein-air handling and loose, light-struck water belong to his later landscape work around the Domotkanovo estate.
collection-of-beauty-7222-adoracion-de-l: The Magi present their gifts to the Virgin and Child in a packed Byzantine-inflected composition, gold-edged drapery wheeling around the kneeling kings. Painted in Crete around 1568-69 before El Greco's move to Venice, the small panel on poplar belongs to his late icon-painter phase and is now in the Museo Soumaya, Mexico City.
collection-of-beauty-ivan-konstantinovic: A moonlit coastal scene at Gurzuf on the Crimean shore, with a glowing disc of moon laid across the water and dark vessels near the foreground rocks. Aivazovsky painted the marine view in 1891; the canvas later passed through Heritage Auctions in Dallas. The Armenian-Russian painter produced thousands of seascapes from his studio at Feodosia on the Black Sea.
collection-of-beauty-vnutrennost-yurty-b: The interior of a wealthy Kyrgyz yurt, its felt walls hung with patterned textiles and the floor spread with carpets. One of Vereshchagin's ethnographic studies from his Central Asian travels of 1869 to 1870, later worked up as part of the Turkestan series.
collection-of-beauty-buddiyskiy-khram-v-: A Buddhist temple at Darjeeling in the eastern Himalayas, its painted woodwork and prayer banners set against the mountains. Vereshchagin made the study during his Indian journey of 1874 to 1876, one of roughly 150 sketches from the trip, oil on canvas in the Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-9: A Southern Song album leaf depicting a spring tide laden with rain, attributed to the court painter Li Di. Soft ink wash and atmospheric distance reflect the lyrical small-format landscape tradition cultivated at the Hangzhou academy.
collection-of-beauty-960px-03-sukiyagahs: The Sukiyagashi district of Edo with Fuji rising beyond rooftops, plate three of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji. The print balances the dense urban foreground against the calm geometric mountain that recurs throughout the series.
collection-of-beauty-960px-13-the-tama-r: The Tama River flows beneath a pale Fuji in this thirteenth design from Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views. Rafts and figures animate the middle distance, while bokashi gradients carry the eye from green water to blue mountain.
collection-of-beauty-960px-evening-snow-: Snow settles on the eaves of Terajima village at dusk, a print from Hasui's revival of landscape woodblock under the shin-hanga movement. Hasui worked closely with publisher Watanabe Shozaburo, prizing atmospheric weather and quiet rural corners over the bustle of the old Edo school.
collection-of-beauty-960px-fox-hunt-1893: A red fox flounders through deep snow as a flock of crows descends, the predator suddenly become prey. Painted at Prouts Neck on the Maine coast, this is the largest canvas of Homer's late career, its compressed Japonist composition and bleak palette signalling the harshness of the northern winter.
collection-of-beauty-960px-hanagami-danj: The warrior Hanagami Danjo grapples with a colossal salamander in the Tonta River of Izumo, a scene of legendary heroism. Kuniyoshi delights in muscular anatomy and reptilian texture, characteristic of the musha-e warrior prints that made his reputation.
collection-of-beauty-960px-hiroshige-fut: The wedded rocks of Meoto Iwa stand off the Futami shore, joined by the sacred shimenawa rope, with Fuji visible across the bay. Plate twenty-seven of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the design pairs Shinto pilgrimage iconography with Hiroshige's signature distant cone.
collection-of-beauty-960px-hiroshige-ii-: The Kintai Bridge arches in five wooden spans over the Nishiki at Iwakuni, a celebrated feat of Edo carpentry. The print belongs to Hiroshige II's One Hundred Famous Views of the Provinces, continuing the meisho tradition his teacher had popularised.
collection-of-beauty-960px-hiroshige-mt-: From the Misaka Pass in Kai Province, Fuji is doubled by its reflection in Lake Kawaguchi below. Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views design exploits the symmetry as a graphic device, layering pine-clad slopes against the still water.
collection-of-beauty-960px-hiroshige-sun: Red maples frame a view of Fuji from the slopes of Meguro at sunset, plate ten of Hiroshige's Thirty-six Views. Printed by Tsutaya Kichizo, the design uses heavy bokashi in the sky to evoke the dying autumn light.
collection-of-beauty-960px-jean-leon-ger: Napoleon on horseback before the Sphinx and pyramids, a meditation on power and antiquity tied to the 1798 Egyptian campaign. Gerome's polished academic finish and ethnographic eye made him the leading French Orientalist of the Second Empire.
collection-of-beauty-960px-lofty-mt-lu-b: Towering peaks of Mount Lu rise in vertically stacked planes of ink, a hanging scroll painted by Shen Zhou as a birthday tribute to his teacher Chen Kuan. A founder of the Wu School of Ming literati painting, Shen here pays homage to the Yuan master Wang Meng's dense, crinkled brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-960px-museo-del-pra: An artist slumps over his desk as bats and owls swarm from the dark behind him, plate forty-three of Goya's Caprichos. The etching with aquatint, issued in Madrid in 1799, became the central emblem of the series' attack on Spanish superstition and unreason.
collection-of-beauty-960px-pieter-bruege: Hunters and their hounds trudge home over a snowbound ridge, looking down on skaters scattered across frozen ponds. The winter panel of Bruegel's series of months, commissioned by the Antwerp merchant Niclaes Jonghelinck, hangs today in Vienna's Kunsthistorisches Museum.
collection-of-beauty-960px-robert-delaun: Delaunay returned to the Eiffel Tower repeatedly across his career, fragmenting its iron lattice into prismatic planes of colour. This late oil sets the monument against tilting Parisian rooftops, channelling the Orphic Cubism he developed with Sonia Delaunay into a near-abstract hymn to modern engineering.
collection-of-beauty-960px-sesshutoyo: An autumn landscape in the haboku (splashed-ink) idiom that Sesshū absorbed during his 1467 study trip to Ming China. Sparse, axe-cut brushwork conjures rocky cliffs and a lone traveller, leaving wide expanses of paper to read as mist — a hallmark of Muromachi suiboku ink painting.
collection-of-beauty-960px-tokyo-junidai: From the series Twelve Scenes of Tokyo, Hasui frames the temple steps of Atagoyama beneath blossoming cherry. A leading figure of the shin-hanga revival, he pairs traditional woodblock craftsmanship with Western perspective and a cool, atmospheric palette of dusk blues.
collection-of-beauty-960px-van-gogh-le-m: Painted during Van Gogh's Paris years, when he lodged with brother Theo in Montmartre and absorbed Impressionist colour. The windmill of the Moulin de la Galette, a dance-hall landmark also painted by Renoir and Toulouse-Lautrec, appears here in muted earth tones still tied to his earlier Dutch palette.
collection-of-beauty-snowscape: A winter landscape of snow-laden peaks and bare trees rising above a misty valley, the foreground pushed to one corner in the asymmetric manner that earned Ma Yuan the nickname 'one-corner Ma'. Attributed to the Southern Song court painter and held in the National Palace Museum, Taipei. Hanging scroll, ink and colour on silk.
collection-of-beauty-a-colored-version-o: A reworked echo of the famous Kanagawa wave, drawn from the later One Hundred Views of Mount Fuji. Hokusai mirrors the composition, removes the fishing boats, and turns the spume into a flock of birds — a meditation on transformation rendered in his late, more graphic woodblock manner.
collection-of-beauty-a-female-martyr-sai: A half-length saint, traditionally identified as Catherine of Alexandria by the spiked wheel of her martyrdom. Gentileschi favoured strong-willed female protagonists set against deep shadow, building flesh in luminous Caravaggesque chiaroscuro across a career that spanned Rome, Florence, and Naples.
collection-of-beauty-a-foolish-virgin-in: A young woman with elaborately knotted braids is shown half-length, turning her oil lamp upside down to show that it is empty — the mark of the foolish virgins of the parable in Matthew 25, who let their lamps run dry before the bridegroom came. The engraving relates to Schongauer's series of the Wise and Foolish Virgins and bears his monogram. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-a-friendly-call: Chase records a sunlit afternoon visit in his Shinnecock summer studio, the parlour a parade of mirrors, framed prints, and white-painted wicker. A leading American Impressionist and influential teacher, he handles light and reflective surfaces with bravura brushwork indebted to Sargent and Whistler.
collection-of-beauty-a-hippopotamus-and-: One of four exotic hunts Rubens painted around 1615 for Maximilian I of Bavaria, blending Flemish pictorial drama with antique pathos. Spear-wielding riders, snarling hounds, and writhing reptiles crash together in a swirling diagonal composition that became a touchstone for Baroque action painting.
collection-of-beauty-a-kitchenmaid-by-jo: A young woman in a white cap dresses a chicken on a kitchen table heaped with pewter, cabbages, and a copper pan, with Christ in the house of Mary and Martha visible through an arch behind her. Signed and dated to around 1620, the Centraal Museum canvas measures 103 by 72 centimetres and is one of Wtewael's last large genre paintings.
collection-of-beauty-a-parisian-lady-edo: A near-life-size portrait of the actress Ellen Andrée in fashionable street dress, her black silhouette set against a flat ground in Manet's signature manner. The picture pursues the figure of the modern Parisienne championed by Baudelaire rather than a sitter's likeness.
collection-of-beauty-a-sketch-of-the-mit: From the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, Hokusai squeezes the snow-capped peak between the tiled roofs of the Mitsui dry-goods emporium. Kites, tradesmen, and a soaring eagle animate the bustling Edo street, the woodblock print pairing commerce and the sacred mountain in one frame.
collection-of-beauty-a-sunday-on-la-gran: Seurat's manifesto of Neo-Impressionism, built over two years from countless oil sketches and conté studies. Bourgeois Parisians promenade along the Seine in frieze-like stillness, their forms assembled from tiny dots of contrasting pigment — the optical method he called divisionism.
collection-of-beauty-a-view-of-the-archb: Submitted to the Royal Academy in April 1790, the month Turner turned fifteen, this was his exhibition debut. The watercolour shows a topographical precision learned from Thomas Malton, the architecture set at sharp angles to flaunt the teenager's grasp of perspective.
collection-of-beauty-a-view-of-the-mount: A horseman crosses the V of Crawford Notch in the New Hampshire White Mountains, dwarfed by twisted pines and the bleached skeletons of trees torn from the slope. Cole painted the gorge in 1839, drawing on memories of the 1826 avalanche that wiped out the Willey family and their farmhands; it hangs in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-a-woman-bathing-in-: A woman in a thin white shift lifts the hem above her knees as she wades into a dark stream, rich brocade and red garments piled on the bank. Painted on a small oak panel in 1655 and signed in the lower right, the picture in the National Gallery is rendered in startlingly free, loaded brushwork that anticipates Rembrandt's late style.
collection-of-beauty-a-woman-whose-face-: A young woman bows her head into her shawl, mouth set and eyes downcast in unconcealed grief. Etching in the crayon manner by W. Hebert, around 1770, the print belongs to the Wellcome Collection's holdings of physiognomic studies that imitated red-chalk drawing through stippled etched dots.
collection-of-beauty-a-woman-with-a-rose: A young woman holds a single rose at her bodice, the figure built up in soft black chalk with the costume left as quick contour. Catalogued by the British Museum as entry 749307, the drawing dates from Gainsborough's Bath years, when he sketched women's portraits at speed in chalks before working them up in oil.
collection-of-beauty-a-young-lady-s-adve: A small female figure picks her way across a fantastical landscape of arrows, plant forms, and disembodied eyes in watercolour and pencil on paper. Made in 1922 during Klee's first years teaching at the Bauhaus in Weimar and held at Tate Modern, the sheet belongs to the inventive, fairy-tale graphic vocabulary he developed alongside his colour theory lectures.
collection-of-beauty-galatskaya-bashnya-: The Galata Tower rises over the Golden Horn under moonlight, masts and rooftops picked out in silver across the water. Aivazovsky painted this view in 1845 after visiting Constantinople with Grand Duke Konstantin Nikolaevich; the oil measures about 52 by 80 cm.
collection-of-beauty-abigail-adams-by-gi: The former First Lady, in her late sixties, sits in a black gown with a white lace cap and ruff, painted at her Quincy farm during Stuart's visits between 1810 and 1815. The unfinished canvas at the National Gallery of Art in Washington was begun as a pendant to the matching seated portrait of John Adams.
collection-of-beauty-accolade-by-edmund-: A medieval-revival fantasy of a queen knighting a young warrior with the flat of a sword, set in a sun-streaked palace hall. The picture is by Edmund Blair Leighton, a late Victorian academic painter whose chivalric scenes drew on Pre-Raphaelite costume study and theatre design.
collection-of-beauty-adachi-moor: A scene from Yoshitoshi's series One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, illustrating the legend of the demon-hag of Adachigahara. The Meiji-era ukiyo-e master combines traditional brushwork with psychological intensity, sharpening a kabuki-derived horror tale into a single moonlit confrontation.
collection-of-beauty-adam-and-eve-uk-cia: Cranach returned to Adam and Eve dozens of times after 1509, refining a courtly Reformation iconography of the Fall. Eve hands the apple across the Tree of Knowledge while a serpent watches and a menagerie of stag, sheep, and roe gather symbolically around the first couple.
collection-of-beauty-adameveparadisecran: An early treatment of the Fall by the Wittenberg court painter, set within a paradise teeming with stags, lions, and small game. Cranach's slender, mannerist nudes and crisp linear drawing reflect his proximity to Luther's circle, where the subject carried fresh theological weight.
collection-of-beauty-admiral-of-the-whit: A swagger portrait of Admiral Lord Rodney, victor over the French at the 1782 Battle of the Saintes, the captured ensign of the Ville de Paris draped behind him. Gainsborough's feathery brushwork and silvery palette soften the formal demands of state portraiture.
collection-of-beauty-adolph-menzel-baupl: Menzel turns a humble Berlin construction site, fringed by drooping willows, into a study of weather and labour. The unposed subject and freshly observed light anticipate the realist vein the Prussian painter would pursue across decades of obsessive sketching from life.
collection-of-beauty-adolph-menzel-das-b: An empty room, white curtains billowing at the open balcony door, a sofa half-glimpsed in a wall mirror. Menzel made the small oil for himself, capturing transient sunlight with the immediacy of a snapshot decades before plein-air Impressionism reached Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-adolph-menzel-eisen: A grimy panorama of the Königshütte rolling mill in Upper Silesia, with workers wrestling glowing iron under shafts of furnace light. Menzel spent months on site making hundreds of drawings, producing one of the first ambitious European paintings to take heavy industry as its subject.
collection-of-beauty-adolph-menzel-flote: Menzel reconstructs an evening concert at Sanssouci, with Frederick the Great playing flute beside C.P.E. Bach at the harpsichord and Quantz, Benda, and the Margravine Wilhelmine listening. Painted under Friedrich Wilhelm IV, it crowns the artist's long Prussian historical project.
collection-of-beauty-adoration-of-the-ma: A Neapolitan-period altarpiece in which the Magi crowd around the Virgin and Child by torchlight. Gentileschi pushes the figures close to the picture plane and stages the gift-giving in heavy raking light, drawing on the Caravaggism she had carried south from Rome.
collection-of-beauty-adoration-of-the-sh: Shepherds press forward to venerate the naked Christ Child held by the Virgin, a lamb bound at the foreground as a foreshadowing of sacrifice. The earthy palette and tender, everyday types reflect Murillo's early debt to Ribera and the Spanish naturalist tradition before his manner softened in later years.
collection-of-beauty-aeltje-uylenburgh-b: An elderly woman in a starched ruff and embroidered cap, the lined face turned slightly toward the light. Signed and dated 1632, this portrait of Aeltje Pietersdr. Uylenburgh, cousin of Rembrandt's future wife Saskia, hangs in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and dates from the painter's first Amsterdam year in the workshop of Hendrick Uylenburgh.
collection-of-beauty-after-benjamin-west: Self-portrait of the Pennsylvania-born history painter Benjamin West, then in his late thirties and established in London as historical painter to George III. The National Gallery of Art version, oil on canvas at 75.8 by 63 cm, is an 18th-century copy after a slightly earlier West original.
collection-of-beauty-after-rubens-anne-o: An early seventeenth-century studio copy of a lost Rubens portrait of Anne of Austria, queen consort of Louis XIII. The Spanish-born queen wears stiff court dress and an elaborate ruff, recorded with the smooth porcelain finish typical of Rubens's diplomatic likenesses of European royalty.
collection-of-beauty-after-the-attack-pl: Vereshchagin painted the carnage of the Russo-Turkish siege of Plevna from first-hand experience as a war correspondent attached to the Russian army. The unsentimental documentary realism he made his trademark exposes the human cost behind official communiqués of imperial conquest.
collection-of-beauty-after-the-battle-of: From the twenty-canvas Slav Epic that Mucha worked on for nearly two decades, this scene shows the aftermath of the 1410 Polish-Lithuanian victory over the Teutonic Knights. The Art Nouveau poster designer here deploys monumental tempera-and-oil composition to advance a pan-Slavic political mythology.
collection-of-beauty-aivasovsky-i-c-ship: The Black Sea Fleet flagship Twelve Apostles rides a moderate swell under full sail, her tiers of ports run out. Painted in 1897 on a 105 by 139 cm canvas now at the Feodosia gallery named for the artist, the picture commemorates the 120-gun ship of the line that served as Kornilov's flagship in the 1840s.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-bosporus: Caïques and sailing barges drift on the calm waters of the Bosporus below the silhouette of Constantinople, lit by a low Mediterranean sun. Painted in 1878, the canvas belongs to the long series of Bosphorus views that Sultan Abdul Hamid II would acquire directly from Aivazovsky, eventually accumulating around forty works by the artist for the Ottoman court.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-brig-mer: The 18-gun Russian brig Mercury fires from between two towering Ottoman ships of the line off the Bosphorus in May 1829, smoke and wind shredding the sails. Aivazovsky returned to the legendary encounter repeatedly, this 1892 canvas painting the small brig as a luminous wedge between dark hulls.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-by-bolot: Ivan Aivazovsky, full-bearded and in dark formal coat, is shown by his fellow academician Dmitry Bolotov in a sober three-quarter view. Painted in 1876, when Aivazovsky had been principal painter of the Russian Navy for thirty years, the portrait belongs to a small group of likenesses Bolotov made of senior figures of the Imperial Academy of Arts.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-catholic: Catholicos Mkrtich Khrimian, patriarch of the Armenian Apostolic Church, walks the dusty road near the cathedral of Echmiadzin with Mount Ararat rising beyond. Aivazovsky, himself Armenian, painted the elderly Khrimian Hayrik in 1895 shortly after his election to the Catholicosate.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-chaos-18: An angel of God hovers in cruciform pose above the dark turbulent waters of creation, light tearing the cloud apart behind him. Aivazovsky painted Chaos in Rome in 1841, his early twenties; it earned him a gold medal from Pope Gregory XVI and now hangs at the Mechitarist monastery of San Lazzaro degli Armeni in Venice.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-gibralta: An American three-master rides at anchor in the calm waters off the Rock of Gibraltar, the limestone bulk rising behind it under a clear southern sky. Painted in 1873 by Aivazovsky, principal painter of the Russian Navy, the canvas belongs to his long series of marine views worked entirely from memory in the Feodosia studio.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-look-to-: The Grand Cascade tumbles down its sixty-four gilded fountains toward the Marine Canal at Peterhof, with the long facade of the Great Palace stretched along the upper terrace. Aivazovsky painted the view in 1837 as a graduating student of the Imperial Academy of Arts in Saint Petersburg; it is now in the State Museum-Reserve at Peterhof.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-passage-: Moses leads the Israelites between two walls of suspended water as Pharaoh's army drowns in the closing flood behind, a column of cloud lit by lightning above the procession. Aivazovsky painted the biblical subject in 1891, drawing on the marine effects he had spent four decades perfecting at the Russian Imperial Academy and along the Black Sea coast.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-portret-: Anna Nikitichna Burnazyan-Sarkisova, the painter's second wife, gazes out from a semi-transparent veil that softens the dark ground behind her. Aivazovsky married Anna in 1882, nearly forty years his junior; the portrait hangs in the Aivazovsky Art Gallery in Feodosia, a rare exercise in formal portraiture from a painter best known for storms at sea.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-sea-coas: A small bonfire glows on a rocky shore beside a lighthouse, with figures gathered at the water's edge and moonlight cutting across the swell beyond. Aivazovsky painted the seascape in 1837, the year he graduated from the Imperial Academy with a gold medal and was named official painter to the Russian Navy; it hangs in the Aivazovsky Gallery in Feodosia.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-self-por: Aivazovsky, in his late fifties and at the height of his European reputation, faces the viewer in dark formal dress with a sober, level gaze. Painted in 1874 at the request of the Accademia di Belle Arti in Florence, the canvas entered the Uffizi self-portrait collection alongside Orest Kiprensky as only the second Russian artist so honoured.
collection-of-beauty-aivazovsky-view-of-: Caïques and Ottoman steamers drift on the Bosphorus beneath the silhouette of Constantinople, the domes and minarets of Süleymaniye and Hagia Sophia rising through golden haze. Aivazovsky visited the city several times in the 1840s and 1850s and made the Bosphorus panorama one of his recurring set pieces for Russian and Ottoman patrons alike.
collection-of-beauty-akashi-strand-akash: A solitary pine bends over the moonlit waters of Akashi Bay as sailboats drift in the distance. Tsuchiya Kōitsu designed the print for the Watanabe Shin-hanga workshop, which carried the lyric landscape tradition of Hiroshige into the twentieth century.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1910: A seated woman in a heavy blue dress holds a bowl of phlox beside a window opening onto a faceted landscape. Gleizes signed the canvas 'Alb Gleizes 10' and showed it in Room 41 of the 1911 Salon des Indépendants, the public debut of group Cubism, and again at the 1913 Armory Show. The 81 by 100 cm oil now belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1911: The writer Jacques Nayral stands three-quarter length in Gleizes's garden at Courbevoie, the foliage broken into the mobile facets of an early Cubist scheme. The 162 by 114 cm canvas was shown at the 1911 Salon d'Automne and reproduced in Du Cubisme, the manifesto Gleizes wrote with Metzinger in 1912. Tate acquired the picture in 1979.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1912: Cubist footballers lunge across the canvas in a tangle of jersey stripes, limbs, and faceted ground plane. Oil on canvas, 225.4 x 183 cm, the work entered the National Gallery of Art in Washington as one of Gleizes's largest Salon-scale figure compositions of 1912-13.

Cubist bathers stand and recline along a river bank rendered as a shallow stage of interlocking planes. Oil on canvas, 105 x 171 cm, Les Baigneuses entered the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris after being shown at the 1912 Salon de la Section d'Or, the exhibition that defined the Puteaux group.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1913: A reclining figure swings in a Cubist hammock, the suspending ropes and surrounding garden broken into faceted planes of green and ochre. Oil on canvas, 130 x 155.5 cm, the picture entered the Albright-Knox Art Gallery in Buffalo after its 1913 debut at the Galerie La Boétie Salon de la Section d'Or.

The publisher Eugène Figuière sits behind a desk stacked with books and journals, surrounded by Cubist planes that name his most important authors. Oil on canvas, 143.5 x 101.5 cm, the portrait was painted to mark Figuière's publication of Gleizes and Metzinger's manifesto Du Cubisme in 1912; it hangs at the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1914: Faceted planes assemble into the seated figure of the composer Florent Schmitt at the keyboard. Gleizes executed the pastel between 1914 and 1915 at 36 by 27 centimetres, the small format and chalky medium softening the angular Cubist syntax he had codified with Metzinger in 'Du Cubisme' three years earlier.

Madame Raymond Duchamp-Villon sits in a large armchair with her dog and two cats, wedding band and beads picked out among the shifting Cubist planes. Gleizes finished the nearly two-metre canvas in February 1914 and showed it at the Salon des Indépendants that spring; the work passed through Marcel Duchamp's collection and has been at the Peggy Guggenheim Collection in Venice since 1940.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1915: A schematic head-and-shoulders study of the young Jean Cocteau, reduced to a few angled planes and contour lines in Gleizes' Cubist idiom. Drawn during the artist's military service at Toul, it was reproduced in Josep Maria Junoy's Catalan avant-garde review Troços in October 1917.

Bright wedges of colour pivot around tilted black bars in a square 73-centimetre composition. Gleizes painted the work in 1915 on cardboard now mounted to Masonite during his stay in New York; it entered the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum as part of the founding Cubist holdings.

A returning poilu, rifle and pack flattened into Cubist scaffolding, appears in this wood engraving captioned 'Retour de Bois-le-Prêtre'. Gleizes contributed the print to issue 20 of Le Mot on 1 July 1915, the wartime Parisian weekly co-edited by Paul Iribe and Jean Cocteau, while the artist was himself serving at Toul.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-1920: A standing woman wearing a black glove fragmented into curving and angular planes of muted earth tones. Painted in 1920 and measuring 126 by 100 centimetres, the canvas belongs to Gleizes's post-war reformulation of Cubism into a rhythmic, decorative system he later codified in his treatise La Peinture et ses lois.

A woman holding a child constructed from intersecting curving and angular planes in muted tones. Reproduced in 1921 in Gleizes's published portfolio, the composition belongs to his early-twenties efforts to integrate the figure into the rhythmic translation-rotation system he set out in his book La Peinture et ses lois.

A Cubist composition of a mother and child built from interlocking curving planes, surviving only through a black-and-white photographic reproduction. The painting was shown at the Exposition Internationale d'Art Moderne in Geneva in the winter of 1920-21 as catalogue number 185; its dimensions and present location remain unknown.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-l-ho: A tall, narrow Cubist portrait of the doctor Théo Morinaud on a Paris balcony, the city beyond him fragmented into stacked facets. Oil on canvas, 195.6 x 114.9 cm, the picture entered the Philadelphia Museum of Art via the Louise and Walter Arensberg Collection in 1950.
collection-of-beauty-albert-gleizes-port: Broad overlapping planes and intersecting diagonals reassemble Major Mayer-Simon Lambert, regimental surgeon in charge of the military hospital at Toul. Gleizes painted the canvas between 1914 and 1915 while serving in the garrison there; it now hangs in the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York, and at least eight preparatory sketches survive.
collection-of-beauty-albinus-skeleton-w-: A plate from Bernhard Siegfried Albinus's Tabulae sceleti et musculorum corporis humani (Leiden, 1747), engraved by Jan Wandelaar. The skeleton is set in a poetic landscape with a rhinoceros, marrying anatomical exactitude to Enlightenment-era pictorial staging.

Another plate from Albinus's Tabulae sceleti et musculorum, in which Wandelaar layers the superficial muscles over the skeleton in a posed standing figure. The series was prized for its proportional accuracy, achieved with grids and double-perspective drafting unusual for medical illustration of the period.
collection-of-beauty-albinus-tabulae-sce: An engraving from Tabulae sceleti et musculorum corporis humani (Tables of the Skeleton and Muscles of the Human Body, 1747), the anatomical atlas of the Leiden anatomist Bernhard Siegfried Albinus, with plates drawn and engraved by Jan Wandelaar. The second table presents a full-length male ecorche displaying the superficial layer of muscles, posed with one arm extended before a parkland backdrop where a big cat watches from behind a masonry wall; Wandelaar's pictorial settings were meant to lend the figures depth and life. This impression is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-altdorfer-: Commissioned by Duke William IV of Bavaria, Altdorfer compresses Alexander's 333 BC victory over Darius III into thousands of tiny figures swarming under a cosmic sky. The Danube School master treats landscape and weather as protagonists, the curving horizon and apocalyptic sun lifting the battle into world-historical drama.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-adam: Dürer's celebrated copperplate engraving applies the canon of human proportion he had absorbed from Jacopo de' Barbari in Nuremberg. Adam and Eve flank the Tree of Knowledge amid a forest stocked with elk, ox, rabbit, and cat — emblems of the four humours soon to be unbalanced by the Fall.

Two life-size oil panels showing the first humans isolated against black grounds, Dürer's first attempt to model nudes in the Italian manner after his second Venice trip. Each figure is treated as a study in idealized anatomy, paired across the diptych held by the Prado.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-barb: A charcoal portrait of the artist's mother drawn weeks before her death, capturing her gaunt cheekbones and sunken eye in unsparing detail. Dürer's inscription records her age and condition, turning the sheet into a private memorial as much as a likeness.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-der-: A watercolor and gouache study of a severed roller's wing, its ultramarine, turquoise, and rust feathers laid out with near-scientific precision. The sheet exemplifies Dürer's habit of treating natural specimens as objects of sustained, meditative observation.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-druc: The only surviving copper printing plate from Dürer's hand, engraved with Christ praying in Gethsemane while the apostles sleep. Held by the Bamberg State Library, the worn matrix attests to the dense burin-work behind his late religious prints.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-hare: A young hare crouches alert against a blank ground, its fur built up in fine watercolour and bodycolour strokes that distinguish guard hairs from softer underfur. Among the most exacting nature studies of the Northern Renaissance, the sheet even records the cross-barred reflection of a studio window in the animal's eye.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-head: A late brush drawing of a bearded ninety-three-year-old man Dürer met in Antwerp, prepared as a study for a never-executed Saint Jerome. The economical washes catch sagging skin and patriarchal beard with the artist's signature analytic eye.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-mele: An engraving from Dürer's so-called Master Prints in which a winged figure broods amid scattered tools of geometry, a polyhedron, and a magic square. The image has been read as an emblem of artistic genius stalled by melancholic temperament.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-pray: A brush study in white and grey on blue prepared paper, drawn as a detail for an apostle in the Heller Altarpiece. The folded hands have since detached from their context to become one of the most reproduced devotional images in Western art.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-selb: Painted shortly after his first Italian journey, the twenty-six-year-old Dürer presents himself as a gentleman scholar in tasselled cap and silk-trimmed jacket rather than a craftsman. The Alpine landscape glimpsed through the window signals his new cosmopolitan ambitions for the German artist.
collection-of-beauty-albrecht-durer-the-: A small woodcut from the Small Passion series, showing an angel driving Adam and Eve from Eden through a narrow gate. Dürer compresses the drama into densely cut parallel hatching that gives the bodies sculptural weight.

Christ stands bound to a tall column in a vaulted hall while a crowd of tormentors presses in from every side, scourges raised; a small dog at the foot of the column underlines the casual cruelty of the scene. The woodcut belongs to Dürer's Large Passion, the ambitious series he began around 1496-97 and published as a book in 1511. The dense, swarming composition shows the young Dürer pushing the woodcut toward an expressive power the medium had never carried before.

The four horsemen of the Apocalypse ride down humanity in the most celebrated woodcut from Durer's Apocalypse series of 1498, illustrating the vision of Revelation 6. This impression is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

A watercolour and gouache study of a clump of meadow plants, dandelions and grasses, viewed at ground level with botanical exactitude. The work is a touchstone of Renaissance nature study and prefigures modern ecological imagery.

An early woodcut of six men relaxing around a Nuremberg bathhouse pump, several modelled on Dürer's friends and possibly himself. The crowded composition lets him show male anatomy from multiple angles in a vernacular setting.

A woodcut of an Indian rhinoceros gifted to King Manuel I of Portugal, drawn from a written description and a sketch since Dürer never saw the animal. He sheathes it in armour-like plates, an invented anatomy that dominated European imagery of the species for centuries.
collection-of-beauty-alexander-iii-recep: A wide-format Russian historical scene of Tsar Alexander III addressing village elders gathered in the Petrovsky Palace courtyard during his coronation. Repin orchestrates the crowd with his characteristic eye for individuated peasant types and ceremonial pomp.
collection-of-beauty-alexandra-and-elena: A double portrait of Grand Duchesses Alexandra and Elena Pavlovna, daughters of Paul I, painted soon after Vigée Le Brun's arrival at the Russian court in exile from revolutionary France. Soft pastel-like flesh and silvery silks display the courtly grace that made her Marie Antoinette's preferred portraitist.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-1896-a: From the four-panel decorative series The Seasons, this allegorical figure stands among ripening fruit and ochre foliage. Mucha frames her in the slender vertical format and circular halo motif that defined his Parisian poster style.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-1896-s: Part of Mucha's first Seasons cycle, the figure plays a lyre fashioned from a branch, surrounded by fresh blossoms and songbirds. The pale palette and arabesque hair are signatures of his early Champenois lithographs.

From the Seasons quartet issued by Champenois, a languid woman trails her feet in water beneath ripe poppies. Mucha sets her in the elongated whiplash silhouette that became shorthand for fin-de-siècle Paris.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-1896-w: Closing the Seasons set, a fur-cloaked woman warms a small bird against a snow-laden branch. The cool blue-grey palette and stylized snowfall demonstrate Mucha's command of decorative colour lithography.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-1898-d: Part of The Arts panel series, an entranced female personification floats through swirling drapery and autumnal leaves. Mucha treats movement itself as ornament, threading line through the figure in continuous arabesques.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-1898-t: From the four-panel Flowers series, a virginal figure rises among towering white lilies in a symmetrical decorative niche. Mucha equates the woman with the bloom, fusing botanical study and Art Nouveau allegory.
collection-of-beauty-alfons-mucha-the-mo: From the pair The Moon and the Stars, a pale-skinned figure leans against a glowing lunar disc among night clouds. The cool silvers and indigos show Mucha working in a more nocturnal, dream-laden register than his daylight posters.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-018: The Seine at Bougival, low banks and a pale sky reflected in still water. Sisley painted the riverside in 1876 during the years he worked the villages downstream of Paris, oil on canvas, the broken touch typical of his mature landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-020: Two haystacks stand in a stubble field at Moret under a wide sky, casting long shadows across the cut ground. Sisley painted the pair in 1895, working the thatch in broken strokes of gold and russet. The horizon sits low, giving most of the canvas to the changing light overhead.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-023: The cast-iron suspension bridge across the Seine at Villeneuve-la-Garenne, with a stone pier at its centre and rowing boats below. Sisley painted the span during a campaign in the Argenteuil district in 1872, oil on canvas, now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (gift of Mr. and Mrs. Henry Ittleson Jr., 1964).
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-038: The church of Notre-Dame at Moret-sur-Loing seen close up, its Gothic buttresses and stonework filling the upper canvas above a row of low houses. Sisley painted a series of views of the church between 1893 and 1894, varying the light across its west front. He worked the masonry in short strokes of cream, ochre and grey-blue.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-050: Sailing boats and spectators on the Thames at Molesey, bright bunting strung along the bank for the local regatta. Sisley painted the scene during a four-month stay in England in 1874, oil on canvas, bequeathed by Gustave Caillebotte and now in the Musée d'Orsay (R.F. 2787).
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-057: A still life of black grapes and walnuts spread on a white cloth, a knife laid across the table edge. Sisley rarely painted still life, making the 1876 canvas unusual in his output, which is dominated by river and village landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-062: Floodwater standing in the streets of Port-Marly, a wine merchant's house rising from the inundated quay with a rowing boat alongside. Sisley returned to the flooded village several times in 1876, producing a small series of canvases of the high Seine.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-064: The banks of the river Loing at Moret-sur-Loing, with low buildings and a stand of trees mirrored in the slow water. Sisley settled in the Moret district from 1880 and painted the Loing repeatedly until his death in 1899. The sky occupies the upper half of the canvas, worked in pale blue and grey above the green riverbank.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-065: The bank of the Seine under autumn foliage, reflections breaking across the water in short horizontal strokes. Sisley painted the riverside subject in 1876, oil on canvas, working in the loose touch he developed alongside Monet in the villages west of Paris.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-the-l: The Canal du Loing at Moret recedes between rows of bare poplars whose trunks are doubled in the still water. Oil on canvas of 1892, given to the Musée du Luxembourg by friends of the painter led by Claude Monet after his death and now in the Musée d'Orsay (INV 20723). Sisley kept to the canal's straight perspective lines through many canvases of the early 1890s.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-the-r: A road running past garden walls towards Hampton Court, figures walking under a high, clouded sky. Painted during Sisley's 1874 stay near London, when he produced a series of nearly twenty views of the non-tidal Thames, oil on canvas, now in the Neue Pinakothek, Munich.
collection-of-beauty-alfred-sisley-women: Figures on the main street of Marlotte, a village at the edge of the Fontainebleau forest, the women setting out to gather firewood. Oil on canvas, about 65 by 92 cm, painted in 1866. Sisley showed it at the Paris Salon that year, the first time the jury accepted his work.
collection-of-beauty-allee-de-chataignie: An avenue of chestnut trees in the woods at La Celle-Saint-Cloud, the path running back between heavy trunks toward a clearing. Among Sisley's earliest plein-air canvases, painted in the mid-1860s alongside Bazille in the same woods. Oil on canvas, in his pre-Impressionist Barbizon-inflected manner.
collection-of-beauty-allegory-of-paintin: A female personification of Painting holds her palette and brushes amid putti and the attributes of the art, set on a low dais. Painted by Boucher in 1765, the year he was appointed Premier Peintre du Roi, the canvas is held by the Smithsonian's National Gallery of Art in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-almina-daughter-of-: Almina Wertheimer poses cross-legged in Persian costume, a long-necked sarod balanced across her lap. Painted in 1908 when the sitter was about twenty-two, this was the last of Sargent's nine portraits of the Wertheimer family, bequeathed to the British nation in 1922 and now in Tate.
collection-of-beauty-along-the-river-dur: A Qing court reinterpretation of the celebrated Song handscroll documenting Qingming festivities along the Bian River. Shen Yuan, an academician under the Qianlong emperor, executes the panorama in fine ink line touched with sparing ochre washes.
collection-of-beauty-altaarstuk-van-het-: The altarpiece of the Antwerp joiners' guild, with the Lamentation at centre flanked by wing scenes of the martyrdoms of John the Baptist and John the Evangelist. Completed by Quinten Metsys in 1511 for the cathedral of Our Lady, the triptych is now held by the Royal Museum of Fine Arts in Antwerp under inventory numbers 245-248.
collection-of-beauty-alte-nationalgaleri: Wilhelm Gentz's monumental oil on canvas, more than two and a half meters wide, records the entry of Crown Prince Friedrich Wilhelm of Prussia, the future Emperor Frederick III, into Jerusalem in November 1869, a visit made on his journey to the opening of the Suez Canal. The prince rides a white horse at the center of a teeming procession outside the city walls, surrounded by dignitaries, onlookers in Ottoman and Arab dress and waving palm fronds, with the domes of Jerusalem beyond. Gentz, a specialist in Orientalist subjects, completed the painting in 1876, when it was acquired by the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin.

Franz Kruger records a military parade held on Berlin's Opernplatz in 1822, with cavalry drawn up before the opera house and a dense crowd of recognisable Berliners given as much attention as the royal party, which includes Frederick William III of Prussia and the future Tsar Nicholas I. Commissioned by Nicholas, then Grand Duke of Russia, the monumental oil on canvas - roughly 2.5 by 3.7 metres - occupied the painter from 1824 to 1830. It entered the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin in 1928.
collection-of-beauty-amalia-van-solms-ge: Amalia van Solms, widow of Frederick Henry, stands at knee-length beside a balustrade and column, an olive branch of peace in her right hand. Painted in 1650 as the pendant to her husband's posthumous portrait, the canvas commemorates the Treaty of Münster that ended the Eighty Years' War.
collection-of-beauty-ambroise-vollard-av: The dealer Ambroise Vollard wrapped in a red headscarf, the bare head and heavy features set against a warm ground. Renoir painted Vollard, who handled much of his work after 1900, in 1906; oil on canvas, now in the Petit Palais, Paris. The close-keyed reds and softened modelling are typical of the artist's late Cagnes years.
collection-of-beauty-ambrosius-and-hans-: Two boys in caps, the brothers Ambrosius and Hans Holbein the Younger, share a single sheet drawn from life by their father. Executed in silverpoint on white-coated paper at 10.3 by 15.5 cm, the 1511 study is preserved in the Kupferstichkabinett of the Berlin State Museums.
collection-of-beauty-amor-vincet-omnia: A naturalistic Cupid in the Berlin Gemäldegalerie, who clambers grinning over scattered emblems of music, war, science, and rule. Caravaggio's tenebrist lighting and the boy's frank nudity made the picture notorious among Roman collectors.
collection-of-beauty-amsterdam-musee-van: Painted during Monet's brief stay in the Dutch bulb fields near Sassenheim, this canvas spreads horizontal bands of red and yellow tulips before distant windmills. The high-keyed palette previews the saturated colour Monet would later push at Giverny.
collection-of-beauty-an-afternoon-stroll: Chase paints his wife and one of their children walking through the dunes at Shinnecock, Long Island, where he ran his summer school of plein-air painting. Loose, sun-bleached brushwork shows his absorption of French Impressionism into an American idiom.
collection-of-beauty-an-experiment-on-a-: A candle-lit demonstration of a vacuum pump, with a cockatoo gasping in its glass globe as a mixed audience reacts in awe, fascination, and dread. Wright transposes religious chiaroscuro onto the new theatre of Enlightenment science.
collection-of-beauty-anatomy-wellcome-l0: A full skeleton stands facing the viewer in a lush river landscape, left arm extended, while a winged putto hovers at its shoulder holding up a billowing drape. The 1747 etching follows the anatomical tables of Bernhard Siegfried Albinus, whose atlas famously set its specimens in living, pastoral scenery to give the bones scale and vitality; this plate was engraved for the English edition by Charles Grignion. The impression comes from the Wellcome Collection, London.

A skeleton seen from behind with the left arm extended, engraved by Gérard Jean-Baptiste Scotin after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Bernhard Siegfried Albinus's anatomical atlas. Albinus's plates, first published in Leiden in 1747, set a new standard of precision by posing the skeleton like a living figure within a measured grid. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.

A standing skeleton in side view with the left arm extended, engraved by Simon François Ravenet after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Albinus's anatomical atlas of 1747. The plates combined exacting anatomical measurement with the poise of classical statuary, and were widely copied across Europe. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.

An écorché figure seen from the front, engraved by Charles Grignion after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Albinus's anatomical atlas. The grazing rhinoceros in the background is Clara, the celebrated Indian rhinoceros who toured Europe in the 1740s — Wandelaar sketched her in Leiden and used her to lend scale and life to the plates. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.

The companion écorché figure seen from behind, engraved by Charles Grignion after Jan Wandelaar's drawings for Albinus's anatomical atlas, again with the rhinoceros Clara in the background. Pairing the flayed figure with the exotic animal made these among the most recognisable anatomical prints of the eighteenth century. This impression is held by the Wellcome Collection.
collection-of-beauty-anbetung-der-konige: Bruegel sets the Adoration of the Magi inside a snowbound Flemish village, the Holy Family barely visible amid woodcutters, skaters, and falling flakes. Painted in tempera on panel, it is one of the earliest snow scenes in Western painting.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-del-sarto-as: The Virgin rises on a bank of clouds while apostles cluster around the empty tomb below, their cloaks twisting in the agitated rhythm Sarto carried into late maturity. Known as the Poppi Altarpiece for the Tuscan town it was painted for in 1530, the panel is now in the Galleria Palatina at the Palazzo Pitti.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-del-sarto-he: The severed head of John the Baptist lies on a metal charger, eyes closed, the matted hair falling away from a relaxed jaw. Painted around 1523 and now at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the small devotional panel exemplifies Andrea del Sarto's tender Florentine modelling.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-del-sarto-pi: The dead Christ rests against the Virgin's lap, attended by Mary Magdalene, Saint Peter, Saint Paul and Saint Catherine in a tight pyramidal group. Painted between 1523 and 1524 for the convent of San Pietro a Luco in the Mugello, the altarpiece is now in the Palazzo Pitti in Florence.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-del-sarto-po: A young man in a black doublet turns toward the viewer with one hand resting on a parapet, his face emerging from a darkened ground. Andrea del Sarto painted the sitter around 1517, and the picture was long thought to be a self-portrait; Vasari wrote that had Andrea's spirit matched his judgement he would have been without equal among Florentine painters.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-mantegna-014: Saint Sebastian stands bound to a fragmented classical column, his body bristling with arrows against a ruined ancient cityscape. Mantegna fuses humanist antiquarianism with Christian martyrdom, a recurring preoccupation in his Mantuan years.
collection-of-beauty-andrea-mantegna-the: Christ's body is laid on a marble slab and seen in radical foreshortening from the soles of his pierced feet. Mantegna's hard, sculptural line and reduced palette turn the Lamentation into an exercise in perspectival shock.
collection-of-beauty-anisimov-alexander-: The icon historian Alexander Ivanovich Anisimov is shown seated, hand resting near a book, in muted greys against a sober wall. Kustodiev painted the portrait in 1915 from his wheelchair after spinal surgery; Anisimov was a leading scholar of medieval Russian painting and would later be arrested and shot in the Stalinist purges.
collection-of-beauty-ann-fairchild-bowle: Ann Fairchild Bowler, wife of the Newport merchant and politician Metcalf Bowler, sits in a blue silk gown with a fold of drapery behind her. The 1758 canvas is one of a pair of pendant portraits Copley painted of the Bowlers during his early Boston practice and now belongs to the Colby College Museum of Art in Waterville, Maine.
collection-of-beauty-anna-alexandrovna-g: A Hermitage portrait of the Georgian-born Princess Galitzin, painted during Vigée Le Brun's long Russian exile after the Revolution. Pale silks and a soft sfumato face exemplify the flattering ancien-régime manner she carried across European courts.
collection-of-beauty-anna-hillmayer-1829: Anna Hillmayer, daughter of a Munich game merchant, sat for this picture as part of Ludwig I's Gallery of Beauties. Stieler departs from aristocratic convention to record a tradesman's daughter with the same idealised serenity and porcelain finish he gave his royal sitters.
collection-of-beauty-anna-payne-cutts-by: Dolley Madison's younger sister Anna Payne Cutts, wife of Massachusetts congressman Richard Cutts, sits in a soft white gown against a neutral ground. Stuart painted her in Washington shortly after her marriage, working in the bust-length format he reserved for society wives of the early Republic.
collection-of-beauty-anne-de-cleves-hans: Anne of Cleves stands frontally in a richly embroidered Saxon gown and gabled headdress, her hands folded low in front of her. Holbein painted the small panel on parchment in 1539 during his diplomatic mission to Düren; Henry VIII chose his fourth wife from it, with consequences both sitter and painter would regret. Now in the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-annibale-carracci-c: An early devotional work from the Bolognese reformer of late-Mannerist painting, the composition tightens onto the suffering Christ as winged attendants steady his body. Carracci leans on the warm chiaroscuro and sculptural drapery he absorbed from Correggio and Venetian sources.
collection-of-beauty-annibale-carracci-p: The dead Christ slumps across the Virgin's lap as two grieving angels hold up his arm and a crown of thorns. Carracci's restrained classicism, Bolognese in its rigour, became a key model for seventeenth-century devotional painting.
collection-of-beauty-annibale-carracci-r: An ideal river view in which figures crossing a wooden bridge are dwarfed by the broad waterway and distant hills. Carracci helped invent the classical landscape tradition later codified by Poussin and Claude, balancing observed Italian topography with a calm, ordered geometry.
collection-of-beauty-annibale-carracci-s: The chaste Susanna recoils as two elders intrude on her bath, the biblical pretext for a study of startled flesh against shaded foliage. Carracci stages the assault with the firm contour and idealised anatomy he was simultaneously developing for the Farnese ceiling.
collection-of-beauty-annibale-carracci-t: Two aproned butchers work among hanging carcasses and joints of meat, one trimming a cut while the other hangs a side — a small canvas of the early 1580s, the more compact of Carracci's two butcher-shop pictures (the larger is at Christ Church, Oxford), now in the Kimbell Art Museum, Fort Worth. Carracci's interest in low-life genre, drawn from northern prints and direct observation, gives the scene an unusually frank realism for its date.
collection-of-beauty-anonymous-brustbild: A bust-length study of a young man, plainly dressed and turned slightly toward the viewer, kept in the Belvedere as part of the German Romantic holdings. Runge favoured this kind of clear, almost severe portrait pared back to face and gaze.
collection-of-beauty-anonymous-ten-thous: An eleven-metre handscroll on silk that travels the Yangtze from its mountain source to the sea, opening section by section in the hand of the viewer. Long attributed to the Southern Song master Xia Gui, it strings together mist, gorges, fishing villages and city walls in characteristic axe-cut brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-anthonis-van-dyck-0: The Genoese noblewoman descends a terrace beneath a parasol held by an African page, the pairing a familiar device in van Dyck's Italian portraits of patrician women. Crimson drapery, towering verticals and a reserved, columnar pose set the template for European court portraiture.

The wine-soaked Silenus, fleshy and unsteady, is propped up by satyrs and a maenad in a tightly cropped Bacchic ensemble. The composition descends from Rubens's workshop, where the young van Dyck assimilated the older master's ruddy, full-bodied paint handling.
collection-of-beauty-anthony-van-dyck-ma: A tender likeness of the painter's Scottish wife, posed with a quiet half-smile against a neutral ground. Van Dyck reserves his usual aristocratic finery for a domestic intimacy, the silvery silks softened by his late, more thinly brushed manner.
collection-of-beauty-anthony-van-dyck-ra: Rachel de Ruvigny, Countess of Southampton, is shown as Fortune perched on a globe, a moralised allegory of worldly mutability much favoured in Caroline court portraiture. Cool blue satins and a still, ovular face are vintage van Dyck.
collection-of-beauty-antoine-coypel-man-: A reclining man sleeps with his head pillowed against a woman's lap, her hand still resting on his temple. Coypel painted the small intimate scene around 1716, near the end of his life, the loose handling and pastoral mood already prefiguring the fetes galantes of Watteau.
collection-of-beauty-antoine-coypel-self: Coypel turns toward the viewer in a powdered wig and dark coat, the painter aged into the senior office of First Painter to the King. The self-portrait dates to 1715, the year before his death, when he had been directing the Academie royale and the royal painting collections under Louis XIV.
collection-of-beauty-anton-van-dyck-anto: The Genoese patron rides forward beneath a heavy classical arch, a swaggering equestrian formula van Dyck adapted from Rubens and Titian. Now in the Palazzo Rosso, the canvas anchors the painter's six-year Italian sojourn.
collection-of-beauty-anton-van-dyck-sams: Delilah leans forward in shock as Philistine soldiers seize the shorn Samson from her lap, the moment of betrayal pitched between sensuality and violence. Van Dyck reworks Rubens's earlier composition with cooler colour and a more refined, elongated drawing.
collection-of-beauty-aphonse-mucha-rose-: A young woman wreathed in roses stands within a decorative arch, her flowing hair and gown merging with the surrounding blooms. Part of Mucha's Flowers series of four panel decorations, the design exemplifies the Art Nouveau idiom he refined in Paris in the late 1890s.
collection-of-beauty-apocalypse-vasnetso: Conquest, War, Famine and Death ride abreast through a churning sky above a burning landscape, the Lamb of God visible in the upper register. Vasnetsov painted the seventy-two by one hundred and thirty-six centimetre oil in 1887; the canvas is held by the Glinka State Central Museum of Musical Culture in Moscow, with a preparatory study in the Museum of the History of Religion in St Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-arabian-nights-3-by: A finely worked Orientalist scene drawn from the Thousand and One Nights, set inside one of the tiled, latticed interiors Lewis studied during his decade in Cairo. He is best known for the jewel-bright watercolour technique that lets sunlight pick its way across carpets and costume.
collection-of-beauty-arcimboldo-air-copy: Birds of every order roost on and form a human profile, one of four allegories of the elements painted for the Habsburg court. Arcimboldo's composite portraits flatter the encyclopaedic ambitions of Maximilian II while showing off the painter's natural-history library.
collection-of-beauty-arcimboldo-earth: A bust assembled from terrestrial mammals — stag, lion, hare, ox — interlocking to form a crowned Habsburg profile. The conceit, painted at the Prague court, casts imperial dominion as a literal incorporation of the natural world.
collection-of-beauty-arcimboldo-les-sais: A male head built from the harvest, with a pear nose, apple cheeks, a pomegranate chin and a crown of grapes and vine leaves bound by a barrel-stave neck. Part of the Seasons series Arcimboldo painted for the Habsburg court in 1573, the version at the Louvre carries the imperial monogram tying the cycle to Emperor Maximilian II.
collection-of-beauty-arcimboldowater: A profile fashioned from fish, crustaceans, coral and pearls, completing the Vienna set of the four elements. Arcimboldo treats the composite as both witty courtly device and a serious display of zoological knowledge.
collection-of-beauty-arethusa-by-benjami: The nymph Arethusa bathing in a stream, drawn from Book V of Ovid's Metamorphoses, the viewer positioned where the river god Alpheus first catches sight of her. Painted in 1802 and shown that year at the Royal Academy in London while West was its president, the canvas now hangs at the High Museum of Art in Atlanta.
collection-of-beauty-argenteuil-a14692: Sailboats lie along the bank of the Seine at Argenteuil, the suburban boating town where Monet settled after the Franco-Prussian War. Quick comma-strokes break the water and sky into the broken, prismatic colour that became the signature of early Impressionism.
collection-of-beauty-arnaut-and-his-dog-: A Balkan mercenary in Ottoman service exhales pipe smoke into the muzzle of a patient hound on a sunlit Cairo street. Gérôme's enamel-smooth surface and ethnographic exactitude are typical of his late Orientalist studies of idle, picturesque soldiery.
collection-of-beauty-arsene-vigeant-john: The Metz fencing master Arsene Vigeant sits at a table with his fingers marking a page in a thick book, his foil pushed back into a far corner of the canvas. Sargent painted the oil in 1885, registering his sitter's transition from swordsman to scholar of fencing history; Vigeant bequeathed the picture to the city of Metz, where it entered the Musee de la Cour d'Or in 1920.
collection-of-beauty-artemisia-gentilesc: The Egyptian queen lies dead across her bed, asp at the breast, in a foreshortened nude that confronts the viewer at close range. The picture sits within the Gentileschi family's repertoire of half-length heroines of antiquity, attributed variously to Artemisia and her father Orazio.

The Argive princess reclines as Jupiter's golden shower falls into her lap, her maid scrambling to gather the coins. The picture, long shared between Artemisia and her father Orazio, channels Caravaggesque tenebrism into a sensuous, half-length nude.

Judith and her servant pause in Holofernes's tent, alerted by a sound outside; a single candle throws Judith's shielding hand into silhouette and glances off the discarded gauntlet. The Detroit canvas is among Artemisia's most theatrical exercises in Caravaggesque candle-light.

A young Virgin offers her breast to the sleeping Christ Child in a quiet domestic register. Painted near the start of Artemisia's Roman career, it shows her absorbing Caravaggio's bare interiors and her father's silver-cool flesh tones.

The penitent Magdalene twists in her chair, gold gown slipping, hand pressed to her breast in conversion. Artemisia gives the Counter-Reformation subject the muscular, psychologically charged female protagonist that is her hallmark.
collection-of-beauty-artlib-gallery-1387: A requiem on a frozen plain: a priest swings a censer over a field of fallen Russian soldiers after the Russo-Turkish War. Vereshchagin painted the scene from direct experience as a war correspondent, part of his unsparing campaign against martial glamour.
collection-of-beauty-arundel-mill-and-ca: A water mill on the River Arun in the foreground, with Arundel Castle's keep rising through trees on the slope beyond. Constable spent the entire day of 31 March 1837 putting the last touches on the canvas and died unexpectedly that night; his friend C. R. Leslie sent it to the Royal Academy summer exhibition the following year as his final work.
collection-of-beauty-as-the-old-sing-so-: A multi-generational Flemish family bellows around a table while a child blows a pipe, illustrating the proverb inscribed at the top: as the old sing, so the young pipe. Jordaens returned to the boisterous moralised feast many times, this version inscribed Ut genus est genius.
collection-of-beauty-asakusa-honganji-te: A roofer kneels on the great tiled ridge of the Asakusa Hongan-ji while a kite drifts past and Mount Fuji rises in the distance. Plate four of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji turns the sacred peak into a small constant glimpsed across Edo's working rooftops.
collection-of-beauty-at-eternity-s-gate-: An old man sits on a plain chair, fists pressed to his eyes in a posture of complete despair. Van Gogh painted the canvas at Saint-Rémy in early May 1890, returning in oil to a lithograph he had made in The Hague in 1882 of the same model, the almshouse pensioner Adrianus Jacobus Zuyderland. It is in the Kröller-Müller Museum, Otterlo.
collection-of-beauty-at-first-glance-he-: A glowering giant's face is, on closer look, made up entirely of squirming naked men — a sly anatomical pun on the proverb in the title. Kuniyoshi produced such jigsaw figures to slip past Tempō-era censorship that restricted depictions of named actors and courtesans.
collection-of-beauty-at-the-beer-garden-: A crowded Munich beer garden seethes with waitresses, top hats and bourgeois families under the chestnut trees. Menzel, the chronicler of modern German urban life, packs the canvas with the sharp-eyed, almost photographic detail he gathered in pocket sketchbooks.
collection-of-beauty-at-the-stock-exchan: The banker Ernest May, top-hatted and pince-nez'd, listens to a colleague leaning over his shoulder while the trading floor blurs into faceless agitation behind them. Degas painted his collector and admirer in 1878,79, applying Edmond Duranty's call for portraits that read a sitter's profession in his bearing.
collection-of-beauty-at-volga-kustodiev: A young woman in a bright sarafan stands on a bluff above the Volga, with steamboats and white-walled churches visible along the bend of the river. Painted in 1922, the canvas belongs to Kustodiev's late series of provincial pastorals that rebuilt the lost world of the Russian merchant towns from memory.
collection-of-beauty-auguste-renoir-a-gi: A small girl in a blue dress and lace-trimmed pinafore stands on a garden path holding a watering can, flowers scattered at her feet. Renoir painted the figure in 1876, oil on canvas, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington (Chester Dale Collection).
collection-of-beauty-auguste-renoir-en-e: A dark-eyed young woman sits outdoors in a loose white blouse, her hair undone — the painter's model and lover Lise Tréhot cast as a summer bohémienne. The picture predates Renoir's full Impressionist break and still owes a debt to Courbet's full-bodied realism.
collection-of-beauty-auguste-renoir-la-g: Bathers and rowboats cluster around the floating café on the Seine at Bougival, the spot where Renoir and Monet spent the summer of 1869 painting side by side. Broken touches of opaque colour on the water mark one of the foundational moments of Impressionism.
collection-of-beauty-auguste-renoir-the-: A young woman stands on a rope swing in a garden talking with a man seen from behind, sunlight falling in patches of blue and rose through the leaves.
