Renoir painted it in the summer of 1876 in the gardens below the Moulin de la Galette, oil on canvas, now in the Musée d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-auguste-renoir-youn: Two girls in white and pink dresses lean over an upright piano, one seated and playing while the other follows the score. Renoir painted this version in 1892 as the first of his works acquired by the French state, placed in the Musée du Luxembourg and now in the Musée d'Orsay. He made several oil and drawn repetitions of the composition for dealers and collectors.
collection-of-beauty-augustins-le-christ: Rubens stages the Crucifixion with the two thieves flanking Christ, the muscular bodies twisting against a darkened sky in the dynamic Counter-Reformation idiom. Originally painted for a Flemish religious setting, the altarpiece deploys the diagonal energy and ruddy flesh tones characteristic of his Antwerp workshop, and now hangs in the Musée des Augustins in Toulouse.
collection-of-beauty-autoportrait-au-ber: The painter shown half-length in a soft beret and dark coat, turned slightly from the viewer with a guarded expression. Oil on canvas of about 1898 to 1900, in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. It is among the last of the roughly two dozen self-portraits Cézanne made across his career.
collection-of-beauty-autoportrait-au-tur: Rigaud, the great portraitist of Louis XIV's court, presents himself in an exotic turban, a studio prop conveying artistic vanity and learned cosmopolitanism. The lustrous fabrics and confident chiaroscuro foreshadow the polished grandeur he would soon bring to royal portraiture.
collection-of-beauty-autoportrait-avec-u: A bearded self-portrait set against a dull olive-green wallpaper whose pattern Cézanne echoes in the modelling of the head. Painted in Paris around 1880 to 1881, oil on canvas, now in the National Gallery, London. The dome of the skull is built from short oblique patches of white, red and ochre, the ear and crown outlined in blue.
collection-of-beauty-ave-caesar-morituri: Jean-Leon Gerome's academic vision of the Roman arena shows gladiators saluting the emperor with the famous formula "Hail Caesar, those who are about to die salute you." The painting epitomizes the meticulous archaeological detail and theatrical staging of nineteenth-century French history painting.
collection-of-beauty-ayvaz-sredy-voln: Foaming swells crest under a torn, luminous sky in a wholly unpeopled marine. Aivazovsky painted Among the Waves in 1898 at the age of eighty-one, judging it the finest canvas of his late career; it remains in the gallery he founded at Feodosia in Crimea.
collection-of-beauty-b159-rembrandt: A rare still life from Rembrandt's etched oeuvre, depicting a single cone shell (Conus marmoreus) rendered with delicate cross-hatching and drypoint burr. The print attests to the Dutch fascination with exotic naturalia gathered through global trade.
collection-of-beauty-b320-rembrandt: An early self-portrait etching from Rembrandt's Leiden years, the young artist studies his own face under a soft cap, probing expression and shadow. Such prints functioned as exercises in physiognomy and as advertisements of his graphic virtuosity.
collection-of-beauty-afganets: A standing portrait of an Afghan man in regional dress. Oil painting from Vereshchagin's Turkestan series, made in 1867 to 1868 after the artist joined General Kaufman's expedition to Central Asia. Vereshchagin combined ethnographic portraits of this kind with the battle scenes drawn from the same campaign.
collection-of-beauty-back-view-of-fuji-f: Hiroshige reverses the conventional southern view of Fuji, glimpsing the sacred peak from Kai Province on the mountain's far side. Part of his first Thirty-six Views series, the design uses graduated bokashi printing to layer mist, peak, and foreground.
collection-of-beauty-bad-war: Swiss pikemen and German Landsknechts close in the murderous melee known as der schlimme Krieg, where pikes have become useless and halberds and short swords decide the fight. The early sixteenth-century woodcut by Hans Holbein the Younger is preserved among the Albertina's holdings in Vienna.
collection-of-beauty-baglione: Baglione's allegory pits divine love against earthly desire, a youthful angel descending upon a slumbering Cupid. The picture famously rivalled Caravaggio's treatment of the same subject and helped fuel the bitter feud between the two Roman painters.
collection-of-beauty-baigneurs-a-asniere: A preparatory study for Une Baignade, Asnieres, this seated nude shows Seurat working out volume through hatched conte crayon on textured paper. The drawing predates his fully pointillist technique but already pursues the luminous tonal gradations he called irradiation.
collection-of-beauty-bakst-self: A young Léon Bakst presents himself in three-quarter view against a neutral ground, the brushwork loose and the modelling kept to essentials. Painted in 1893, well before his Ballets Russes designs reshaped European stage costume, the self-portrait dates from Bakst's early years training in Saint Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-bakst-uhzin1902: A theatrical interior scene by Léon Bakst, painted on 24 January 1902 in the years before he became the principal designer for Diaghilev's Ballets Russes. The early canvas belongs to his St Petersburg period, when he was still working primarily for the World of Art circle.
collection-of-beauty-baldassare-castigli: Raphael portrays his friend, the courtier and author of The Book of the Courtier, in a restrained palette of grey, black, and pearly white. The composed three-quarter pose and steady gaze became a touchstone for European court portraiture, admired and copied by Rembrandt and Rubens.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-apullia-i: An early classical landscape by J. M. W. Turner, exhibited at the British Institution and pointedly modelled on Claude Lorrain to challenge the older master's reputation. Sunlit foliage, distant temples and a literary Ovidian subject mark Turner's ambition to inherit the grand European pastoral tradition.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-lake-luce: A watercolour from Turner's late Swiss tours, when he returned repeatedly to Lake Lucerne in search of atmospheric subjects. From the heights above Brunnen the bay opens in pale washes of blue and pearl, mountains dissolving into the luminous haze that defined his final manner. The sheet belongs to a celebrated group of Swiss studies now held by Tate Britain.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-shipping-: A loose marine sketch from Turner's mature years, when his oils and watercolours of shipping abandoned topographic detail for weather and mood. Hulls and masts emerge from a smear of sea and sky, the kind of working study that fed his later exhibited storm and harbour pictures.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-story-of-: A late mythological landscape by Turner, the Ovidian chase staged across a golden Italianate valley bathed in the swirling light he had brought back from his Roman travels. Figures dwindle beside vast trees and rivers, drama dissolved into atmosphere in the manner of his ageing Claude homages.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-stromy-se: A late Turner oil sketch in which a burning ship is nearly engulfed by towering surf and smoke. Paint is scrubbed and scraped into vortices of orange and lead grey, rendering catastrophe as pure elemental force. The work belongs to the Tate Bequest of unfinished canvases that Turner left in his studio at his death.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-the-lake-: A small oil sketch from the series of sample studies Turner produced during his extended stays at Petworth House as guest of the 3rd Earl of Egremont. The lake dissolves into flat horizontal bands of pink, gold and lavender beneath a low sun, anticipating the radical atmospheric freedom of his late visionary landscapes. The study remained in Turner's studio and entered the Turner Bequest at Tate Britain.
collection-of-beauty-barcelona-the-new-m: A small seaside scene from Turner's late period, where two children quarrel over a lost boat and a hoop on a wide tidal shore beneath a pale new moon. The trivial human anecdote is set against an expansive luminous sky and estuary, characteristic of Turner's mature handling of atmosphere and light. The work entered the national collection through the Turner Bequest and is held at Tate Britain.
collection-of-beauty-barrikade-in-der-br: A barricade of paving stones and overturned carts blocks the Breite Strasse in Berlin during the March 1848 revolution, a tricolour flag planted at the summit. Gaertner, the city's leading topographical painter, sketched the uprising on the spot and worked it up in oil that same year.
collection-of-beauty-bartlett-cabbage-ma: Stallholders weigh cabbages under canvas awnings in a busy provincial market square. Bartlett painted the watercolour in 1900, more than a decade before the Honolulu and shin-hanga prints that defined his later career; the sheet was sold at Bonhams Bond Street, London.
collection-of-beauty-bartolome-esteban-m: The first canonised saint of the Americas kneels in the white and black habit of a Dominican tertiary, gazing on the Christ Child seated on a cushion above her workbasket. Murillo presents the Limeña mystic with the gentle sweetness and silvery half-light that defined his late religious painting.
collection-of-beauty-bartolome-esteban-p: Joseph stoops to play with the infant Jesus and a small bird while Mary pauses at her spinning, the goldfinch a traditional emblem of the Passion to come. The domestic warmth and soft chiaroscuro are typical of Murillo's Sevillian devotional pictures, which translated sacred subjects into the rhythms of family life.
collection-of-beauty-bartolomeo-magagnos: A pencil head-and-shoulders study of Bartolomeo Magagnosco, inscribed Nice, January 1875, when Sargent was nineteen and travelling on the Riviera with his family. Now in the Philadelphia Museum of Art, the sheet shows the assured contour drawing that underpinned the oil portraits with which Sargent would debut at the Paris Salon two years later.
collection-of-beauty-bartolomeo-nazari-p: The celebrated castrato Carlo Broschi, known as Farinelli, stands in court dress with the score of an operatic aria in hand. Bartolomeo Nazari painted the oil on canvas in 1734, the year the singer arrived in London to join the Opera of the Nobility, the company set up in rivalry to Handel's. The portrait belongs to the Royal College of Music, London.
collection-of-beauty-bartolommeo-nazari-: A bewigged sitter in a dark coat turns three-quarters toward the viewer against a plain ground. Painted by the Venetian late-Baroque portraitist Bartolomeo Nazari, who trained under Angelo Trevisani and worked for the British nobility on Grand Tour stops, the canvas entered the Fogg Museum at Harvard with the accession number 1943.116.
collection-of-beauty-basket-fishing-in-t: From the Oceans of Wisdom series on traditional fishing methods, Hokusai shows villagers wading the Kinu with woven basket traps. The flattened riverbank and tight figural grouping demonstrate his mature handling of genre subjects in the 1830s.
collection-of-beauty-bathsheba-c-1827-by: Hayez retells the Old Testament episode with a Venetian sensuousness, Bathsheba caught at her bath under King David's distant gaze. The smooth modelling and warm flesh tones reflect the Italian Romantic painter's debt to Titian.
collection-of-beauty-battle-of-revel: Russian ships of the line drive the Swedish fleet onto the rocks off Revel in May 1790, broken masts and shattered hulls littering the Baltic. Aivazovsky painted the action for the Naval Museum in St Petersburg, where it still hangs as part of his cycle of imperial sea victories.
collection-of-beauty-battle-of-sinope: Russian warships pound the Ottoman fleet at anchor in the harbour of Sinope, flames erupting from the wooden hulls against a black sky. Aivazovsky painted the November 1853 engagement, an early Crimean War victory for Admiral Nakhimov, from official accounts the year it occurred.
collection-of-beauty-battle-poitiers: King John II of France swings his battle-axe from horseback in the thick of the Anglo-French clash of 19 September 1356, English knights closing on him from every side. Commissioned by the Duchess of Berry in 1829 and finished in 1830, the canvas hangs in the Louvre and turns the medieval defeat into a swirling Romantic mêlée.
collection-of-beauty-battle-scene-after-: A press of armoured horsemen and pikemen tangles around a fallen standard in a sixteenth-century copy after a lost design by Hans Holbein the Younger. The composition descends from drawings Holbein made in Basel around 1530, part of the cycle of mercenary and tournament scenes that fed his designs for stained glass and printed broadsheets.
collection-of-beauty-bauakademie-schinke: The brick cube of Schinkel's Bauakademie rises on the Spreeinsel, its rhythmic terracotta façade and the figures crossing the Schleusenbrücke caught in clear afternoon light. Gaertner painted Schinkel's school of architecture in 1868, four decades after its completion; the building was destroyed in 1945 and demolished in 1962.
collection-of-beauty-bauernfeind-gustav-: Bauernfeind, the leading German Orientalist of his generation, records a crowded Jerusalem street where pilgrims and traders converge at the gates of Haram al-Sharif. His near-photographic precision rests on sketches gathered during repeated journeys to Palestine.
collection-of-beauty-bayron-s-visit-to-s: Lord Byron arrives by gondola at the Armenian monastery of San Lazzaro in the Venetian lagoon, greeted by Mekhitarist monks on the quayside. Aivazovsky painted the scene in 1899 from his own memories of working at the monastery in 1840, where he prepared the album Voyage to Venice with the abbot Gabriel Aivazian, his brother.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-and-camille: A figure study made for Monet's lost large-scale Dejeuner sur l'herbe, showing the painter Frederic Bazille and his future wife Camille Doncieux among forest light. The brisk plein-air handling already announces the broken touch that would define Impressionism.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-ai: The medieval ramparts of Aigues-Mortes seen across flat marshland under a wide sky. Oil on canvas, 46 by 55 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. Bazille made several views of the walled Camargue town during a summer in the region.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-fl: A dense bouquet rising from a vase set on a console table, catalogued as Vase de fleurs sur une console. Oil on canvas, 130 by 97 cm, painted between 1867 and 1868 and now in the Musée de Grenoble.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-la: A seated nude attended by two servants, one kneeling to dry her foot, the other holding cloth, in a curtained interior. Oil on canvas, 130 by 128 cm, painted between December 1869 and March 1870 and now in the Musée Fabre, Montpellier.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-po: A standing portrait of Alphonse Tissié in the uniform of a cuirassier, his plumed helmet and breastplate set off against a plain ground. Oil on canvas by Bazille, held at the Musée Fabre in Montpellier.

Bazille's friend Edmond Maître seen in full profile, seated and reading a book in his lap, the ground darkening toward the upper left. Oil on canvas painted in 1869, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-su: Young men in swimming costume resting and wrestling along the wooded bank of the Lez near Montpellier. Bazille drew the figures in his Paris studio before placing them in the open-air setting; the oil was shown at the Salon of 1870 and is now in the Harvard Art Museums (Fogg).
collection-of-beauty-bazille-frederic-vi: A young woman in a striped dress seated on a stone ledge above the village of Castelnau-le-Lez, the Hérault landscape spread behind her. Oil on canvas, painted in 1868 at the Bazille family property near Montpellier and now in the Musée Fabre.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-nature-mort: A dead heron and other birds laid on a table, a study in greys and browns. Oil on canvas, 98 by 78 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. Bazille painted it in a Paris studio alongside Sisley, who treated the same heron in his own canvas.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-pecheur-a-l: A nude male fisherman casting a circular throw-net at the water's edge, his back to the viewer. Bazille painted the canvas in 1868; it later entered the Rau Foundation for the Third World in Zurich, and stands among his experiments with the open-air male figure.
collection-of-beauty-bazille-sutdio-in-t: A corner of a sparsely furnished studio with two armchairs and a doorway opening onto a bedroom and a grey winter sky. Oil on canvas, painted in 1865 and held by the Musée Fabre, Montpellier. The room is the studio at 6 Place de Furstenberg that Bazille shared with Monet, in the building that now houses the Musée national Eugène Delacroix.
collection-of-beauty-beardsley-peacocksk: Beardsley's ink illustration for Oscar Wilde's Salome shows the princess in a sweeping skirt patterned with peacock eyes, confronting Herodias. The economy of black silhouette and decorative line, drawn from Japanese prints, became a touchstone of Art Nouveau graphic design.
collection-of-beauty-bellini-madonna-and: A close-framed Madonna and Child after Giovanni Bellini, the Virgin's mantle filling the panel behind the standing infant. The image was uploaded to Wikimedia Commons in 2023 by Gleb Simonov under a CC0 dedication, reproducing the late Bellini composition from around 1510.
collection-of-beauty-bellini-madonna-mit: The seated Virgin holds the Christ Child between a young John the Baptist and an elderly Elizabeth, a sacra conversazione gathered against a dark ground. Produced in Bellini's Venetian workshop in the 1490s and now in the Städel in Frankfurt, the panel uses the format to compress four figures into a tight half-length frieze.
collection-of-beauty-bellini-pieta-marti: The dead Christ is supported by the Virgin and a youthful John on a parapet, with a desert landscape and small towns of Vicenza, Ravenna and Cividale strung along the horizon. Signed on the rock beside Mary and painted around 1505, the panel was Giovanni Bellini's last Pietà and entered the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice from the Donà delle Rose collection.
collection-of-beauty-bellows-cliffdwelle: Tenement crowds spill from fire escapes, stoops, and laundry-strung windows on a sweltering summer evening on Manhattan's Lower East Side. Painted in May 1913 and now at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art, the canvas belongs to Bellows's Ashcan record of immigrant New York.
collection-of-beauty-bemberg-fondation-t: Monet paints fishing boats hauled up beneath the chalk cliffs of Étretat, a Norman coast he returned to repeatedly in the 1880s. The pale beach and overcast sea are built from short, broken strokes that record shifting weather rather than narrative incident. The canvas now resides at the Bemberg Foundation in Toulouse.

An early self-portrait by the painter best known for his hushed flower pieces and group portraits of the Parisian avant-garde. The dark ground and concentrated gaze owe much to his close study of seventeenth-century Dutch masters in the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-waterhouse: Benjamin Waterhouse, the Newport physician who later introduced smallpox vaccination to America, sits in a buttoned waistcoat with his hand at his lapel. Stuart painted the portrait in 1775, before either sitter or painter had left for medical and artistic training in London. The Redwood Library and Athenaeum in Newport holds it.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-005: British General James Wolfe lies dying among his officers on the Plains of Abraham after the 1759 capture of Quebec, a Mohawk scout watching at his side. West broke history-painting decorum by showing his subjects in contemporary uniform rather than classical dress, and the canvas at the National Gallery of Canada was widely copied in engraving.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-1738-: Edward III leads his army across the tidal ford at Blanchetaque in August 1346, mounted knights pressing forward as French defenders contest the far bank. Part of the Windsor history cycle commissioned by George III, West's canvas was painted in 1788 and is catalogued in the Royal Collection as RCIN 404566.

Edward III embraces his sixteen-year-old son the Black Prince on the field of Crecy in August 1346, French dead heaped at their feet. The 1788 canvas belongs to West's eight-picture chivalric cycle for the Audience Chamber at Windsor Castle, where it remains as RCIN 407523.

Double portrait of the future George IV in state robes alongside his younger brother Prince Frederick, later Duke of York, painted in 1777 for George III. West executed the canvas (RCIN 403399, Royal Collection) while serving as historical painter to the king, a post he had held since 1772.

Joseph Banks, just back from Cook's first Pacific voyage, stands in a long Maori cloak of dogskin with a taiaha at his feet and a tattooed mere on the table. West painted the portrait between 1771 and 1772 in London, presenting Banks as the gentleman naturalist of the Endeavour. The picture belongs to the Usher Gallery in Lincoln.

Six leading citizens of Calais, ropes around their necks and city keys in hand, kneel before Edward III as Queen Philippa pleads for their lives. West's 1789 canvas illustrates the chronicle by Froissart of the surrender of 1347 and forms part of the Windsor history cycle for George III, catalogued in the Royal Collection.

The French knight Bayard, mortally wounded by an arquebus shot during the retreat from the Sesia in 1524, leans against a tree to receive the rites as his enemy the Constable de Bourbon kneels beside him. West painted the canvas in 1772 for George III; it remains in the Royal Collection.

The Roman consul Marcus Atilius Regulus tears himself from his wife and children to return to certain torture in Carthage, having kept his oath to the enemy. The first picture George III commissioned from West, RCIN 405416, established the painter's role as history painter to the King and now hangs in the Royal Collection.

Edward III invests the founding knights of the Order of the Garter in 1348, the Black Prince kneeling at the centre of a crowded hall hung with banners. West painted the picture for George III's Audience Chamber at Windsor as part of a chivalric history cycle; it remains in the Royal Collection as RCIN 407521.

The young Hannibal kneels at an altar before his father Hamilcar Barca, swearing the lifelong oath of enmity against Rome. Painted as a pendant to The Departure of Regulus for George III, RCIN 405417 in the Royal Collection, the picture pairs Carthaginian and Roman exemplars of stoic resolve.

Thusnelda, wife of the Cheruscan chief Arminius, stands captive with her son before the Roman general Germanicus after the campaigns of 15 AD. West painted the Tacitean episode in 1773 for George III as part of the Windsor history series, in oil on canvas. It remains in the Royal Collection.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-agrip: The widow Agrippina disembarks at the Italian port of Brundisium carrying the urn that holds her husband Germanicus's ashes, flanked by mourners and her children. Commissioned by Archbishop Robert Hay Drummond after a passage in Tacitus, the picture launched West's Neoclassical history practice in London and now hangs at Yale.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-alexa: Colin Fitzgerald spears a charging stag as the young King Alexander III recoils on his horse, the hunt party scattering in the Highland glen. Commissioned in 1786 by Francis Humberston Mackenzie to assert his clan's descent from Fitzgerald, West treats the medieval Scottish episode with the heroic compositional logic he had established in The Death of General Wolfe.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-by-gi: The history painter Benjamin West sits in his London studio, brush and palette set aside, the face turned in three-quarter view. Stuart painted his teacher and patron around 1783 to 1785 during his apprentice years on Newman Street, paying back the older painter who had taken him in when he arrived from Newport.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-cleom: Leonidas II points his son-in-law Cleombrotus toward exile while the younger man's wife pleads at his feet with their children. West drew the episode from Plutarch's Life of Agis, treating Spartan civic duty in the friezelike arrangement that marked his Neoclassical history pictures of the late 1760s.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-cupid: The winged god Cupid lifts his sleeping mortal bride Psyche into an embrace against a dim chamber, after the Apuleius tale. West painted the 1808 canvas, now at Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art, during his presidency of the Royal Academy, the heroic nudes typical of his late mythological commissions for London collectors.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-danie: Daniel points to the burning letters MENE TEKEL UPHARSIN on the wall of Belshazzar's banquet hall as the Babylonian king recoils among his cowering courtiers. West painted the canvas in 1775, drawing on the Book of Daniel for one of his early biblical histories. The Saint Louis Art Museum acquired it in 2018.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-engli: Benjamin Franklin sits on a cloud, surrounded by putti operating the kite-and-key apparatus of his 1752 lightning experiment, while a thunderhead breaks overhead. West painted the apotheosis around 1816 in London, knowingly framing his late countryman as a deified Promethean figure in the manner of Rubens or Reni.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-gentl: Two anglers in tricornes cast lines into a willow-shaded river, their dog watching from the bank under a pale English sky. West painted the modest cabinet picture in 1794 during his Hammersmith years, a rare departure from the grand-manner history subjects that occupied his Royal Academy practice.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-helen: Venus and Cupid lead Helen of Troy toward the kneeling Paris in West's neoclassical history painting, oil on canvas at roughly 143 by 198 cm, now at the Smithsonian American Art Museum. West, painter to George III, made the work in 1776 while balancing royal patronage against his American birth on the eve of revolution.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-isaac: Abraham's servant Eliezer fastens the gold bracelet on Rebecca's wrist at the well, marking her as the chosen bride for Isaac. West painted the Genesis episode in 1775 in oil on canvas. The composition belongs to a series of Old Testament subjects he produced for English patrons in the 1770s.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-john-: Lawyer John Eardley Wilmot sits at a writing desk, a quill in hand and an allegorical group of dispossessed American Loyalists behind him on the wall. West painted the 1812 canvas as a homage to Wilmot, who had chaired the British commission that compensated refugees from the Revolution, the picture-within-a-picture summarising the sitter's public service.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-king-: Lear rages bareheaded on the heath as the Fool and disguised Edgar shelter against a wind-torn hovel, the storm tearing across a black sky. Painted in 1788 for John Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery, West's canvas illustrates Act III, scene 4; it now belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-maria: Maria Hamilton Beckford, wife of the Fonthill builder William Beckford, sits in a high-waisted white gown holding a closed book. West painted the National Gallery portrait in 1799, the same year his patron's gothic abbey at Fonthill was beginning its first stages under James Wyatt.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-mary-: Mary Hopkinson holds a sheet of music against a dark ground, painted by West in 1764 shortly after he settled in London. The sitter was the sister of Francis Hopkinson, signer of the Declaration of Independence, and the picture entered the Smithsonian American Art Museum in 1926.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-milkm: Milkmaids sell pails of fresh milk to passers-by in the open ground of St James's Park, the towers of Westminster Abbey rising in the haze beyond. West painted the London genre scene in 1801, now at the Yale Center for British Art, joining royal pastoral subjects with a documentary view of city trade.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-omnia: Cupid wrestles a heavy lion to the ground in a wooded clearing, illustrating Virgil's tag that love conquers all. West signed the canvas in 1809 and it entered the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1895 as accession 95.22.1, one of his late London allegories aimed at the British print market.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-pylad: Pylades and Orestes stand bound before the priestess Iphigenia at the altar of Diana at Tauris, the moment before she recognises Orestes as her brother. Painted by West in 1766 from Euripides, the canvas was a key statement of the new neoclassical history painting and is held by Tate.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-self-: The American-born president of the Royal Academy faces the viewer in old age, palette in hand. West succeeded Joshua Reynolds as RA president in 1792 and held the post until his death in 1820, the year after this late self-portrait was painted.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-the-b: Admiral George Rooke stands sword aloft in a boat amid the wreckage of the French fleet during the 1692 engagement off La Hogue, with the Soleil Royal running aground in the distance. West began this version in 1778, then his pupil John Trumbull completed it in 1785 and West retouched it in 1806, now at the National Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-the-d: Modello showing William Pitt the Elder collapsing in the House of Lords on 7 April 1778 after speaking against surrendering the American colonies. West, painter to George III, prepared this 71.4 by 92.1 cm oil at the Yale Center for British Art but abandoned the larger project, leaving the subject to his protégé Copley.

Vice-Admiral Nelson collapses on the quarterdeck of HMS Victory at Trafalgar, surrounded by officers and ratings in a tightly compressed crowd. West composed the 1806 canvas, now at the Walker Art Gallery in Liverpool, in deliberate echo of his own Death of General Wolfe, applying his epic modern-history formula to a second imperial martyr.
collection-of-beauty-benjamin-west-venus: The newborn Venus stands at the shoreline while the Three Graces drape her with cloth, attended by putti above the waves. Painted in 1799 in oil on canvas laid on panel, the small cabinet picture belongs to West's late mythological output during his presidency of the Royal Academy in London.
collection-of-beauty-besneeuwde-ochtend-: From the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, Hokusai shows tea-house guests in Edo's Koishikawa district pausing over rice and sake to admire snow-clad Fuji at dawn. The white expanse and thin red sun exploit the limited palette of nishiki-e woodblock printing.
collection-of-beauty-bewening-van-christ: The dead Christ lies stretched out on a white shroud over blue drapery, his head fallen back toward the Virgin, who throws her arms wide in grief while Saint John and weeping angels gather around the body beneath a darkened sky. Anthony van Dyck painted this horizontal Lamentation in oil on canvas around 1635, after his return to Antwerp from England. It hangs in the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), inventory number 404.
collection-of-beauty-bibliotekarien-kons: A human bust composed entirely of stacked books, a curtain of pages, ribbon bookmarks for fingers, and a feather duster for hair, traditionally read as a satire on the Habsburg court bibliophile Wolfgang Lazius. Painted in 1562 and now at Skokloster Castle in Sweden, the panel exemplifies the composite portraits Arcimboldo developed for Maximilian II.
collection-of-beauty-blaas-eugen-die-was: The Italian-Austrian painter de Blaas specialised in genteel scenes of Venetian life, here a young woman pausing with her copper water vessel. His glossy academic finish made such picturesque subjects popular with late-nineteenth-century international collectors.
collection-of-beauty-blaas-eugen-von-an-: A young Venetian woman pauses over the white linen piled in her lap, laughing and gesturing mid-conversation toward someone beyond the edge of the picture — the interesting story of the title. Her red kerchief, coral necklace, and yellow skirt supply the bright local color that made de Blaas's scenes of Venetian working girls hugely popular with collectors. The oil painting is a characteristic example of the genre subjects he produced in Venice through the late nineteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-blauwe-irissen-rp-p: Ohara Koson's quiet study of irises pairs sharply cut leaves with delicately gradated petals. The Watanabe workshop produced the design as part of Koson's celebrated kachō-e (bird-and-flower) output, finding international markets in the early twentieth century.
collection-of-beauty-bodhidharmayoshitos: From One Hundred Aspects of the Moon, Yoshitoshi depicts the Zen patriarch Bodhidharma seated in meditation behind a ruined lattice. The late-Edo printmaker tempers the supernatural subject with naturalistic shading, marking his bridge between ukiyo-e and modern Japanese illustration.
collection-of-beauty-boilly-incroyable-p: An 'incroyable', one of the foppish young men of the post-Revolutionary Directory, shown in exaggerated dress with cravat and high collar. Oil on canvas in a private collection, painted in 1797. Boilly satirised the muscadin fashions then on display along the Parisian boulevards.
collection-of-beauty-boilly-louis-leopol: A sleeping woman waking in disarranged bedclothes, the subject of Boilly's 'Le Doux Réveil' (The Gentle Awakening). Oil on canvas, catalogued J 7 in the Musée Cognacq-Jay, Paris. The boudoir scene is one of the lightly erotic interiors Boilly produced in the 1790s.
collection-of-beauty-bonneville-savoy-by: An Alpine view from Turner's first Continental tour following the Peace of Amiens, recording the town of Bonneville against the Mont Blanc range. The classical compositional structure recalls Claude Lorrain, whom Turner studied closely as a young Royal Academician.
collection-of-beauty-boris-kustodiev-por: The bass Fyodor Chaliapin in a long fur coat stands on a hillside above a winter fairground, with sledges, posters, and onion-domed churches spread out below. Painted in 1922 and now divided between versions at the Russian Museum and the Theatre Museum in Saint Petersburg, the picture frames the singer against the same provincial holiday world Kustodiev had been imagining throughout his late career.
collection-of-beauty-boris-kustodiev-sel: Kustodiev paints himself in hunting dress under the title On the Hunt, rifle and gear marking the rural retreats he favoured around the Volga. The 1905 canvas is held by the State Russian Museum in Saint Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-boris-kustodiev-shr: Snow-covered Russian rooftops, golden church domes and bare birches frame troikas and crowds celebrating Maslenitsa beneath a pink and gold sky. Kustodiev painted the 1916 canvas at the State Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg, from his wheelchair following spinal surgery; it draws openly on the bright flat colour of the lubok print tradition.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-04-louvr: Botticelli treats the popular Florentine subject of the infant Christ greeted by the young John the Baptist, a tondo-like intimacy enclosed within a vertical panel. The crisp contour drawing and Mary's downcast features are hallmarks of his Quattrocento workshop.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-a-virgem: An early devotional panel from Botticelli's apprenticeship in the orbit of Filippo Lippi, the Madonna and Child are accompanied by an attendant angel offering fruit. The soft modelling and delicate linearity announce the Florentine grace of his mature style.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-allegori: A standing female personification of Abundance leads a procession of putti laden with sheaves of wheat and fruit, drawn in pen, ink and chalk on tinted paper. The sheet, in the British Museum, is one of Botticelli's most finished surviving drawings, datable to the mid 1480s on the basis of its links to the Primavera figure types.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-annuncia: Painted for the Cestello convent in Florence, the panel shows Gabriel kneeling before a swaying Virgin whose body bends in a lyrical S-curve. The cool palette and tiled floor demonstrate Botticelli's late, more austere mode under the influence of Savonarola's preaching.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-incorona: A predella scene from the San Marco altarpiece, showing John the Evangelist receiving his vision on the rocky island of Patmos. The miniature format allowed Botticelli's workshop to compress dramatic landscape and visionary light into a narrow horizontal panel.
collection-of-beauty-botticelli-prado-49: From the four-panel Boccaccio cycle commissioned by Lorenzo de' Medici for the Pucci-Bini wedding, this episode shows the cursed huntsman pursuing his lover through a pine wood at Ravenna. Botticelli unfolds the moral tale across staged tableaux of refined courtly pageantry.
collection-of-beauty-boucher-leda-lacma: Leda reclines on a riverbank as the swan presses against her thigh, a companion nymph half-turning behind her. Boucher painted the 1742 mythology in a pale, sugared palette and the canvas now hangs at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-boucher-marquise-de: Madame de Pompadour reclines on a green silk sofa in an embroidered floral gown, surrounded by books, sheet music, a quill, and her spaniel Inès. Signed and dated 1756 and now in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich, the full-length state portrait shows Louis XV's official mistress as the educated patron of Diderot, Voltaire and the philosophes.
collection-of-beauty-boucher-par-gustav-: Boucher turns from his easel with palette in hand, the painter at the height of his Parisian career. Lundberg presented the pastel as his reception piece to the Academie royale de peinture on 28 January 1741, the work that secured his admission as an academician.
collection-of-beauty-boucher-vulcan-pres: The muscular smith god offers Venus the armour he has forged for her son Aeneas, after the eighth book of the Aeneid. Boucher produced the 1757 canvas, now in the Louvre and over three metres square, as the cartoon for one of four tapestries on the Loves of the Gods commissioned for Louis XV alongside designs by Vanloo, Pierre and Vien.
collection-of-beauty-bouquet-of-mallows: A loose still life of pink mallows arranged in a glass vase, painted at Vetheuil during a difficult personal year for Monet. The tabletop dissolves into rapid, comma-like strokes that anticipate the all-over surface of his late garden pictures.
collection-of-beauty-boy-with-a-basket-o: An early Roman work made soon after Caravaggio entered the household of Cardinal del Monte, the youth offers a basket spilling with grapes, peaches, and figs. The naturalistic still life, with its bruised leaves and worm-eaten apples, helped found a new Italian tradition of painting fruit from life.
collection-of-beauty-boys-in-a-dory-met-: Four boys in straw hats drift in a flat-bottomed dory on still harbor water, one perched on the bow with bare legs dangling, while schooners ride at anchor in the haze beyond. Homer painted the sheet in watercolor and gouache during the summer of 1873 at Gloucester, Massachusetts — his first sustained campaign in the medium that would become central to his art. It is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-brjullov: Bryullov, in his sixtieth year, faces the viewer in a dark coat, his hand resting against a cushion, the long illness that would soon kill him visible in his pale features. He painted the self-portrait in Rome in 1848 during convalescence; it now hangs in the State Tretyakov Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-brjullov-italianski: A young Italian woman reaches into a sun-shot vine to pluck a heavy cluster of grapes, her white blouse loosened in the midday heat. Painted in 1827 during Bryullov's residency in Italy on a stipend from the Society for the Encouragement of Artists, the picture now belongs to the State Russian Museum.
collection-of-beauty-brjullov-italiansko: A young woman bathes her face at a stone fountain in dappled morning light. Bryullov painted the canvas in Rome in 1823 as part of his pensioner programme for the Society for the Encouragement of the Arts, who sent it to Tsar Alexander I; it remains one of his earliest Italian successes.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-jun: Cattle graze in a sunlit New Jersey pasture under a broad green canopy, with the white spire of a Montclair church showing through the trees. Inness painted the canvas in 1882, soon after renting the Dodge estate in Montclair where he would settle for the rest of his life; the work entered the Brooklyn Museum and remains an early example of his Barbizon-rooted American manner.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-sno: Kunisada, the prolific Utagawa-school designer, sets a kabuki-style figure against falling snow on the banks of an Edo river. The plush patterned kimono and densely speckled white sky show his command of beauty prints and the expanded palette of nineteenth-century woodblock printing.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-stu: Chase, the leading American Impressionist teacher, captures a young model in a borrowed kimono with rapid, fluid brushwork. Such japoniste studio subjects were fashionable in Gilded Age New York and reveal his admiration for Whistler and Sargent.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-sun: A low horizon of water meets a heavy, gold-flecked sky, the sun dropping behind dissolving vapour. Held by the Brooklyn Museum, the 1887 oil shows Inness working at the edge of abstraction, building the marine through scumbled glazes rather than drawn incident.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-tab: From his first Souvenirs of Travel series, Hasui depicts the Tsuta hot spring deep in the mountains of Mutsu, framed by stands of beech and birch. The cool tonal harmonies typify the shin-hanga revival of landscape woodblock printing he led with publisher Watanabe Shozaburo.
collection-of-beauty-brooklyn-museum-wil: The Philadelphia sculptor William Rush works at his studio bench, carving an allegorical female figure of the Schuylkill River from a wooden block while the nude model stands posed nearby. Eakins returned to the 1877 composition in 1908, the only subject he is known to have reworked in his career. The canvas is in the Brooklyn Museum.
collection-of-beauty-brullovkp-osadapsko: Russian defenders sally from a breach in the white walls of Pskov as Stefan Batory's Polish-Lithuanian army storms the city in 1581. Bryullov worked on this large historical canvas from 1839 until his death in 1852, leaving it unfinished; it hangs in the State Tretyakov Gallery in Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-bruni-christ: Christ's head crowned with thorns is set against a darkly modelled ground in Fyodor Bruni's devotional study, painted with the careful chiaroscuro of the academic tradition. Bruni held the chair of historical painting at the Imperial Academy of Arts in St Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-bust-of-pseudo-sene: Rubens drew this gaunt, furrowed head from the famous Hellenistic bust then believed to portray the Stoic philosopher Seneca — an identification since abandoned, hence 'Pseudo-Seneca.' The sheet is worked in pen and brown ink over black chalk, heightened with white and gray wash, with the searching intensity Rubens reserved for his studies after antique sculpture. He owned a version of the bust himself and reused the head in paintings such as The Death of Seneca; the drawing is now in the Robert Lehman Collection at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-byam-shaw-omphale-1: The Lydian queen Omphale stands draped in the lion-skin of Hercules, who served her in bondage as punishment for murder. Byam Shaw, a late Pre-Raphaelite, treats the mythological role-reversal with jewel-toned costume detail and decorative outline drawn from his Birmingham School training.
collection-of-beauty-ca-rezzonico-matrim: The Christ Child reaches from the Virgin's lap to place a ring on Saint Catherine's finger, attended by angels. Attributed to the Bolognese painter Biagio Pupini, called Dalle Lame, a follower of Francesco Francia who absorbed Raphael's manner through Sienese intermediaries, the panel hangs at the Ca' Rezzonico in Venice with the inventory number 236.
collection-of-beauty-ayvazovskiy-i-k-vol: A single dark wave rolls toward the viewer in Aivazovsky's most reductive late seascape, the painter's lifelong subject distilled to a meeting of water and sky. The Russian marine painter made the canvas in 1889 in his Crimean studio at Feodosia.
collection-of-beauty-caillebotte-gustave: An unidealised nude sprawls across a rumpled divan, her clothing tossed over the chair beside her. Painted early in Caillebotte's career, the canvas treats the female body with a candid, almost photographic objectivity that was startling to Salon-trained eyes.
collection-of-beauty-caillebotte-l-homme: A top-hatted bourgeois leans on the wrought-iron railing of a Haussmann balcony, surveying the boulevard below. Caillebotte, an engineer by training, repeatedly used the steep diagonal of Paris's new avenues to investigate the modern viewer's detached urban gaze.
collection-of-beauty-campo-de-trigo: A field of standing wheat under a broad sky, the grain laid in with quick yellow and green strokes and no incident to interrupt the view. Renoir painted the landscape in 1879, probably near Wargemont on the Bérard family estate in Normandy; it belongs to the Carmen Thyssen-Bornemisza Collection in Madrid.
collection-of-beauty-canestra-di-frutta-: A wicker basket of grapes, figs, peaches and a withered apple sits at eye level on a bare ledge, projecting slightly into the viewer's space. Often cited as the first autonomous still life in Italian painting, the work is unsparing about wormholes and decay; its plain ground is a later overpaint.
collection-of-beauty-caravaggio-i-musici: Four young musicians, one tuning a lute, prepare to perform in a tightly packed half-length composition. Commissioned by Cardinal Francesco Maria del Monte for his Roman household, the picture launched Caravaggio's career and introduced his trademark modelling of flesh against deep shadow.
collection-of-beauty-caravaggio-judith-b: The Hebrew widow grips the Assyrian general's hair and saws through his neck while her aged maid waits with a sack. Caravaggio renders the ugly mechanics of beheading with forensic clarity, the spurting blood lit as starkly as the white sheets.
collection-of-beauty-caravaggio-la-depos: Christ's lifeless body is lowered onto the anointing stone, his arm and shroud dropping toward the viewer. Painted for the Chiesa Nuova in Rome, the altarpiece compresses the mourners into a powerful diagonal lit by Caravaggio's signature raking shaft.
collection-of-beauty-caravaggio-medusa-g: The Gorgon's severed head shrieks the instant of decapitation, her snakes still writhing. Painted on a convex tournament shield as a gift from Cardinal del Monte to the Grand Duke of Tuscany, the work conflates mirror, weapon, and self-portrait.
collection-of-beauty-caravaggio-sette-op: All seven corporal acts of mercy, from burying the dead to Roman Charity, unfold in a single torch-lit Neapolitan alley. Painted for the Pio Monte della Misericordia, the altarpiece set the template for Neapolitan tenebrism that Ribera and the Caravaggisti would extend.
collection-of-beauty-cardinal-fernando-n: Cardinal Fernando Niño de Guevara sits in a heavy upholstered chair, his red moire silk robes brilliant against a green wall, a pair of round spectacles set on his nose. Painted around 1600 in Toledo and now at the Met, the portrait shows the Grand Inquisitor of Spain and is one of El Greco's few seated, full-state ecclesiastical likenesses.
collection-of-beauty-carl-friedrich-seif: Sunlight refracted through the submerged entrance of Capri's Grotta Azzurra fills the cavern with the cobalt glow that made it a Grand Tour pilgrimage site. The picture is in fact by Berlin landscapist Carl Friedrich Seiffert, who specialised in luminous Italian veduta.
collection-of-beauty-carl-joseph-begas-f: A portrait of Wilhelmine Bock, the painter's wife, painted in 1828, three years after their marriage in Berlin. Begas had returned from Paris and Rome to settle in the Prussian capital, turning increasingly to portraiture in the Biedermeier decades; the sitter would bear him several sons, including the sculptor Reinhold Begas.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-013: A pair of conspirators in a courtyard puzzle over a love letter snatched from its addressee. The narrative anecdote, the costumed protagonists, and the pinpoint architectural detail are textbook Spitzweg, drawn from a stage tradition rather than direct observation.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-036: A bourgeois family in their Sunday best parades down a country path under a parasol, the children straggling behind. Spitzweg captures the small comedies of Biedermeier ritual with affectionate, miniaturist precision.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-das-a: A weathered statue of blindfolded Lady Justice stands with broken scales while a soldier loiters in shadow behind her, a wry Biedermeier comment on the gap between law and power. The panel was sold under Nazi duress by Jewish collector Leo Bendel and only restituted to his heirs in 2019.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-der-a: A penniless poet huddles under an umbrella in his garret bed, scribbling verses while the roof leaks. Spitzweg's most famous Biedermeier image, now in Munich's Neue Pinakothek, distils the era's fondness for affectionate caricature of the eccentric outsider.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-der-b: A village postman trudges along a sun-drenched lane in the Rosenthal, satchel slung at his hip. Spitzweg, a trained pharmacist who painted in his spare hours, made a career of these affectionately ironic small-town vignettes.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-der-e: An aged hermit has nodded off in his rocky retreat, breviary slipping from his hand. Spitzweg favoured these solitary cassocked figures as Biedermeier emblems of harmless retreat from the noisy modern world.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-der-m: A plein-air painter has stretched out on his back beneath a propped umbrella in a forest clearing, paint box at his feet. The compact panel is a gentle self-mockery of the Romantic ideal of the artist communing with nature.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-der-s: A frock-coated naturalist tiptoes through tall grass with raised butterfly net, lost in Linnaean reverie. The collector-eccentric, beloved subject of Spitzweg's Biedermeier comedies, is here painted on a vertical panel that exaggerates the man's spindly absurdity.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-im-da: Carl Spitzweg's oil painting shows an elderly man in cap and spectacles leaning from his garret window to water the flowers crowding his window box, birdcages hanging from the eaves above and church towers rising over the rooftops; far below, a child tends potted plants at another window. Painted around 1848-49, it is characteristic of Spitzweg's affectionate Biedermeier observations of modest life in old German towns. The painting is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-im-ha: An odalisque reclines under fretwork screens in a Munich painter's idea of a Turkish harem, the orientalist staffage rendered with Spitzweg's trademark twinkling humour. The artist drew his exotic detail entirely from prints and travel literature, never having visited the East.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-in-th: A small group winds along a high alpine track with the Wendelstein massif rising behind them. Late in his career Spitzweg loosened his touch under Barbizon influence, and the airy mountain palette here is closer to plein-air observation than to his earlier studio finish.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-stand: A hopeful suitor stands beneath a balcony serenading an unseen sweetheart, while neighbours watch from their windows. Spitzweg returned often to this nocturnal Ständchen subject, savouring the gap between Romantic gesture and small-town audience.
collection-of-beauty-carl-spitzweg-the-b: Spitzweg's elderly bibliophile stands high on a library ladder, spectacles on his nose, a volume open in his hands and more books wedged under both arms and between his knees, oblivious to everything but the shelf marked 'Metaphysics'. Painted around 1850, the picture is a gentle Biedermeier satire of bookish absorption and one of Spitzweg's best-loved subjects.
collection-of-beauty-carlos-v-en-muhlber: The Habsburg emperor rides out armoured in pike and lance to commemorate his 1547 victory over the Schmalkaldic League at Mühlberg. Painted in Augsburg and now in the Prado, Titian's portrait fixed the equestrian image of sovereign authority that Velázquez and Van Dyck would inherit.
collection-of-beauty-carlyle-maclise-ori: Thomas Carlyle leans against a pillar, top hat in hand, in a full-length character study by his fellow Scot Daniel Maclise. The portrait belongs to the celebrated Fraser's Magazine series of literary lions Maclise drew during the 1830s.
collection-of-beauty-carnegiemuseumofvin: Furrowed wheat fields on the plain of Auvers, the soil glistening after a storm, painted in the final weeks of Van Gogh's life. The high horizon, ribbon-like brushwork, and rain-washed greens belong to the productive Auvers months that ended in July 1890.
collection-of-beauty-carp-leaping-up-a-c: A koi battles upstream against a thundering waterfall, illustrating the Chinese legend that any carp scaling the falls of the Dragon Gate is transformed into a dragon. The motif, emblematic of perseverance and male coming-of-age, was a staple of East Asian ink painting and ukiyo-e print design.
collection-of-beauty-casincaillebotte: Caillebotte's mother, aunt, cousin, and a family friend sit reading and sewing on the lawn at the family's Yerres estate, viewed from above through a steep garden perspective. The bourgeois leisure scene combines Impressionist plein-air light with Caillebotte's almost geometric staging of figures in space.
collection-of-beauty-caspar-david-friedr: A procession of monks bears a coffin into the snow-rimed ruin of a Gothic abbey, the gnarled oaks around them silhouetted against a pale winter dusk. Friedrich exhibited the canvas in Berlin alongside Mönch am Meer as a Romantic meditation on death and resurrection.

A wayside crucifix stands atop a fir-clad alpine peak, gilded by rays of an unseen setting sun. Originally an altarpiece for the Tetschen chapel, the work provoked the so-called Ramdohr controversy by daring to treat pure landscape as a vehicle of religious revelation.

A weathered oak rises at the centre of a Bohemian valley at dawn, its dead crown set against luminous distant mountains. Friedrich uses the broken tree as a quiet emblem of endurance, paired with the morning panorama as one half of a meditation on the cycle of day and life.

A solitary figure stands on a pale dune before an immense, near-empty expanse of sea and sky. Friedrich strips the composition to horizontal bands, dwarfing the human silhouette to evoke spiritual confrontation with the infinite — a foundational image of German Romantic landscape.

Five figures on a Baltic shore correspond to five sailing vessels at varying distances — an allegory of the ages of human life rendered in Friedrich's late, hushed palette. The painting was made near the artist's birthplace of Greifswald and is now in Leipzig's Museum der bildenden Künste.

Two women and a man on a rocky shore watch sailing ships approach beneath a rising moon, the sky banded violet and gold. Friedrich repeated the moonlit-sea motif throughout his career as a Rückenfigur meditation on faith, return, and the threshold between visible and unseen.

Three figures peer over the dizzying white precipices of Rügen onto the Baltic far below, framed by an arch of beech branches. Painted shortly after Friedrich's honeymoon, the picture invests a real coastal panorama with Romantic allegories of marriage, faith, and mortality.

Seen from behind on a rocky outcrop, the wanderer surveys a swirling fog that swallows the peaks below. Friedrich's signature Rückenfigur device invites the viewer into the figure's vantage, making the landscape an interior as much as a topography of the Elbe Sandstone Mountains.
collection-of-beauty-cassatt-mary-lydia-: Cassatt's elder sister Lydia, often her sitter in these years, leans into her work at a vertical tapestry loom in soft afternoon light. The picture belongs to the artist's series of women absorbed in domestic occupations, painted with the loose Impressionist touch she had absorbed in Degas's circle.
collection-of-beauty-cassatt-mary-matern: A bare-shouldered mother cradles her child against her, the two faces close in quiet intimacy. Cassatt returned to the maternité theme repeatedly after 1880, treating the secular subject with the formal gravity of a Renaissance Madonna while keeping her brushwork bright and contemporary.
collection-of-beauty-cats-suggested-as-t: Kuniyoshi, a noted cat lover, replaces every post town on the Tōkaidō highway with a cat whose pose or attribute puns on the station's name. The triptych is a tour de force of Edo wordplay (mitate) and ukiyo-e woodblock printing, made when actor prints had been restricted by Tenpō reform censorship.
collection-of-beauty-cawing-crow-by-ohar: A black crow opens its beak mid-call on a bare branch, the empty ground around it giving the cry pictorial space. Koson specialised in kachō-e (bird-and-flower) prints for the early-twentieth-century shin-hanga revival, exporting subdued, naturalistic studies like this one to Western collectors.
collection-of-beauty-cb9001fb: The basalt sea-stacks of Chongseokjeong rising from the East Sea coast, the fourth leaf of Kim Hong-do's album of the four districts of Geumgang. Ink and light colour on silk, roughly 30 by 44 cm, painted about 1788 after a tour the court painter made of Mount Geumgang and Gangwon Province under King Jeongjo. The clustered hexagonal columns are drawn in fine vertical strokes.
collection-of-beauty-boy-skifov-so-slavy: Mounted warriors locked in combat, lances raised and horses entangled across the steppe. Vasnetsov painted this Battle of the Slavs and Scythians in 1881, oil on canvas, now in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg. The subject draws on the Primary Chronicle and the artist's interest in early Russian legend.
collection-of-beauty-cezanne-ambroise-vo: The dealer Ambroise Vollard sits forward with hands clasped, his bald head catching the light against a brown studio wall. Cézanne painted the portrait in 1899; it is held by the Petit Palais in Paris. Vollard recalled posing more than a hundred times, after which the painter declared only the shirtfront finished.
collection-of-beauty-cezanne-fwn-1974: A landscape study in pencil and watercolour, the forms of trees and rock laid in with translucent patches of blue and ochre over open paper. Catalogued as FWN 1974 in the online Cézanne catalogue raisonné among the works on paper. Cézanne built such sheets from overlapping washes, leaving the white of the paper to carry the light.
collection-of-beauty-cezanne-le-printemp: A female personification of Spring stands with a garland of blossom, one of four season panels Cézanne signed 'Ingres'. He painted them about 1860 to 1861 for the salon alcove of the family estate, the Jas de Bouffan near Aix; the panels were later transferred to canvas and given to the Petit Palais, Paris.
collection-of-beauty-cezanne-thyssen: A man in a wide-brimmed hat sits against a pale terrace balustrade, his features summarily indicated and patches of bare canvas left in reserve. Painted in 1905-06, oil on canvas, the sitter is Vallier, the gardener at Cézanne's studio at Les Lauves near Aix-en-Provence; the work has been in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, Madrid, since 1993.
collection-of-beauty-charing-cross-bridg: Monet painted the railway bridge across the Thames repeatedly during winter stays at the Savoy Hotel, working on dozens of canvases at once as the light shifted. The composition dissolves bridge, smoke, and water into veils of mauve and pale orange characteristic of his London series.

One of nearly forty variants Monet made of Charing Cross Bridge, focused here on the trembling reflections beneath the iron span. The series, painted between 1899 and 1904, was the artist's sustained study of London fog as a coloured atmospheric medium rather than a mere obscurant.
collection-of-beauty-charles-le-brun-dae: Daedalus binds the wax wings to the shoulders of the eager young Icarus, his own face shadowed with foreknowledge of the flight to come. Painted about 1645 and now in the State Hermitage, Saint Petersburg, the canvas is an early work by Le Brun, completed before the long Roman study under Poussin that shaped his mature classicism.
collection-of-beauty-charles-le-brun-la-: Sheet from the Méthode pour apprendre à dessiner les passions, showing the face of Anger with brows drawn together, nostrils flared and teeth bared. Le Brun's 1668 lecture at the Académie Royale built a Cartesian taxonomy of emotion for painters, and the engraved sheets circulated in artist pattern books well into the nineteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-charles-le-brun-les: The mother, wife and daughters of the defeated Darius prostrate themselves before Alexander and Hephaestion in the Persian camp after Issus. Painted between 1660 and 1661 and shown to Louis XIV at Fontainebleau, the canvas won Le Brun his role as premier peintre and ushered in his cycle of Alexander histories for the Crown.
collection-of-beauty-charles-le-brun-pri: Louis XIV reviews the rapid surrender of Ghent in March 1678, his cavalry drawn up before the captured citadel during the Franco-Dutch War. Le Brun designed the composition between 1681 and 1684 as one of the painted panegyrics intended for the Galerie des Glaces programme at Versailles.
collection-of-beauty-charles-le-brun-the: Studies of emotive heads, including wonder, despair and joy, from the series Le Brun developed to illustrate his 1668 lecture at the Académie Royale de Peinture et de Sculpture. Published posthumously as Méthode pour apprendre à dessiner les passions, the drawings codified facial expression for two centuries of academic teaching, with the eyebrows treated as the primary diagnostic feature.

Polyxena is led to the altar to appease the ghost of Achilles while her mother Hecuba reaches to restrain her and the soldier Neoptolemus lifts his sword. Le Brun painted the subject from Ovid's Metamorphoses in 1647, before his career as premier peintre to Louis XIV.
collection-of-beauty-charles-w-bartlett-: Pilgrims and worshippers gather at the marble pool surrounding the Golden Temple in Amritsar, the gilded sanctuary mirrored in the still water. Bartlett based the design on sketches from his 1913 Indian travels; the 22 by 30 centimetre colour woodcut was published in Tokyo in 1916 by Watanabe Shōzaburō, one of twenty-one Bartlett prints Watanabe issued that year.

Volcanic cliffs and palms along the windward coast of Maui rendered in transparent watercolour washes over ink. Painted in 1920 after Bartlett settled in Honolulu, the sheet belongs to the Hawaiian landscape work that occupied him after his Asian travels and that informed the prints he developed with Watanabe Shozaburo's Tokyo workshop.

Bartlett pictures himself in watercolour, painted in Honolulu in 1933, the year he helped found the Honolulu Printmakers. The English-born artist had settled in Hawaii in 1917 after travels in Japan and India, where he had learned colour woodblock from Watanabe Shozaburo and become a central figure of the shin-hanga movement.
collection-of-beauty-charlotte-dubourg-p: Fantin-Latour's sister-in-law sits in dark dress against a neutral ground, hands loosely clasped. The portrait carries the muted tonality and quiet psychological focus the artist learned from his admiration of the Old Masters and his friendship with Whistler; it now hangs in the Musée d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-chase-mrs-meigs-pia: Mrs. Meigs is shown at her piano-organ in a richly furnished aesthetic interior, her white dress glowing against dark panelling. Chase exhibited several such society portraits in the early 1880s, deploying the bravura tonal handling he had absorbed from Frans Hals and Velázquez.
collection-of-beauty-chase-william-merri: Sand, scrub, and pale sky meet under bright Long Island light at Shinnecock, where Chase ran his pioneering open-air summer school from 1891. The painting's broad horizontal bands and feathery brushwork mark his absorption of French Impressionism into an American plein-air idiom.

Chase portrays his fellow expatriate sympathiser in the dandyish black-and-grey register Whistler himself favoured, monocle and cane in hand. The two artists painted each other in London that summer; their friendship soured shortly after over the resulting likenesses.

Dora Wheeler, a designer trained alongside Chase in Munich, sits in a blue gown amid the embroidered hangings of her mother Candace's Associated Artists studio. The portrait won a medal at the 1883 Paris Salon and helped establish Chase's reputation for atmospheric, aesthetic-movement interiors.

Painted in his Fourth Avenue studio late in life, Chase shows himself in a dark suit among the bric-à-brac collection that doubled as his teaching tool. The bravura handling and theatrical self-presentation summarise the persona he cultivated at the Art Students League and Chase School.

An early student work made during Chase's Indianapolis years, the cut watermelon is laid out with the dark ground and dramatic highlights of the Munich-school tradition he would soon study at first hand. The picture predates his shift toward looser, brighter American Impressionism.
collection-of-beauty-chaumiere-italienne: An Italian peasant cottage with a thatched roof crouches beneath a stand of windswept trees, two figures at the threshold. Fragonard etched the small landscape in 1775 from sketches made during his second Italian journey with the abbe de Saint-Non. An impression is held at the Ghent University Library.
collection-of-beauty-chen-rong-nine-drag: Nine dragons surge through clouds, mist, and crashing water across a long handscroll of ink and wash on paper. Chen Rong, a Southern Song scholar-official, painted the work in 1244; it is celebrated for its splashed-ink dragons and is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-chichester-canal-18: The still water of the Sussex canal mirrors a tall-masted ship and a sky drenched in late sun. Turner painted the scene for his patron the Earl of Egremont, one of a set of canvases made for the panelled dining room at Petworth House and now in the Tate.
collection-of-beauty-childe-harold: Inspired by Byron's Mediterranean poem, Turner builds a luminous Italian campagna of crumbling arches, distant hills, and a glowing sky. The picture is part of the artist's long late dialogue with Claude Lorrain, dissolving classical landscape architecture into atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-chinese-warship-tin: The German-built ironclad Tingyuan, then the largest warship in the Far East, lies at anchor in a Japanese port flying her flags. Kōitsu records the ship's Meiji-era courtesy visit in a colour woodblock print that combines ukiyo-e tradition with the new Western subject matter of steam and steel.
collection-of-beauty-christ-on-the-cross: Christ hangs alone on the cross against a darkened sky, his pale body lit sharply against the gloom and his head sunk toward his shoulder. Rubens painted this single-figure devotional crucifixion in oil on oak panel, stripping away mourners and thieves to concentrate everything on the modelling of the body. The painting belongs to the Bavarian State Painting Collections in Munich.
collection-of-beauty-christian-ix-of-den: Tuxen assembles Christian IX — the so-called father-in-law of Europe — with his children and royal grandchildren in the garden hall of Fredensborg Palace. Commissioned for the king's golden wedding anniversary, the group portrait records the Danish dynastic ties that linked the courts of Britain, Russia, and Greece.
collection-of-beauty-circle-of-pieter-br: Villagers skate and slide on a frozen river beside snow-covered houses, while at right a propped board baited with grain forms a trap for unwary birds. One of around a hundred surviving versions after Pieter Bruegel the Elder's composition, it pairs winter genre with a quiet emblem of human precariousness.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-021: Anglers in small boats work a quiet stretch of the Seine framed by leafy banks, painted from Monet's floating studio. The Poissy years were unhappy ones, but they yielded several of his most luminous river scenes in delicate greens and silvers.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-022: Jeanne-Marguerite Lecadre, a relative, stands among flowering beds in the family garden at Sainte-Adresse near Le Havre. The picture's bright local colour and crisp shadows show Monet absorbing the lessons of Manet and Japanese prints.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-023: Suzanne Hoschedé strides up a grassy slope, parasol angled against the wind that flattens her white dress. The picture revisits the 1875 Argenteuil composition of Camille, now reworked as a near-anonymous figure study with the face deliberately blurred.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-029: A modest fisherman's cottage perched above the Norman coast, painted during Monet's productive campaigns at Pourville and Varengeville. Broken brushwork dissolves cliff, sea, and sky into a single weathered atmosphere, the cottage anchoring the composition against the windblown grass.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-044: One of the late Giverny pond pictures, painted as Monet was preparing the monumental Grandes Décorations now in the Orangerie. Lily pads drift across a mirrored surface in which sky, willow, and water trade places, the paint laid in long, lapping strokes of green, mauve, and rose.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-051: A still life of chrysanthemums in a glazed pot, painted at Argenteuil during a season when Monet turned indoors to floral subjects. Loose, prismatic touches break the petals into shimmering points of colour, treating the bouquet with the same outdoor optics he brought to his river views.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-052: A dense bouquet of sunflowers arranged in a glazed vase, painted in Vétheuil years before Van Gogh took up the same motif in Arles. Monet builds the heavy heads from short, comma-like strokes of chrome yellow and ochre, contrasting their warmth against a cool blue-grey ground.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-1840-1: A field at Giverny rimed with hoarfrost, painted soon after Monet settled at the Norman village that would consume the rest of his career. Broken touches of pale violet, rose, and silvery blue register the chill morning light without recourse to white.

From the late Nymphéas cycle, the canvas dissolves the lily pond into floating pads, drowned grasses, and reflected sky. Working at monumental scale in his Giverny studio, Monet abandoned the horizon altogether to let surface and depth fuse into a single chromatic field.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-1867-r: Sailboats and onlookers crowd the beach at Sainte-Adresse, the Norman resort where Monet spent the summer with relatives. The crisp horizontals and bright local colour are still indebted to Boudin and Jongkind, but already announce the open-air manner that Impressionism would soon codify.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-1870-l: Painted on the Norman coast during Monet's summer honeymoon with Camille, the breakwater at low tide is laid down in rapid, salt-scratched brushwork. Sand was famously found mixed into the paint of his Trouville canvases, a record of their plein-air making in the wind off the Channel.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-1875-t: A locomotive idles at the Argenteuil station, its dark bulk and red signal lamps set against snow and bare trees. Monet returned often to the new railway as a subject, treating engine smoke and winter light as kindred atmospheric phenomena; the canvas is now at the Musée Marmottan Monet, Paris.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-a-corn: An interior view of the Monet family's Argenteuil home, with young Jean standing at the end of a darkened hallway between hanging plants and curtained light. The painting marks one of Monet's rare domestic interiors, balancing silhouetted shadow against a glowing window.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-a-seas: A nocturnal Channel scene with moonlight breaking through cloud over distant sailing vessels. Made during Monet's formative summers on the Normandy coast, the picture follows the marines of Boudin and Jongkind, with feathery brushwork capturing reflected silver on dark water.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-a-walk: Figures stroll through tall summer grass beside the Seine at Argenteuil, the village where Monet lived from 1871 to 1878. The high horizon and broken touch dissolve foreground wildflowers into a tapestry of pure colour, a defining experiment of his Argenteuil years.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-adolph: The painter's father sits in a straw hat among flowering plants in the family's seaside garden at Sainte-Adresse. Painted during the same productive Norman summer as the Regatta, the picture combines a tender domestic portrait with Monet's emerging interest in dappled outdoor light.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-alice-: Alice Hoschedé, who would become Monet's second wife, stands among foliage at Vétheuil. The portrait belongs to a small group of garden figures from this transitional period, in which Monet treats the sitter as one luminous accent within a tangle of green.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-antibe: A view across the Mediterranean toward the snow-capped Alps, made during Monet's four-month campaign on the Côte d'Azur in early 1888. The pink and turquoise palette he developed here pushed his colour further than ever, anticipating the serial canvases of the 1890s.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-argent: A view of the Seine at Argenteuil, the suburban boating town where Monet settled after the Franco-Prussian War. Sailboats and reflections on calm water became his central subject here, painted from a floating studio he converted from a small skiff.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-arriva: Steam billows beneath the iron-and-glass shed of the Gare Saint-Lazare as a locomotive pulls in from the Normandy line. One of twelve canvases Monet made of the station in 1877, the series treated industrial vapour as a modern equivalent of mist on the Seine.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-automn: Riverside trees in russet and gold are doubled in the still surface of the Seine. Painted from the bank at Argenteuil, the picture exploits Monet's preferred device of mirrored reflection, the upper and lower halves of the canvas answering one another in horizontal bands.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-camill: An intimate domestic scene of Monet's first wife, Camille Doncieux, seated at an embroidery frame in their Argenteuil home. The painter treats the patterned tapestry, dress, and wall hangings as a single woven field of colour, dissolving figure and interior into a continuous surface of touches.

Monet painted his first wife within hours of her death from uterine cancer at age thirty-two, the brushwork dissolving her features into a veil of violet, grey and white. He later confessed unease at finding himself analysing her colour rather than mourning her.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-champ-: A summer wheatfield treated as an almost abstract field of warm strokes under a high sky. The subject anticipates the haystacks Monet would begin painting in series a decade later, where the same agrarian motif became a vehicle for studying changing light.

Crimson poppies scatter through summer grass on the slopes above Vétheuil, where Monet lived in straitened circumstances after leaving Argenteuil. The motif of wildflowers as red dabs against green became a signature device, repeated through the late 1870s.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-cliff-: Two women in white stand on a wind-swept Channel cliff above sailing boats, their parasols echoing the curve of clouds and grass. Painted during a working summer at Pourville in 1882, the canvas balances figural anchor against the broad Norman sky.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-der-ko: A rare portrait by Monet, depicting the white-aproned cook of the Hôtel Blanche at Pourville. Painted during the same Normandy stay that produced the cliff-walk pictures, it captures the chef's ruddy face and twin chins in dense, almost caricatural impasto.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-die-we: A willow standing on the bank of the Epte near Giverny, caught in the pale, cool light of a spring morning. The pastel palette and feathery brushwork are typical of Monet's mid-1880s riverside studies, in which he began to anchor compositions around a single tree as a recurring motif.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-eglise: The Norman cliff-top church catches early sun above a mist-veiled coastline near Dieppe. Monet worked on the Varengeville motif repeatedly during his 1882 stay, treating the small chapel as a study in shifting maritime light.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-entree: Boats crowd the harbour mouth of the Norman resort of Trouville, where Monet honeymooned with Camille in the summer of 1870. The pictures from that holiday — sand still embedded in some of the canvases — were the last he made before fleeing the war to London.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-etreta: Beached fishing caïques dominate the foreground as the chalk Falaise d'Amont curves out into a green sea. Monet returned to Étretat repeatedly in the 1880s, drawn by the sculpted cliffs Courbet had also painted a generation earlier.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-fishin: Sail-rigged fishing boats slip out of Le Havre on a misty morning, the harbour walls and shipping reduced to muted silhouettes. Monet painted the port of his boyhood repeatedly in the early 1870s, and works of this kind directly preceded Impression, Sunrise of 1872.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-flower: A bank of the Seine near Argenteuil shimmers under summer foliage and scattered blossom. The high-keyed greens and broken touch are characteristic of Monet's most concentrated Impressionist years, when he and Renoir painted side by side along the river.

An orchard at Vétheuil seen through a haze of white spring blossom. Monet treats the subject — long established in Japanese printmaking, which he collected — as an all-over screen of pale flecks against pale ground, the trees almost dissolving into the field.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-french: An early still life arranging garden blooms alongside ripe pears and grapes on a draped surface.
