Painted before Monet committed fully to plein-air landscape, the canvas shows him testing dense impasto and saturated colour against the conventions of Salon still-life painting.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-grayst: A single haystack rises against a flushed sky from one of Monet's most influential serial campaigns. Working from his Giverny window over the winter of 1890–91, he painted twenty-five Grainstack canvases tracking the same motif through every shift of weather and hour.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-hotel-: Holiday-makers parade beneath a row of fluttering tricolours along the boardwalk of Trouville's grandest hotel. Painted on the eve of the Franco-Prussian War, the picture is a brisk exercise in plein-air reportage, with sand still trapped in the paint surface.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-houses: The Palace of Westminster looms through Thames fog at a moment of breaking sun. Monet painted some nineteen Parliament views from a balcony at St Thomas's Hospital between 1900 and 1904, returning to his hotel each evening to refine the series from memory and notes.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-in-the: Two of Alice Hoschedé's daughters work and read in the dappled woods near Giverny, where Monet had moved in 1883. Blanche, herself a painter, would later marry Monet's son Jean and become his nurse and companion in his final years.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-interi: A lamp-lit domestic interior from Monet's youth, with figures gathered after a meal. Indoor subjects are unusual in his work; here the warm artificial light and dark-keyed palette betray a debt to the realism of Manet and Bazille more than to his later high-colour outdoor practice.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-jardin: An ornamental garden at the Norman seaside resort where Monet's aunt and family summered. The bright flower beds, brisk handling and high horizon look forward to the celebrated Terrace at Sainte-Adresse painted the following summer at the same property.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-jean-p: Monet's son Michel and stepson Jean-Pierre lie among grasses on the banks of the Epte, the small tributary of the Seine that ran past Giverny. The figures' white shirts vanish into a meadow rendered in feather-light strokes — a key example of Monet's late figural work.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-l-ete-: A bank of red poppies climbs a sunlit slope above figures lost in the grass. The canvas is one of several Monet devoted to the motif of wildflower meadows, the bright dabs of red functioning as both botanical record and pure chromatic accent.

Camille and Jean lie among long grass and poppies under a high summer sky. The picture belongs to a small group of figure-in-meadow compositions Monet made at Argenteuil, treating the family as colour incidents within a continuous field of warm growth.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-la-cor: Olive groves and pines tumble toward the Mediterranean from the cliff road outside Monaco. Painted during Monet's early 1884 trip to the Riviera with Renoir, the picture pushes into hotter, more saturated colour than anything he had attempted on the Seine.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-la-man: The vast natural arch of the Manneporte rises from the surf at Étretat, one of three rock formations Monet painted obsessively during his Normandy campaigns of the early 1880s. The view from below dramatises the cliff's mass against breaking sea.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-la-poi: Wagons and figures cross the wet sand below the headland of La Hève near Le Havre, Monet's home town. Shown at the Salon of 1865 — his official debut — the canvas owes much to the marine realism of Boudin and Courbet.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-la-sei: A bend of the Seine at Vétheuil, the village where Monet lived through the bleakest years of his middle career. The river, opposite bank and sky are resolved into three horizontal bands of broken colour, a structural simplicity that points toward his coming serial work.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-le-bat: Monet's floating studio, the converted boat he commissioned in Argenteuil so he could paint the Seine from on the water itself. Reflections of hull, mast, and bankside trees fragment across the surface in short broken strokes, the picture as much about looking from the boat as at it.

The floating studio Monet had built at Argenteuil, a small cabined skiff that let him paint directly on the Seine. Reflections double the boat in rippling vertical strokes, an image of the artist's working method as much as a landscape.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-le-gra: Looking down the Grand Canal toward Santa Maria della Salute, Monet renders Venice as drifting reflections of pink and turquoise on water. The view comes from his only visit to the city, in autumn 1908, which yielded a late series exhibited at Bernheim-Jeune in 1912.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-le-pal: The Doge's Palace rises from the Venetian lagoon in dissolving pinks and aquamarines, painted during Monet's two-month stay in the city. The facade is treated less as architecture than as a screen for refracted light, with broken brushwork knitting stone, water and sky into a single luminous fabric.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-le-par: One of nineteen views of the Houses of Parliament that Monet worked on from a balcony at St Thomas' Hospital across the Thames. Westminster's Gothic silhouette is silhouetted against a sun-soaked fog, the river burning with reflected colour as atmospheric haze flattens detail into pure tonal envelope.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-le-pon: The iron railway bridge at Argenteuil cuts across the Seine in flat planes of pale stone, a steam train trailing white smoke above. Monet treats modern infrastructure as a legitimate motif of plein-air painting, balancing its industrial geometry against the soft river bank.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-les-ca: Sailboats and rowers drift on the Seine at Argenteuil, the Parisian suburb where Monet lived through the early 1870s and turned regatta-day leisure into a recurring subject. Quick comma-strokes describe water and rigging with equal economy.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-les-py: The jagged sea stacks off Belle-Île-en-Mer, painted during Monet's bracing autumn campaign on the Breton coast. Granite is built up in dense, crusted strokes against a churning Atlantic, a darker and rougher palette than his Norman seascapes.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-neige-: A muffled village street under fresh snow, part of Monet's sustained study of Argenteuil winters. The white ground is laid in with cool blues and lilacs rather than pure white, a decisive Impressionist break from academic monochrome.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-nymphe: An early canvas in the great water-lily cycle Monet pursued at his Giverny pond for the last three decades of his life. The horizon has already vanished; only floating pads, reflected sky and submerged depth remain, organised purely by colour.

A large-scale water-lily canvas of 1915, painted in the studio Monet built at Giverny to accommodate his ever-bigger formats. The pond has lost its banks entirely; tangled reflections of weeping willow descend through deep blues and violets while pads float as flat islands of green.

From the Giverny series, the Japanese-style pond seen close-up with no shore in sight. Lily pads punctuate broad zones of mauve and green reflection, the painted surface oscillating between water-skin and pure abstraction.

Held by the Musée Marmottan Monet, which inherited the artist's studio holdings, this Nymphéas frames the pond as an unbroken field of reflected light. Pads cluster as horizontal accents across deep blues and rose, the composition organised by colour weight rather than perspective.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-on-the: A young woman trails her hand in the water from a small skiff, her dress and the boat's interior dissolving into the river's green reflections. The high viewpoint and cropped framing show Monet's lasting absorption of Japanese ukiyo-e composition.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-pond-w: A vertical Giverny canvas in which the lily pond is rotated almost into pure surface pattern. Pinks and violets float over deep greens, the brushwork loose enough that the pads sometimes read as drifting clouds of pigment.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-poplar: From the Poplars series, painted from a flat-bottomed boat moored in the river Epte near Giverny. The slender trunks form a rhythmic vertical lattice, doubled by reflection, that anticipates the decorative serial logic of the later Rouen Cathedrals.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-poppy-: Camille and the young Jean Monet wade through high summer grass at Argenteuil, scarlet poppies dotted across the field in dabs of vermilion. A second figure-pair higher on the slope mirrors the first, knitting two moments into one composition.

A sun-flooded meadow of red poppies near Vétheuil, where Monet lived after Argenteuil. The horizon is pushed high so the field reads as a near-flat carpet of broken colour, a structure he would return to throughout his rural landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-red-an: Two opium poppies — one deep crimson, one pink — and a closed bud rise on long stems from a slim glass vase, their silvery scalloped leaves brushed loosely against a pale ground. The canvas is signed at upper left and painted in an unusually tall, narrow upright format. Monet's flower still lifes belong chiefly to the early 1880s, when work indoors filled the gaps between landscape campaigns.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-reflec: A late, large-scale Giverny panel related to the Grandes Décorations Monet was preparing for the Orangerie. Clouds are present only as inverted reflections, the painting collapsing sky, water and lily into one immersive plane.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-regatt: Sails crowd the Seine basin at Argenteuil, doubled in vivid downward strokes that read almost as flames on the water. The painting's loose vertical reflections were among the works that helped define the Impressionist handling of moving light on water.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-regnv-: Rain over Étretat: the Norman cliffs and arched rock recede behind a grey curtain of weather, the Channel rendered in broken slate strokes. Monet often returned to Étretat through the 1880s, attracted by its dramatic chalk geology under shifting marine light.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-road-a: A sunken Norman lane cuts down toward the sea at Pourville, where Monet spent productive months in 1882. Banks of grass and gorse frame a small triangle of bright Channel water, a composition organised by the steep diagonal of the path.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-rocks-: A rocky inlet at Port-Domois on Belle-Île, painted during Monet's autumn 1886 campaign on the storm-battered Breton coast. The granite is worked in dense, dragged strokes of plum and ochre against an unusually saturated turquoise sea.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-spring: A young woman, almost certainly Camille, sits reading in dappled shade beneath flowering trees. Pink-white blossoms and green foliage are dissolved into a single shimmering screen of broken touch, an early statement of Monet's plein-air figure painting.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-still-: Game birds laid out on a bare table in muted earth tones, a rare still life from a year of personal hardship for Monet following his wife Camille's death. The handling is broader and more sober than his contemporary garden pictures.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-street: An early view of the seaside resort north of Le Havre, where Monet stayed with his aunt during a formative summer. Architecture is still drawn with relatively firm contour, but the bright Norman light and high-keyed palette already point toward Impressionist practice.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-temps-: The Channel at Pourville under settled weather, painted during Monet's first sustained Norman coast campaign. Long horizontal bands of beach, sea and sky are differentiated almost entirely by close-valued blues and pearly greys.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ar: The road bridge at Argenteuil, rebuilt after the Franco-Prussian War, frames moored sailboats on the Seine. Monet used the same bridge in several canvases of 1874, varying the viewpoint and weather to test how a single motif behaves under changing light.

Rows of irises beneath espaliered fruit trees in the artist's own garden at Giverny, which he designed and tended as obsessively as he painted it. The diagonal furrows of mauve and violet flowers organise the canvas as a near-abstract chromatic grid.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-cl: The famous Falaise d'Aval at Étretat, with its natural arch piercing the chalk cliff. Monet, who painted this Norman site repeatedly, here works with broken touches of cream, lilac and pale green to render limestone under shifting Channel light.

A view of the chalk cliffs and natural arches at Étretat on the Normandy coast, a motif Monet returned to repeatedly in the mid-1880s. He works the chalk face in pinks and creams against the green-blue Channel, alert to how the light shifts across the porous stone.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-du: Geese gather at a farmyard pond in this rural scene from Monet's Argenteuil years, painted at the moment Impressionism crystallised around the first group exhibition. The whitewashed wall and reflecting water carry the picture's main optical work, dappled with quick, flickering touches.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-fo: The old fortifications of Antibes seen across the bay, from Monet's 1888 Riviera campaign. The southern light pushed his palette toward saturated pinks, turquoises and ochres, the Mediterranean treated as a high-keyed counterpart to his northern coasts.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ga: A locomotive pulls under the iron-and-glass shed of the Gare Saint-Lazare, steam rolling up to merge with the smoke-stained light. Part of a twelve-canvas series for which Monet secured permission to set up his easel inside the working terminus.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-hi: The road bridge at Argenteuil propped on temporary timber scaffolding after wartime damage. Monet treats the construction site as a fully serious motif, the geometry of beams and trestles balanced against the soft Seine below.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ho: The Gothic silhouette of Westminster dissolves into a haze of violet and orange across the Thames. Painted from a terrace at St Thomas's Hospital, the canvas belongs to Monet's London series, in which he tracked the same motif under shifting fog, smoke and sun.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ma: A single black bird perches on a wattle gate in a snowbound Norman garden, casting a faint blue shadow on the drift. One of Monet's earliest essays in coloured shadow, the picture was rejected by the 1869 Salon and now hangs in the Musée d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ra: A modern iron rail bridge strides across the Seine on concrete piers, a small steam train trailing white smoke above sailing boats. Monet repeatedly painted this junction of leisure and industry during his Argenteuil years.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-ro: A rutted country road leads the eye between hedgerows toward the village rooftops on the Seine. Painted soon after Monet settled at Vétheuil following financial collapse in Paris, the canvas favours dry, broken brushwork over tonal finish.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-va: The dry Ligurian valley opens out beneath ridge-line pines and a distant town, painted on Monet's January journey along the Riviera with Renoir. The high-key palette of pinks, ochres and lilacs reflects his fascination with Mediterranean light.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-wa: Pale lilies float on a luminous pond crossed by the trailing reflections of weeping willows. The panel forms part of the Grandes Décorations cycle Monet painted at Giverny for the oval rooms of the Musée de l'Orangerie in Paris, where pond, sky and bank dissolve into a continuous surface.

Floating pads drift across a mirror of green leaf-shadow, with no sky or bank to anchor the view. The canvas is a study toward the Grandes Décorations Monet eventually donated to the French state for the Orangerie.

Pale dawn light catches the lily pads on the Giverny pond, the water dissolving into broad horizontal sweeps of mauve and cream. The work belongs to the great cycle Monet developed in his late, near-blind years for the Orangerie ovals.

Banks of cloud are reflected on the still pond surface, the lilies riding across them like islands. Painted as Monet wrestled with cataracts, the panel forms part of his bequest of mural-scale Décorations to France.

Two weeping willows frame the composition like proscenium curtains, their trunks pale against drifts of pink and blue water. The mural-scale study belongs to Monet's late Giverny project conceived as continuous, all-encompassing decoration.
Inverted trees and clouds shimmer in the pond, lily pads punctuating the surface as the only signal of where water meets reflection. The picture pushes Monet's late style toward near-abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-the-wi: A brick polder mill stands across one of Amsterdam's quieter canals, its sails set against a wind-swept Dutch sky. Monet painted it during his autumn 1874 Dutch trip, a return to the country he had first sketched while waiting out the Franco-Prussian War.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-tulip-: Bands of red and yellow tulips run to the horizon under a brisk sky, with windmill sails turning at the field's edge. Monet visited the Dutch bulb fields in spring 1886 expressly to confront these violently saturated stripes of colour.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-vase-o: Red-and-yellow and white tulips splay from a slender dark vase against a pale ground, the leaves swept in as long strokes of blue-green and the blooms built up in thick wet-in-wet colour; the canvas is signed at lower right. Monet painted flower still lifes chiefly in the early 1880s, between landscape campaigns, and this bouquet belongs to that vein of his work.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-vetheu: A view of the Seine-side village of Vétheuil, where Monet settled with his struggling household in 1878. He renders the church and clustered roofs through a screen of shimmering river reflections, treating the whole town as a single envelope of haze and light.

Drift ice clogs the Seine beneath the half-frozen village, painted during the brutal winter of 1879-80 when the river broke up in spectacular fashion. The chalky palette of bone-white and pewter records one of the coldest seasons of the century.

The riverside village rises from the Seine to its squat Romanesque church, mirrored in the slow water. Monet painted dozens of variants of this view during his impoverished Vétheuil years, working out of a small studio boat.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-view-o: The riverside village climbs from the Seine to its Gothic church tower, viewed from a boat moored among reeds. Monet rented a house at Vétheuil in 1878 and worked tirelessly along this stretch of water following Camille's death.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-villas: White Italianate villas nestle among twisting umbrella pines and palms above a glittering Mediterranean. Monet wrote to Alice Hoschedé from Bordighera that the colours demanded a palette of diamonds and gemstones to be rendered honestly.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-voir-l: Snow lies along the riverbank at Argenteuil, with the white plain crossed by a lone walker and faint footprints. Monet's winter pictures from this period set warm rooftops and clothed figures against muted blue-grey snow.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-water-: Lily pads float in even rhythms across green-blue water, with a pale band of sky-reflection running along the upper edge. The picture comes from the first mature group of Nymphéas exhibited by Durand-Ruel in 1909.

A canvas from the second great wave of Nymphéas pictures, painted as Monet exhibited forty-eight pond views at Durand-Ruel's Paris gallery. Pads drift across reflections of cloud and sky, the water surface flattened into a pure field of colour with no horizon to orient the viewer.

The pond surface fills the canvas edge to edge, lilies massing in clusters of rose and ivory among dark vegetal reflections. Painted as Monet's eyesight deteriorated, the picture's looser, more saturated handling anticipates mid-century abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-waterl: A horizontal screen of lily pads hovers over reflected sky on the Giverny pond. By 1906 Monet had abolished the bank entirely, treating the water as a self-contained world the eye could enter at any point.

Clusters of lilies drift on a pond shot through with violet and rose reflection, the pads rendered in short, scumbled strokes. The 1907 group is among Monet's most chromatically daring before his cataracts began to dull his vision.

Lily blossoms sit like white embers on a deep mauve pond, the surface broken only by their slow geometry. The canvas dates from Monet's last full-sighted summers at Giverny before cataract surgery would alter his colour sense.

The bridge's arches dissolve into Thames fog while the smoke-stained palette of the south bank glows behind. Monet worked on the Waterloo and Charing Cross views from a balcony at the Savoy Hotel, juggling many canvases as the light shifted.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-windmi: A girl walks the dyke path between Oostzaan and Zaandam, windmill sails turning over flat polder land. Painted during Monet's 1871 Dutch sojourn after his English exile, the picture's narrow tonal range catches a typical overcast Holland sky.
collection-of-beauty-claude-monet-woman-: Camille turns under a green parasol while young Jean stands among grasses on a windy bluff, painted from below so the figures rise into a billowing sky. The picture, now in Washington's National Gallery, is Monet's bid to handle the figure outdoors with full plein-air conviction.
collection-of-beauty-claudemonetbanksoft: The Seine winds past the village of Lavacourt across from Vétheuil, where Monet lived from 1878. The riverbank views he painted there mark the brightening palette and broken brushwork of his fully mature Impressionism, made under the strain of his wife Camille's final illness.
collection-of-beauty-clearing-sky-after-: A plate from Hasui's Twenty Views of Tokyo, depicting the Sensō-ji temple complex at Asakusa under fresh snow. A leading figure of the shin-hanga revival, Hasui rebuilt the older ukiyo-e collaboration of designer, carver, and printer to record a modernising city in soft, atmospheric colour woodblock.
collection-of-beauty-cleopatra-and-caesa: Cleopatra steps from the unrolled carpet to confront Caesar at his writing table, the ancient anecdote staged with the polished historicism Gérôme made his trademark. Smooth porcelain finish, archaeologically researched props, and a controlled tonal palette anchor the picture in academic theatre.
collection-of-beauty-clevelandart-1962-3: Cupid sits on the edge of the bed where Psyche still sleeps, smirking as he reaches for his quiver. David inverts the usual idealized adolescent, painting the god as an ungainly teenager registering sexual conquest, a deliberate provocation produced during his Brussels exile and now at the Cleveland Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-cliffs-at-pourville: One of Monet's 1882 views from the Norman village of Pourville, where he worked along the cliff path between Dieppe and Varengeville. Tall grasses are whipped into rapid green-and-violet strokes, the Channel pushed to a high horizon so that the cliff and sky carry most of the picture's air.
collection-of-beauty-climbing-on-mt-fuji: A late plate from Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, showing pilgrims roped along the rocky upper slopes of the sacred peak. Hokusai records the climb itself rather than the silhouette, using the famous bero-ai imported Prussian blue for the cold air at altitude.
collection-of-beauty-col-tempo-by-giorgi: An elderly woman behind a parapet turns toward the viewer with her mouth half open, holding a small slip inscribed 'Col tempo,' so it goes with time. Painted on canvas around 1506, the work is one of the earliest unflinching portrayals of old age in Italian painting; it hangs in its original frame at the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice.
collection-of-beauty-cole-thomas-der-pok: A colossal vegetation-encrusted goblet rises from a wooded plain, classical ruins crowning its rim and tiny boats sailing on its glassy water. Painted in 1833 and rejected by Cole's patron Luman Reed, the canvas now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art has been read variously as the Norse world-tree Yggdrasil and a Greek mythological cup.
collection-of-beauty-cole-thomas-expulsi: Adam and Eve flee across a rocky bridge from the lush green interior of Eden into a darkened landscape of storm, volcano and ravening beasts, the divine flaming sword at their backs. Painted in 1828 as a pendant to The Garden of Eden, the canvas hangs at the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, a gift of the Karolik collection.
collection-of-beauty-cole-thomas-the-con: The third canvas in The Course of Empire shows a fictive classical city at its zenith, with porticoes, rotundas, statuary and a triumphal procession crossing a marble bridge above the harbour. Cole painted the five-part allegory for his patron Luman Reed's Greenwich Street picture gallery between 1833 and 1836; Reed died in June 1836 without seeing the series completed.
collection-of-beauty-cole-thomas-the-oxb: Storm clouds break over a shattered foreground of cliffs and lightning-struck pines while, below the precipice, the Connecticut River loops in a brilliant U around the cultivated farms of Northampton. Cole interrupted The Course of Empire to paint the canvas for the 1836 National Academy exhibition; it sold to Charles N. Talbot for 500 dollars and is now at the Metropolitan Museum.
collection-of-beauty-cole-thomas-the-tem: The unfinished Doric temple at Segesta in western Sicily rises above scrub-covered hills, with a tiny seated figure of the painter sketching at lower left. Cole worked the canvas up in 1843 from drawings made during his second European tour, and the picture entered the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-colonel-john-bulloc: Colonel John Bullock of Faulkbourne Hall stands at three-quarter length in scarlet uniform, his hand resting on a sword hilt. Gainsborough painted the militia officer in the early 1770s, during the Bath years when his commissions from county gentry and military sitters were at their height.
collection-of-beauty-columbus-and-his-so: Columbus arrives at the Franciscan monastery of La Rabida with his young son Diego, footsore after the failure of his Portuguese petitions. Painted in 1838 and now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the canvas inaugurated Delacroix's pair of Columbus subjects, the second showing the explorer's later reception at the Spanish court.
collection-of-beauty-confusion-of-tongue: An illustration to Genesis 11 from Doré's English Bible, depicting the workers scattering as the Tower of Babel founders mid-construction. Doré stages the scene with vertiginous architecture and a gulf of stormy sky, exploiting the dense black hatching of wood-engraving to dramatise divine judgement.
collection-of-beauty-constable-osmington: Osmington Bay on the Dorset coast spreads under a sky of broken cumulus, the cliffs running off toward Weymouth. Constable painted the small oil on his 1816 honeymoon at the village of Osmington, where the rector John Fisher had married him to Maria Bicknell that October.
collection-of-beauty-constable-salisbury: A late, emotionally charged view of Salisbury Cathedral seen across the water meadows under a rainbow, painted in the wake of Constable's wife's death. Flickering white highlights, the celebrated Constable snow, animate trees and sky in a picture that fused topographic affection with personal grief.
collection-of-beauty-constable-seascape-: A small open-air oil sketch of the sea off Brighton, where Constable spent summers for his wife's health. He records a single squall in rapid, loaded brushwork, the sky's grey-violet rain veil treated with the empirical attention to weather he called the chiaroscuro of nature.
collection-of-beauty-constable-the-cornf: A boy drinking from a stream beside a flock of sheep on the sunken Fen Lane between East Bergholt and Dedham, a cornfield opening to a church tower in the middle distance. Painted in Constable's London studio in early 1826 and shown at the Royal Academy that summer, the picture was bought by subscription after his death and presented to the National Gallery in 1837.
collection-of-beauty-constable-the-wheat: Reapers and gleaners work a Suffolk wheat field under a high summer sky, painted on Constable's home ground near East Bergholt in 1816. The canvas, now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington with accession 2007.8.27, dates from the months around his marriage and prefigures the six-foot landscapes he began the following year.
collection-of-beauty-constable-view-on-t: Barges and bargemen on the Stour at Dedham, with Dedham church tower distant under broken cloud. The third of Constable's six-foot Stour canvases, exhibited at the Royal Academy in 1822 and now at the Huntington in San Marino.
collection-of-beauty-constantinople-la-m: The Nusretiye Mosque rises from pink mist above the Tophane waterfront of Istanbul, twin minarets catching gold light while a small caique drifts in the foreground. Aivazovsky worked the 115.5 by 90.5 cm oil from memories of his 1845 Mediterranean voyage; the canvas entered the Musee des Beaux-Arts de Brest in 1884.
collection-of-beauty-copley-col-fitch-si: Colonel William Fitch stands in scarlet army uniform beside his charger, flanked by his sisters Sarah in neoclassical white and Ann in dark mourning. Copley painted the family group between 1800 and 1801 in London, where the American expatriate had settled and the Fitch siblings had gathered in widowhood.
collection-of-beauty-cornard-wood: An early woodland scene from Gainsborough's Suffolk years, made before he turned full-time to portrait commissions in Bath and London. Drawing on Dutch landscape models, particularly Ruisdael, he threads a sandy track through scrubby oaks under a broken English sky.
collection-of-beauty-cornelia-vetterlein: A portrait from Stieler's Munich practice, where he served as court painter to the Bavarian kings. The sitter is set against a smooth dark ground in the artist's signature manner, soft modelling of the face giving way to crisp, jewel-like attention at lace and ribbon.
collection-of-beauty-cornelis-cornelisz-: A monk and a beguine paired in earthy proximity, a stock anticlerical jab popular in late-sixteenth-century Dutch genre. Cornelis softens his Mannerist drawing for the satirical mode, fixing the figures in close focus against a plain dark ground.

Ixion plunges into Tartarus among a tangle of rebellious giants in this Haarlem Mannerist tour de force of foreshortened nudes. Cornelis exaggerates musculature and contorted pose under crisp lighting, the kind of athletic, learned composition prized by Karel van Mander's circle.

The defeated Titans tumble headlong from heaven, their nude bodies twisting around each other in a virtuoso lattice of foreshortening. Cornelis treats the mythological subject as an excuse for anatomical display, central to the late-sixteenth-century Haarlem Mannerism he developed with Goltzius and Van Mander.
collection-of-beauty-cornelis-de-vos-el-: A Flemish baroque procession of Bacchus and Ariadne, with putti, satyrs, and tipsy revellers wreathed in vine. De Vos, best known for his crisp portraits of Antwerp burghers, here works closer to Rubens's mythological idiom, ordering the throng with broad, ruddy modelling.
collection-of-beauty-cornelis-springer-a: The Jodenbreestraat in Amsterdam, with the house once occupied by Rembrandt at number 4-6 reimagined in its supposed seventeenth-century guise, the Sint-Antoniesluis at right and the tower of the Zuiderkerk rising behind. Springer, a Romantic topographical painter, treated the city as a chain of historicising stage sets rather than the contemporary streetscape.
collection-of-beauty-corner-in-voyer-d-a: A summer corner of an Asnières park from Van Gogh's Paris years, when he absorbed Impressionism and Neo-Impressionism in the company of Bernard and Signac. Short divided strokes of green, lemon, and rose lighten his palette decisively before he carried it south to Arles.
collection-of-beauty-correggio-leda-and-: An erotic mythology painted for Federico II Gonzaga of Mantua as part of a series of Loves of Jupiter intended as a gift to Charles V. Correggio orchestrates Leda's encounter in soft chiaroscuro and a continuous lateral rhythm of figures, the smoky modelling that would inspire Parmigianino and the Carracci.
collection-of-beauty-correggio-ritratto-: A standing woman in dark mourning dress holds a bowl in a wooded landscape, her gaze direct and reserved. Signed with the Latinised "Anton. Laet.", the portrait is sometimes identified as Veronica Gambara and marks Correggio's transition into a more refined, psychologically attentive manner.
collection-of-beauty-countess-siemontkow: A society portrait from Vigée Le Brun's twelve-year exile after fleeing revolutionary Paris, when she travelled the courts of Italy, Vienna, and Saint Petersburg. Soft pastel-key flesh tones, a feathered hat, and a deliberately informal pose carry forward the Marie-Antoinette idiom that made her career.
collection-of-beauty-courbet-autoportrai: An early self-portrait from Courbet's Romantic-tinged youth, the painter shown smoking a long pipe with hooded eyes and a tilted head. Strong dark-on-dark modelling and a deliberately bohemian air announce the self-mythologising persona he would build through the 1850s.
collection-of-beauty-courbet-l-hallali-d: A vast hunting picture, over five metres wide, in which hounds bring down a stag in deep snow under the eye of a mounted huntsman. Courbet draws on his Franche-Comté upbringing and the Flemish hunt tradition, scaling a popular subject up to the format of history painting in keeping with his Realist programme.
collection-of-beauty-courbet-the-sailboa: Two fishing boats heel through heavy chop, their tan sails straining against a pale sky while the foreground dissolves into churned green water laid on with the palette knife. The canvas dates from around 1869, when Courbet was painting the Channel coast at Étretat and produced some of the most physical seascapes of the nineteenth century. It is in the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute, Williamstown, Massachusetts.
collection-of-beauty-courtyard-with-luna: A small tin-plate painting from Goya's recovery after the illness that left him deaf, drawing on a violent scene he claimed to have witnessed in Zaragoza. Naked inmates wrestle under a barred opening while a warden flogs them, the cell's harsh chiaroscuro foreshadowing the Black Paintings.
collection-of-beauty-coypel-democritus: The laughing philosopher of Abdera turns from his open book, a bony skull and globe at his elbow indicating his meditations on human folly. Coypel painted the bust-length allegory in 1692, treating the Greek thinker in the Caravaggesque half-light then fashionable for half-figures of antique sages.
collection-of-beauty-cranach-madonna-und: The Virgin cradles the Christ Child against a dark fir backdrop, a German alpine motif that replaces Italian landscape conventions with Saxon woodland. Cranach's panel, painted for Breslau Cathedral, balances tender intimacy against the spiky verticals of conifer needles, a hallmark of his court style at Wittenberg.
collection-of-beauty-cristo-en-casa-de-m: A bodegón that folds a domestic kitchen scene around a small framed vignette of Christ admonishing Martha. The young Velázquez sets garlic, eggs and a glistening fish in tight tenebrist focus, signalling the Sevillian taste for moral allegory dressed as still life.
collection-of-beauty-crossing-the-river-: Charon ferries a soul across the underworld river, with paradise and a fiery hell flanking the panel in classic Netherlandish duality. Patinir, credited as the first dedicated landscape painter, expands the mythological subject into a panoramic geography of cliffs, water and atmospheric distance.
collection-of-beauty-crow-and-blossom-by: A solitary crow perches on a flowering branch, the bird's blue-black plumage set against pale petals. Koson's shin-hanga woodblock print refines Edo-period kachō-e bird-and-flower conventions for early-twentieth-century export collectors, prizing economical line and atmospheric ground.
collection-of-beauty-crucifixion-andrea-: The central panel of Mantegna's San Zeno altarpiece predella, showing Christ crucified between the thieves on a rocky knoll. Mantegna deploys archaeological architectural detail and sharp foreshortening, treating the figures with the chiselled severity of Roman relief sculpture.
collection-of-beauty-cult-of-beauty-001: Whistler's full-length portrait of his model and lover Joanna Hiffernan in a white muslin dress, holding a lily. Conceived as a study in tonal harmony rather than narrative, the picture became a touchstone for the Aesthetic movement's pursuit of art for art's sake.
collection-of-beauty-v-gorakh-alatau: A view across the Alatau range of the Tien Shan, painted during Vereshchagin's Central Asian travels. The canvas belongs to the Turkestan group of works the artist produced from sketches made on his journeys of 1869 to 1870 through what is now eastern Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan.
collection-of-beauty-dance-at-bougival: A young couple turns on the floor of a riverside dance hall outside Paris, the woman's pink bonnet glowing against the dappled crowd. Renoir worked from sittings with Suzanne Valadon and Paul Lhote to fix Impressionist plein-air light into a tightly composed figural scene.
collection-of-beauty-danceringreen: A ballet dancer in a green tutu adjusts her costume in the wings, captured from Degas' habitual cropped, off-axis vantage. Pastel hatching layers powdery greens and pinks, a chromatic shorthand the artist refined throughout his Opéra de Paris series.
collection-of-beauty-dancers-1900-degas: Three ballet dancers adjust the straps of their pale tutus in a backstage clearing, their poses caught between rehearsal and rest. Degas worked the pastel around 1900 as his eyesight failed, scaling up the figures and pushing the colour into intense orange and emerald.
collection-of-beauty-daniel-crommelin-ve: The nine-year-old Daniel Crommelin Verplanck of New York sits under a tree in a tan coat, a tame squirrel on a chain in his lap. Now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the canvas was painted at the Verplanck family seat on lower Wall Street in 1771, during Copley's late colonial period.
collection-of-beauty-daniel-in-the-lion-: Daniel kneels at dawn among nine life-sized lions, hands clasped upward as the beasts prowl, yawn and stare. Rubens drew the lions from observation in the menagerie of Archduke Albert and worked them into a Counter-Reformation meditation on faith preserved.
collection-of-beauty-dans-la-foret-de-fo: Figures rest in the dappled clearing of the Forest of Fontainebleau, the wooded preserve south of Paris that drew the Barbizon and early Impressionist painters. Renoir's youthful palette is still rooted in earthy Courbet-like tonality before his shift to brighter spectral colour.
collection-of-beauty-dans-la-prairie-by-: Camille Monet reads in a meadow strewn with poppies and daisies, her parasol propped beside her. Monet's broken brushwork dissolves figure and field into a single screen of high-keyed colour, a Giverny-era exercise in the Impressionist treatment of figures outdoors.
collection-of-beauty-danwon-bbalrae-teo: Women beating laundry at a stream while a passing scholar peers over a rock, from Kim Hong-do's Danwon pungsokdo cheop. The sheet, ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, is held by the National Museum of Korea and belongs to the album of genre scenes that established his reputation as the great chronicler of everyday Joseon life.
collection-of-beauty-danwon-mudong: Dancing boy with musicians playing flute, drum, and zither, a scene from the Danwon pungsokdo cheop. Kim Hong-do worked in ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, with the album of genre studies now held by the National Museum of Korea and considered a benchmark of late 18th-century Joseon painting.
collection-of-beauty-danwon-nongali: Farmers driving an ox-drawn plough through a paddy field, from the Danwon pungsokdo cheop. Kim Hong-do painted the leaf in ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm, part of the album of agricultural and artisanal scenes held by the National Museum of Korea as a record of common life under King Jeongjo.
collection-of-beauty-danwon-ssireum: Two wrestlers locked in a ssireum hold while spectators ring the contest, divided into upper and lower groups around the action. From the Danwon pungsokdo cheop in the National Museum of Korea, the sheet is ink and light colour on paper at 27 by 22.7 cm and counts as the most reproduced image of Joseon genre painting.
collection-of-beauty-darmstadtmadonna: The Virgin stands on a shell-headed niche above the kneeling family of Burgomaster Jakob Meyer zum Hasen, the Christ Child raising a small hand in blessing. Commissioned in 1526 from Holbein the Younger during his first Basel residency, the panel is now in the Johanniterkirche in Schwäbisch Hall after a long sojourn at Schloss Darmstadt.
collection-of-beauty-david-brutus: The Roman consul Brutus sits in shadow as lictors return the bodies of his sons, executed for treason on his order. David exhibited the picture at the Salon weeks after the storming of the Bastille, and Revolutionary audiences read its civic stoicism as immediate political instruction.
collection-of-beauty-david-dessinant-mar: Jacques-Louis David sketches Marie Antoinette in the tumbril as she is led to the guillotine, the queen seated upright with her hands bound behind her. Painted in 1900 by the Belgian artist Joseph-Emmanuel van den Büssche, the canvas dramatises the famous October 1793 sketch David made from a window on the rue Saint-Honoré.
collection-of-beauty-david-etienne-mauri: General Étienne Maurice Gérard, a Napoleonic comte d'Empire then in exile in Brussels, sits in dark civilian dress with the cordon of the Légion d'honneur visible at his collar. David painted the portrait in 1816, sharing exile with his sitter after the Hundred Days, the canvas now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-david-napoleon-cros: Bonaparte in an orange cloak reins in a rearing piebald horse on the slopes of the Great St Bernard Pass, the names of Hannibal and Karolus Magnus carved into the rock at his feet. David painted the Malmaison version in 1800, the first of five autograph variants commissioned by Charles IV of Spain after the Marengo campaign.
collection-of-beauty-david-portrait-of-m: The chemist Antoine Lavoisier looks up from a manuscript while his wife Marie-Anne leans on his shoulder, their pneumatic apparatus arrayed on a red-draped table. David completed the double portrait in 1788, the year Lavoisier published the Traite elementaire de chimie; it entered the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 1977 as accession 1977.10.
collection-of-beauty-david-s-leonidas-an: Jean-Nicolas Laugier's calcographic engraving after David's vast Louvre canvas, with the Spartan king seated bare-chested among his three hundred men as they prepare to defend the pass against Xerxes. David worked on the original from 1799 to 1814, returning to the subject as European armies closed in on Napoleon's empire.
collection-of-beauty-david-self-portrait: David paints himself at the easel in shirtsleeves and a loose dark coat, palette in one hand, brush poised in the other. He executed the self-portrait in 1794 while imprisoned in the Luxembourg Palace after the fall of Robespierre; the canvas is now in the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-david-the-death-of-: Socrates sits upright on his prison bed, one hand reaching for the cup of hemlock, the other raised in mid-discourse as his grieving disciples surround him. David painted the canvas in 1787 for Charles-Michel Trudaine de la Sabliere, exhibiting it at the Salon as a Neoclassical exemplum of stoic civic virtue; it now hangs at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-david-vilain: Sophie-Louise-Zoé de Feltz, Comtesse Vilain XIIII, sits in a Brussels garden in white empire dress with her five-year-old daughter Louise leaning at her knee. David painted the double portrait in 1816 during his Belgian exile; it remains one of the most tender of his late commissions and is now held by the National Gallery in London.
collection-of-beauty-david-wilkie-chelse: Veterans cluster outside a Chelsea pub as a despatch announcing the victory at Waterloo is read aloud. Commissioned by the Duke of Wellington, Wilkie filled the genre tableau with regimental specificity, prompting crowd-control rails when it was shown at the Royal Academy in 1822.
collection-of-beauty-david-with-the-head: The young David holds out the severed head of Goliath, in which Caravaggio is widely thought to have painted his own features. Made in his fugitive late period and probably sent to Cardinal Scipione Borghese as a plea for pardon, the canvas distils tenebrist drama into a single beam of light.
collection-of-beauty-david98: Anne-Marie-Louise Thelusson, Comtesse de Sorcy, sits in a white empire-line gown with a pink shawl, her dark curls falling against an unornamented grey wall. David painted the Geneva banker's daughter in 1790, the austere setting and unbroken contour typifying his Revolution-era female portraits; the picture is now in the Neue Pinakothek, Munich.
collection-of-beauty-de-gion-brug-te-hon: Kawase Hasui's view of the Gion bridge crossing at Hondo on the Amakusa islands, from his series Selected Views of Japan. The print pairs the cool blues of an evening landscape with the softly graded skies that became his signature.
collection-of-beauty-de-grote-lantaarn-v: Pilgrims climb the steps beneath the giant red lantern that marks the entrance to the Kannon temple at Asakusa. Kasamatsu Shirō issued the design through the Watanabe publishing house at the height of the Shin-hanga revival of traditional ukiyo-e subjects.
collection-of-beauty-de-humani-corporis-: A muscleman écorché stands in a Paduan landscape, layers of musculature peeled back to reveal underlying anatomy. The plate, cut for Vesalius' 1543 treatise, was carved in the Titian workshop circle and revolutionised medical illustration by binding observation to a humanist visual language.

Another of the Fabrica's flayed figures, posed against a continuous Veneto skyline that links the seven plates into a single panorama when arranged in sequence. Vesalius insisted on direct dissection, and the woodcut renders the layered musculature with unprecedented anatomical accuracy.

A deeper écorché stage from the Fabrica, with skin and superficial muscle stripped away to expose the trunk and limbs. Printed in Basel by Oporinus, the plates set a new standard for the integration of artistic skill and dissection-based medical knowledge.

A skeletal study from Vesalius' Fabrica, the bones articulated in a contemplative pose against an architectural ruin. The volume's woodcuts carried Renaissance memento-mori conventions into the empirical project of anatomy.
collection-of-beauty-de-pruimenboomgaard: A celebrated plum tree in the Kameido garden east of Edo, its blossoming branch thrust across the foreground while visitors stroll behind in a red-suffused dusk. Hiroshige's print from One Hundred Famous Views of Edo was later copied in oil by Van Gogh.
collection-of-beauty-de-rand-van-de-shin: Lanterns burn in the haze of a foggy evening at Ueno Park, with figures passing beside the still water of Shinobazu Pond and a pagoda rising behind. Kasamatsu Shirō was a leading designer of the second Shin-hanga generation; this print was issued by Watanabe Shōzaburō in 1932.
collection-of-beauty-de-warme-bronnen-va: Lit hotels line the Katsura River at the hot-spring town of Shuzenji on the Izu peninsula, with cherry blossom in the foreground. Kasamatsu Shirō's 1937 design pairs the meticulous block-cutting of Shin-hanga with a romanticism inherited from late nineteenth-century landscape prints.
collection-of-beauty-death-of-camilla-by: Horatius stands over the body of his sister Camilla, whom he has just killed for mourning her Curiatii lover, drawn from Livy's account of the early Roman duel. Fyodor Bruni painted the canvas during his Italian pensioner years for the Imperial Academy; it now hangs in the Russian Museum, Saint Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-death-of-the-virgin: The Virgin lies dying on a great canopied bed surrounded by the twelve apostles: one reads the office of the dying, another places a taper in her hands, and a tall candlestick stands at the foot of the bed. Engraved around 1470-75, it is one of Schongauer's largest and most influential prints, copied across Europe and studied closely by the young Dürer. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-degas-a-woman-seate: Madame Valpinçon glances aside while a riotous bouquet dominates the canvas, the figure pushed to the edge in a deliberate inversion of conventional portrait hierarchy. Degas treats the flowers with thick impasto, the sitter with restrained drawing-led brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-degas-cafekonzert-s: A café-concert performer leans forward mid-song, mouth open, her gloved hand suspended before her face to mark the physical effort of projection. The 1878 pastel on canvas, now at Harvard's Fogg Museum, belongs to Degas's run of theatre subjects in which he and Mary Cassatt were testing pastel against the glare of gas footlights.
collection-of-beauty-degas-deux-danseuse: Two dancers rest between exercises in tutus and bodices, one adjusting her shoulder strap while the other stands behind her. The 1879 sheet, pastel and gouache on paper at roughly 46 by 67 cm, belongs to Degas's long preoccupation with the lulls of the rehearsal room rather than the polished performance.
collection-of-beauty-degas-frau-mit-stad: The actress Ellen Andrée stands in everyday street dress, her face cast in shadow beneath a small hat. Degas drew this 1879 pastel as part of his series of modern Parisiennes, the same sitter whose absinthe-stupor he had captured for In a Café three years earlier.
collection-of-beauty-delacroix-barque-of: Dante and Virgil cross the Stygian marsh in Phlegyas's skiff as the damned claw at the gunwale, drawn from the eighth canto of the Inferno. Delacroix's Salon debut in 1822, the picture was bought by the state and now hangs in the Louvre; the dripping water beads on the nude bodies pay direct homage to Rubens.
collection-of-beauty-delacroix-eugene-fe: A nude woman reclines on shimmering striped draperies, reaching up to stroke a green parrot perched above her head. Painted in 1827 and now at the Musée des Beaux-Arts in Lyons, the small Orientalist canvas was one of several private cabinet pictures Delacroix produced alongside the Salon spectacular Death of Sardanapalus.
collection-of-beauty-delacroix-louis-dor: Louis I, Duke of Orléans lifts the bedclothes to display the lower half of his sleeping mistress to her own husband, the chamberlain Albert Le Flamenc, who fails to recognise her in the half-shadow. Painted in 1825-26 and now in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza, the small canvas draws on an anecdote from Brantôme's Vie des dames galantes.
collection-of-beauty-delacroix-marc-aure: The dying emperor Marcus Aurelius commends his unworthy son Commodus to a grave circle of Stoic counsellors. Delacroix exhibited the picture at the 1845 Salon, where Baudelaire singled out its sombre violet and ochre palette as the chromatic distillation of Romantic history painting.
collection-of-beauty-delaunay-champdemar: The Eiffel Tower rises in fractured red and ochre planes above the Champ de Mars. Delaunay's Orphic Cubism dismantles the engineered iron icon into prismatic facets, part of his sustained series treating the tower as a modern motif of Parisian light and movement.
collection-of-beauty-delaunay-portuguese: A Portuguese woman pours from a pitcher, her costume and the surrounding still life dissolved into chromatic discs and arcs. Delaunay painted the canvas in oil and wax in 1916 during the family's stay in the Portuguese village of Vila do Conde near Oporto; the work, also known as the Tall Portuguese, is held by the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid.
collection-of-beauty-delftsedonderslag: A topographical record of the gunpowder explosion that levelled a quarter of Delft on 12 October 1654, killing van der Poel's own daughter. The artist made the catastrophe his recurring subject, painting smouldering rubble, broken roofs and bewildered survivors with documentary specificity.
collection-of-beauty-descent-from-the-cr: Christ's slack body is lowered from the cross onto a white shroud while torchlight picks out Joseph of Arimathea, the weeping Virgin and a clamouring crowd below. Signed and dated 1634, the canvas in the State Hermitage, Saint Petersburg, is the second of Rembrandt's full-scale Passion pictures commissioned by Stadholder Frederick Henry of Orange.
collection-of-beauty-descente-de-croix-r: A workshop variant of Rubens' Antwerp Cathedral altarpiece, with the pale body of Christ lowered diagonally onto a white shroud held by mourners. The composition's coiling diagonals and contrasted flesh tones became a Counter-Reformation template repeated across Catholic Europe.
collection-of-beauty-destruction-of-levi: God smites the sea-monster Leviathan with a sword, the beast writhing in the deep amid lightning-lit clouds. Doré's wood-engraved illustration appeared in his folio English Bible, blending Romantic sublimity with the dense cross-hatching that defined his commercial print style.
collection-of-beauty-die-kreuzabnahme-ru: A Descent from the Cross after Rubens, transposing the master's Antwerp altarpiece composition into reproductive form. The diagonal sweep of Christ's pallid body lowered onto a white winding-sheet preserves the Baroque dramaturgy of the original.
collection-of-beauty-die-landschaft-mit-: Three trees crown a low rise above a flat Dutch polder, with a thunderstorm rolling in from the left and tiny figures fishing and sketching at the margins. Rembrandt's largest landscape etching combines drypoint and engraving to model an unusually dramatic sky.
collection-of-beauty-dolley-madison: Dolley Madison, then wife of the Secretary of State, faces the viewer in a low-cut white Empire-waisted gown, a string of pearls at her throat and dark curls framing her face. Stuart painted the portrait in 1804 in Washington, four years before her husband became president and she emerged as the capital's leading hostess.
collection-of-beauty-domenikos-theotokop: Gabriel descends through a vortex of cherubim toward the kneeling Virgin, his lily and her sewing basket linking the heavenly and domestic registers. Painted for the Hospital Tavera in Toledo as part of his final commission, El Greco stretches the figures into the flickering, candle-flame elongation that defines his last decade.
collection-of-beauty-don-juan-by-eugene-: Survivors of a foundered ship draw lots for cannibalism in an open boat, an episode adapted from Byron's poem. Delacroix turns the literary Romantic subject into a study of taut, sea-tossed bodies and overcast Channel light in the wake of Géricault's Raft of the Medusa.
collection-of-beauty-don-quijote-illustr: Don Quixote rides out across the Spanish meseta with Sancho Panza behind, an illustration from Doré's monumental 1863 edition of Cervantes. The wood-engraved plates, cut by a battery of Parisian engravers, fixed the public image of the knight-errant for the next century.

A wood-engraved plate from Doré's celebrated illustrated edition of Cervantes' novel, in which the gaunt knight and his squire move through a finely hatched landscape. The attribution to Dürer is a cataloguing slip; the image belongs to Doré's nineteenth-century print cycle.
collection-of-beauty-dong-yuan-mountain-: Attributed to the tenth-century master Dong Yuan, this hanging scroll in ink and light colour on silk imagines a paradise hall of the Immortals deep in the mountains, its pavilions nested among mist-wrapped peaks. The towering vertical composition, over 1.8 metres tall, is held in the National Palace Museum, Taipei.
collection-of-beauty-dong-yuan-rivers-de: A detail from a long handscroll associated with the Southern Tang master, depicting the misted reaches of the Xiao and Xiang rivers in Hunan. Dong Yuan's soft hemp-fibre brushstrokes and graded ink washes established the canonical southern landscape mode followed for centuries.
collection-of-beauty-dore-gustave-la-sai: A Counter-Reformation altar composition showing the Trinity enthroned amid swirling clouds and angels. Rubens deploys his characteristic ruddy flesh tones, golden draperies and dynamic Baroque diagonals to lift the eye toward the heavenly group.
collection-of-beauty-dore-i-had-done-a-h: A wood-engraving from Doré's late illustrated edition of Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner, showing the sailor clinging to the rigging after slaying the albatross. Dense parallel hatching builds the storm-charged sea and the cramped vertigo of the crow's nest.
collection-of-beauty-dortordordrecht: A luminous view of the Dutch port of Dordrecht with the packet-boat becalmed at sunrise, openly indebted to Cuyp. Turner dissolves shipping, water and sky into a single golden haze that anticipates his later atmospheric experiments.
collection-of-beauty-dr-deijman-s-anatom: A foreshortened cadaver lies on the dissection table while Dr Joan Deijman, his hands shown above, performs an autopsy on the brain. Painted in 1656 for the Amsterdam Surgeons' Guild as a sequel to the Tulp anatomy of 1632, most of the canvas was destroyed by fire in 1723; only the central fragment survives in the Amsterdam Museum.
collection-of-beauty-dr-richard-price-dd: The dissenting minister and political philosopher Richard Price sits in his study reading a 1784 letter from Benjamin Franklin, a longstanding correspondent. West painted Price in 1784, the year the National Library of Wales journal records the sittings; the portrait now belongs to the National Museum of Wales.
collection-of-beauty-dragomirov-by-repin: A bust-length state portrait of the Russian general and military theorist, hero of the crossing of the Danube in 1877. Repin works in his vigorous realist manner, building the weathered face and braided uniform from loaded, broken strokes.
collection-of-beauty-drawing-of-mules-by: Three mules stand and graze in a campagna pasture, one shown full length in profile, the others lightly sketched behind. A brush drawing in brown wash over graphite of 143 by 257 mm in the British Museum, the sheet documents the patient livestock studies Claude made on his walks out of Rome, later transposed into the foregrounds of his idyllic ports and harbours.
collection-of-beauty-duchess-of-polignac: A portrait of Marie Antoinette's intimate favourite, shown in a soft straw hat and informal muslin dress holding a sheet of music. Vigée Le Brun's pearly flesh tones and feathery brushwork epitomise the late ancien régime ideal of natural elegance.
collection-of-beauty-durer-academie-de-f: A pen study of a standing female nude seen from behind, holding a staff from which a veil falls. Made during Dürer's first Italian journey, the sheet shows him grappling with classical proportion and the contrapposto idealised by his Venetian contemporaries.
collection-of-beauty-durer-agnes-durer-m: An intimate pen drawing inscribed "mein Agnes," showing the artist's wife in domestic dress with downcast eyes. The sheet, preserved at the Albertina in Vienna, is among the earliest surviving spousal portraits in Northern art.
collection-of-beauty-durer-ecureuil: A watercolour and gouache study of two red squirrels rendered with near-zoological precision, each tuft of fur picked out in fine brush. The sheet belongs to Dürer's lifelong investigation of nature, alongside his hare and great piece of turf.
collection-of-beauty-durer-hieronymus-ho: A late portrait of the Nuremberg patrician and councilman, rendered with almost forensic attention to white curling hair and weathered skin. Painted the year before Dürer's Four Apostles, it distils a lifetime of observing individual character.
collection-of-beauty-duse-by-repin: A charcoal portrait of the Italian tragedienne Eleonora Duse, capturing the famously expressive actress in a moment of inward concentration. Repin exploits the chalky drag of charcoal on canvas to model her face while leaving the gown in summary, atmospheric strokes.
collection-of-beauty-e-v-pavlov-by-repin: A documentary group composition showing the surgeon Evgeny Pavlov operating in a St Petersburg theatre, witnessed by gowned colleagues. Repin treats the modern clinic as a secular history piece, marshalling sharp tonal contrasts and a tightly bracketed perspective around the patient.
collection-of-beauty-e1924-3-16-pma2018: A meander of the Epte near Giverny, the small river that fed Monet's water-garden. The canvas is built from short, broken touches that knit foliage, bank and reflection into a single shimmering surface, characteristic of his late 1880s plein-air practice.
collection-of-beauty-eakins-ashbury-w-le: The elderly Philadelphian Ashbury Wright Lee is shown three-quarter length in a dark coat, the loose handling of the face typical of Eakins's late portraiture. Painted around 1905, the canvas belongs to the unsparing commissioned likenesses Eakins produced for friends and acquaintances in his final productive decade.
collection-of-beauty-eakins-selfportrait: Eakins faces the viewer in dark suit and uneven moustache, his rumpled hair contrasting with the buttoned formality of the waistcoat. Painted as the diploma piece for his 1902 election to the National Academy of Design, it is one of only two unadorned self-portraits the Philadelphia realist ever produced.
collection-of-beauty-eakins-thomas-wrest: Two locked grapplers studied with the anatomical exactness Eakins demanded of his Philadelphia students. The earthy palette, low viewpoint and frieze-like composition reflect his admiration for ancient athletic sculpture filtered through photographic study of the male body.
collection-of-beauty-east-cowes-castle-t: Racing yachts heel into the wind as they beat to windward through a choppy Solent, with the wooded shoreline of East Cowes Castle beyond. Turner painted this oil on canvas and a companion view for the architect John Nash after staying at the castle, Nash's residence on the Isle of Wight, during the Cowes regatta of 1827, and exhibited both at the Royal Academy in 1828. This canvas is in the Indianapolis Museum of Art; its pendant, showing the regatta boats starting for their moorings, is in the Victoria and Albert Museum.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-1834-19: A nude bather seen from behind braces one hand against her lower back as she steps from a shallow tub, the towel and washstand sketched in rough strokes. The pastel of around 1887, now at the Honolulu Museum of Art, belongs to the bathers series Degas pursued through the late 1880s, treating the toilette as an unselfconscious physical act observed through a keyhole.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-achille: The artist's younger brother Achille stands in the dark uniform of a French naval cadet, a gold aiguillette at his shoulder and one hand resting on a stone ledge. Painted around 1856-57 while Degas was beginning his Italian study years, the canvas is held by the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-after-t: A nude woman bends low over her thigh to dry her leg, her hair piled and the bath linens crumpled around her. Degas built the pastel by laying tracing paper over an earlier study and copying the figure exactly before mounting it on cardboard; the sheet entered the Norton Simon Foundation collection in 1978 and bears the catalogue date 1884-1886.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-at-the-: A landau parked at a country racecourse, the Valpinçon family attending to their newborn son under the shade of a parasol. Degas crops the carriage and horses with photographic abruptness, turning a polite outing into a study of asymmetric modern composition.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-ballet-: Dancers in tutus drift through a stage rehearsal, one yawning behind a flat, the ballet master and observers grouped in shadow at the wings. The Metropolitan's version, in oil thinned to a near grisaille, is one of three closely related compositions Degas worked on around 1874, the largest of which appeared in the first Impressionist exhibition that April.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-before-: Thoroughbreds and jockeys mill restlessly along the rail before the start, presented in a scatter of angled poses rather than a single tableau. Degas painted the small panel between 1882 and 1884, one of three identically titled canvases that drew on the stop-action horse photography then being published by Eadweard Muybridge. Henry Walters bought it in 1910 for the museum in Baltimore.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-chasse-: Young ballerinas gather in a high-windowed rehearsal room of the Paris Opera, one working at the barre while the others wait their turn or adjust their dress. This small oil, roughly 19 by 27 centimetres and painted around 1870-1872, stands at the very beginning of Degas's ballet series, in which the company's working spaces served as a laboratory for studies of light and arrested movement. It came to the Metropolitan Museum of Art with the H. O. Havemeyer bequest in 1929.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-dancers: Two dancers in green and orange tutus stretch along a barre in the corner of a studio, the floor tipping forward toward the viewer. Degas worked the canvas around 1900 and it now hangs in the Phillips Collection, Washington, an example of the broad late handling in which contour and colour come close to abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-in-a-ca: The actress Ellen Andrée and the engraver Marcellin Desboutin sit side by side at a marble café table, the woman staring blankly past a tall glass of cloudy absinthe. Originally exhibited under the title Dans un café and reset as L'Absinthe at its London showing of 1893, the picture was painted at the Nouvelle-Athènes in Pigalle and is now in the Musée d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-place-d: Ludovic-Napoléon Lepic, cigar in hand and umbrella tucked under his arm, strides across the windswept square with his two daughters and a borzoi, a solitary man cropped at the left edge. Painted in 1875 and now at the Hermitage by way of the Gerstenberg collection and Soviet trophy art transfers, the picture places Lepic's silhouette over the statue of Strasbourg, then a recent emblem of loss to Prussia.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-portrai: Hortense, the young daughter of Degas's childhood friend Paul Valpinçon, leans against a table and steadies a half-eaten apple in her hand. Painted in 1871 at the family's Normandy estate of Ménil-Hubert on a remnant of striped mattress ticking when no proper canvas was at hand, the portrait is now at the Minneapolis Institute of Art.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-the-bal: In a rehearsal room of the old opera house on the rue Le Peletier, dancers in white tutus practise at the barre and rest along the back wall while the ballet master Jules Perrot leans on his long staff at the centre. Degas worked on the oil on canvas between 1871 and 1874, repeatedly revising the poses. One of the founding pictures of his ballet series, it now hangs in the Musee d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-the-bel: Degas's aunt Laura Bellelli stands in mourning black with her two daughters in their Florence apartment, her husband Gennaro turned away in an armchair at right, a chalk portrait of her recently dead father pinned to the wall behind. Begun during the artist's 1858-59 stay with the family and completed in Paris, the canvas is now the centrepiece of the early Degas rooms at the Musée d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-the-mil: Two women bend over a worktable strewn with ribbons and pinned hats, their faces lost in concentration. Degas returned to the millinery subject through the 1890s; the 1898 canvas entered the Saint Louis Art Museum in 2007 and shows the late thickening of the paint into broad, almost tapestry-like surfaces.

A milliner in a green wool dress and long gloves leans across a counter, inspecting a wide-brimmed hat with both hands; the unsold stock crowds the foreground. Degas reworked the canvas between 1879 and 1886; x-rays show he reduced the trim and ornament until the figure's class, customer or worker, became deliberately unreadable. The painting entered the Art Institute of Chicago in 1933.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-the-orc: Degas looks into the orchestra pit of the Paris Opera, where the bassoonist Desire Dihau, a friend of the painter, dominates the foreground among portrait heads of fellow musicians, while the stage above is reduced to a frieze of cropped dancers' legs and glowing tutus. Painted around 1870, the oil on canvas now hangs in the Musee d'Orsay. Its abrupt cropping and off-axis viewpoint anticipate the compositional devices of the ballet pictures Degas pursued over the following two decades.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-the-tub: A nude woman stands in a shallow metal tub, bending forward as she sponges the bath, her body modelled in chalky strokes against a blue-grey ground. Degas exhibited the 1886 pastel with the rest of his bather suite at the Eighth and final Impressionist Exhibition that year, drawing critics' attacks on the bluntness of the poses.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-ukraini: A group of dancers in embroidered Ukrainian costume swing forward in a circle, ribbons and flowered headdresses caught mid-step. Degas worked the pastel around 1899 from a touring folk troupe seen in Paris; the sheet is held by the National Gallery, London, which acquired it from the Burrell bequest by exchange in 2020.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-degas-waiting: On a bench at the Paris Opera, a young dancer in a tutu bends to clasp her ankle beside a woman in black street clothes with a furled umbrella, presumably her mother or chaperone, who stares at the floor. Degas drew the pastel around 1882, setting the silent pair against steeply raked floorboards seen from above. Since 1983 the sheet has been owned jointly by the Norton Simon Art Foundation in Pasadena and the J. Paul Getty Museum.
collection-of-beauty-edgar-germain-hilai: Dancers warming up in the rehearsal room, observed from a raked corner viewpoint that pushes the orchestra rail into the foreground. Degas favoured these unguarded moments of preparation over performance, where artificial light, pastel-keyed tones and oblique geometry could be studied at leisure.

Dancers in white tutus rehearse on a sparsely set stage while the ballet master gestures from the right and men in dark coats - the subscribers admitted backstage - watch from chairs at the wings. Executed around 1874 in pastel over a brush-and-ink drawing on paper, the sheet exploits the steep downward view from a stage box, pushing the floor up against the picture plane in a manner Degas absorbed in part from Japanese prints. One of three closely related versions of the composition, it belongs to the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.

A seated woman leans her head sideways under the hands of a maid who draws a comb through her loose red hair. Degas treated the same gesture in pastel and oil through the mid-1880s, an extension of his suite of women at their toilette exhibited at the Eighth Impressionist Exhibition in 1886.

A nude woman raises both arms to gather her long red hair, seated on the edge of a chair with a white cloth across her thigh. Degas worked the composition in pastel on cardboard around 1885; the Hermitage holds the earliest version of the motif, which he reworked in subsequent variants now in the Metropolitan Museum.

A nude crouches in a shallow zinc tub sponging her neck, beside a marble-topped washstand whose pitcher and brushes are seen from a sharply tilted angle. Degas drew the pastel on heavy wove paper in 1886 and showed it at the Eighth Impressionist Exhibition that May; the sheet entered the Musee d'Orsay as one of his most accomplished bather compositions.

A café-concert singer leans forward at the footlights, her gloved hands shaped like a dog's paws as she performs the popular novelty song known as the Chanson du chien. Worked up between 1875 and 1877 in gouache and pastel over a monotype base, the sheet belongs to a group of small night-life scenes Degas made of the open-air café-concerts along the Champs-Élysées.

A kneeling nude leans forward over a basin, the broad back and braided hair drawn in chalky pastel against an unfinished ground. Degas made the sheet around 1884 as part of the suite of bathers exhibited at the Eighth and final Impressionist Exhibition in 1886, where the ungainly poses drew sharp criticism.

The mixed-race acrobat Anna Olga Albertina Brown, billed as Miss La La, hangs by her teeth from a rope below the Cirque Fernando's painted dome. Degas attended several performances in January 1879 and produced sketches and an oil study before this canvas, his only circus subject, went on view at the Fourth Impressionist Exhibition.

A bather kneels at the edge of a shallow tub, her back to the viewer as a maid in dark cloth steps forward with a towel. Degas worked the late pastel in 1898 on tracing paper laid down on board, building up the chalk in layered hatchings characteristic of his bathing series.

A ballerina holds a low curtsy at the front of the stage, bouquet in hand, the corps blurred behind her in the footlight haze. Degas returned obsessively to such after-performance moments around 1878, drawn to the gap between drilled spectacle and momentary stillness.

Four ballerinas in pale blue tutus stand backstage adjusting their costumes and bodices, their faces averted from the viewer. Degas worked the subject of dancers at rest from the 1870s onward; this canvas, traditionally dated to the late nineteenth century, hangs in the Pushkin Museum in Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-edge-of-the-forest-: A line of dark trees marks the boundary between a sunlit meadow and an unseen interior of woods, a single small figure crossing toward them. Painted in 1891 and held at the Yale University Art Gallery, the canvas belongs to Inness's late Montclair landscapes, where structure dissolves into broad zones of tone.
collection-of-beauty-edinburgh-ngs-singe: Gertrude, Lady Agnew of Lochnaw lounges in a bergère, her white satin gown and lilac sash dashed in with bravura wet-into-wet brushwork. The portrait's frank gaze and easy elegance made Sargent's reputation when shown at the Royal Academy in 1893.
collection-of-beauty-edmund-blair-leight: The medieval philosopher tutoring his young pupil in a richly furnished Parisian interior, the doomed pair already absorbed in one another. Blair Leighton — not the Frederic Leighton credited here — favoured this kind of fastidiously costumed romantic-historical anecdote.

A family taking refuge in a fortified chamber as conflict rages outside, painted in Blair Leighton's polished late-Victorian historical idiom. Stained-glass light, careful armour detail and a contained narrative tension are the artist's stock in trade.

A young woman leaning over a garden wall to chat with the unseen occupant beyond, a typical genre-romance vignette of late-Victorian England. Blair Leighton sets up the gentle social comedy with crisp drawing and a sunlit, almost photographic clarity of detail.

A pretty girl shopping for trimmings at an Old-English haberdasher's stall, the title quoting a popular street-cry. Blair Leighton's love of period costume drama and finely modelled drapery gives the trivial subject the weight of a small historical tableau.

A medieval lady offering or receiving a token of devotion in a candlelit chapel-like interior. Long known only through a 1908 photogravure, the picture is a classic exercise in Blair Leighton's chivalric romanticism, with meticulously rendered velvets and enamels.

A pair of lovers stealing away by torchlight through a Tudor courtyard, the woman lifting her brocade skirts as her companion checks the way ahead. Blair Leighton wraps the runaway plot in crisp costume detail and stage-managed late-Victorian sentiment.

A lutenist seated at a courtly lady's feet as the last chord fades, an invented scene that nods to Tristan and Iseult and Paolo and Francesca without illustrating either. Blair Leighton uses the lull after music to suggest dangerous feeling held in check.

A noblewoman delivered up as surety in a medieval baron's hall, her isolation underscored by the encircling knights and heavy stonework. The picture is one of Blair Leighton's late chivalric tableaux, painted with the costume-drama precision that kept his Royal Academy audience loyal.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-031: On the terrace of a fashionable suburban restaurant, the proprietor's son leans intimately toward a lady lunching alone. Painted en plein air during Manet's late embrace of Impressionist technique, the canvas glows with dappled sunlight and feathery, summery greens.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-at-th: Patrons crowded along the marble counter of a Parisian brasserie, observed with the cool detachment Manet brought to modern social life. Sketchy contours, a high horizon and the cropped figures at the edges signal his late, increasingly Impressionist-inflected handling.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-boati: A boater in straw hat and crisp whites holds the tiller while his companion lounges in the prow against a wall of saturated blue water. The radically cropped composition and high horizon reveal Manet's debt to Japanese prints and his summer at Argenteuil with Monet.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-by-he: Manet stands three-quarter length in dark coat and top hat, gloves and cane in hand, framed against an austere studio ground. Fantin-Latour's portrait, the basis for his role in the group canvas Hommage à Manet, presents the Impressionist forerunner with the dandified self-possession his contemporaries described.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-der-f: A bouquet of white lilacs leans from a clear glass vase against a darkened ground, the flowers worked in loaded, gestural strokes. The picture belongs to the small floral still lifes Manet painted at the very end of his life, when illness had reduced his ambitions to flowers brought by visitors.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-kears: The Confederate raider Alabama lists and burns under fire from the Union sloop Kearsarge off Cherbourg, smoke staining a blue Channel sea.
