Manet, who was reportedly close enough to watch French pilot boats return from the engagement, treats this American Civil War moment with a high horizon and broadly brushed water that anticipates marine Impressionism.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-le-ch: Victorine Meurent, in dark blue with a sleeping puppy in her lap and an open book, sits before the iron railings above the cutting of the Gare Saint-Lazare; beside her, a child in white watches a passing train betrayed only by its cloud of steam. Exhibited at the Salon of 1874 and now at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the picture was Manet's last of his favourite model.

Two angels support the slumped body of the dead Christ, his pallid torso lit against shadow. Manet borrows a traditional Lamentation type but flattens modeling and exposes brushwork in a way that scandalized the 1864 Salon, where critics also faulted the placement of the side wound on the wrong flank.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-olymp: A reclining nude courtesan meets the viewer's gaze with cool defiance, attended by a Black maid bearing flowers from a client. Manet flattens form with stark lighting and sharp tonal contrasts, scandalising the 1865 Salon by transposing Titian's Venus into contemporary Parisian demi-monde.
collection-of-beauty-edouard-manet-the-p: A young woman sits alone at a café table, an unlit cigarette between her fingers and a brandy-soaked plum before her. Manet captures the suspended boredom of modern Parisian leisure with loose brushwork and a muted palette of pinks, creams and pale lilacs.
collection-of-beauty-eduard-gaertner-ans: The crowded rear façades of the middle-class houses lining the Schloßfreiheit drop straight to the Spree, washing visible from upper windows. Gaertner recorded the row in 1855; in 1896 the entire street was demolished to clear the site for the Wilhelmine Monument to Emperor Wilhelm I.
collection-of-beauty-eduard-gaertner-ber: The Brüderstraße on the Spreeinsel in Berlin-Mitte recedes between rows of plastered townhouses toward the tower of the Petrikirche. Gaertner painted the view in 1863, still working in the precise Berlin Biedermeier vedute mode he had practised since the 1820s.

Schinkel's strict new façade for the Gewerbeinstitut faces the baroque Kreutzsche Palais across the Klosterstraße, with the tower of the Parochialkirche rising behind. Gaertner painted himself into the centre of the street greeting the painter Franz Krüger on horseback; the 1830 oil belongs to the Alte Nationalgalerie in Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-eduard-gaertner-die: A narrow Berlin street viewed from the entrance to Klosterstraße, with a coppersmith displaying his wares, women gossiping at an inn and the tower of the Nikolaikirche rising at the far end. Painted by Gaertner in 1831; one version of the composition belongs to the Metropolitan Museum, another to the Nationalgalerie in Berlin.
collection-of-beauty-eduard-gaertner-unt: Berlin's grand boulevard stretches past the equestrian statue of Frederick the Great, with the Königliche Oper on the right and the dome of the Stadtschloss closing the vista. Gaertner, the city's pre-eminent vedutista, charts the Prussian capital with architect's precision under a clear summer light.
collection-of-beauty-eduard-gartner-002: Another panel from the 1834 panorama, with the dome of the Französischer Dom and the colonnade of Schinkel's Schauspielhaus at Gendarmenmarkt rising above pitched tile roofs. Gaertner painted his six-part survey on the roof of the Friedrichswerdersche Kirche almost every day of that summer.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-1893-t: A skeletal figure clutches its head beneath a blood-red sky on a fjord-side bridge, mouth agape in soundless anguish. Munch combined oil, tempera and pastel on cardboard to externalise an attack of existential dread, anchoring the visual vocabulary of European Expressionism.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-1922-s: Painted from the terrace of Munch's Ekely estate outside Oslo, this nocturne reduces landscape to broad zones of indigo, snow-white and shadow. A revisitation of his 1893 motif, it trades earlier symbolism for a quieter, late-career meditation on solitude under the winter sky.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-bathin: Three nude men stride from the surf in a frieze-like composition, painted on the German island of Warnemünde. Munch celebrated sun, sea and male vigour with vehement verticals of brushwork, part of a triptych on the ages of man now in Helsinki's Ateneum.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-jealou: A bearded man stares from the foreground in green-tinged pallor while behind him a woman in red plucks fruit beside another suitor. Munch returned to the jealousy motif repeatedly, treating it as a Garden-of-Eden parable charged with autobiographical anxiety.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-the-br: The English violinist Eva Mudocci, with whom Munch had a brief affair, gazes from a cloud of dark hair in this lithograph. Drawn directly onto stone in Berlin and printed in soft black, it is among Munch's most tender portraits, sometimes called his Mona Lisa.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-train-: A coastal landscape pierced by the white plume of a passing locomotive, its trail snaking across a russet shoreline. Munch cropped the scene around the rhythm of the smoke itself, turning industrial intrusion into a curling, almost serpentine compositional device.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-two-hu: A man and woman stand side by side on a stony shore, facing the sea but never one another. Munch returned to this image of unbridgeable distance for decades in paintings and woodcuts, here rendered in blunt blocks of beach grey, surf white and brooding water.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-vampir: A red-haired woman bends over a man, her lips at his neck while her hair cascades like flowing blood. Originally titled Love and Pain, the picture was rechristened by Munch's Symbolist circle and became a key motif of his Frieze of Life.
collection-of-beauty-edvard-munch-weepin: A naked woman sits on the edge of a bed, head bowed into her hands, the room dissolving in nervous strokes around her. Munch left the figure raw and unidealised, channelling psychological collapse through agitated brushwork rather than narrative detail.
collection-of-beauty-edward-hicks-americ: Pairs of lions, leopards, horses, oxen, and waterfowl plod up the gangplank into Noah's ark under a darkening sky, with the floodwaters already rising on the horizon. Hicks, a Quaker minister and self-taught sign-painter from Bucks County, Pennsylvania, adapted the composition from an 1844 Currier lithograph.
collection-of-beauty-edward-hicks-painti: The elder Edward Hicks at his easel, brush poised over a version of his Peaceable Kingdom showing the lion, ox and child of Isaiah's prophecy. Thomas Hicks, Edward's younger cousin, painted the homage in 1839 when Edward was fifty-nine; the canvas entered the National Portrait Gallery in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-edward-hicks-peacea: A lion lies beside a lamb, a leopard with a kid, and a child rests his hand on the leopard's neck, while in the left background William Penn signs his 1681 treaty with the Lenape on the Delaware. Hicks, a Quaker minister and sign painter, made roughly a hundred versions of the Isaiah 11 prophecy as an emblem of Pennsylvania's promise.
collection-of-beauty-edward-hicks-the-co: A panoramic view of James C. Cornell's prize Northampton, Pennsylvania farmstead, with rows of livestock paraded in the foreground and white outbuildings stretching to the horizon. Hicks painted the canvas in 1848 to commemorate Cornell's prizes at the Bucks County agricultural fair; it entered the National Gallery of Art in Washington in 1964.
collection-of-beauty-edward-hopper-night: An anonymous pedestrian crosses an empty street under a sharply raking street lamp, watched from a high, vertiginous viewpoint. The etching, published in Shadowland magazine, sets out the lonely urban geometry Hopper would later expand into his great oil paintings.
collection-of-beauty-edward-savage-georg: Washington stands in dark civilian dress beside a draped table, his right hand resting on a document. Savage based the National Gallery's circa 1796 portrait on his own life studies of the president, made during sittings in New York in 1789-90 that also fed his print The Washington Family.
collection-of-beauty-edward-savage-the-w: George Washington, Martha, and her two grandchildren stand around a draped table on the Mount Vernon terrace, a map of the new federal city of Washington spread before them. Savage worked on the group portrait between 1789 and 1796 and engraved a popular print after it; the canvas is now at the National Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-el-beso-pinacoteca-: A young couple embrace on a stone staircase, the woman's blue gown and the man's red tights forming the colours of the French and Italian flags. Hayez's most popular canvas became a coded emblem of the Risorgimento and the alliance behind Italian unification.
collection-of-beauty-el-caballero-de-la-: A bearded Castilian gentleman in black silk lays his right hand against his chest, the fingers splayed in a deliberate gesture above the gold hilt of his sword. Painted around 1580 and now in the Prado, the portrait is often read as an oath of loyalty and counts among the most reproduced images of the Spanish Golden Age.
collection-of-beauty-el-coloso: A naked giant rises behind a mountain ridge as a panicked crowd and herds flee across the plain below. Long attributed to Goya and tied to the Peninsular War, the picture stages collective terror with the bituminous darkness of his late, troubled imagination.
collection-of-beauty-el-dos-de-mayo-de-1: Madrileños with knives drag Mamluk cavalrymen of the imperial guard from their rearing horses in the Puerta del Sol. Companion to The Third of May, Goya's painting reconstructs the chaos of the popular uprising against Napoleon's occupation in tumbling diagonals.
collection-of-beauty-el-expolio-por-el-g: Christ in a vivid red robe stands hemmed in by jeering soldiers as a workman bores holes for the nails in the cross at his feet. Painted between 1577 and 1579 for the sacristy of Toledo Cathedral, El Greco's first major Spanish commission compresses the crowd into a vertical wall of heads behind the still, gazing figure.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-christ-as-: Christ raises his hand in benediction above a crystalline globe, his pale features elongated against a stormy sky. The panel belongs to El Greco's Apostolado series in Toledo, where the saviour heads a cycle of the twelve apostles in the artist's signature steel-grey palette.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-domenikos-: Christ swings his cord of whips through the money-changers in a vaulted Renaissance temple, figures recoiling around him in pinks, blues, and acid greens. Painted probably before 1570 during El Greco's Venetian apprenticeship and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the panel is the earliest of his several versions of the subject.

The Trinitarian preacher Hortensio Félix Paravicino sits leaning forward in his black and white habit, a book held shut on his lap. Painted in 1609 and now in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, the portrait depicts the court preacher to Philip III, who returned the favour with four sonnets celebrating El Greco at his death.

The Toledan canon and historian Dr. Francisco de Pisa sits in clerical black with a book on his lap, the hands long and bony in El Greco's late manner. Painted between 1610 and 1614 and now in the Kimbell Art Museum, the portrait records the cleric whose 1605 Descripción de la imperial ciudad de Toledo remains a key source for the city's history.

Jerome appears as a half-length scholar in red cardinal's robes, his white beard cascading over an open book on the desk. Signed in Greek and dated around 1610, the panel at the Hispanic Society of America in New York is one of several variants El Greco produced of this 'Saint Jerome as Cardinal' formula for Toledan patrons.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-portrait-o: A grey-bearded man in a high white ruff turns his head toward the viewer, the eyes set into deep, lined sockets. Painted between 1595 and 1600 and now in the Metropolitan Museum, the panel is generally taken to be a self-portrait, the only securely identified likeness El Greco made of himself.

A young man in a starched white ruff and dark doublet holds the brushes and palette of a painter, his gaze level and composed. Painted between 1600 and 1605, the portrait shows Jorge Manuel Theotocópuli, El Greco's son and workshop heir, who would later complete several of the master's late altarpieces in Toledo.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-the-burial: Saints Stephen and Augustine lower the armoured body of Don Gonzalo Ruiz de Toledo into his tomb while a celestial throng receives his soul above. Painted between 1586 and 1588 for the parish church of Santo Tomé in Toledo, where it still hangs over the count's actual grave, the canvas splits earthly funeral and heavenly vision across a single vertical axis.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-the-vision: Saint John throws up his arms beneath a torn sky as nude figures rise to receive the white robes of the martyrs at the opening of the fifth seal. Painted between 1608 and 1614 for the chapel of San Juan Bautista outside Toledo and now at the Met, the fragmentary canvas was an acknowledged source for Picasso's Demoiselles d'Avignon.
collection-of-beauty-el-greco-view-of-to: A spectral storm rolls over the Spanish hill city, with the Alcázar and cathedral picked out against acid-green hills and ink-black clouds. One of the earliest pure landscapes in Western art, El Greco rearranged Toledo's topography for symbolic, almost visionary effect.
collection-of-beauty-el-jaleo-singer: A near life-size scene of a flamenco dancer mid-stride before a row of seated musicians, lit by raking footlights that cast huge shadows on the back wall. Sargent worked the picture up from sketches made in Spain, marrying Velázquez's tonal economy to a thoroughly modern sense of theatrical staging.
collection-of-beauty-el-jardin-de-las-de: Bosch's triptych unfolds from the Garden of Eden through a teeming central panel of nude pleasure-seekers to a hellscape of musical instruments turned instruments of torture. Painted for a Habsburg patron, its inventory of fantastical hybrids has resisted definitive iconographic decoding for five centuries.
collection-of-beauty-el-jardin-del-amor-: Elegant couples flirt and recline in a balustraded garden while putti scatter roses overhead. Painted soon after Rubens's marriage to Helena Fourment, the scene celebrates conjugal pleasure in his late, pearly Flemish manner and now hangs in the Prado.
collection-of-beauty-el-tres-de-mayo-by-: A Spanish patriot in a luminous white shirt flings out his arms before the firing squad of Napoleonic troops on Príncipe Pío hill. Commissioned after the French withdrawal, Goya treats martyrdom with the brutal lighting and crude paint of modern history painting.
collection-of-beauty-elisabeth-louise-vi: Painted during Vigée Le Brun's émigré years in Saint Petersburg, the Russian countess wears a soft white gown and a velvet wrap. The artist's Russian sitters helped sustain her career through the Revolution and account for many of her finest late portraits.

The painter of picturesque ruins, Hubert Robert, is shown half-length in painter's smock, palette in hand, his unruly hair and quick-eyed glance conveying improvisatory energy. Vigée Le Brun's portrait of her colleague is a touchstone of late Ancien Régime artistic friendship, executed shortly before the Revolution dispersed both sitter and painter.

A half-length portrait of the marine painter Joseph Vernet, palette and brushes in hand, in a powdered wig and dark coat against a neutral ground. Vigée Le Brun renders the older painter with the soft modeling and warm flesh tones that defined her late-Ancien Régime studio practice, treating him as a colleague rather than a patron.

The actress of the Comédie-Italienne turns toward the viewer in a fur-trimmed coat and broad black hat, a muff held loosely at her side. Vigée Le Brun catches the sitter mid-movement with a fresh, animated brushwork that announces the informal, theatrical portraiture of the late ancien régime.

The young duchesse sits in a relaxed pose, an open book in her lap and her powdered hair tumbling in fashionable disarray. Vigée Le Brun, official portraitist to Marie-Antoinette, favoured this informality of dress as a calculated marker of natural sensibility.

A double portrait set out of doors, the Marquise de Pezay seated beside the Marquise de Rougé, whose two young sons press in beside her. Painted on the eve of the Revolution, the canvas blends the natural settings and tender maternal grouping that Vigée Le Brun had refined in her portraits of Marie Antoinette and her circle.
collection-of-beauty-elisabeth-vigee-le-: An allegorical pair: Peace, in classical drapery, gently leads forward Abundance, who carries a sheaf of wheat and a cornucopia. The painting was Vigée Le Brun's reception piece for the Académie Royale, accepted in 1783, and shows her combining Neoclassical subject matter with the warm flesh tones and silken finish of her portrait practice.
collection-of-beauty-elisabeth-vigee-leb: Emma Hamilton turns in the studio with a turbaned head and parted lips, posed as the prophetic Sibyl of Cumae. Vigée Le Brun carried the resulting composition through her exile from Naples to Vienna and Russia as a calling card of her Italian period.

Marie-Jeanne Bécu, the former royal mistress of Louis XV, is shown in a relaxed garden setting with loose curls and a simple white gown. The image belongs to a series of informal portraits painted at Louveciennes, exchanging court formality for the pastoral neoclassical mode then fashionable in Paris.

The Russian countess reclines in a white empire-line gown trimmed with gauze, painted during Vigée Le Brun's emigration years among the European aristocracy. The picture's smooth porcelain finish and pearly tonality typify her courtly manner adapted to Saint Petersburg taste.

The Parisian actress Hyacinthe-Gabrielle Roland — mistress and, from 1794, wife of Richard Wellesley, Earl of Mornington, which later made her Marchioness Wellesley — sits informally with loosened, ribboned hair against a stormy sky. Vigée Le Brun painted her in Rome in 1791, during the Italian years of her emigration from revolutionary France; the portrait now hangs in the Legion of Honor, Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco.

Emma Hart, later Lady Hamilton, sits in three-quarter view with cascading dark hair and an open shawl, her gaze turned outward. The portrait reflects Vigée Le Brun's Italian period and her interest in the antique 'attitudes' for which Hamilton was already celebrated in Naples.

Vigée Le Brun cradles her daughter Julie in a tender embrace, both turning their bare-armed warmth to the viewer. Exhibited at the 1787 Salon, the canvas adapted antique Madonna types to revolutionary tastes for sentiment and natural maternal feeling.
collection-of-beauty-elizabeth-vigee-leb: Tipu Sultan's ambassador to the court of Louis XVI stands full-length in robes of patterned silk, hand resting on a sabre. Painted in Paris in 1788 on the eve of revolution, the work remained in the artist's possession for fifty years as a record of her cosmopolitan clientele.
collection-of-beauty-emmanuel-joseph-sie: The abbé Sieyès, theorist of the Third Estate and architect of the Brumaire coup that brought Napoleon to power, sits in dark coat against a plain ground. David painted the portrait in Brussels, where both artist and sitter were exiled after the Bourbon Restoration of 1815.
collection-of-beauty-enbu-by-hayami-gyos: Black-winged moths spiral upward through tongues of flame, set against a ground of deep ink. Hayami fused traditional nihonga pigments with the decorative geometry of Rinpa, producing an emblem of Taishō-era modernism now held in the Yamatane Museum.
collection-of-beauty-enoshima-in-the-sag: The tidal causeway to the sacred island of Enoshima opens before pilgrims as Mount Fuji rises in the distance. From Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the print exploits imported Prussian blue and the bold diagonal of the sandbar to organise its broad sea view.
collection-of-beauty-enrique-viii-de-ing: Henry VIII appears half-length in a black slashed doublet and jewelled collar, a glove gripped in his right hand. Dated 1540, the panel hangs in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica at Palazzo Barberini in Rome, one of the autograph small-scale Tudor likenesses Holbein produced for diplomatic circulation.
collection-of-beauty-entree-d-alexandre-: Alexander the Great rides into Babylon in a triumphal chariot drawn by white elephants, the city's defeated populace strewing the path with gold and burning incense before him. Painted between 1664 and 1665 as part of the Alexander cycle for Louis XIV, the canvas hangs in the Louvre and inspired Le Brun's tapestry designs at the Gobelins manufactory.
collection-of-beauty-entree-de-cimetiere: A wrought-iron gate opens onto a hushed graveyard, its crosses and weathered stones receding into mist. Friedrich treats the cemetery as a threshold between visible world and the beyond, his characteristic Romantic meditation on mortality rendered in muted earth tones and silvery atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-epes-sargent-a13818: The Gloucester merchant and shipowner leans nonchalantly against a marble pedestal, his weathered hand resting flat on the stone. Copley, only about twenty-two when he signed the canvas around 1760, borrowed the pedestal from European print sources because carved monuments were rare in the American colonies; the portrait now hangs in the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-erasistratus-the-ph: The court physician Erasistratus takes the pulse of the lovesick prince Antiochus as his stepmother Stratonice enters the chamber, revealing the cause of his illness. West painted the Hellenistic anecdote, drawn from Plutarch, in 1772. The canvas is in the Birmingham Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-erasmus-quellinus-i: Cupid lies sprawled in slumber, bow and quiver set aside, his pearly flesh modelled in the warm glazes Rubens favoured for putti and infants. The motif of disarmed love invites the viewer to contemplate desire's vulnerability when stilled.

Quellinus, a close collaborator of Rubens in Antwerp, retells Ovid's myth of Jupiter abducting the Phoenician princess in the guise of a white bull. The composition pairs Flemish Baroque drama with the polished classicism Quellinus absorbed during his Roman training.
collection-of-beauty-ernst-ludwig-kirchn: Three figures draw bows in a darkened landscape, the foremost woman holding arrows in her hand. Painted in oil between 1935 and 1937 at the Wildboden farm near Davos, the canvas belongs to Kirchner's final phase; he wrote to Carl Hagemann that the large shadowed areas were a new discovery, intended to make the picture 'calm and monumental.'

Doris Große sits in a stiff white pleated ruff, her face turned slightly aside in a pose borrowed from old-master portraiture. The model, whom Kirchner nicknamed Dodo, was his lover and principal sitter from around 1904 until 1911; the circa-1906 canvas entered the Thyssen-Bornemisza collection in 1961 as one of the Baron's first modern acquisitions.

A woman sits with her back to the viewer, the volumes of shoulder and hip cut into broad black slabs. Kirchner produced the woodcut in 1908, printed on blotting paper at roughly 19 by 15 inches, while consolidating the rough-hewn vocabulary of the Brücke group around the studio at Dresden. The impression is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

A soldier and a young woman stand in a wooded clearing under a rising moon, the figures pressed close in the half-light. Painted in 1905 during Kirchner's Dresden student years, the canvas entered the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston as accession number 98.286.

Trams curve around the Berlin square of Nollendorfplatz under a steep, tipped-up perspective, with hurrying figures pressed against the kerb. Kirchner began his Berlin street pictures shortly after the Brücke group relocated from Dresden; the canvas is now held by Stiftung Stadtmuseum Berlin.

The Sertig valley in the Swiss Alps, with steep slopes in autumn ochre and red flanking a narrow flat floor below jagged peaks. Painted on 20 April 1920 from his home above Davos, the canvas belongs to the alpine work Kirchner produced after his wartime nervous collapse, the angular Expressionist vocabulary of the Brücke years cooled by mountain geometry.

Figures wrestle and tumble naked beneath a tree, limbs flattened into broad colour planes of pink, blue and acid green. Painted in 1910 at 77 by 89 cm, the canvas grew out of the Brücke summers at the Moritzburg lakes and now hangs in the Pinakothek der Moderne, Munich.
collection-of-beauty-escola-de-atenas-va: Painted for Pope Julius II's private library in the Stanza della Segnatura, this fresco assembles the philosophers of antiquity beneath a vast coffered vault, with Plato and Aristotle striding through the central arch. Raphael's lucid one-point perspective and idealised figures became a touchstone of High Renaissance harmony.
collection-of-beauty-espagnole-et-agneau: A Spanish woman's face is overlaid with the lamb and other contour images in superimposed line. Made in 1928, the work belongs to Picabia's Transparencies series, begun the previous year, in which he alternated paint with resinous varnish so that motifs drawn from Renaissance frescoes, Catalan murals and popular sources could coexist without fully merging.
collection-of-beauty-etretat-george-inne: The Normandy cliffs and one of the three great natural arches at Étretat rise above a tidal beach where small fires of burning kelp send up white plumes of smoke. Painted by Inness during his European travels of the early 1870s, the canvas is in the Wadsworth Atheneum in Hartford and belongs to his panoramic, atmospheric phase before the late Swedenborgian landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-eugen-de-blaas-the-: Two young Venetians exchange glances across a sunlit doorway, the woman's costume crisp with embroidered linen and a flowered shawl. De Blaas built his career on such genre scenes of working Venice, prized in Edwardian salons for their sparkling finish and gentle theatrics.
collection-of-beauty-eugen-von-blaas-bil: A formal portrait of Arthur Graf Berchtold, a Hungarian magnate and member of the Imperial Diet, posed with the upright bearing of a statesman. De Blaas, better known for genre scenes, here demonstrates his society-portrait register with crisp tailoring and a sober palette.
collection-of-beauty-eugen-von-blaas-der: A young woman lifts a vivid red fan to half-shield her smile, the single warm accent ignites the otherwise restrained tonal harmony. De Blaas exploits such props to focus attention and showcase his command of silk, lace, and the answering blush of skin.
collection-of-beauty-eugen-von-blaas-pla: Two women lean together over a parapet in animated chatter, the title's German for 'small talk' framing the scene as anecdote rather than narrative. De Blaas relishes the textile detail, from the patterned shawl to the starched apron, in his typical lustrous, salon-ready finish.
collection-of-beauty-eugen-von-blaas-sha: A cluster of Venetian women pause from their chores to read aloud from a letter, faces tilted in shared attention. De Blaas mines the city's working-class courtyards for these intimate everyday vignettes, polished with the slick academic technique that earned him Belle Epoque popularity.
collection-of-beauty-eugen-von-blaas-the: A young woman spins thread while a smiling suitor leans in, the title borrowed from Mary Howitt's cautionary verse turning the courtship scene into sly allegory. De Blaas modelled such tableaux on Venetian working girls he knew from his studio quarter near the Zattere.
collection-of-beauty-eugen-von-blaas-two: Two figures stand framed by a worn brick wall, one balancing a copper water vessel, the other looking out beneath a lace-edged kerchief. The painting belongs to de Blaas's prolific Venetian street type, where ethnographic observation meets the polish of academic Salon painting.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-de-blaas-a-p: A solitary young woman pauses at a stone window, chin propped in hand, eyes turned inward. De Blaas reduces his usual courtyard chatter to a single note of quiet introspection, the polished academic finish lending the everyday subject a hint of portrait gravity.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-de-blaas-cur: Two young women lean in conspiratorially, one whispering while the other listens with an expression caught between amusement and disbelief. The intimate framing and high finish are typical of de Blaas's Venetian genre painting, in which gossip itself becomes the subject.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-de-blaas-day: A young Venetian girl rests on the lagoon's edge, her gaze drifting beyond the picture plane while sunlight catches her loose hair and starched blouse. De Blaas pairs his trademark textile precision with a softer, more reflective mood than his lively flirtation scenes.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix: A self-portrait from the artist's late thirties, the painter facing the viewer with steady, somewhat melancholy eyes and a black coat that dissolves into shadow. Delacroix here adopts the sober, unidealised register of seventeenth-century Dutch self-portraiture rather than Romantic flourish.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix-a-: A bandit, slumped in a rocky landscape, drinks from a stream as his life ebbs away, the body twisted in a pose that recalls Delacroix's study of Géricault. The picture distils the young Romantic's taste for outsiders, suffering, and Byronic violence into a single charged moment.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix-ch: Christ asleep in the stern while his disciples haul at the sail and oars of a fishing boat pitched almost vertical by a green wave on the Sea of Galilee. Delacroix returned to the Gospel storm at least six times during his late career; this oil sketch is in the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art in Kansas City.

Christ sleeps in the stern of a fishing boat while terrified apostles wrestle the sail against a green wall of water. Delacroix returned to the Gospel subject repeatedly in the 1850s, each version intensifying the chromatic clash between the storm and the calm figure asleep in its centre.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix-co: Delacroix drew on his 1832 North African journey with Count de Mornay's diplomatic mission to evoke the violent equestrian games of the Moroccan court. The clashing horses and flying robes display the saturated, almost vibrating palette he developed after seeing Maghreb light at first hand.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix-fr: Chopin in three-quarter view, lips parted, eyes lifted, his head silhouetted against a brown ground. Delacroix painted the composer in 1838 as part of a double portrait with George Sand sewing beside the piano; the unfinished canvas was cut in two after the artist's death and the Chopin fragment entered the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix-le: A Natchez couple cradles their newborn on the banks of the Mississippi, fugitives from a colonial massacre, after Chateaubriand's 1801 novel 'Atala'. Delacroix turns the literary source into a sombre meditation on indigenous extinction, exhibited at the Salon of 1835 and now in the Metropolitan Museum.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix-ov: The exiled Roman poet Ovid reclines on the grass of the Black Sea steppe, offered milk and bread by Scythian herdsmen while their horses graze in the background. Delacroix exhibited a smaller version at the 1859 Salon and returned to the subject in 1862, the year before his death; the painting is now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix-ri: A jaguar springs from a thicket onto the haunches of a rearing horse, its rider thrown back as the predator's claws sink into the animal's flank. Delacroix borrowed the motif from Rubens and the Stubbs lion-and-horse tradition, condensing the struggle into a tight vertical of intersecting muscle.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix-sh: A small craft is overwhelmed by churning surf beneath a leaden sky, figures barely visible amid the spray. The late Delacroix returns again to the shipwreck motif as an emblem of human helplessness before nature, treated with a freer, almost atmospheric brush.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix-st: A scarlet lobster, brace of pheasants, hare and tartan game bag arranged on a grassy bank, with red-coated fox hunters galloping across the distant landscape. Painted in 1826-27 for the Napoleonic general Count de Coëtlosquet, the picture was shown at the Salon of 1827 alongside the Death of Sardanapalus and entered the Louvre in 1906.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-delacroix-th: Ophelia clings to a willow branch as it splits above the brook, her white shift catching on the bark while her wreath of flowers drifts away. Delacroix's first version of the subject, drawn from Gertrude's speech in Act IV of Hamlet, was painted in 1838 and is now in the Neue Pinakothek in Munich.

The Assyrian king Sardanapalus reclining on his bed as his slaves, horses and treasures are destroyed at his command, a writhing mass of bodies in red and gold. Oil on canvas, about 3.9 by 5 metres, in the Louvre, Paris, shown at the Salon of 1827. The subject derives from Byron's verse drama, and the picture drew sharp criticism for its turbulent composition.

Victorious Central Asian troops stand among severed heads and abandoned weapons after the action, the celebration unsettling rather than triumphant. Paired with 'After a failure', the picture insists that battlefield outcomes share a single moral landscape of slaughter.

Delacroix records the ecstatic Aissaoua brotherhood spilling through the streets of Tangier, a procession he had witnessed during his 1832 Moroccan trip. The swirling crowd and sun-bleached architecture exemplify his lifelong fascination with North African religious spectacle.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-ferdinand-vi: A North African rider tightens the girth of his white horse against a backdrop of rocky terrain and pale sky. Drawing on sketches made during his 1832 mission to Morocco with the Comte de Mornay, Delacroix returned for decades to the Arab horseman as a Romantic exemplar of dignified physical action.
collection-of-beauty-eugene-murer-hyacin: The pastry cook and collector Eugène Murer, born Hyacinthe-Eugène Meunier, shown bust-length in a dark coat. Renoir painted the portrait in 1877; Murer eventually gathered some 122 Impressionist works, including fifteen by Renoir, and the canvas is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-evening-landscape-a: A reaped wheat field with stacked sheaves lies under a swollen orange moon rising from behind the hills of the Alpilles. Van Gogh painted the canvas, also known as Landscape with Wheat Sheaves and Rising Moon, in the summer of 1889, working from the walled field he could see from his room at the asylum of Saint-Paul-de-Mausole in Saint-Rémy. It is held by the Kröller-Müller Museum in Otterlo.
collection-of-beauty-evening-snow-at-ter: A lone figure trudges past snow-laden trees and a thatched cottage as dusk settles over the rural outskirts of Tokyo. Hasui's shin-hanga woodblock combines Western perspective and atmosphere with the layered ink and pigment registration of the traditional Japanese print.
collection-of-beauty-faded-laurels-by-ed: An elderly soldier sits among trophies of past campaigns, his laurels withered and his armour relegated to memento. Edmund Blair Leighton, working in late-Victorian academic style, treats the chivalric subject with antiquarian precision and the warm anecdotal sentiment of the high Salon.
collection-of-beauty-famille-de-paysans-: A peasant family pauses around a sparse table in a dim cottage interior, each face turned outwards with quiet directness. The Le Nain brothers' rare empathetic treatment of rural poverty, painted in a sober earthen palette, anticipates the realism of Courbet two centuries later.
collection-of-beauty-fantomas-juan-gris: A Synthetic Cubist still life of pipe, newspaper and glass, with the words FANTOMAS and LE JOURNAL legible across the fragmented planes. Painted in 1915 and held in the Chester Dale Collection at the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the title cites the popular pulp anti-hero of Souvestre and Allain's serial novels.
collection-of-beauty-felicien-rops-porno: A blindfolded woman in stockings is led by a pig over a frieze of allegorical figures, while putti tumble overhead. Rops's notorious Symbolist etching, executed on coloured ground, indicts bourgeois hypocrisy by personifying carnal power as a queen guided by base instinct.
collection-of-beauty-female-nude-with-fo: A standing female nude is dappled by the shadows of overhanging leaves, the figure modelled in loose strokes on a rough ground. Painted in oil on cardboard in 1905, the early canvas now in the Kirchner Museum Davos predates the formal founding of Die Brücke later that year in Dresden.
collection-of-beauty-femenine-wave: A graceful, curling wave breaks in undulating tendrils against a void, conceived as the gentler counterpart to Hokusai's better-known 'Masculine Wave'. The print belongs to the artist's late mature exploration of water as pure pattern, where ukiyo-e line approaches abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-femmes-d-alger-dans: Three women lounge with a servant in a tiled Algerian harem chamber, surrounded by hookah, slippers and richly patterned textiles. Painted after Delacroix gained rare access to a domestic interior in 1832, the Louvre canvas became a foundational source of the nineteenth-century Orientalist imagination.
collection-of-beauty-ferdinand-victor-eu: Two Moroccan grooms drive their horses out of the surf onto a stretch of North African beach, the animals shaking water from their flanks. Painted in 1860, three years before the artist's death, the canvas distils thirty years of Delacroix's Maghreb sketchbooks into a single concentrated motif; now at the Phillips Collection in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-fernand-khnopff013: Khnopff portrays his sister Marguerite, a recurring presence in his work, with the cool, hieratic detachment that defines his Symbolist portraiture. The pale palette and flattened space distil her into an emblem of withdrawn, idealised femininity rather than likeness alone.
collection-of-beauty-fernand-le-quesne-l: Le Quesne pairs two nude figures in an intimate, lamp-lit setting, the title casting their pale skin as twin pearls. Exhibited within the orbit of the 1889 Paris Salon, the picture exemplifies the polished sensuality favoured by mainstream French academic painting at the century's close.
collection-of-beauty-fiesta-campestre: Two clothed musicians and two nude women sit in a wooded clearing near Venice, a shepherd driving his flock past in the middle distance. Long attributed to Giorgione, the Pastoral Concert is now generally given to the young Titian and entered the French royal collection by 1671 before passing to the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-figure-studies-met-: A bearded, heavily draped man stands gesturing on a rise of ground, surrounded by figures who kneel, crouch, and sprawl around him — a sheet of studies for a crowded religious composition. Ricci worked it up in pen and brown ink with gray wash over traces of red and black chalk, letting rapid hatching stand in for landscape. Such fluent study sheets were the working currency of Venetian painters of his generation; this one is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-file-ivan-aivazovsk: A storm breaks over the headland of Cape Sounion on the southern tip of Attica, the ruined columns of the Temple of Poseidon picked out above churning sea. Aivazovsky, court painter to the Russian navy, treated the Aegean coastline as a stage for Romantic seascape rather than archaeological record.
collection-of-beauty-fin-d-arabesque-edg: A solo dancer holds the final pose of an arabesque, her right arm extended with a bouquet, her gaze inclined toward her supporting shoulder while other ballerinas wait behind a stage flat. Identified as the Spanish étoile Rosita Mauri, the 1876 sheet is in pastel, essence and oil on paper and belongs to the Musée d'Orsay.
collection-of-beauty-finches-and-bamboo-: A handscroll of finches perched on slender bamboo, attributed to the Northern Song emperor and devoted painter Huizong. The work exemplifies the courtly bird-and-flower idiom: minute feather observation paired with the calligraphic restraint of monochrome bamboo.
collection-of-beauty-five-egrets-descend: Five egrets glide through falling snow toward a quiet shoreline, their white forms dissolving against the pale ground. Koson, the leading kachoga (bird-and-flower) printmaker of the shin-hanga era, captures the species' winter behaviour with delicately graded woodblock impressions.
collection-of-beauty-flaming-june-by-fre: A young woman sleeps curled in a translucent orange-saffron gown, one arm thrown over her head, a sprig of oleander above her. Leighton painted the oil in 1895; after decades of neglect it was bought for the Museo de Arte de Ponce in Puerto Rico in the 1960s. The folded pose fills a square format, the fabric worked in deep orange against a marble parapet and sea.
collection-of-beauty-floorpolishers-male: Three peasants kneel and lunge with floor brushes across a strip of yellow parquet, their bodies thickened into block-like volumes. Catalogued as Nakov F-196, the 78 by 71 cm gouache on paper was shown at the Donkey's Tail exhibition in Moscow in March 1912 and now belongs to the Stedelijk Museum, Amsterdam.
collection-of-beauty-flora-tristan-1838: Portrait of the French socialist and feminist writer Flora Tristan, author of Peregrinations of a Pariah. Published as a lithograph by Aubert in 1838 and reproduced in Le Charivari no. 53 on 22 February 1839, the print circulated her likeness during the years of her workers' organising tours through France.
collection-of-beauty-flowering-meadow-wi: Gnarled pine trunks rise from a meadow thick with long grass and dandelions, some in yellow bloom and some gone to seed, in the garden of the Saint-Paul asylum at Saint-Rémy. Van Gogh painted it in the spring of 1890, during his final weeks there, cropping the view to the ground plane so the flowering grass fills the canvas. Kröller-Müller Museum, Otterlo.
collection-of-beauty-flowers-in-a-rococo: An exuberant bouquet spills from an ornate Rococo vase, painted with the broken touches and shifting planes that mark Cézanne's early move beyond Impressionism. The composition tilts the vessel forward, pressing pigment-laden blossoms against a darkened ground in dense, sculptural facets.
collection-of-beauty-foggy-morning-at-po: Mist swallows the Norman cliffs above Pourville, where Monet spent the summer of 1882 pursuing the dissolving effects of marine atmosphere. Pale lavenders and silvered greens are knit together in short, parallel strokes, leaving the horizon as little more than a suggestion.
collection-of-beauty-follower-of-rogier-: A close adaptation of Rogier van der Weyden's celebrated Descent from the Cross, with the limp body of Christ lowered amid a tightly grouped frieze of mourners. The sharp Netherlandish drawing, jewel-toned drapery, and shallow gilded space follow the prototype's compressed, sculptural staging.
collection-of-beauty-fourth-muscle-man-b: A woodcut from Andreas Vesalius's De humani corporis fabrica, the fourth in the famous sequence of muscle men that strip away the body's musculature layer by layer; here dissected muscles hang loose from the figure's arms as he stands in a landscape of hills and buildings that continues from plate to plate across the series. The blocks, cut for the book's first edition of 1543 and attributed to artists in Titian's circle, transformed anatomical illustration. This impression comes from the 1555 second edition and is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
collection-of-beauty-fox-in-the-snow-cou: A red fox crouches over its prey in a frozen field, painted with the palette knife's broad, material slabs that Courbet championed in his Realist landscapes. The unsentimental subject and the granular, scraped whites of the snow strip the hunt scene of Romantic glamour.
collection-of-beauty-fragonard-coresus-s: The high priest Coresus plunges a dagger into his own breast before the altar to save the maiden Callirhoe from the sacrifice Bacchus had demanded, the temple filled with collapsing onlookers. Fragonard's morceau d'agrément for admission to the Académie Royale in 1765, the canvas was bought immediately by Louis XV and hangs in the Louvre.
collection-of-beauty-fragonard-francois-: The future Duc d'Harcourt, governor to the Dauphin, leans on an open book in a brocaded jacket, his attention caught mid-thought. Oil on canvas, the portrait belongs to Fragonard's group of figures de fantaisie of about 1769, in which sitters appear in fanciful Spanish or Renaissance costume.
collection-of-beauty-fragonard-swing: A young woman in a pink silk gown swings forward through a garden bower, kicking off one slipper as a hidden suitor peers up from the bushes below. Commissioned by the Baron de Saint-Julien for his château, Fragonard's canvas became the defining image of Rococo libertinage.
collection-of-beauty-fragonard-the-reade: A young woman in lemon-yellow silk sits in profile, absorbed in a small book held close to her face, her elbow propped on a velvet cushion. Oil on canvas at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the picture is among the most settled and finished of Fragonard's late-1760s portraits of figures lost in thought.
collection-of-beauty-fragonard-the-see-s: Two young lovers play on a plank-and-log seesaw beneath a sweeping willow, the girl's skirts flaring with the motion. Painted around 1750-52 as the pendant to Blind Man's Buff (Toledo Museum of Art), the canvas was commissioned by Baron Saint-Julien while Fragonard was still in Boucher's studio and now hangs in the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid.
collection-of-beauty-fragonard-woman-w-d: A young woman in a loose pink wrap holds up a small lapdog to kiss its muzzle, the bedclothes tumbling around her. The canvas, now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, belongs to Fragonard's series of intimate boudoir pictures of the late 1760s, painted with a feathery, rapid touch.
collection-of-beauty-fragonardsisters: Two young girls in white muslin dresses lean close together over a basket of flowers, the older steadying the younger on a cushioned bench. The canvas, sometimes called Les Deux Soeurs, belongs to Fragonard's series of intimate domestic groups painted in the late 1760s.
collection-of-beauty-francesco-hayez-056: Samson straddles the lion and pries open its jaws, his musculature lit with the academic clarity Hayez absorbed from study after the antique. The Old Testament hero is staged as a single isolated figure, drawing on the sculptural Romanticism that linked the artist to Canova's circle.
collection-of-beauty-francesco-hayez-oda: A reclining harem figure pauses over a book, her bared shoulders and embroidered cushions rendered with the polished surfaces and erotic restraint Hayez brought to his Orientalist subjects. The smooth modelling and warm half-light reflect his long career as Milan's leading Romantic portraitist.
collection-of-beauty-francesco-hayez-rit: The novelist Alessandro Manzoni, author of I Promessi Sposi, sits in sober dark dress against a neutral ground, fixing the viewer with a measured gaze. Hayez treats the literary patriot of the Risorgimento with the restrained likeness and crisp drawing of the Italian Romantic portrait tradition.
collection-of-beauty-francesco-hayez-sel: Hayez places himself among the painters Giuseppe Molteni and Giovanni Migliara, the sculptor Pelagio Pelagi, and the writer Tommaso Grossi, an intimate Milanese circle gathered around a table. Now in the Museo Poldi Pezzoli, the conversation piece records the cultural milieu that shaped Lombard Romanticism.
collection-of-beauty-francesco-hayez-sus: The biblical Susanna twists modestly at her bath, surprised by the elders whose presence is implied beyond the frame. Hayez handles the polished nude in the National Gallery, London, with a sculptural finish indebted to Canova and the warm tonalities of his Venetian training.
collection-of-beauty-francesco-hayez-the: Inhabitants of the Greek town of Parga gather their dead and their belongings before fleeing the 1819 Ottoman occupation, a contemporary tragedy embraced by Italian liberals. Hayez orchestrates the crowded shoreline as a Romantic tableau of exile, in line with his patriotic history paintings.
collection-of-beauty-francis-brooks-chad: A bust-length oil sketch of the Boston-born painter Francis Brooks Chadwick, set on a small panel just under fourteen inches high. Sargent painted his friend in Haarlem in 1880, where the two had travelled with Ralph Wormeley Curtis to study the Dutch masters at first hand.
collection-of-beauty-francis-osborne-5th: Francis Osborne, 5th Duke of Leeds, in a star-spangled court coat, painted by Benjamin West in the final years of the artist's London career. Osborne served briefly as Foreign Secretary under Pitt the Younger; the portrait was given to the National Portrait Gallery, London in 1888.
collection-of-beauty-francis-picabia-191: The terraced hills above Cassis stack up in flat patches of pink, ochre and pine green under a Mediterranean light. Painted in December 1911 in oil on canvas at roughly 50 by 62 cm, the landscape belongs to the brief Fauve-derived phase Picabia ran through before swinging into the Section d'Or Cubism of 1912.

A near-square canvas of nearly two and a half metres on each side, dissecting a mountain spring into broad facets of ochre and grey-green. Picabia showed La Source at the 1912 Salon d'Automne in Paris; the picture later entered the Museum of Modern Art in New York.

Robed penitents and processional banners pulse through a Sevillian street in a Cubist-Orphist lattice of cones and curves. Inspired by Picabia's travels in Spain, the square canvas was shown at the 1912 Salon de la Section d'Or and travelled to the 1913 Armory Show; it now hangs at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

Three metres square, the canvas threads abstract bands of rose, blue, and ochre around a memory of a dancer and a watching cleric seen on Picabia's Atlantic crossing. The invented title interleaves the French words étoile and danse; the picture was shown at the 1913 Armory Show and is now at the Art Institute of Chicago.

Curving metallic planes and tubular forms hurtle across a near-square canvas almost three metres on each side. Picabia painted Udnie in 1913 after watching Polish dancer Stasia Napierkowska perform on the ship carrying him to the Armory Show; the picture now hangs at the Musée National d'Art Moderne, Centre Pompidou, Paris.

Mechanical schematic of an alarm clock rendered in ink, its dial, springs, and bell drawn with engineer's precision and labelled in handwritten French. Made in 1919 and held by Tate in London, the drawing belongs to Picabia's machinist Dada period, when he used technical diagrams to satirise human function as mere mechanism.
collection-of-beauty-francis-picabia-192: Concentric black rings around a frontal female figure, with letters and the title Optophone inscribed at the edges, executed in ink, watercolour, and pencil on board at roughly 72 by 60 centimetres. Made around 1922, the work nods to Raoul Hausmann's invented optophone device, a Dada-era machine for converting light into sound.
collection-of-beauty-francis-picabia-ici: Alfred Stieglitz appears as a broken bellows camera, with an automobile gearshift in neutral and an engaged handbrake, reaching toward the word IDEAL. Picabia's mechanomorphic portrait was based on a Vest Pocket Kodak advertisement and ran on the cover of issue 5-6 of the New York review 291 in July 1915.
collection-of-beauty-francis-picabia-tra: Overlapping female figures, classical heads, and floral silhouettes are laid over one another in translucent washes, a study from Picabia's Transparences series. Picabia began the layered figural compositions around 1928 after his Dada years, drawing on Botticelli, Piero della Francesca, and Catalan Romanesque frescoes to build pictures readable at several depths at once.
collection-of-beauty-francisco-de-goya-s: From the Black Paintings Goya applied directly to the walls of his Quinta del Sordo, the titan Cronus tears into one of his children, eyes blazing in a void. The savage handling, sooty palette, and private setting belong to the bleak, late vocabulary now reassembled in the Prado.
collection-of-beauty-francisco-de-zurbar: A bound lamb lies on a grey ledge against a dark ground, an Agnus Dei meditation on Christ's sacrifice rendered with extraordinary fleecy detail. The picture, in the Prado, distils Zurbarán's ascetic Sevillian piety into one of the most economical still lifes of the Spanish Baroque.

Saint Luke, traditionally credited with painting the Virgin's likeness, leans on a palette and gazes up at the crucified Christ, conflating the evangelist with the artist's own self-portrait. The sober brown ground and clipped lighting are characteristic of Zurbarán's monastic Sevillian commissions.

A life-size crucified Christ emerges from impenetrable darkness, the body modelled with sculptural tenebrism that fooled at least one early viewer into thinking the work a polychrome carving. Painted for Seville's Dominican monastery of San Pablo, it announced Zurbarán's austere devotional manner.
collection-of-beauty-francois-boucher-00: The painter sits in shirtsleeves at his easel, brush poised over a canvas, with prints and plaster casts arranged in the cluttered studio behind. Boucher painted the small genre piece between 1730 and 1735, in the years immediately after his return from Rome, where he had studied at the French Academy.

A pastoral with figures crossing a wooden bridge over a stream, the trees and ruined masonry arranged in the manner Boucher adapted from Claude Lorrain. The 1751 canvas keeps the Rococo formula of small shepherd figures lodged in a luxuriant decorative landscape, a type Boucher repeated throughout the 1750s for the Parisian and court market.
collection-of-beauty-francois-boucher-17: Travellers and washerwomen pause beside a thatched mill with a turning wheel, in a landscape of leafy trees and a circular ruin recalling the Temple of Vesta at Tivoli. Boucher signed and dated the canvas 1755 and set the imaginary scene in the rolling country near Beauvais; the picture is now National Gallery NG6374.
collection-of-beauty-francois-boucher-dr: A shepherdess in a pink silk bodice reclines against a mossy bank with her crook and a basket of flowers beside her, her sheep dozing in the background. Painted around 1763, the canvas exemplifies Boucher's pastorale galante, the courtly fantasy of country life that filled the boudoirs of Madame de Pompadour and her circle.
collection-of-beauty-francois-boucher-la: Jupiter, disguised as the chaste Diana, leans toward the nymph Callisto with the seducer's eagle hidden above a pink satin curtain. Signed and dated 1759 and acquired by the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art in Kansas City through the William Rockhill Nelson Trust, the small canvas concentrates the late Rococo into a tight palette of pinks, greens and blues.
collection-of-beauty-francois-boucher-sk: An oil sketch of the king's official mistress standing before a mirror, holding her hat. Boucher worked up the small panel as a study for one of the full-length state portraits he produced for Madame de Pompadour, his principal patron for nearly two decades. The sketch entered the Rothschild collection and is now at Waddesdon Manor.
collection-of-beauty-francois-boucher-th: Venus rises from the sea attended by Tritons and Nereids, doves wheeling above the rococo curl of foam. Boucher painted the canvas in 1740 for the Swedish ambassador Carl Gustaf Tessin, who carried it back to Stockholm where it now hangs in the Nationalmuseum.

Venus is borne across the swell on a surge of nereids, tritons, and dolphins, while putti tumble through the air trailing a great loop of rose-patterned silk above her head. Painted in 1740, the canvas is Boucher's definitive statement of the mythological marine fantasy — flesh, spray, and drapery dissolving into a single silvery-blue arabesque. It was acquired by Count Carl Gustaf Tessin, the Swedish ambassador in Paris, and hangs today in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm.
collection-of-beauty-francois-boucher-yo: A barefoot peasant girl raises her skirts and lifts a tambourine as she dances, painted in the late 1760s for a private Paris client. Boucher's pastorale prettifies rural labour into a courtly entertainment, and the picture passed through the Marchioness of Cholmondeley's collection.
collection-of-beauty-francois-joseph-nav: Jacques-Louis David, painted in Brussels exile by his Belgian pupil François-Joseph Navez. Navez had followed David to Belgium in 1817 and produced this respectful study of the elderly master, who continued teaching from his Rue Léopold studio until his death in 1825.
collection-of-beauty-frans-snijders-keuk: A loaded kitchen table heaves with game, fruit and copper vessels in the lavish Antwerp manner that Snyders developed alongside Rubens. Strong diagonals and life-size scale push the still life toward decorative grandeur, intended for the dining halls of patrician collectors.
collection-of-beauty-frans-snyders-a-gre: A lean greyhound seizes a piglet boar in mid-flight across a wooded clearing, captured with the anatomical precision Snyders brought to Rubens's hunt commissions. Slashing brushwork in the foliage and a smoky sky heighten the violent Baroque drama.
collection-of-beauty-frans-snyders-and-w: Hounds tear at a cornered boar in a churning Baroque mêlée, the kind of large hunting piece Snyders supplied with workshop assistance for aristocratic galleries. Sweeping diagonals, splayed limbs and a bruised sky echo the dynamic compositions he had honed beside Rubens.
collection-of-beauty-frans-snyders-conce: An owl serves as conductor while a riot of songbirds reads from a sheet of music, a witty allegorical conceit Snyders treated repeatedly. The tightly observed plumage of finches, parrots and birds of prey reflects his standing as Antwerp's premier animal specialist.
collection-of-beauty-frans-snyders-cook-: A market cook arranges deer, swans and waterfowl across a generous table while a cat and dog skirmish below, staging abundance as theatre. The display piece, scaled for a Flemish patrician dining room, is typical of Snyders's collaboration with Rubens's circle.
collection-of-beauty-frans-snyders-lying: A lioness rests in profile against a darkened landscape, her tawny coat brushed with the loose, confident strokes Snyders reserved for living animals. The study likely served as a model for the great Antwerp hunt pieces produced with Rubens's workshop.
collection-of-beauty-frans-snyders-orphe: Orpheus charms a menagerie of beasts and birds with his lyre, the Ovidian subject becoming a pretext for Snyders's encyclopaedic display of fur, feather and scale. The composition crowds exotic species into a forested clearing in the Flemish Baroque manner.
collection-of-beauty-franz-von-stuck-004: A nude woman emerges from shadow with an enormous serpent coiled across her shoulders, its head reared at her ear. The picture, replicated in several versions, distils von Stuck's Symbolist creed: a frontal nude, deep gilded frame, and femme-fatale eroticism rendered in glazed, almost lacquered pigment.
collection-of-beauty-franz-von-stuck-by-: A late self-portrait on board, signed and dated 1923, presents the Munich Secession founder in dark dress against a neutral ground. The clipped scale and sober finish reflect von Stuck's habit of treating his own image as part of his public persona as artist-prince.
collection-of-beauty-franz-von-stuck-sal: Salome dances before a moonlit sky, the platter bearing the head of the Baptist held up by a grinning attendant. Von Stuck stages the subject with bare midriff, jewelled adornments and the brooding theatricality favoured by fin-de-siècle Munich Symbolism.
collection-of-beauty-franz-von-stuck-the: Two nude warriors lock in combat over a sprawling female nude, a Symbolist allegory of erotic rivalry typical of von Stuck's Munich Secession output. Hard contour, bronzed flesh and a smouldering ground push the mythic theme toward late nineteenth-century decadence.
collection-of-beauty-franz-von-stuck-wou: A bare-breasted Amazon staggers from the field clutching her side, her body silhouetted against a stormy ground in von Stuck's customary bituminous palette. The classical subject is treated with the muscular Symbolist eroticism he made the signature of the Munich Secession.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-bazille-00: A direct self-portrait set against a dark ground, the painter holding his palette and brushes. Oil on canvas, 108.9 by 71.1 cm, executed in 1865 to 1866 and held by the Art Institute of Chicago, which purchased it in 1962. Bazille was in his mid-twenties when he painted it.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-bazille-ba: The painter's studio at 9 rue de la Condamine in the Batignolles quarter of Paris, hung with canvases and peopled by his circle, Bazille himself shown at the easel. Painted in 1870; Manet contributed the figure of Bazille, and the work has been in the Musée d'Orsay since 1986.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-bazille-na: A still life of fish laid out on a kitchen table. Oil on canvas, painted in 1866 and held by the Detroit Institute of Arts. Bazille took up still life repeatedly in the mid-1860s, treating fish, game and a heron in turn.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-bazille-po: A bust-length portrait of a young man costumed as a medieval troubadour, his collar and cap evoking the Romantic revival of the type. The sitter is identified as the poet Paul Verlaine; Bazille painted the canvas in 1868, and it is now in the Dallas Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-bazille-th: A boy in white breeches, a pink shirt and a boater stands in a planted garden under a bright sky. Oil on canvas, about 128 by 169 cm, painted in 1866 to 1867 and held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Houston. Bazille left the foreground unfinished, the bare canvas still visible.

A young woman in a pink-and-white striped dress seen from behind, seated on a wall and looking out over the sunlit village of Castelnau near Montpellier. Oil on canvas, 147 by 110 cm, painted in 1864 and now in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. The sitter is Bazille's cousin Thérèse des Hours.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-bazille-yo: A Black woman holding out a bouquet of pink-and-white peonies beside a basket of tulips, roses and lilac, posed as a flower seller. Oil on canvas, 60 by 75 cm, painted in 1870 and now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington; a related version is at the Musée Fabre.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-leighton-b: Frederic Leighton seated in his Academician's gown, left elbow hooked over the chair back, hands loosely clasped. Watts painted this oil from sittings in 1881, the year Leighton sat for the work now in the National Portrait Gallery, London (NPG 1049). It is one of three portraits Watts made of his friend across their long acquaintance.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-leighton-c: A long procession bears Cimabue's altarpiece of the Madonna through Florence toward Santa Maria Novella, the painter Cimabue leading with the boy Giotto. Leighton painted this over two metres tall and more than five metres wide in Rome between 1853 and 1855; Queen Victoria bought it on the opening day of the 1855 Royal Academy exhibition for 600 guineas.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-leighton-k: A reclining woman in pale drapery plays with a litter of kittens, her arm stretched along a couch. Leighton's canvas measures roughly 119 by 79 cm and treats a domestic subject far removed from the classical and mythological scenes for which he was known.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-leighton-p: May Sartoris, about fifteen, stands in a dark riding habit with a red scarf and a wide black hat, a felled tree at her side. Leighton painted the portrait around 1860; the oil measures 152.1 by 90.2 cm and is held in the Kimbell Art Museum, Fort Worth.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-leighton-t: Three nymphs recline beneath an apple tree, the serpent Ladon coiled around its trunk to guard the golden fruit that was Hera's gift. Leighton painted the tondo about 1892; it is held by the Lady Lever Art Gallery in Port Sunlight. The circular format sets the sleeping figures within the curve of the tree's foliage.

Hermes lifts Persephone up from the underworld toward her mother Demeter, who reaches down through a gap of light at the cave mouth. Leighton painted the oil in 1891 and it hangs in Leeds Art Gallery. The figures form a single rising diagonal from the dark earth into the bright opening above.
collection-of-beauty-frederic-lord-leigh: Andromeda is chained naked to the rocks while the dragon spreads dark wings over her and Perseus dives in from above on the winged horse Pegasus. Leighton painted the oil in 1891; it entered the Walker Art Gallery in Liverpool. The arched composition wraps the monster's body around the upper edge like a canopy.
collection-of-beauty-frederick-law-olmst: Sargent painted the landscape architect of Central Park during work on the Biltmore Estate grounds, posing him among the rhododendrons he had laid out. Loose, plein-air handling of the foliage gives way to a tighter likeness of the sitter, knitting Realist portraiture to Impressionist surface.
collection-of-beauty-frederick-leighton-: A close head-and-shoulders study of a fair-haired young Italian girl, her white blouse laced with a dark bodice, titled with the Italian for the blonde one. The oil belongs to the Hamburger Kunsthalle and is dated by the museum to 1879.

A half-length young woman in a black and gold dress turns to one side, her head resting against her hand. The model was Edith Pullen, sister of Leighton's regular model Dorothy Dene; the picture dates to 1883. Leighton kept his contours smooth and his palette restrained in the manner of his classicising portraiture.

A single draped woman seated on a rock above still water in a deep mountain hollow. Oil on canvas painted around 1890; Leighton described the setting as a place worn so deep that absolute silence holds. The picture is now in the Maryhill Museum of Art, Washington State.
collection-of-beauty-frederik-hendrik-15: Frederick Henry of Orange-Nassau, three years dead at the time of painting, stands at knee-length in burnished armour beside a column. The picture is a posthumous workshop replica from the Honthorst atelier, designed to hang as a pendant to the portrait of his widow Amalia van Solms in the Stadholder's gallery at the Rijksmuseum.
collection-of-beauty-fritillaria-imperia: A crown imperial (Fritillaria imperialis) with its ring of pendent orange bells beneath a tuft of upright leaves, drawn life-size against a plain ground. Plate from Redouté's Les Liliacées, the eight-volume folio issued in Paris between 1802 and 1816. The image is a colour stipple engraving after Redouté's watercolour on vellum, finished by hand.
collection-of-beauty-frosty-morning-mont: A bare-branched tree stands in a frozen New Jersey field at dawn, the grass blanched with frost and a thin band of pale sky beyond. Inness signed the canvas in 1885, the year he settled permanently in Montclair, where his looser, tonal handling broke with the high finish of his earlier Hudson River training.
collection-of-beauty-fujiwara-no-yasumas: A late triptych by Yoshitoshi shows the Heian courtier Fujiwara no Yasumasa playing his flute on a moonlit moor while the bandit Hakamadare, disarmed by the music, looks on. Long stretches of muted ground and the cool autumnal palette demonstrate Yoshitoshi's reformed late style for the Meiji woodblock market.
collection-of-beauty-fuseliartistmovedto: Fuseli's draughtsman slumps against a colossal antique foot and hand, overwhelmed by the ruins of classical achievement. Drawn in red chalk and sepia wash during his Roman years, the sheet captures the Sublime sense of inadequacy before antiquity that shaped Anglo-Continental Romanticism.
collection-of-beauty-futsuka-zuki-by-kaw: A slender new moon hangs above a quiet hillside in sumi ink and faint colour on silk, mounted as a hanging scroll. Kawai Gyokudō, a leading figure of the modern Nihonga movement, won first prize at the 1907 Tokyo industry exhibition with this lyrical evocation of the second-night sky.
collection-of-beauty-g-caillebotte-le-ja: A snow-blanketed view of the painter's own riverside garden across the Seine from Argenteuil, where Caillebotte spent his final years tending plants and painting boats. The muted whites and bare branches show the late, looser brushwork he developed after retreating from Paris's Impressionist circle.
collection-of-beauty-g-caillebotte-nastu: A close, plunging view of nasturtium leaves and blossoms painted in Caillebotte's Petit Gennevilliers garden. The unusual cropping and high vantage echo the steep perspectives he favoured in his urban scenes, applied here to a horticultural subject he cultivated himself.
collection-of-beauty-g-caillebotte-un-ba: Two top-hatted men gaze down from the wrought-iron balcony of the artist's apartment at 31 Boulevard Haussmann, the same Parisian vantage point Caillebotte used in several canvases of the period. The plunging perspective and modern bourgeois subject typify his engagement with Haussmann's reshaped city.
collection-of-beauty-g-caillebotte-villa: Pastel seaside villas line the Normandy coast at Trouville, a fashionable resort favoured by Parisians on holiday. Caillebotte's looser handling and brighter palette here reflect his shift from urban scenes toward the open-air subjects of his later career.
collection-of-beauty-gaertner1: The southern segment of the 1834 Berlin panorama, recording rooftops, courtyards and chimneys spread out below the lantern of the Friedrichswerder church. Gaertner's six-part view was purchased by Friedrich Wilhelm III and a replica was later carried to Russia for Tsarina Alexandra Feodorovna.
collection-of-beauty-gaertner5: One panel from Gaertner's six-part angular panorama of Berlin, taken from the roof of Schinkel's Friedrichswerdersche Kirche in the summer of 1834. The architectural painter worked daily in a wooden booth atop the church, recording the new buildings of the Schinkel circle for King Friedrich Wilhelm III.
collection-of-beauty-gaertner6: An interior view by the Berlin painter Eduard Gaertner, whose careful perspectival studies of Prussian streets and rooms defined the city's 19th-century image. Gaertner trained at the royal porcelain manufactory before specializing in architectural vedute prized by Friedrich Wilhelm III and IV.
collection-of-beauty-gainsborough-grace-: Full-length portrait of the courtesan Grace Dalrymple Elliott, known as 'Dally the Tall', in a yellow Van Dyck-style gown with a towering 1770s coiffure. Commissioned by her lover the Earl of Cholmondeley and shown at the Royal Academy in 1778, the canvas measures 234.3 by 153.7 cm and is now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-gainsborough-thomas: Elizabeth and Mary Linley, daughters of the Bath composer Thomas Linley, sit close together in a wooded glade, the elder holding a sheet of music. Gainsborough painted the double portrait around 1772 and retouched it in 1785, after Elizabeth's elopement with Sheridan. It belongs to the Dulwich Picture Gallery in London.
collection-of-beauty-gamaun: The Slavic prophetic bird Gamayun perches on a bare branch above a blood-red dawn, woman-headed and crowned with dark plumage. Vasnetsov painted the panel in 1898 and exhibited it the following year; the imagery prompted Alexander Blok's 1899 sonnet of the same name.
collection-of-beauty-garcon-au-gilet-rou: The Italian model Michelangelo di Rosa in a red waistcoat, one of several studies Cézanne made of the boy around 1889 to 1890. This watercolour version, in the Barnes Foundation, Philadelphia, leaves the paper bare in places between washes. Cézanne used the repeated pose to test the figure against surrounding space.
collection-of-beauty-garden-at-bordigher: Painted during Monet's winter trip to the Italian Riviera, this view of a Bordighera garden captures the silvery light he found so disorienting after Normandy. Twisting olives and palms are rendered in feathery, near-pastel strokes, the morning haze softening every contour into vibrating colour.
collection-of-beauty-gathering-bamboo-sh: A color woodblock print by Suzuki Harunobu of a young woman in a wide straw hat digging in deep snow with a hoe, where a single bamboo shoot has broken the surface beneath snow-laden bamboo. The unseasonable subject evokes the Chinese filial-piety tale of Meng Zong, who dug for bamboo shoots in midwinter to feed his ailing mother, recast in Harunobu's fashion as a scene with an elegant contemporary beauty. The print, from about 1765, is in the Art Institute of Chicago.
collection-of-beauty-gauguin-bretonne: A young woman in the white coif and dark dress of Pont-Aven posed during Gauguin's first Brittany sojourn. The simplified silhouette and reserved palette anticipate the cloisonnist flattening he would push further in following summers among the Breton peasantry.
collection-of-beauty-gauguin-huttes-sous: Thatched cottages glimpsed through tree trunks, painted during Gauguin's stay in Martinique in 1887. The tropical light and broad colour areas mark his decisive turn away from Impressionist division of tone toward the synthetist style of Pont-Aven.
collection-of-beauty-gauguin-nature-mort: A pair of dead parrots lies on a tabletop beside a small terracotta idol Gauguin had himself modelled, possibly the Polynesian moon goddess Hina. Painted in Atuona on Hiva Oa in 1902, the canvas was acquired by Ivan Morozov in Moscow and now hangs in the Pushkin Museum, originally inscribed Oiseaux morts on the stretcher.
collection-of-beauty-gauguin-paul-sacred: Two Tahitian girls stand by a pool ringed with dancing women, the foreground figure holding a red fruit while the other rests her hand on her companion's shoulder. Painted in Paris in 1894 from sketches of his first Tahitian trip, Nave nave moe entered the Hermitage with the Shchukin collection.
collection-of-beauty-gauguin-paul-still-: A bearded young man in profile crops the right edge of the canvas, staring at a ceramic pot the painter had thrown himself and a cluster of pears on a white cloth. Gauguin painted his friend and pupil Charles Laval in late 1886 after returning from Pont-Aven; the cut-off face nods to Degas's framing while the parallel strokes in the fruit pay tribute to Cezanne. Indianapolis Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-gauguin-selbstbildn: Gauguin paints himself in three-quarter view against a flat olive ground, the gaze inward and the brushwork pared back. Inscribed to his Parisian dealer Daniel de Monfreid, the canvas was sent from Tahiti as a token of the friendship that sustained his correspondence during the second Polynesian period.
collection-of-beauty-general-sir-david-b: A vast late history painting commemorating the British general's discovery of Tipu Sultan's body after the storming of Seringapatam in 1799. Wilkie staged the torch-lit scene with theatrical chiaroscuro, working in the grand manner he adopted following his travels in Spain.
collection-of-beauty-gentile-and-giovann: Saint Mark addresses a crowd of turbaned Mamluks and Venetian onlookers in a sun-bleached square dominated by a domed basilica conflating San Marco with Alexandrian architecture. Begun by Gentile Bellini around 1504 and completed by his brother Giovanni after 1507, the canvas was painted for the Scuola Grande di San Marco and now hangs in the Pinacoteca di Brera.
collection-of-beauty-gentileschi-allegor: A self-portrait in the guise of Pittura, the female personification of Painting, holding brush and palette in mid-stroke. Gentileschi exploited her gender to claim an allegorical role her male peers could not assume, presenting herself as the embodiment of the art itself.
collection-of-beauty-gentileschi-artemis: The biblical queen swoons before the Persian king as she pleads for her people, a subject Gentileschi treats with operatic gesture and sumptuous fabrics. Painted during her Neapolitan years, it shows her assimilation of Caravaggesque drama into a more courtly, decorative key.
collection-of-beauty-gentileschi-lucrezi: The Roman matron Lucretia turns the dagger on herself rather than live with dishonour, a subject Gentileschi returned to repeatedly. The compressed half-length composition and raking light typify her late Naples manner, where female protagonists confront violence with stoic resolve.
collection-of-beauty-george-augustus-eli: The defender of Gibraltar stands in scarlet uniform on the ramparts, the Rock's batteries smoking behind him during the Great Siege. Copley painted the portrait in 1787 as a study for his vast Siege of Gibraltar canvas, now in the National Portrait Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-george-frederic-wat: Orlando lunges after the fleeing sorceress Fata Morgana, a scene drawn from Boiardo's epic 'Orlando Innamorato'. Watts began the canvas in Italy in 1846 and finished it in London by 1848; the oil, 165 by 120 cm, was given by the artist to the Leicester Museum and Art Gallery in 1888.

The Minotaur leaning on a parapet and gazing out to sea, a small bird crushed in his fist. Watts painted the oil in 1885 as a protest against the child prostitution exposed that summer by W. T. Stead in the Pall Mall Gazette. It entered the Tate in 1897 (N01634).
collection-of-beauty-george-frederick-wa: The artist at seventeen, with loose hair and a fixed gaze, the face firmly modelled while the clothing is left as bare canvas. Watts painted this oil, his first self-portrait, in 1834; it measures 53.3 by 38.1 cm and remains at the Watts Gallery in Compton, Surrey.
collection-of-beauty-george-inness-home-: A farmhouse and barn sit half-screened by bare trees on a damp New Jersey hillside, with figures and livestock dissolved in soft brown and ochre. Inness painted the view from his own property in Montclair where he settled in 1885, and the canvas now belongs to the Sterling and Francine Clark Art Institute.
collection-of-beauty-george-inness-in-th: A herdsman drives cattle along a country road through the rolling western Massachusetts hills, with farms and a steeple visible in the valley below. Inness painted the picture between 1848 and 1850 in the Hudson River School idiom of his early career, before his shift toward the Barbizon manner; it hangs in the Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid.
collection-of-beauty-george-inness-milto: A view of the Hudson Valley near Milton, New York, with grazing cattle in a meadow and the broad river opening behind.
