Inness was working in the wake of his European study trips, still close to the Hudson River School idiom before his later turn toward Barbizon-influenced softness; now in the Yale University Art Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-george-inness-the-h: A heron stands almost lost in a marshy thicket of yellow reeds and dark pools, the whole scene veiled in golden mist. Inness painted the canvas in 1893, the final full year of his life, and the work now belongs to the Art Institute of Chicago.
collection-of-beauty-george-inness-the-l: A reclining figure on a hillside looks down on the new Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad roundhouse outside Scranton, Pennsylvania, with a locomotive trailing smoke through cleared stumps. Commissioned by the railroad's first president as a promotional image, Inness's panorama frames American industrial expansion within a pastoral Hudson River idiom; now at the National Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-george-spencer-2nd-: George Spencer, 2nd Earl Spencer, faces the viewer in a brown coat and white stock, his powdered hair above the blue sash and breast star of the Order of the Garter. Copley painted the portrait around 1800, while Spencer served as First Lord of the Admiralty under William Pitt, overseeing the Royal Navy through Camperdown and the Nile.
collection-of-beauty-george-washington-1: Washington faces the viewer in a black coat with white stock, his powdered hair brushed back from a high forehead. The 1795 canvas at the Metropolitan Museum (accession 07.160) belongs to the so-called Vaughan type, the first of three Washington portrait formats Stuart developed from life sittings.
collection-of-beauty-georges-de-la-tour-: Another of La Tour's penitent Magdalens, the saint absorbed in candlelit thought before a skull and crucifix. The repeated subject across his oeuvre allowed him to refine the pictorial logic of a single flame describing flesh, fabric and bone.

An angel appears to the sleeping Joseph in a candlelit interior, the standard Lorraine nocturne formula put to a religious end. The shielded flame, smooth modelling and quiet psychology are characteristic of La Tour's mature devotional pictures.

Job sits naked on his dunghill while his wife berates him by the light of a single candle. La Tour treats the Old Testament confrontation as an intimate two-figure nocturne, the flame between them mapping every fold of skin and cloth.

A tightly cropped nocturne in which a woman shields a candle as another presents a swaddled child, often read as a Nativity in contemporary dress. The smooth, sculptural surfaces and concealed flame are hallmarks of La Tour's late Lorraine candlelit manner.

Itinerant street musicians come to blows over a hurdy-gurdy, one wielding a knife as a companion squeezes a lemon to feign a wound. La Tour stages the brawl in cool daylight, his earlier Caravaggesque manner before he fully turned to candlelit nocturnes.

A pipe-smoker leans into his glowing taper, the small flame illuminating cheek, hand and clay bowl against deep shadow. La Tour reduces the genre subject to a meditative still life in light, the kind of intimate nocturne that defines his late Lunéville workshop.

A naive young man has his palm read by an old gypsy while her accomplices pick his purse and cut his medal chain. La Tour stages the swindle in cool daylight rather than candlelight, exploiting fixed sidelong glances to spell out the deception.

The penitent saint sits in shadow with hand on skull, contemplating an oil lamp whose smoking wick stands for the brevity of life. One of several Magdalen meditations La Tour painted, it reduces the iconography to flame, flesh and the geometry of darkness.

The Magdalen sits before a mirror that reflects only a candle and skull, her jewels discarded at her feet. La Tour pares the vanitas iconography to its essentials and lets the single flame model her face and hands with mathematical calm.
collection-of-beauty-georges-seurat-019: Seurat's last, unfinished canvas captures a circus performance with a bareback rider, ringmaster and tiered audience. The arabesque rhythms and yellow-blue contrasts apply Charles Henry's theories of expressive line and colour, pushing pointillism toward decorative stylisation.
collection-of-beauty-georges-seurat-026: A quiet riverbank study made while Seurat was finishing his Grande Jatte campaigns. The Seine flows past the island in patiently calibrated dots of complementary colour, a small-format demonstration of the optical mixing his divisionist method depended on.
collection-of-beauty-georges-seurat-048: Labourers at work levelling earth, a subject from the industrial fringes of Paris that Seurat tackled in his early career. The broad balayé brushwork and sober palette precede the ordered dots of his pointillist maturity.
collection-of-beauty-georges-seurat-c-18: An early still life painted while Seurat was still absorbing Barbizon and Impressionist precedents. The dense impasto and earthy palette show him before the systematic divisionism of dots that would define his mature work later in the decade.
collection-of-beauty-georges-seurat-land: An early landscape from the industrial outskirts north of Paris, painted before Seurat formulated his pointillist method. Loose, almost Corot-like brushwork registers river, sky and bank in muted tones, a quiet rehearsal for the rigorous technique to come.
collection-of-beauty-georges-seurat-les-: Three views of the same studio model — facing, in profile and from behind — set against the painter's own Grande Jatte. Seurat used the picture as a programmatic demonstration of pointillism applied to the academic motif of the nude.
collection-of-beauty-georges-seurat-seat: A preparatory oil study for one of the bathers in Une Baignade, Asnieres, the large canvas that announced Seurat's ambitions in 1884. Built from broad criss-crossed strokes in the conté-drawing manner he called balayé, it precedes his fully developed pointillist technique.
collection-of-beauty-georges-seurat-view: A coastal view from Grandcamp on the Normandy shore, part of the seaside campaigns Seurat undertook each summer to test his divisionist method against changing light. Tiny calibrated dots dissolve fortification, sea and sky into a luminous, near-abstract grid.
collection-of-beauty-georgianaofdevonshi: Georgiana Cavendish, Duchess of Devonshire, stands beside a stone urn in a white silk dress and a wide tilted black hat trimmed with feathers. Gainsborough painted the Whig hostess between 1785 and 1787; the canvas was stolen from Agnew's gallery in 1876, recovered in Chicago in 1901, and is now at Chatsworth.
collection-of-beauty-gerard-honthorst-gu: Engraved portrait of Gerard van Honthorst published in 1662 in Cornelis de Bie's Het Gulden Cabinet der edel vry schilder const, the Antwerp directory of painters. Pieter de Jode II cut the plate after a Honthorst self-portrait, with the print issued by Joannes Meyssens for an entry that placed the Utrecht master among the leading Northern painters of his century.
collection-of-beauty-gerard-van-honthors: Shepherds crowd around the manger holding lambs and a bagpipe, their weathered faces lit from below by the radiant Christ child. The 1622 canvas, now known mainly from a Web Gallery of Art photograph after the original burned in Munich in 1945, shows Honthorst transferring his Roman nocturne into a vertical Nativity composition.

Caiaphas leans across the table to question Christ, the two faces lit only by a single candle set between them. Honthorst painted the canvas in Rome around 1617 for the Marchese Vincenzo Giustiniani, and the radical nocturne earned him the Italian nickname Gherardo delle Notti.

A young man slumped at a table, drink in hand, his lute and books pushed aside in a candlelit interior. Catalogued as number 391 in the Bavarian State Painting Collections, the panel belongs to Honthorst's series of moralising tavern scenes in which Utrecht Caravaggism is bent toward the theme of squandered learning.

The princess Granida, lost while hunting, accepts a drink of water from the shepherd Daifilo at a forest spring. Signed and dated 1625, Honthorst's canvas takes its subject from Pieter Cornelisz Hooft's pastoral play Granida, the most popular Dutch theatrical source of the period and a frequent vehicle for veiled court portraiture.

The crowned David bows over the strings of his harp, eyes lifted in song, his ermine-trimmed robe and golden instrument picked out against deep brown shadow. Painted in 1622 after Honthorst's return from Rome, the canvas shows him adapting his hidden-light nocturne to a single biblical musician.

A young man in a striped doublet and feathered beret plucks a lute, glancing sideways with a faint smile. Honthorst signed the canvas in 1624 among the Utrecht single-figure musicians he produced in volume for the open market, the format derived from his studies after Caravaggio's followers in Rome.

A bearded musician in a slashed doublet bows a viola da gamba, his hand stilled on the fingerboard as if pausing between phrases. Signed and dated 1631, the canvas hangs in the Lviv National Art Gallery and continues the half-length musician type Honthorst had popularised after returning from Rome in 1620.

Margaretha Maria de Roodere stands at her easel painting a portrait while her parents look on from either side, framing her practice within the family. Honthorst signed and dated the picture in 1652, recording his sitter as one of the few documented women painters working in Utrecht in the mid-seventeenth century.

A laughing young woman in a feathered cap leans toward a richly dressed gallant while an older bawd counts coins behind them. Signed and dated 1625, the panel is in the Centraal Museum, Utrecht, and ranks among the earliest Northern transpositions of Caravaggio's candlelit bordello scenes into the Dutch market.

A young woman in a white chemise and red bodice strums a guitar, her gaze tilted up and slightly to one side. Painted around 1624, the canvas is one of Honthorst's Utrecht single-figure musicians, the open neckline and direct address pitching it between portrait and genre piece for the cabinet market.
collection-of-beauty-gerechtigkeit-1537: Justice personified as a nude woman holding sword and scales, a humanist subject Cranach's Wittenberg workshop produced in many versions for Saxon patrons. The sinuous body type and dark ground are signatures of his late mythological and allegorical nudes.
collection-of-beauty-gerhard-von-kugelge: A bust-length likeness of Caspar David Friedrich painted by his close friend in Dresden. Kügelgen catches the Romantic landscapist with sharp side-lit features and inward gaze, fixing the public image of the painter at the height of his early career.
collection-of-beauty-gericaulthorseman: A mounted officer of Napoleon's Imperial Guard wheels his rearing chestnut horse against a smoke-streaked sky. Géricault's Salon debut at twenty-one announced a new Romantic energy in French painting, with Rubensian colour and a kinetic diagonal that broke decisively from Davidian decorum.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-an-idyll-185: An early pastoral by Gérôme in the vein of his Néo-Grec circle, reaching back to Anacreontic and Pompeian models. Slender nudes, shallow stage-like space and porcelain-cool color place the picture closer to his Greek Interior than to his later Orientalist scenes.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-cave-canem: A reclining nude rests in a Pompeian-style interior beside a watchful dog, the title quoting the famous mosaic threshold inscription 'beware of the dog'. Gérôme blends archaeological staging with cabinet-picture eroticism in a tightly polished surface.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-eminence-gri: Capuchin friar François Leclerc du Tremblay descends a staircase at the Palais-Cardinal, courtiers bowing to the grey habit while ignoring the man inside it. Gérôme stages the scene as silent political theatre, contrasting the friar's coarse wool against polished marble and gilded livery.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-execution-of: A cold December morning at the Luxembourg gardens: Napoleon's marshal lies face down in the mud as the firing squad turns away, posters of his condemnation peeling on the wall behind. Gérôme uses an austere, almost reportorial composition to deliver a quiet indictment of Bourbon vengeance.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-femme-circas: A bust-length study of a young Circassian woman whose features are nearly hidden by a fine white veil, her dark eyes the only direct address to the viewer. Gérôme exploits the contrast between hyper-fine gauze and the heavy embroidered cap to flaunt his control of texture.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-haggin-horse: A bustling North African market scene rendered with Gérôme's characteristic ethnographic precision: tethered Arabian horses, robed traders, and sun-bleached architecture under a hot, even light. The picture belongs to the Haggin Museum's deep Gérôme holding, assembled by California financier James Ben Ali Haggin.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-haggin-saddl: A crowded Cairo saddler's stall hung with embroidered tack, leather cushions and ornate stirrups. Gérôme treats the merchandise as still life within a genre scene, balancing meticulous draftsmanship of leatherwork with the sun-flooded stone arcades he studied on repeated trips to Egypt.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-haggin-the-a: A late self-reflexive subject: Gérôme depicts himself in his studio carving a tinted marble figure, addressing his lifelong campaign for polychrome sculpture. Smooth academic finish gives way to studio clutter of mallets, plaster casts and pigment pots, declaring painting and sculpture as kindred crafts.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-haggin-unfol: A standard-bearer in Cairo unfurls the green banner of the Prophet before a mosque facade, surrounded by attentive figures. Gérôme stages the ceremony like a frieze, using crisp profile poses and tile patterns rendered with near-photographic care.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-l-entree-du-: Christ on the donkey descends a road white with Judean dust, the procession trailing behind him under a sky bleached by glare. Gérôme treats the Gospel scene as travel reportage from his Holy Land journeys, scattering the crowd into a long, frieze-like recession.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-painting-bre: An ancient Greek artisan paints a terracotta Tanagra figurine, the Latin title declaring that 'painting breathes life into sculpture'. The picture is Gérôme's manifesto for polychromy, arguing that the white marbles museums revered were originally as colored as this little figure.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-summer-after: A rare unpopulated landscape from Gérôme: still water, a wooded shore and a single skiff under hazy summer light. Stripped of his usual ethnographic figures, the picture shows the careful tonal control underlying his more theatrical work.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-the-two-maje: A male lion crouches on a desert outcrop facing the setting sun, the two 'majesties' of the title. Gérôme strips the picture to silhouette and burning sky, pursuing in paint the same monumental animal studies that fed his bronze sculpture practice.
collection-of-beauty-gerome-venus: Venus emerges from the sea trailing the morning star, her body lit with the pale, enamel finish Gérôme cultivated late in life. The composition revisits the Anadyomene tradition while flirting with the polychrome sculpture project that preoccupied his final decades.
collection-of-beauty-gerrit-van-honthors: A candle-lit brothel scene in which an old procuress brokers a young woman to a leering client. Honthorst, nicknamed Gherardo delle Notti in Rome, transplanted Caravaggio's tenebrism north; here a hidden flame carves the faces from the dark in glowing reds and ochres.

A grinning fiddler in a plumed hat leans through an open window, bow raised and glass of wine in hand. Honthorst painted the canvas in 1623, now in the Rijksmuseum, as a near-full-length variant of the brothel and tavern figures that made his Utrecht workshop the most successful in the city.

Five musicians lean over a painted balustrade to play viols, a flute, and a lute, looking down at the viewer as if from a real loggia overhead. Honthorst signed and dated the ceiling canvas in 1622 for an unknown Utrecht patron, applying the di sotto in su perspective he had studied in Italian palazzi.

A violinist in a slashed doublet and feathered hat raises a glass of wine while the bow hangs in his other hand. Painted around 1624, the half-length is one of several near-identical merry musicians Honthorst's Utrecht workshop produced for the bourgeois market, varied chiefly by costume and instrument.
collection-of-beauty-gherardo-delle-nott: The newborn Christ lies on the manger straw radiating his own light, watched by the Virgin, Joseph, and two shepherds whose faces emerge from surrounding darkness. The Uffizi panel from around 1619 is the source of Honthorst's Italian nickname Gherardo delle Notti, and it remains the clearest statement of his hidden-light technique.

Five figures gather around a candlelit table, a young lutenist tuning his instrument while a woman pours wine and an older man laughs. Gerrit van Honthorst, called Gherardo delle Notti in Italy for his nocturnal candlelight scenes, painted the canvas around 1619 after his Roman years, channeling Caravaggio into a Utrecht genre subject now in the Uffizi.
collection-of-beauty-giaele-e-sisara-ca-: Jael drives a tent peg through the temple of the sleeping Canaanite general Sisera, a biblical assassination Artemisia returned to repeatedly. Caravaggesque chiaroscuro isolates the act against deep shadow, with the heroine's calm, deliberate grip typical of Gentileschi's strong-willed women.
collection-of-beauty-giambattista-pitton: Bartolomeo Nazari shows his fellow Venetian Giambattista Pittoni at the easel, the leading Rococo history painter of the lagoon city. The portrait survives in the Museo Correr and was reproduced in Laura Coggiola Pittoni's 1907 monograph Dei Pittoni, Artisti Veneti. Pittoni would later co-found the Venetian academy in 1750 and succeed Tiepolo as its president.

The Carthaginian noblewoman receives the cup of poison sent by Masinissa, surrounded by attendants as she chooses suicide over Scipio's Roman triumph. Pittoni, a founding member of the Venetian Academy in 1750, treats the Livy episode with the pale flesh and silver-grey palette typical of his late Rococo manner.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-1755: The tragedian John Philip Kemble appears bust-length in a dark coat and white cravat, the face modelled with the sober directness Stuart used for his stage portraits. Painted in 1785 around the time of Kemble's London debut as Hamlet, the canvas is NPG 49 in the National Portrait Gallery, London.

The tragedienne Sarah Siddons sits in a powder-blue dress, her gaze direct, her hair upswept under a soft cap. Stuart painted the portrait in 1787 during his London years, when Siddons was the leading Shakespearean actress at Drury Lane; it now hangs at the National Portrait Gallery as NPG 50.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-bish: Jean-Louis Lefebvre de Cheverus, French émigré priest and first Catholic bishop of Boston, in episcopal robes with a small crucifix at his breast. Stuart painted the portrait in 1823, shortly before Cheverus returned to France to take up the see of Montauban; the canvas belongs to the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-cath: Catherine Brass Yates sews with white thread, her head turned in a half-glance, a black cap framing her grey curls. Stuart painted the New York merchant's wife in 1793 just after his return from Dublin; the canvas is now in the Andrew W. Mellon Collection at the National Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-geor: Washington stands full-length in a black velvet suit, his right hand extended over a table covered with bound volumes and a quill, an upholstered chair and crimson drapery behind. Stuart painted the Lansdowne portrait in April 1796 for William Petty, Marquess of Lansdowne, the British statesman who had supported American independence.

The unfinished bust of Washington against a brown ground shows the sixty-four-year-old president from the chest up, his hair powdered and his mouth set over the new wooden dentures. Stuart began the Athenaeum portrait on 12 April 1796 and kept the original at his easel as the master from which he produced more than seventy replicas.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-jame: James Madison in old age, in dark coat against neutral ground, painted years after his presidency ended. Stuart had first taken Madison's likeness in 1804; this late repetition, now at the National Gallery of Art, descends from that earlier sitting.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-majo: Henry Dearborn, the Jefferson-era Secretary of War newly returned to active command at the outbreak of the War of 1812, sits in dark blue uniform with gold epaulets. Stuart painted him in 1812; the canvas entered the Art Institute of Chicago as accession 1913.793.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-mart: Martha Washington, in a white cap and shawl, faces left in a half-length pose left unfinished against a brown ground. Stuart painted the canvas as a pendant to his Athenaeum portrait of the president in 1796, both works retained by the artist as templates and now jointly held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, and the National Portrait Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-mrs-: Sally Foster Otis, wife of the Federalist senator and mayor of Boston, sits in a white empire-line gown with a red shawl draped at her elbow. Stuart painted her in Boston in 1809, the canvas now held by the Reynolda House Museum of American Art in Winston-Salem.

Hepzibah Clarke Swan, wife of the speculator James Swan, sits in a high-waisted dress with a sheer wrap around her shoulders. Stuart painted her in Boston in 1808; the portrait, accession 27.539 at the Museum of Fine Arts, joined the museum from the sitter's descendants over a century later.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-sir-: Sir Joshua Reynolds, first president of the Royal Academy, sits in a brown coat with his wig powdered, glancing alertly at the viewer. Stuart painted his master in 1784 during the years he spent in Reynolds's London circle; the portrait is held by the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-gilbert-stuart-thom: Thomas Jefferson in old age, painted by Stuart from earlier sittings taken in 1805 during Jefferson's second presidency. Stuart kept the original Edgehill portrait in his Boston studio for years, working up replicas like this one for collectors and family members.
collection-of-beauty-ginger-pot-with-pom: A glazed ginger jar bound with cord stands among pears and a split pomegranate on a rumpled white cloth. Oil on canvas of 1893, held by The Phillips Collection in Washington. Cézanne tipped the tabletop forward so the fruit reads against the dark ground rather than receding into it.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-029b: Three robed men stand at the entrance of a rocky outcrop, the youngest seated with a compass and tablet, the older two conferring behind, a sunlit valley falling away to the right. The Three Philosophers, painted around 1508 for the Venetian collector Taddeo Contarini, hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-adoration: Two shepherds kneel before the Christ Child at the mouth of a dark cave, Mary and Joseph adoring beside them, a pastoral landscape opening to the left. The Allendale Nativity, painted around 1505 to 1510 and now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington, is among the most secure attributions to Giorgione.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-bildnisgi: The young Florentine Giovanni Borgherini sits with his tutor Trifone Gabriele behind him, the pupil holding a celestial sphere as the older man gestures in instruction. The double portrait on canvas, dated 1509 to 1510 and held by the Bavarian State Painting Collections in Munich, was traditionally attributed to Giorgione and is now debated between him and the young Titian.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-judith: Judith stands above the severed head of Holofernes with a long curving sword, her bare foot pressing on his temple against a wooded landscape. The panel, signed and dated 1504 and now in the Hermitage, was originally a small devotional cabinet picture, later transferred to canvas in the eighteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-pala-di-c: A sacra conversazione altarpiece commissioned for the chapel of Tuzio Costanzo in Castelfranco Veneto, with the enthroned Virgin lifted high above SS. Francis and Nicasius. Giorgione's softly fused light and twilight landscape behind the parapet anticipate the lyrical mood of Venetian painting to come.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-sleeping-: A nude Venus reclines along a hillside, eyes closed, her body echoing the gentle curves of the landscape. Begun by Giorgione and finished after his death by Titian, who is thought to have added the drapery and setting, the picture launched the long line of reclining Venuses culminating in the Urbino Venus.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-the-tempe: A nursing woman sits on the right bank of a stream while a young man with a staff watches from the left, a thunderstorm breaking over the small walled city behind them. Painted in oil on canvas around 1505 and listed in Marcantonio Michiel's notes of 1530, the picture entered the Gallerie dell'Accademia in Venice in 1932.
collection-of-beauty-giorgione-young-wom: A young woman in a fur-trimmed red mantle turns to the viewer with one breast bared against a sprig of laurel, the leaves giving the panel its traditional title. Inscribed on the reverse with the date 1 June 1506, the picture is the earliest dated work by Giorgione and hangs in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-an: Olympian gods picnic in a wooded clearing while Priapus reaches under the sleeping nymph Lotis at right, a satyr filling cups from a wine bowl. Signed by Giovanni Bellini in 1514 for Alfonso d'Este's camerino in Ferrara, the landscape background was overpainted by Titian around 1529 and the picture is now at the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-ch: Christ raises his right hand in blessing and holds a transparent orb in his left, a dawn landscape with cypresses opening behind him. Signed and dated around 1500, the oil-on-panel image is in the Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth and reflects Bellini's late preference for a single, half-length devotional figure.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-cr: Christ hangs on the cross in a walled Jewish cemetery, the foreground crowded with Hebrew-inscribed steles among grasses and wildflowers. Known as the Niccolini da Camugliano Crucifixion and dated around 1480 to 1485, the panel was rediscovered in a private collection and is now held by the Banca Popolare di Vicenza.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-fe: A bearded man in a dark cap and tunic faces three-quarters left against a plain ground, painted in the bust-length format Bellini used for Venetian senators and merchants. The portrait belongs to the cluster of sitter studies he produced through the 1490s as he refined the model later adopted by Giorgione and the young Titian.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-ho: A tiled marble terrace beside a lake gathers the Virgin enthroned, saints, and the infant Christ playing with cherubs beneath an apple tree, while pilgrims and a centaur wander a rocky shore. Long known as the Sacred Allegory, the small panel of around 1490 is one of Bellini's most enigmatic compositions and entered the Uffizi from the Habsburg collection in 1793.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-sa: Jerome reads at the mouth of a rocky grotto with the lion crouched beside him, a fortified town and distant horsemen visible beyond. The oil-on-wood panel, 151 by 113 cm, hangs in the Uffizi and shows Bellini integrating northern landscape detail into a Venetian devotional altarpiece.

Saint Jerome sits reading in a rocky Venetian landscape, his lion resting nearby, the cardinal's hat and crucifix arranged among the stones. The small devotional panel, now in the Barber Institute in Birmingham, is among Bellini's earliest treatments of a hermit-saint subject he would return to throughout his career.
collection-of-beauty-giovanni-bellini-st: Francis stands barefoot outside his rocky cell, arms slightly spread, lit by a raking light that ignites a slender laurel and bends the surrounding plants toward him. Oil on poplar, around 1480, the panel is at the Frick Collection in New York and is among the earliest devotional pictures to place an outdoor landscape on equal footing with the saint.
collection-of-beauty-girl-carrying-a-bas: A young woman trudges along a windswept English coast with her basket, painted during Homer's stay at the fishing village of Cullercoats. The Northumbrian sojourn shifted his palette toward greyed blues and ochres and gave his figures the weathered seriousness that marks his late marines.
collection-of-beauty-girl-in-the-sunligh: Serov's cousin Maria Simonovich rests against a tree at Domotkanovo, dappled sun falling across her blue blouse and a fold of birch trunks behind. Painted in 1888 and acquired by the Tretyakov Gallery, the portrait pairs with Girl with Peaches as the second of the two early canvases that announced Serov as a major colourist.
collection-of-beauty-girl-in-white-by-vi: A young peasant girl in a white pinafore and yellow straw hat stands against a green wheatfield, a hand of red poppies held against her skirt. Painted at Auvers-sur-Oise in June 1890 in the last weeks of Van Gogh's life and now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington, the figure is built up in ribbed parallel touches of green, gold and white.
collection-of-beauty-girl-with-a-hoop: Marie Goujon, aged nine, in a blue dress and sash holding a hoop against a screen of foliage. Oil on canvas painted in 1885 and commissioned by her father, the physician Étienne Goujon, now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, from the Chester Dale Collection.
collection-of-beauty-giuseppe-arcimboldi: Emperor Maximilian II stands with his consort Maria of Austria and their children Anna, Rudolf, and the infant Ernst in a cradle, dressed in mid-century Spanish court fashion. Painted around 1563 after a model from 1553-54, the dynastic group is preserved in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.
collection-of-beauty-giuseppe-arcimboldo: Part of the Four Elements cycle painted for Maximilian II in Vienna, Fire builds a head from candles, oil lamps, flintlocks and burning kindling. Arcimboldo's witty composite portraits flatter the Habsburgs as masters of the elements while showcasing his Mannerist appetite for paradox.

A grizzled head turned in profile, with a wrinkled tree-bark cheek, a cluster of cherries and grapes for the brow, withered leaves for the hair and a stump for the throat. Painted in his final Milanese years around 1590, Arcimboldo collapses the earlier Four Seasons cycle into a single allegorical face about aging and the passage of time.

A profile bust composed entirely of spring blossoms, with a face of pink and white petals, lilies for collar and lips, and a torso of leaves and flowering branches. Painted in 1573 for Emperor Maximilian II, the panel belongs to a Four Seasons set that Arcimboldo presented as a courtly conceit on Habsburg dominion over the natural world.

The painter looks out frontally in a black cap and dark doublet, presenting himself in straightforward likeness rather than as a composite. Drawn in the 1570s while in service to the Habsburg court in Prague, the sheet stands apart from his fruit-and-fish portraits as a record of how Arcimboldo wished to be remembered by his employers.

A profile head built from peaches, cherries, plums, ears of wheat, a cucumber nose, and an artichoke breastplate, the collar inscribed with the artist's name and the date. Painted in 1563 as part of the first Four Seasons cycle for Maximilian II, the panel is now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum, Vienna.

A figure assembled from cellar vessels: a wine cask for the torso, a copper jug for the head, smaller flasks and bottles for the limbs. Painted around 1574 in the same vein as the Seasons and Elements, the image extends Arcimboldo's composite-portrait method from natural produce to the working tools of the imperial wine cellar.
collection-of-beauty-giuseppe-bartolomeo: The chaste Susanna twists away from two leering elders who corner her at her bath, the apocryphal subject a favorite vehicle for the female nude. Chiari, a pupil of Carlo Maratta, paints in a late-Roman Baroque idiom of cool flesh tones and theatrical gesture.
collection-of-beauty-glazunov-by-repin: A three-quarter-length portrait of the young composer Alexander Glazunov, who meets the viewer with a level, brooding gaze, one hand tucked into his dark coat against a deep red ground. Repin works with the loose, painterly attack of his portrait practice in the late 1880s, when he documented much of the Russian musical and literary intelligentsia.
collection-of-beauty-goethe-kugelgen: A sober three-quarter portrait of Goethe at fifty-nine, painted in Weimar by the Dresden academician Gerhard von Kügelgen. The poet wears civil dress against a plain dark ground, the smooth Neoclassical handling presenting him as statesman of letters rather than Romantic genius.
collection-of-beauty-golden-autumn-zolot: A bend in a slow river runs between banks of yellow-leaved birches under a high autumn sky. Isaac Levitan's 1895 canvas, oil on a 58 × 68 cm support and signed at the lower right, was exhibited at the Munich Secession in 1896 and became the public face of the Russian mood landscape.
collection-of-beauty-goltzius-s-right-ha: A virtuoso pen-and-ink study of the artist's own drawing hand, deformed since childhood by a burn. Goltzius turns the disability into a manifesto of skill, building the form from his signature swelling-and-tapering parallel hatchings copied across Europe.
collection-of-beauty-gowy-atalanta-prado: Hippomenes sprints past Atalanta as she stoops for the golden apple of Aphrodite, the wager that costs the huntress her freedom. The Prado canvas is a workshop version after Rubens's design, retaining the diagonal sweep of bodies and the fluttering drapery typical of his Ovidian commissions for Philip IV.
collection-of-beauty-goya-maja-naga2: A reclining nude meets the viewer's gaze without mythological alibi, the first life-size unidealized female nude in Spanish painting. Commissioned by prime minister Manuel Godoy for a private cabinet, the picture later drew the Inquisition's attention to Goya himself.
collection-of-beauty-goya-the-garroted-m: An etching of a condemned prisoner slumped in the iron collar of the garrote, crucifix in hand. Goya pares the scene to a single lit body against deep aquatint shadow, prefiguring the political grimness of the Disasters of War.
collection-of-beauty-goyo-hashiguchi-191: A young woman freshly emerged from the bath gathers her loosened hair, skin warm against the cool indigo of her robe. Hashiguchi, a leading shin-hanga designer, revived the bijin-ga tradition of Utamaro with modern psychological intimacy and richly burnished woodblock printing.
collection-of-beauty-grant-wood-american: A stern Iowa farmer and his daughter stand before a white frame house with a Carpenter Gothic window, the pitchfork echoing the seams of his overalls. Wood used his sister Nan and his dentist as models, fashioning a dry, hard-edged image that became shorthand for rural America.
collection-of-beauty-grecian-interior-le: A scene in the women's quarters of a Greek house, with nudes lounging amid braziers, drapery and patterned tile. The picture is one of Gérôme's Néo-Grec confections, dressing up an academic studio nude in archaeological props derived from Pompeian wall painting.
collection-of-beauty-griffin-met-dp82001: A griffin — eagle's head, beak and wings joined to the body of a lion — stands in profile, its tail curling over its back and its front talons gripping the ground. The small engraving, one of Schongauer's rare secular subjects, bears his monogram below the creature. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, acquired through the Harris Brisbane Dick Fund.
collection-of-beauty-group-portrait-of-t: An assembly of the World of Art group, with Bakst, Benois, Roerich, Somov, Dobuzhinsky, and other members gathered around a table. Painted in 1920 as a study for an unrealised composition, the canvas portrays the Saint Petersburg circle that had shaped Russian fine printing and Diaghilev's early ballet productions before the Revolution dispersed it.
collection-of-beauty-gsskater: William Grant of Congalton glides on the frozen Serpentine in a black coat and hat, arms folded, with skating figures and Westminster trees behind. Stuart's 1782 portrait, exhibited at the Royal Academy, established his London reputation and is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-guercino-martirio-d: A Bolognese Baroque altarpiece depicting the martyrdom of the Roman brothers John and Paul, beheaded under Julian the Apostate. Guercino orchestrates the figures along a steep diagonal, his characteristically warm tenebrism modelling flesh against deep shadow with the loose, painterly touch of his mature Roman period.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-aged-phoenix-i: A withered, balding phoenix stands on stick legs, the grotesque bird rendered in fine etched line on zinc plate. Plate 9 of the Inventionen cycle of eleven satirical etchings made between 1903 and 1905, the work is held by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum and was first shown at the 1906 Munich Secession.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-dancers: Two figures swing through a loose woodcut composition, the angular limbs and reduced palette typical of the Brücke group's early experiments. Made in 1906, the year after Kirchner co-founded Die Brücke in Dresden, the print is held by the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-eiffel-tower: The lattice of the tower rises among the rooftops of Paris in flat planes of orange, green and blue. Painted between 1926 and 1928, the canvas belongs to Delaunay's second Eiffel campaign, in which he reworked aerial photographs taken from a balloon by Schelchner and Omer-Decugis; the painting entered the Solomon R. Guggenheim collection in New York.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-hilterfingen: A sketch of the Lake Thun shoreline at Hilterfingen, drawn from the steamer with quick pencil strokes for the wooded slope above the water. The fifteen-year-old Klee dated the sheet 19 July 1895; it entered the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum as part of the Hilla von Rebay bequest.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-nudes: Two figures lean against a stove in the bare interior of Kirchner's Dresden studio, their bodies sketched in quick, angular contours. The painting belongs to the cycle of studio nudes Kirchner produced around 1908, part of the Brücke programme of working from unprofessional, freely posed models. The canvas is in the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, New York.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-old-woman-and-: An old woman and a young woman in a Davos interior, their faces stretched into angular masks and the room flattened into bands of acid colour. Painted in 1921 and held at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, the canvas dates from Kirchner's Swiss alpine period when he returned figure compositions to the angular tension of his pre-war Brücke work.
collection-of-beauty-gugg-saint-severin-: The ribbed vaults and ambulatory columns of Saint-Séverin in the Latin Quarter buckle inward as if pulled by the weight of stained-glass light. Delaunay made seven canvases of the Gothic church between spring 1909 and early 1910, and this 114 by 89 cm oil belongs to that series. It now hangs at the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum.
collection-of-beauty-gunseondo: From Gunseondo, Kim Hong-do's screen of Daoist Immortals painted in 1776 for the newly enthroned King Jeongjo. Designated National Treasure 139, the work shows the Sennin as full-figured, robust heroes, departing from Kim's linear style and securing his reputation as the leading court painter of the Joseon dynasty.
collection-of-beauty-guo-zhongshu-travel: Cargo ships with stern-mounted rudders glide through a snow-stilled river, accompanied by a smaller craft. Painted in fine ink on silk, the work exemplifies early Song dynasty jiehua, the precise ruled-line technique used to render boats and architecture with engineering accuracy.
collection-of-beauty-gustaf-lundberg-her: The Swedish merchant Herman Petersen sits in a dark coat against a neutral ground, the soft pastel medium giving his face a powdery bloom. Lundberg trained in Paris under Boucher and the pastellist Rosalba Carriera before returning to Stockholm to become the most sought-after portraitist at the court of Adolf Frederick.
collection-of-beauty-gustaf-lundberg-lou: Louis XV is shown in armour beneath the blue sash of the Order of the Holy Spirit, his wig tightly curled in the high court fashion of the late 1730s. Lundberg drew the king in pastel around 1740, the portrait once attributed to Louis-Michel van Loo before research reassigned it to the Swedish pastellist working in Paris.
collection-of-beauty-gustaf-lundberg-mar: Marie Anne de Bourbon-Conde sits in court dress, her powdered coiffure dressed with pearls and a small lace fontange. Lundberg made the 1720 pastel after a painted prototype by Jean-Baptiste Santerre, the Parisian portraitist whose flattering formulae he carried back into Swedish court fashion.
collection-of-beauty-gustaf-lundberg-por: Pastel portrait of the Swedish industrialist and entomologist Friherre Charles de Geer, shown in coat and powdered wig against a neutral ground. Lundberg, court painter in Stockholm after a long apprenticeship in Paris under Boucher and La Tour, built his reputation on exactly these intimate pastel likenesses of Sweden's eighteenth-century aristocracy.

A Swedish sitter in powdered hair and pink-trimmed gown, around the time of her 1750 marriage to the mill owner Vilhelm Schröder. Lundberg trained for two decades in Paris under Boucher's circle before returning to Stockholm as court portraitist, importing the French pastel manner that made him the leading Rococo portraitist in Sweden.
collection-of-beauty-gustav-bauernfeind-: A bustling Damascus thoroughfare rendered with the German Orientalist's exacting eye for tilework, lattice and crowd. Bauernfeind, trained as an architect, treated the city's facades almost archaeologically, balancing photographic detail with the strong overhead light of the Levant.

Pilgrims and worshippers gather between the Mamluk-era Sabil of Qaytbay and the gleaming Dome of the Rock on the Haram al-Sharif. Bauernfeind, who eventually settled in Jerusalem, painted the site repeatedly, prizing the geometry of its mosaic and stone over picturesque incident.

The walled Old City catches first light from the Mount of Olives, the Dome of the Rock luminous above the Kidron Valley. One of Bauernfeind's last major canvases, painted after he made Jerusalem his home, it trades street bustle for an almost devotional topographic stillness.

Figures cluster at the threshold of one of Islam's oldest monuments, the painter dwelling on the carved stone, polychrome marble inlay and worn thresholds of the Bab al-Barid. The composition is typical of Bauernfeind's Damascene pictures, framing dense human activity within rigorously drawn architecture.

An elderly warden stands sentinel in the courtyard of the Umayyad Mosque, his white robe set against patterned stone. Bauernfeind treats the single figure with quiet dignity, the surrounding architecture rendered with the meticulous draftsmanship of his architectural training.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-caillebotte: A solitary oarsman pulls down the Yerres river near the artist's family estate, the viewpoint set startlingly low and close to the rower's straining body. Caillebotte's boating scenes treat leisure with the engineer's eye for mechanism, anticipating the cropped framing of modern photography.

A wet-cobbled Place de Dublin in Haussmann's rebuilt Paris, viewed from Rue de Moscou. Caillebotte, the Impressionists' patron and engineer, here departs from their feathery touch for a cool, photographic precision, deploying steep perspective and a near-life-size foreground couple.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-courbet-029: Painted during Courbet’s 1865 stay at Trouville, this canvas shows a young woman in profile with freshly caught seagulls slung over her shoulder, their wings spilling across the picture plane. The subject came from the fishing life of the Normandy coast, handled with the dense, kneaded paint of Courbet’s Realist maturity.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-courbet-038: A young spinner has fallen asleep at her wheel, distaff drooping in her lap. Courbet treats the rural genre subject with monumental gravity, applying paint thickly with knife and brush so that the homely interior carries the weight of a Salon picture.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-courbet-jo-: A portrait of Joanna Hiffernan, model and lover of Whistler, gazing into a hand mirror as she draws her copper-red hair through her fingers. Courbet painted at least four versions, the dense impasto and earth-toned palette characteristic of his Realist studio practice.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-courbet-la-: A breaking wave rears in heavy impasto under a brooding Channel sky, the horizon pushed high and the surf laid on with palette knife. Courbet painted dozens of these studies on the Normandy coast at Étretat in 1869, treating seascape as a study of matter rather than picturesque incident.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-courbet-le-: A wide-eyed self-portrait, the young Courbet clutching his hair and staring directly out at the viewer. Painted in his early twenties, it announces the confrontational self-fashioning that would define his career and the Realist project.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-la-sie: A recollection of Doré's Spanish travels, figures resting under midday heat in a sun-bleached landscape. Better known as a wood-engraver, Doré painted ambitious oils late in his career, here applying the dramatic chiaroscuro of his book illustrations to a Romantic genre subject.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-la-val: A column of suffering humanity processes through a darkened valley toward the figure of Christ bearing the cross. Painted in Doré's final years and exhibited posthumously, the canvas extends his Bible illustrations into vast, sermon-like oil, with the steep tonal contrasts of his engravings.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-landsc: A Highland glen under turbulent skies, painted after Doré's salmon-fishing expeditions to Scotland in the 1870s. As an Alsatian outside the Parisian academy, he turned to landscape oils late, importing the grand vistas and atmospheric drama of an earlier Romantic generation.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-mont-s: A panoramic view in the Vosges of the wooded heights of Mont Sainte-Odile, ringed by the prehistoric drystone enclosure known as the Pagan Wall. Better remembered for his book illustrations, Doré here works at large scale in oil, treating his native Alsace with a dark Romantic grandeur.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-roland: A wood engraving from Quatrelles' Légende de Croquemitaine, depicting the Carolingian hero Roland in full armour. Doré's chivalric illustration trades on the same dense crosshatching and theatrical lighting that made his Don Quixote and Bible plates ubiquitous in nineteenth-century print culture.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-st-joh: Death rides forth as the pale horseman of Revelation, illustrating Saint John's vision in the Apocalypse. The print belongs to Doré's widely circulated Bible illustrations, where dense wood-engraved hatching and theatrical lighting gave Victorian readers their dominant visual image of scripture.
collection-of-beauty-gustave-dore-the-ho: The frontispiece to Doré's 1866 illustrated Bible: humans and a tigress alike struggle to save their young as the floodwaters rise. Engraved in dense black-and-white from Doré's design, the plate established the visual template for the Deluge in popular imagination for generations.
collection-of-beauty-guy-johnson-by-benj: Colonel Guy Johnson, British superintendent of Indian affairs for the northern colonies, stands in a green ranger's coat beside the Mohawk diplomat Karonghyontye, with Niagara Falls in the distance. West painted the double portrait around 1775 in London during Johnson's visit to lobby for Iroquois alliance. The National Gallery of Art in Washington holds the canvas.
collection-of-beauty-hampstead-heath-by-: View looking across the undulating ground of Hampstead Heath, where Constable lived for stretches of his later life. The British Museum sheet, watercolour at 124 by 206 mm, belongs to the artist's sustained engagement with the Heath as a working subject for cloud and weather studies.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-d-a-00: Katharina Schwarz of Augsburg stands holding the attributes of her name-saint Catherine of Alexandria, the broken wheel and the sword at her side. Painted around 1509 to 1510 as a donor portrait, the panel is among the late works of Hans Holbein the Elder before his move to Issenheim and Lucerne.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-d-a-po: A clean-shaven man in a black cap and dark cloak fills a narrow panel, the modelling concentrated in the smooth planes of cheek and brow. Painted between 1518 and 1520, the portrait is held by the Museo Thyssen-Bornemisza in Madrid and shows the Augsburg branch of the Holbein workshop in its last years.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-d-j-he: The bust of a young woman in a starched white coif inclines slightly to her right, the contours laid in with sharp metalpoint and chalk. Dated 1522, the drawing is an early study from Holbein the Younger's Basel years, before he left for England and the Tudor portraits that would define his late practice.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-da-und: Saint Thecla sits with her back to the viewer in a long mantle, identified by the small lion at her feet. The panel, produced around 1500 in the Augsburg workshop of Hans Holbein the Elder, treats a hagiographic subject rarely depicted in southern German painting of the period.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-der-ju: The Hanseatic merchant stands in his London counting-house among scales, signet rings, a glass vase of carnations, and a quill clock, every object precisely catalogued on the lacquered table. Painted in 1532 for the German Steelyard community at the Thames, the panel is now in the Berlin Gemäldegalerie.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-the-el: The Augsburg master draws his own face in middle age, beard cropped close, eyes set in a thoughtful, sidelong look. Inscribed and dated 1516, the silverpoint sheet is among the latest self-portraits by Hans Holbein the Elder before his move to Issenheim and Lucerne in his final years.

The Virgin lies on her deathbed surrounded by the apostles, one holding a taper, another reading aloud from a book, Christ receiving her soul above. The panel of 1491 to 1492 is part of a Marian altarpiece from the Augsburg workshop of the elder Holbein, father of the better-known portraitist.
collection-of-beauty-hans-holbein-the-yo: Charles de Solier, Sieur de Morette, French ambassador to the English court, stands three-quarter length in a dark fur-trimmed coat, his hand resting on a sword hilt. Holbein painted the panel around 1534 during the sitter's Tudor mission; it entered the Saxon collections in the seventeenth century and now hangs in the Gemäldegalerie Alte Meister, Dresden.

The infant Edward Tudor, future Edward VI, stands frontally in red and gold brocade with his right hand raised in blessing and a golden rattle held like a sceptre in his left. Likely presented to Henry VIII as a New Year's gift in 1539, the panel carries a Latin inscription by Richard Morrison and now belongs to the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

Holbein portrays Edward Tudor, the future Edward VI, as an infant in a red velvet cap and gold-embroidered dress, his right hand raised in a gesture borrowed from adult royal portraiture. A Latin inscription below urges the boy to equal and surpass his father Henry VIII. The panel was likely presented to the king as a New Year's gift in 1539 and now hangs in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.

The painter shows himself in three-quarter view against a gold ground, bearded and cap-clad, his eyes shadowed. Drawn in coloured chalks around 1542, the sheet in the Uffizi was later enlarged and reworked, but enough of the original survives to confirm Holbein's hand in the last year of his life before his death from plague in London.

The Lord Chancellor sits in a green velvet gown with a heavy gold collar of esses, his hands resting on a knee, gaze fixed beyond the viewer. Painted in 1527 during Holbein's first stay in London under Erasmus's introduction, the portrait now hangs at the Frick Collection in New York.

Jean de Dinteville, French ambassador to Henry VIII, stands beside Georges de Selve, Bishop of Lavaur, with a globe, lute, Lutheran hymnal, and astronomical instruments on a shelf strewn between them. Across the foreground lies a famous anamorphic skull, decipherable only from an oblique angle, painted in 1533 and now in the National Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-harlech-castle-from: An early oil painting by J. M. W. Turner of Harlech Castle on its crag above the Welsh coast, seen across the estuary from Tygwyn Ferry in the fading light of a summer evening. Turner exhibited the picture at the Royal Academy in 1799, the year he was elected an Associate of the Academy, translating his watercolour studies of Welsh castles into the atmospheric oil manner of his early maturity. The painting is in the Yale Center for British Art.
collection-of-beauty-harmensz-van-rijn-r: Saskia van Uylenburgh in the guise of the goddess Flora, an enormous garland of tulips and irises crowning her head, a flowered staff in her hand. Signed and dated 1634, the canvas at the Hermitage in Saint Petersburg was painted in the year of Rembrandt's marriage, recasting his young wife in Venetian pastoral fancy dress.
collection-of-beauty-harunobu-2-pers: A pair of figures in the slender, doll-like proportions Harunobu favoured, set within a softly muted interior. He was the pioneer of full-colour nishiki-e printing in 1760s Edo, shifting ukiyo-e away from hand-tinted limited palettes toward layered woodblock impressions.
collection-of-beauty-harunobu-bijin-sur-: An oversized nishiki-e showing a woman on a veranda outside a chamber where a party is underway, parodying the Muken-no-Kane scene from the play Hiragana Seisuiki. Harunobu's mitate updates classical drama into the language of the Edo pleasure quarters, with his characteristically delicate, almost weightless figures.
collection-of-beauty-harunobu-jouvenceau: An unsigned chuban egoyomi, or pictorial calendar print, in which the days of the long and short months are concealed within the design. Harunobu produced these privately commissioned prints for poetry circles in the mid-1760s, and their experiments drove the development of full-colour brocade printing.
collection-of-beauty-harunobu-kanzan-et-: A mitate of the Chinese Chan eccentrics Hanshan and Shide, Jittoku identifiable by his ever-present broom. Harunobu reimagines the Buddhist pair in the contemporary dress of Edo youths, the kind of layered classical-vernacular play that defined his refined nishiki-e output.
collection-of-beauty-harvard-theatre-col: Watercolour set design for Act I of Daphnis and Chloe, with a wooded grove and rocky outcrop sketched in pale washes. Bakst made the drawing in 1912 for the Ballets Russes production choreographed by Fokine to Ravel's score; the sheet survives in the Harvard Theatre Collection at Houghton Library.
collection-of-beauty-harvesting-at-winds: Reapers cut and bind sheaves in the fields below Windsor Castle, whose towers rise on the wooded ridge beyond. West painted the harvest scene in 1795 while serving as Surveyor of the King's Pictures, part of a series of rural subjects for George III recording the royal estate at work.
collection-of-beauty-hasegawa-tohaku-pin: The right wing of the celebrated Pine Trees screens, designated a National Treasure of Japan. Tōhaku, founder of the Hasegawa school, paints the pines with rapid sumi ink in pale wash and dry brush, leaving vast areas of unpainted paper to suggest swirling mist — a high point of Momoyama monochrome ink.
collection-of-beauty-hashiguchi-goyo-wom: A woman in a sheer blue summer kimono draws a comb through her loosened hair, her concentration absolute. Hashiguchi was a leading shin-hanga designer who oversaw every stage of his prints; the work uses mica grounds and subtle keyblock embossing to revive the bijin tradition for the Taishō era.
collection-of-beauty-hasui-kawase-evenin: A shin-hanga woodblock print by Kawase Hasui from 1940. Mount Fuji rises with rose-colored evening light on its snows, framed between the dark trunks and boughs of pines, while a farmer leads a loaded horse cart across the fields of Tagonoura below, a stretch of coast whose views of Fuji have been celebrated since classical poetry. An impression is held by the Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-hasui-kawase-shinag: Rain slants across a canal in Shinagawa's old fishing quarter at dusk: roofed boats lie moored along the bank, a figure under a blue umbrella hurries past the weathered houses, and a single lit window warms the gray-blue scene. The 1931 color woodblock print is characteristic of Hasui's shin-hanga landscapes, which revived the ukiyo-e tradition with Western atmosphere and a fascination for rain, snow, and nightfall. Shinagawa was the first post station of the old Tokaido road out of Edo.
collection-of-beauty-hatred-or-jealousy-: A grimacing head with knotted brow and bared teeth illustrates Hatred or Jealousy, plate from Heads Representing the Various Passions of the Soul published by Robert Sayer in 1765. The series engraves Le Brun's 1668 Paris lecture diagrams, turning the French academy's physiognomic codes into a drawing manual for English students.
collection-of-beauty-hatsuhana-doing-pen: From the series Lives of Wise Women and Virtuous Wives, Hatsuhana of the joruri play Hakone Reigen prays under the icy Tonosawa falls to obtain her crippled husband's revenge. Kuniyoshi treats the ascetic subject with characteristic dynamism, the cascading water rendered in steep blue parallel lines.
collection-of-beauty-havremonet: A canvas of Le Havre's commercial basin, the harbour from which Monet had launched Impression, Sunrise two years earlier. Painted with rapid broken touches, the work continues his investigation of Channel-port atmospheres, where masts, smoke and reflected light become almost interchangeable.
collection-of-beauty-hawaiian-fisherman-: A Native Hawaiian fisherman stands waist-deep in the surf casting his throw-net, the line of the horizon held high in the frame. Bartlett designed the print after settling in Honolulu in 1917, where the outbreak of the First World War turned an intended brief visit into a permanent residency; the woodblock was cut in Watanabe Shōzaburō's Tokyo workshop and is one of only three completed Hawaii subjects in his shin-hanga output.
collection-of-beauty-hayez-francesco-acc: A Venetian noblewoman pauses by the bocca di leone, the lion's-mouth letterbox into which secret denunciations were dropped under the Republic. Hayez, leader of Italian Romantic painting, often coded contemporary Risorgimento politics into such historical scenes, here rendered with his porcelain-smooth flesh and rich brocades.
collection-of-beauty-hayez-lot-con-le-fi: Lot's daughters offer their father wine in a cave above the destroyed city of Sodom, Francesco Hayez's treatment of the episode from Genesis 19. Painted in 1833, the canvas stages the scene in a sharply lit grotto, combining Romantic theatricality with the polished figure modelling Hayez retained from his early years in Canova's circle in Rome. The work is recorded in both major catalogues raisonnes of the artist.
collection-of-beauty-hayez-selbstportrat: A late self-portrait at age seventy-eight, the Milanese master appraising himself with calm, unflattering directness. The restrained palette and tightly painted head reflect the academic rigour Hayez upheld at the Brera even as Romanticism gave way to verismo.
collection-of-beauty-hayez-tamar-di-giud: The biblical Tamar, daughter-in-law of Judah, is rendered as a brooding half-length figure veiled in shadowed reds. Hayez, the central painter of Italian Romanticism, treats Old Testament heroines with the same charged sensuality and theatrical chiaroscuro he brought to his patriotic allegories.
collection-of-beauty-head-of-a-monk-1625: A bowed monk's head in profile, the cowl shading the face while bold parallel hatching models the cheek and brow. Brush drawing in brown wash measuring 277 by 196 mm, held by the British Museum, the sheet belongs to the body of studies Zurbarán made for the austere Carthusian and Mercedarian friars who populate his Seville altarpieces.
collection-of-beauty-head-of-cyrus-broug: Herodotus' Massagetae queen receives the severed head of the Persian king Cyrus, whom she will plunge into a vessel of blood. Rubens stages the Antwerp workshop's signature pile-up of muscular soldiery and silken courtiers, the carmine drapery and pearled flesh tones unmistakably his.
collection-of-beauty-heirin-ji-nobidome-: A late woodblock print by Kawase Hasui, published in 1952, of Heirin-ji, a Rinzai Zen temple at Nobidome in Saitama prefecture. The temple's dark timber gate stands in deep shadow while sunlight breaks through the foliage in bright patches across the flagstone path, autumn maples burning orange in the middle distance. An impression is held by the Aichi Prefectural Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-hendrick-goltzius-d: The Terentian motto — without Ceres and Bacchus, Venus grows cold — is set as a chiaroscuro nocturne, the goddess illuminated by a torch held by a satyr. Goltzius, the virtuoso Haarlem engraver, here works with brush on prepared ground in his late painterly mode.
collection-of-beauty-hendrick-goltzius-f: The colossal Farnese Hercules, leaning on his club with the apples of the Hesperides behind his back, observed from below by two awed connoisseurs. Goltzius' celebrated engraving exaggerates the antique's swelling musculature with his trademark swelling-and-tapering burin lines.
collection-of-beauty-hendrick-goltzius-p: The Haarlem brewer and shell connoisseur is shown surrounded by exotic conches and a nautilus, emblems of the Wunderkammer culture flourishing in the early Dutch Republic. Goltzius records both the sitter's penetrating gaze and the iridescence of his collection with equal precision.
collection-of-beauty-hendrick-martensz-s: A young man tunes his lute in a quiet Rotterdam interior, a music sheet open before him. Sorgh, a pupil of Teniers and Buytewech, specialised in such genteel domestic genre scenes, building tone with a warm brown ground beneath crisp local colour.
collection-of-beauty-hendrik-avercamp-wi: Skaters, kolf players and bundled townsfolk fan out across a frozen canal under a low pearly sky. The deaf-mute Avercamp made the panoramic winter landscape his exclusive subject, populating each ice with hundreds of carefully observed figures in a high horizon line inherited from Bruegel.
collection-of-beauty-henri-fantin-latour: A group portrait of the avant-garde gathered around Manet at his easel, with Renoir, Bazille, Monet and Zola among the standing figures. Fantin-Latour records the Batignolles circle as a sober Salon homage, painted in the muted blacks and greys he preferred to his friends' brighter palette.

Roses, peaches and grapes are arrayed on a plain tabletop against a neutral ground. Fantin-Latour's still lifes, prized in England via his dealer Edwin Edwards, distil the Dutch tradition into quiet, almost photographic studies of bloom and bloom-bearing skin.

The English etcher and printer Edwin Edwards sits at his desk while his wife Ruth stands behind him, both rendered in Fantin's habitual sober blacks. The Edwardses were the artist's closest patrons, channelling his still lifes into the lucrative London market.

A glass carafe, scattered fruit and a small bouquet are composed on a dark cloth in disciplined Salon order. Among Fantin-Latour's earliest mature still lifes, it shows the precise tonal modelling that drew Whistler's circle to his work.

A loose spring bouquet — striped and red tulips, yellow wallflowers, clusters of small daisy-like blooms and a sprig of lilac — fills a round glass vase, with a white porcelain coffee cup, saucer and silver spoon set before it on the polished tabletop. The canvas is signed and dated at lower right. Fantin-Latour built much of his reputation on quiet flower pieces of exactly this kind, which found an especially eager market among English collectors.
collection-of-beauty-henri-julien-felix-: Two costumed lovers stand at the edge of a leafless winter wood beneath a cold full moon, a tiny lit lantern hovering at the treeline. One of Rousseau's earliest important canvases, it already shows the naive precision of silhouette and dreamlike stillness that would define the Douanier's vision.
collection-of-beauty-henri-matisse-1902-: The cathedral seen from Matisse's quai Saint-Michel apartment late on a winter afternoon, its towers reduced to slate-blue silhouettes over the Seine. Painted on paper during a precarious year before Fauvism, the picture already pushes structural colour ahead of topographical accuracy.
collection-of-beauty-henri-matisse-1920-: A reclining model in striped pantaloons inhabits the patterned Nice studio Matisse converted into a North African stage set. The early Riviera odalisques mark his return to sensuous, decorative figuration after the austerity of the war years.
collection-of-beauty-henri-meunier04: A poster, L'Heure du Silence, by the Belgian Art Nouveau designer Henri Meunier, lithographed in the flat planes and sinuous contour the Brussels school adopted from Japanese prints. Meunier worked extensively in advertising, treating commercial commissions with the same graphic refinement as his fine-art prints.
collection-of-beauty-henri-rousseau-la-e: A dark silhouetted figure pipes serpents from a moonlit jungle on a riverbank, commissioned by the mother of Robert Delaunay. Rousseau, a self-taught customs officer, never left France; his jungles were composed from the Jardin des Plantes, picture books and dream, layered in his deliberate, flattened naïve manner.
collection-of-beauty-henri-rousseau-the-: In a dense jungle at sunset, a lion sinks its teeth into the neck of a collapsing antelope while other creatures — an owl among the branches, a dark feline half-hidden in the foliage — look on. Rousseau exhibited the huge canvas at the 1905 Salon d'Automne with a long narrative caption, in the same room as Matisse and his circle, whose paintings prompted the label 'fauves.' It is now in the Fondation Beyeler near Basel.
collection-of-beauty-henry-fuseli-titani: The fairy queen, drugged by Oberon's love-juice, fawns over the ass-headed weaver from A Midsummer Night's Dream. Fuseli, a key contributor to Boydell's Shakespeare Gallery, exaggerates limbs and eyes into a mannerist dream-language drawn from Michelangelo and his own night terrors.
collection-of-beauty-henry-laurens-1782-: The South Carolina statesman Henry Laurens sits at a writing table in a dark coat, a quill and papers at hand. Copley painted Laurens in London in 1782 shortly after his release from the Tower of London, where he had been held for two years as a captured American envoy.
collection-of-beauty-henry-rice-met-dp20: Boston merchant Henry Rice sits in a dark coat and high white collar against a misted sky, the loose brushwork of the unfinished cravat typical of Stuart's late style. The picture, painted around 1815, entered the Metropolitan Museum's collection and reflects Stuart's final decade as the preferred portraitist of the New England mercantile class.
collection-of-beauty-henry-viii-of-engla: The Tudor king fills the panel frontally, broad-shouldered in slashed white silks and gold chains, his small eyes set above a bull neck. Painted around 1537, the type was disseminated through workshop versions after Holbein's lost Whitehall mural, fixing the image of Henry VIII that survives in every later reproduction.
collection-of-beauty-hercules-lucha-con-: Hercules grapples with the many-headed Hydra of Lerna, his muscular body twisting against the dark serpentine coils. The canvas belongs to a series of ten Labours of Hercules painted for the Hall of Realms in the Buen Retiro Palace, where Zurbarán's stark tenebrism set the hero against an almost theatrical void.
collection-of-beauty-het-drijvende-pavil: A lantern-lit wooden temple stands on the snowy shore of Lake Biwa during a night snowfall. Tsuchiya Kōitsu's 1934 print exemplifies the Watanabe Shin-hanga workshop's mastery of weather and luminous nocturne.
collection-of-beauty-het-suwa-meer-in-de: Hokusai's view across Lake Suwa, with Mount Fuji on the far horizon and a shrine and two windswept pines on a rocky outcrop in the foreground. The sheet belongs to the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, printed by Nishimura Yohachi in shades of blue using imported Prussian pigment.
collection-of-beauty-het-zojo-heiligdom-: The Zōjō-ji temple at Shiba, captured by Kawase Hasui for Twenty Views of Tokyo. Hasui became the most prolific landscape designer of the Shin-hanga revival, working closely with the publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō from the early 1920s.
collection-of-beauty-hieronymus-bosch-th: When closed, the triptych shows the world on the third day of Creation in grisaille: a translucent globe enclosing a dark, watery earth, with God depicted small in the upper left. The muted tonality contrasts sharply with the saturated colour of the interior panels, framing the work as an unfolding cosmological drama.

A pen drawing illustrating the Flemish proverb that walls and woods betray secrets, with eyes scattered through the meadow and ears sprouting on tree trunks. The sheet, in the Berlin Kupferstichkabinett, is among the few autograph drawings linking Bosch's moralising imagination to his painted demonology.
collection-of-beauty-hieronymus-bosch-tr: The desert hermit Anthony is besieged by a phantasmagoria of hybrid demons, burning villages and blasphemous rites across three panels now in Lisbon. Bosch's most influential triptych, it codified the visual vocabulary of grotesque temptation that fed Bruegel and the later Surrealists alike.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshi-yoshida-hik: Two sailing junks lean before the wind on the dazzled water of the Inland Sea. From the Setonaikai series, the print is one of six in which Yoshida had identical blocks printed in different lighting keys, demonstrating his mastery of multi-impression woodblock colour.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshi-yoshida-kum: Pale clouds of Kumoi cherry blossom hang over a Japanese garden in the soft tonal gradations Yoshida coaxed from up to thirty separate woodblock impressions. Trained in Western oil painting before turning to shin-hanga, he supervised every stage of carving and printing personally.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshi-yoshida-yom: A color woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida of the Yomeimon, the lavishly carved and gilded gate of the Tosho-gu shrine at Nikko, with small figures on the steps below and towering cedars closing in behind. Yoshida renders the gate's dense ornament in a subdued harmony of golds and greys, capturing the gleam of gilding in deep forest shade. The print was made in 1937.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-1838-two-: Two mandarin ducks float together among reeds, the drake's plumage rendered in patterned blocks of vermilion, ochre, and indigo. Paired oshidori were a long-standing kachō-e symbol of marital devotion; Hiroshige treats the subject with the calligraphic economy of his late bird-and-flower work.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-53-statio: A daimyō procession sets out across Edo's Nihonbashi bridge at dawn, opening Hiroshige's Tokaido Road series for the publisher Hōeidō. The print establishes the journey's ceremonial scale before the road's weather and incident take over.

Travellers cross the open plain at Hara station while Mount Fuji rises in pink-tinged morning light, breaking the sheet's upper border. The Hōeidō Tokaido is among the most successful print series of the Edo period, sold in tens of thousands of impressions.

Three muffled figures trudge through deep night snow at Kanbara, the white sky bokashi-graded into a heavy grey. Long counted among Hiroshige's finest landscape prints, the design treats silence and stillness as subject in their own right.

Travellers approach a thatched teahouse on the windswept Sarugababa heath outside Futagawa station. Hiroshige builds the scene from broad fields of muted ochre and pine green typical of the Hōeidō Tōkaidō's middle stretch.

Workmen scaffold the Toyokawa River bridge at Yoshida station while Yoshida castle rises beyond. Hiroshige uses the diagonal of the bridgework as a vehicle for his characteristic recession into atmospheric distance.

Serving women aggressively haul reluctant travellers into an inn at Goyu, a stock comic episode of the Tōkaidō. The print is one of several in the series in which Hiroshige slips genre observation into what is nominally a landscape.

An Akasaka inn courtyard is shown in cross-section: maids preparing to receive guests on one side, bathing travellers on the other, separated by a clipped sago palm. The bird's-eye plan demonstrates the architectural curiosity Hiroshige brought to genre interiors.

Station Chiryū from the Tōkaidō series, depicting the early-summer horse fair on a grassy plain where merchants and tethered animals scatter under wide skies. Hiroshige uses subtle bokashi gradations along the horizon to evoke seasonal atmosphere; the Hoeidō publisher seal marks this as part of his career-making 1833 edition.

Station Yokkaichi shows a lone traveler bracing against the wind beside the Mie River, a hat tumbling away across the reeds. The sweeping diagonals and muted blues are characteristic of Hiroshige's Hoeidō Tōkaidō, a series that fixed the iconography of journey and weather in Edo print culture.

The penultimate station of the Tōkaidō, Kusatsu was famed for its meibutsu tateba teahouse where porters rested with fast palanquins. Hiroshige captures the bustle of arriving travelers under banners, his linework crisp and his palette anchored by the deep indigo blues of the early Hoeidō printing.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-a-large-w: From the late series Famous Views of the Sixty-odd Provinces, this vertical print shows the Yōrō Falls of Mino plunging through a wooded ravine. Hiroshige exploits the tall format to stretch the cataract into a single white ribbon against deep green cliffs, with figures dwarfed at its base.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-a-shrine-: A small wayside shrine stands half-hidden in a stand of trees on an open moor, its torii a quiet vertical accent in the landscape. Hiroshige favored such modest sacred sites in his rural views, treating them as pauses in the broader rhythm of travel.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-atake-sou: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, figures hurry across the Shin-Ōhashi bridge as a sudden summer downpour falls in fine engraved lines over the Sumida. The compressed perspective and slanting rain made the print a touchstone for European Japonisme; Van Gogh later copied it in oil.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-full-moon: The Autumn Moon at Ishiyama Temple, from Eight Views of Ōmi, shows the bright disc rising over Lake Biwa behind the temple's wooded bluff. Hiroshige draws on the classical meisho tradition, pairing a literary scenic theme with his characteristic graded blue skies.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-heavy-rai: Night Rain at Karasaki, from Eight Views of Ōmi, isolates the great pine of Karasaki shrine as wind and rain lash its dark canopy. The near-monochrome palette and dense parallel lines give the print the hush of a literary classical theme treated in late ukiyo-e.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-traveller: Figures hurry across a wooden bridge as a slate-grey downpour streaks the air in fine parallel lines, a device Hiroshige made his signature for sudden weather. The composition's daring crop and atmospheric mood would later astonish Whistler and Van Gogh.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige-view-of-a: Evening Glow at Seta, from Eight Views of Ōmi, depicts the Karahashi bridge stretching across the southern reaches of Lake Biwa under a flushed sky. Hiroshige uses bokashi gradations to model dusk, a printing technique that gives the series its meditative tonal character.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige11-hakone: Hakone, the most mountainous station of the Tōkaidō, rises in jagged, faceted peaks shaded in flat planes of color. A small daimyō procession threads through the pass beside Lake Ashi, a composition Hiroshige used to dramatize the human scale against terrain.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige19-ejiri: Ejiri, set on Suruga Bay near the Miho pine grove, looks across a calm inlet dotted with sailing boats. Hiroshige flattens the distance into bands of graded color, a hallmark of his ukiyo-e landscape mode that influenced later Western printmakers.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige20-fuchu: Travelers ford the Abe River at Fuchu, carried piggyback or on platforms by the station's licensed porters. The rhythmic figures across the shallow water exemplify Hiroshige's interest in the practical theater of travel along the Tōkaidō road.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige22-okabe: The Okabe station turns inland through the gorge of Utsu Pass, where a stony stream cuts between steep wooded slopes. Hiroshige's compressed verticals and overlapping rocks give the print a closed, intimate atmosphere unusual for the series.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige25-kanaya: Kanaya sits on the western bank of the Ōi River, reached only by porters who carried travelers across its broad flats. Hiroshige looks down on the receding scene from a high vantage, ordering the mountains and water into clean horizontal registers.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige28-fukuroi: At Fukuroi, travelers rest at a tea stand pitched beneath a leafy tree, a kettle steaming on the open fire. The genre vignette is set against a low, level landscape, demonstrating Hiroshige's gift for everyday observation within the Tōkaidō format.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige30-hamamat: Hamamatsu features a great solitary pine on a windswept field, with figures gathered around a small fire at its base. The motif distills Hiroshige's recurring concern with weather and season, the bare branches and grey sky reading as winter on the road.
collection-of-beauty-hiroshige38-fujikaw: Fujikawa shows a daimyō procession entering the station under banners, met by villagers prostrated in formal greeting. The print documents the parade etiquette of sankin-kōtai, the alternate-attendance system that drove Tōkaidō traffic in the Edo period.
