Monet's brief 1886 Holland trip yielded five tulip-field canvases, in which the riot of cultivated colour gave him a ready-made experiment in pure chroma.
collection-of-beauty-monet-veduta-di-rou: A youthful landscape of Rouelles in the Le Havre hinterland, often cited as Monet's earliest surviving oil. The careful, almost Corot-like handling of trees and stream marks the threshold before his conversion to outdoor, sketch-based painting.
collection-of-beauty-monet-view-of-bordi: Painted on Monet's 1884 Italian Riviera campaign at Bordighera, where the unfamiliar light and exotic vegetation pushed his palette toward hot pinks, oranges, and turquoise. The Mediterranean produced what he called colours he had to invent.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w-106: A coastal scene from Monet's formative years on the Channel, when he was working alongside Boudin and Jongkind. The handling is broader than academic landscape of the period and already shows his interest in transient light over fixed topography.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w-208: Painted in the early 1870s as Monet established the visual language of Impressionism, the picture trades finish for immediacy, applying paint in mosaic-like touches. Works of these years preceded and prepared the 1874 group exhibition that gave the movement its name.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w-235: A river or harbour subject from 1872, the year of the famous Impression, Sunrise, sharing its concern with reflections, vapour, and the dissolution of form on water. The vibrating shorthand of small coloured strokes marks Monet's break with conventional finish.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w-272-apple-t: Apple trees in full blossom, their pinkish-white canopies set against fresh spring green and dabbed in short broken strokes. The subject was a favourite of the early Impressionists, who valued orchards as outdoor studios where colour and light could be studied together.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w-290-autumn-: A view along the Seine at Argenteuil, where Monet was based through much of the 1870s, painted at the moment when foliage flares into copper and gold. The water carries the autumn colour back as a lattice of broken reflections, a hallmark of his river pictures from these years.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w-338: Painted during the year of the first Impressionist exhibition, this work shows Monet's mature open-air method fully formed. Pigment is laid down in distinct touches that resolve into atmosphere only at viewing distance, refusing the smooth surface prized by the Salon.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w-42: An early landscape from Monet's mid-twenties, when he was painting outdoors in the forest of Fontainebleau and along the Norman coast. The dark tonal range and tighter handling reflect his Barbizon-school roots before the lighter Impressionist palette emerged.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w-763-the-pat: A garden or woodland path drawing the viewer between flanking masses of foliage, painted with the interwoven greens and lilacs typical of Monet's Giverny work. The motif reduces landscape to a corridor of pure colour and dappled shade.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w0145: A snow-covered country road caught in the last warm light of a winter sunset, painted in 1869. The picture passed through the celebrated Max Silberberg collection and is now in the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rouen (43 × 65 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1001: A country road near Giverny, the Norman village where Monet had settled in 1883, painted in 1885 (65 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1001; the work remains in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1003: A view of the Seine valley at Port-Villez, the hamlet on the river bank opposite Giverny, painted in 1885 (65 x 92 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1003 and held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1010: A view of the Falaise d'Amont, one of the chalk cliffs framing the beach at Étretat on the Normandy coast, painted during Monet's 1885 campaign there. Wildenstein 1010; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1016: The chalk cliff of the Falaise d'Aval at Etretat on the Normandy coast, silhouetted against a setting sun, painted during Monet's 1885 campaign there (81 x 100 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1016, it now hangs in the Pola Museum of Art in Hakone, Japan.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1018: A view of the Porte d'Aval, the great natural chalk arch at Étretat on the Normandy coast, painted during Monet's 1885 stay. Wildenstein 1018; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1032: Sailboats run before the wind beneath the Aiguille — the slender needle rock that rises off the cliffs of Étretat on the Normandy coast. Claude Monet returned to Étretat repeatedly through the 1880s, treating its arches, rocks, and weather in a sustained series catalogued by Daniel Wildenstein as W.1032 and its neighbours.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1035: The Manneporte, the largest of the three natural rock arches at Etretat, painted at high tide during Monet's 1885 stay on the Normandy coast (65 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1035; private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1042: The Aiguille (rock needle) and the Porte d'Aval arch at Etretat seen from the west, painted in 1886 in an unusual vertical format (81 x 65 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1042, it belongs to the Kreeger Museum in Washington, D.C.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1048: Heavy seas break against the cliff face beneath the Porte d'Amont, the northern of Étretat's three natural arches. Monet treated the Étretat coast in a long sequence of canvases through the mid-1880s, captured in Wildenstein's catalogue raisonné as W.1048 among neighbouring entries.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1050: The needle rock at Etretat framed through the arch of the Porte d'Aval, painted in 1886 (73 x 92 cm). One of several canvases Monet devoted to this view; catalogued as Wildenstein 1050 and held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1054: A snow-covered landscape at Falaise, a hamlet near Giverny, painted in the hard winter of 1885-86 (66 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1054; private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1056: A winter scene at Limetz, a village on the Epte just upstream from Giverny, painted during the snowy winter of 1885-86 (65 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1056 (Effet de neige a Limetz); Wikidata records it in the Hasso Plattner Collection at the Museum Barberini, Potsdam.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1061: A broad view of Vernon on the Seine, the small town a short distance downstream from Monet's home at Giverny. Catalogued in Wildenstein as W.1061, the canvas belongs to the painter's quieter landscapes of the Seine valley made alongside his more famous Giverny garden series.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1065: Fruit trees in spring blossom near Giverny, painted in 1886 (65 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1065 and held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1075: A plein-air figure study from 1886 (102.5 x 75 cm) related to Monet's two large Woman with a Parasol canvases of that year, for which his stepdaughter Suzanne Hoschede posed on a riverbank near Giverny. Catalogued as Wildenstein 1075; private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w108: A portrait of the artist's infant son Jean Monet asleep, painted in 1868 (42 x 50 cm) during the family's straitened years on the Normandy coast. Catalogued as Wildenstein 108, it belongs to the Ny Carlsberg Glyptotek in Copenhagen.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1089: Wave-battered rocks on the wild Atlantic coast of Belle-Ile-en-Mer, Brittany, painted during Monet's ten-week campaign there in autumn 1886 (65 x 81 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1089; private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w109: Heavy seas breaking against the pier at Le Havre, with the harbour lighthouse beyond, painted in 1868. At 147 × 226 cm it is one of the very large marine compositions of Monet's Salon-ambitious early years. Private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1120: A squall of rain sweeping the coast of Belle-Ile-en-Mer, painted in an unusual square format (60 x 60 cm) during Monet's stormy autumn 1886 stay in Brittany. Catalogued as Wildenstein 1120; Wikidata places it in the Musee des Beaux-Arts de Morlaix.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1121: Rain over the rocky coast of Belle-Ile-en-Mer in Brittany, painted in autumn 1886 (60 x 73 cm), a companion to the square-format version of the same subject. Catalogued as Wildenstein 1121; private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1135: Part of Monet's poplar series on the banks of the Epte, painted from a flat-bottomed boat moored among the trees. The verticals march across the canvas in a near-decorative rhythm, sunlight filtered into juxtaposed greens, lavenders and rose.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1138: A field of irises near Monet's house at Giverny, painted in 1887 in a strongly horizontal format (45 x 100 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1138; a close variant, Field of Yellow Irises (W1137), is in the Musee Marmottan Monet. Private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1155: Poplar trees in the meadows near Giverny, painted in 1887 (73 x 92 cm), several years before Monet's famous 1891 Poplars series on the Epte. Catalogued as Wildenstein 1155; Wikidata records it in the Hasso Plattner Collection at the Museum Barberini, Potsdam.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1179: A view across the Mediterranean from Antibes toward the snow-capped Alps, painted during Monet's early-1888 campaign on the Cote d'Azur (59 x 84 cm). Also known as The Mediterranean at Antibes; catalogued as Wildenstein 1179 and held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1200: One of Monet's paintings of the meadows around his home at Giverny, recording the light of early morning across the fields in 1888. Wildenstein 1200; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1245: A spring landscape of the meadows at Giverny painted in 1890, part of Monet's sustained study of the fields around his home under changing seasons. Wildenstein 1245; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1296: One of Monet's 1891 Poplars series, showing the trees lining the River Epte near Giverny at dusk (100 x 65 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1296 (Peupliers au bord de l'Epte, crepuscule); Wikipedia places it in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1336: Ice floes drifting on the Seine near Bennecourt during the freeze of winter 1893 (65 x 100 cm), part of a small group of ice-breakup canvases that includes the Metropolitan Museum's Ice Floes (W1335). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1336; private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1370: A view of the Seine at Port-Villez, near Giverny, painted in 1894 (La Seine à Port-Villez). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1370, it belongs to the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Rouen.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w148: The road at Louveciennes under melting snow, lit by a low winter sunset, painted in 1869. It dates from the winter Monet spent working in the villages west of Paris alongside Pissarro, testing how much colour a white landscape could hold. Private collection (40 × 54 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1524: From the Charing Cross Bridge series painted on visits to London between 1899 and 1904. Monet worked from a balcony at the Savoy, watching trains cross the Thames as fog and smoke turned bridge and water into shimmering bars of mauve and gold.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1558: From the London series Monet painted from his rooms at the Savoy Hotel between 1899 and 1901, showing Waterloo Bridge under an overcast sky with the smoking chimneys of the south bank beyond. Wildenstein 1558; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1563: Waterloo Bridge over the Thames under an overcast sky, from Monet's London series painted from his window at the Savoy Hotel between 1899 and 1901 (65 x 100 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1563; private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w159: Camille Doncieux on the beach at Trouville during the family's stay in the summer of 1870, painted in the open air with sand reportedly still embedded in the paint. The handling is rapid and sketch-like, capturing wind, light and the moment of leisure.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1636: A morning view of the village of Vetheuil across the Seine, painted in 1901 when Monet returned to motifs from his 1878-1881 residence there (89 x 92 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1636 (Vetheuil, effet du matin); private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1656: From the early water-lily series of 1903, showing clouds reflected on the surface of the lily pond at Giverny (Le bassin des nymphéas, nuages). Wildenstein 1656; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1668: The Japanese footbridge arching over the water-lily pond in Monet's garden at Giverny, painted in 1905 (90 x 100 cm). Catalogued as Wildenstein 1668; private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1675: One of the Nymphéas canvases Monet painted in his water-lily pond at Giverny in 1905, catalogued as W.1675 in the Wildenstein catalogue raisonné. The square-format composition (89 x 92 cm) fills the frame with floating lily pads and reflections, dispensing with any horizon line. It is held in a private collection in the United States.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1695: A Nymphéas canvas from 1907, part of Monet's long series painted in the water garden at Giverny and catalogued as W.1695 in the Wildenstein catalogue raisonné. The painting belongs to the Mohamed Mahmoud Khalil Museum in Cairo.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1708: An early canvas from the Water Lilies series begun in earnest after 1903, when Monet shifted from views of the Japanese bridge to the pond's surface alone. Floating pads anchor a shimmering ground in which clouds and willows are fused as reflection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1725: One of the water-lily canvases of 1908, in which the pond surface fills the entire frame and the water lilies float against reflections of sky and foliage. Wildenstein 1725; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1726: A water-lily canvas of 1908 from the Giverny pond series, with the flowers scattered across a mirror-like surface of reflected light. Wildenstein 1726; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1781: A late view of the lily pond at Giverny with the rose arches of the garden (Bassin aux nymphéas, les rosiers), painted between 1914 and 1917. Wildenstein 1781; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1786: A large late water-lily canvas (130 x 150 cm) painted between 1914 and 1917, when Monet was working toward the monumental Grandes Décorations. Wildenstein 1786; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w182: Windmills along the waterways of Zaandam, painted during Monet's stay in Holland in 1871 as he returned from his London exile after the Franco-Prussian War. The Dutch canals and mills furnished him with some two dozen canvases that year. Private collection (48 × 73 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1883: A canvas from the Japanese-bridge and water-garden series of Monet's last years, painted as his cataracts deepened and his palette warmed toward reds and oranges. Form gives way almost entirely to colour and reflected light.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1884: One of the monumental late water-lily canvases (about 130 x 200 cm) Monet painted in his water garden at Giverny around 1917-1919, catalogued as Wildenstein 1884 under the French title Le Bassin aux nympheas. Wikidata records it in the Hasso Plattner Collection at the Museum Barberini, Potsdam.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1897: A large late canvas of the lily pond at Giverny (100 x 200 cm), painted between 1917 and 1919 in the loose, immersive manner of the Grandes Décorations years. Wildenstein 1897; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1900: A two-metre-wide late canvas of the Giverny lily pond painted between 1917 and 1920. Catalogued as Wildenstein 1900, it entered the National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art in Seoul as part of the Lee Kun-hee collection donation.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w197: The town of Argenteuil viewed from the petit bras, the quiet side channel of the Seine around the Île Marante, painted in 1872 during Monet's first year living there. The small arm became one of his favourite early Argenteuil motifs. Private collection (50 × 65 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w1976: The centre panel of the monumental Agapanthus triptych (Wildenstein 1975-1977), a roughly two-by-four-metre canvas painted at Giverny between about 1915 and 1926. This panel belongs to the Saint Louis Art Museum; its companions are in the Cleveland Museum of Art and the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w199: A spring landscape painted at Argenteuil in 1872, shortly after Monet settled in the town on the Seine that became the heartland of early Impressionism. The painting (W.199) is in the Portland Museum of Art in Maine.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w222: An Argenteuil scene from the year of the first Impressionist exhibition's gestation. Monet works en plein air, registering reflections on water and the play of leaves with rapid, divided touches.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w224: The Seine at Argenteuil in late-afternoon light, with a sailboat resting on the broad reach of the river, painted in 1872. The horizon sits low, giving most of the canvas to sky and water. Private collection (60 × 81 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w24: The road running past the Saint-Siméon farm above Honfleur, painted around 1863-64 during Monet's earliest Normandy campaigns. The farm's inn was the gathering place of Boudin, Jongkind and the other plein-air painters who mentored the young Monet. Wikidata records the canvas (59 × 80 cm) in the collection of the Bank of Italy.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w265: Sailboats off Sainte-Adresse, the resort beach just north of Le Havre where Monet had painted since the mid-1860s. This canvas dates from an 1873 return to the Normandy coast at the height of his Argenteuil years. Private collection (48 × 74 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w288-the-shel: A tree-lined country path painted in 1873, during Monet's productive years at Argenteuil. The painting (W.288) belongs to the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w327: A stretch of the Seine near Argenteuil, painted in 1874, the year of the first Impressionist exhibition. River, bank and sky are knit together in the broken touch Monet had made his signature on this water. Private collection (55 × 66 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w357: Argenteuil under snow, painted during the hard winter of 1875 when Monet produced an extended group of snow effects around the town. The canvas (55 × 74 cm) is now in the Musée d'Art et d'Histoire in Geneva.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w368: Pleasure boats moored on the Seine at Argenteuil, painted in 1875. The boat basin, with its rented sailboats and weekend traffic from Paris, was among the motifs Monet repeated most often during his years there. Private collection (54 × 65 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w386: Monet's family in the garden of their Argenteuil home, painted in 1875. It belongs to the run of domestic garden pictures from these years in which figures sit half-absorbed into beds of flowers and foliage. Private collection (61 × 80 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w392: Monet's floating studio, a converted boat moored on the Seine that let him paint from the water itself. Manet had recorded him at work in it; here the vessel becomes the subject, half-shaded under a bank of trees.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w397: A pruned, ball-shaped tree standing at the water's edge at Argenteuil, its round crown doubled in the river's reflection, painted in 1876. Monet makes the mirrored geometry of tree and reflection the whole subject. Private collection (60 × 81 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w419: The Pond at Montgeron, painted at the country estate of the collector Ernest Hoschede, who commissioned a group of decorative panels from Monet. Reflections on still water already prefigure the Giverny obsession to come.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w421: A train arriving at Montgeron, painted during Monet's 1876 stay at Ernest Hoschedé's estate of Rottembourg outside Paris. The railway subject anticipates the Gare Saint-Lazare series he would begin the following year. Private collection (81 × 60 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w429: Evening at Argenteuil, in which the Seine carries the warm pinks and lilacs of a fading sky. Sailboats are noted with a few economical strokes, the picture organised entirely by horizontal bands of reflected light.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w433: A hunting scene from 1876, an unusual subject for Monet, who almost never painted narrative motifs. It belongs to the decorative panels commissioned by Ernest Hoschede for the chateau de Rottembourg at Montgeron.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w472: A bouquet of gladioli, from the brief stretch of still life Monet produced after settling at Vetheuil. The blossoms are massed in vertical accents of red and pink, paint laid on thickly to register petal against petal.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w502: The country road leading into Vétheuil, painted in 1878, the year Monet moved his family to the small Seine village downstream from Paris. The roads and fields around the town occupied him as much as the river itself. Private collection (49.5 × 60 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w526: A view of Vétheuil and the Seine valley around it, painted in 1879 during Monet's difficult first years in the village. The canvas (60 × 73 cm) is in the Musée d'Orsay, Paris.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w579-springti: A view of Vétheuil in spring, painted in 1880 while Monet was living in the small village on the Seine downstream from Paris. The painting (W.579) is in the Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen in Rotterdam.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w58: A path cutting through tall trees, painted in 1865 when Monet was working in the Forest of Fontainebleau around Chailly while preparing his Déjeuner sur l'herbe. The canvas (79 × 58 cm) is held in the Rau Collection for UNICEF at the Arp Museum Bahnhof Rolandseck in Remagen, Germany.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w593-1: A field of red poppies set against summer greens, the kind of motif Monet revisited near Vetheuil and Giverny. Dabs of vermilion are scattered with calligraphic ease across a haze of grass, demonstrating his interest in saturated complementary colour.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w601: The quiet side channel of the Seine at Vétheuil, painted in 1880 as Monet worked obsessively along the river's bends around the village. Private collection (68.5 × 90 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w611: A landscape of willow trees painted in 1880 during Monet's years at Vétheuil. The painting (W.611) is in the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w646-jetty-at: A storm-tossed view of the jetty and lighthouse at Fécamp, painted during Monet's campaign on the Normandy coast in spring 1881. Waves break against the pier under heavy weather. The painting (W.646) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w647: A view near Fecamp on the Normandy coast, where Monet painted from the chalk cliffs in early 1881. Salt air and grey-green sea are rendered through agitated, short brushstrokes, the palette muted toward the silver tones of the Channel.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w648: A view over the Channel from the clifftops at Fécamp, painted during Monet's 1881 stay on the Normandy coast. The painting (W.648) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w649: The sea below the chalk cliffs at Fécamp in calm weather, painted during Monet's spring 1881 campaign on the Normandy coast — his first sustained cliff series. Private collection (60 × 81 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w651-morning-: A morning view of the cliffs of the Normandy coast near Fécamp, painted in 1881. The painting (W.651) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w653: The chalk cliff at Grainval, just south-west of Fécamp on the Normandy coast, painted in 1881 during Monet's spring campaign there. Private collection (61 × 80 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w658: The shingle beach at Fécamp beneath the cliffs, painted in 1881 on Monet's spring campaign along the Normandy coast. Private collection (46 × 80 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w662: A pure study of open sea and sky, painted in 1881 during Monet's campaign on the Normandy coast around Fécamp. With no shore or figure to anchor it, the canvas is carried entirely by the movement of water and weather. Private collection (50 × 73 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w663: A seascape painted at Fécamp on the Normandy coast, showing waves breaking under a heavy grey sky. Catalogued as Wildenstein 663 and also known as Rough Sea (Mer agitée), it is dated 1881, when Monet worked repeatedly along the Fécamp cliffs. The painting is in the National Gallery of Canada, Ottawa.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w664: The cliffs at Les Petites-Dalles, a small bathing village up the coast from Fécamp where Monet's brother Léon kept a holiday house, painted in 1881. It belongs to the first of the Normandy cliff campaigns that occupied Monet through the early 1880s. Private collection (60 × 74 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w668: A view of the Seine at Vétheuil under a setting sun, painted in 1881 during Monet's final months living in the village. Commons categorizes it among his sunset paintings of the Seine at Vétheuil. The work remains in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w678-lane-in-: A path through poppy fields on the Île Saint-Martin-la-Garenne, a river island in the Seine near Vétheuil, painted in 1880. The painting (W.678) belongs to the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w679: Painted in 1881 on the Île de Saint-Martin-la-Garenne, an island in the Seine near Vétheuil where Monet often worked. Formerly in the Paul G. Allen collection, it now belongs to the Hasso Plattner Collection shown at the Museum Barberini in Potsdam.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w683: One of the 1881 canvases of the sunflower-lined steps in Monet's garden at Vétheuil, painted just before he left the village for Poissy. This version hangs in the Norton Simon Museum in Pasadena; a larger variant of the same composition is in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w684: Another of the 1881 views of Monet's garden at Vétheuil, looking up the central path past tall sunflowers toward the house. It belongs to the same series as the versions in the National Gallery of Art and the Norton Simon Museum, but this canvas has remained in private hands.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w691: A 1881 view of the gate into Monet's garden at Vétheuil, one of the garden subjects he painted in his last year living there. The painting is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w694: A tall, narrow still life of gladioli in a vase, painted in 1881 — a rare flower-piece format for Monet at roughly 99 by 41 centimeters. The painting is held by the Pola Museum of Art in Hakone, Japan.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w700-near-vet: A landscape painted in the countryside around Vétheuil in 1881, near the end of Monet's three years living in the village on the Seine. The painting (W.700) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w706: An evening view of the harbor at Dieppe, painted in 1882 when Monet first arrived on the Normandy coast for his Pourville campaign. The painting belongs to the Dixon Gallery and Gardens in Memphis, Tennessee.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w712-low-tide: The beach and cliffs at Pourville near Dieppe at low tide, painted during Monet's 1882 campaign on the Normandy coast. The painting (W.712) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w717: A coastal landscape painted at Pourville, the fishing village just west of Dieppe where Monet spent much of 1882. The painting is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w724: A seascape painted near Dieppe in 1882, studying how fog dissolves the Normandy coastline — an early instance of the atmospheric 'effects' that would define his later series. The painting is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w726-the-chur: The medieval clifftop church of Saint-Valery at Varengeville, silhouetted against the Channel sky. Monet returned to this motif repeatedly in 1882, treating it as a study in tonal envelope, here flushed with the warm rose and orange of evening.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w736: The small customs officer's cottage perched above the sea at Varengeville, painted in morning light in 1882. Monet was drawn back to this lone cabin repeatedly, making it the subject of a full series in the 1890s. This canvas is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w752: A clifftop view at Pourville on the Normandy coast, painted during Monet's 1882 stay. The painting is now part of the Hasso Plattner Collection shown at the Museum Barberini in Potsdam.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w753: A path cutting through ripening wheat on the clifftops above Pourville, painted in 1882. The painting belongs to the Denver Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w757: One of Monet's 1882 clifftop views at Pourville (French title 'Bords de la falaise à Pourville'), looking along the chalk cliffs of the Normandy coast. The painting is now in the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w759: A view of the chalk cliffs at Dieppe painted in 1882 during Monet's Normandy coast campaign. The painting (French title 'La Falaise à Dieppe') is held by the Kunsthaus Zürich.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w764: A 1882 view of Pourville-sur-Mer, the small resort village on the Normandy coast where Monet worked through much of that year. The painting is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w767: Wave-worn rocks exposed at low tide on the beach at Pourville, painted in 1882. The painting belongs to the Memorial Art Gallery in Rochester, New York.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w772: An open seascape painted near Étretat on the Normandy coast in 1882, a few years before Monet's sustained campaigns around the famous cliffs there. The painting is in the Philadelphia Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w776: The beach at Pourville at low tide beneath the Normandy cliffs, painted in 1882 (French title 'Marée basse à Pourville'). The painting is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w778a: A small 1882 canvas of the chalk cliffs at Pourville on the Normandy coast, from the year Monet painted the area intensively. The painting is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w787: The beach and cliffs at Pourville in morning light, painted in 1882. The painting (French title 'Bord de mer et falaises de Pourville le matin') is held by the Tokyo Fuji Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w807: The sweep of beach below the cliffs at Pourville, painted in 1882. It is the only Monet in a Polish public collection, held by the National Museum in Poznań; the canvas was stolen from the museum in 2000 and recovered a decade later.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w81: A snow-covered stretch of the road leading up to the Saint-Siméon farm above Honfleur, painted in 1867. It belongs to the group of winter effects Monet made on this road, returning to the site of his earliest plein-air apprenticeship. Private collection (49 × 65 cm).
collection-of-beauty-monet-w812-vase-of-: A still life of chrysanthemums in a vase, painted in 1882 — one of the flower pieces Monet produced between his coastal landscape campaigns. The painting (W.812) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w816: The Porte d'Aval, the famous arched chalk cliff at Étretat, seen at sunset. Monet painted it during his stay at Étretat in early 1883. The painting (W.816) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w822: The pierced cliff at Étretat, a motif Monet returned to repeatedly, framed here through the natural arch and seething water below. The paint is laid in directional strokes that follow the swell, the chalk faces caught in mauve and ochre half-light.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w835: Wooded islets in the Seine at Port-Villez, across the river from Vernon, painted in 1883 — the year Monet settled in nearby Giverny. The painting is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w844: A 1883 view across the Seine toward Vernon, with the medieval Collégiale Notre-Dame rising over the riverside houses. Painted shortly after Monet moved to Giverny, a few kilometers upstream; the canvas is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w849: A tall still life of poppies in a porcelain vase, painted in 1883, the year Monet moved to Giverny. The painting (W.849) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w867: Painted at Bordighera on the Italian Riviera during Monet's nearly three-month painting campaign of early 1884. It shows a gardener's house (maison du jardinier) set among the lush coastal vegetation that fascinated him there. Wildenstein 867; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w868: A study of olive trees painted at Bordighera during Monet's 1884 stay on the Italian Riviera, where the silvery foliage of the olive groves became a recurring subject. Wildenstein 868; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w871: One of several studies of olive groves Monet painted at Bordighera on the Italian Riviera in 1884, capturing the flickering light through the silvery leaves. Wildenstein 871; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w875: Painted during Monet's 1884 campaign at Bordighera, whose palm gardens he described as almost impossibly exotic to paint. The upright canvas (92 x 73 cm) is catalogued as Wildenstein 875 and remains in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w885: A view up the Nervia valley toward the medieval village of Dolceacqua in the Ligurian Alps, painted on an excursion inland from Bordighera in 1884. Wildenstein 885; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w891a: A rare self-portrait, showing the painter seated in his studio, dated to around 1884. Catalogued as Wildenstein 891a, it belongs to the Musée Marmottan Monet in Paris, home of the largest Monet collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w891b: A view over the bay of Monaco with boats on the water, painted during Monet's 1884 trip along the Riviera coast. Wildenstein 891b; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w892: A panoramic view over the bay of Monte Carlo from Roquebrune, on the heights between Monaco and Menton, painted during Monet's 1884 Riviera campaign. Wildenstein 892; the painting is in the Portland Museum of Art, Maine.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w904: The chalk cliffs at Les Petites-Dalles on the Normandy coast in Seine-Maritime, painted in 1884. The painting (W.904) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w922: A small, frieze-like still life of daffodils (French title 'Jonquilles'), only about 16 by 40 centimeters, dated between 1882 and 1885. The painting is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w928: A small frieze-like flower study of daffodils (Jonquilles), only 16 x 40 cm, painted in 1885. Wildenstein 928; held in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w948: A still life of a potted white azalea, painted in 1885 at Giverny. The painting (W.948) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w961: A snow-covered winter landscape at Giverny, painted in 1885, two years after Monet settled in the village. The painting (W.961) is in the Pola Museum of Art in Hakone, Japan.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w962: A winter view of the Seine at Port-Villez, across the river from Giverny, painted under snow in 1885. The painting (W.962) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w965: A snow-blanketed view of the village Monet had recently made his home, painted with muted pinks and blues that register the cold light of a winter afternoon. Such effets de neige let him test how a single subject changes under shifting weather and atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w977: A Norman cliffside cottage dissolves into a wash of grey-violet fog, the architecture barely legible against the saturated air. Monet painted the Falaise coast repeatedly in the mid-1880s, fascinated by how mist erases line and reduces form to colour.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w982: Riverside trees in spring at Giverny, painted in 1885. The painting (W.982) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w986: A spring landscape at Giverny in morning light, painted in 1885; Monet painted a companion afternoon version (W.987) of the same motif. The painting (W.986) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-w996: A flowering meadow at Giverny, painted in 1885 during Monet's early years in the village. The painting (W.996) is in a private collection.
collection-of-beauty-monet-water-lilies-: A nearly square oil on canvas from the group of water-lily paintings Claude Monet completed in 1907, depicting the lily pond of his garden at Giverny. The water surface fills the entire field of view: rafts of lily pads bearing pink blossoms drift across reflections of sky and trees rendered in veils of lavender, green and rose. The painting is in the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, accession number 19.170.

Clouds reflected on the surface of the lily pond drift in pale pink and white across deep blue-green water scattered with lily pads, the composition running across three abutting canvases of mural scale. The triptych belongs to the Grandes Décorations, the cycle of monumental water-lily paintings Monet worked on at Giverny from about 1914 until his death in 1926.

The surface of the lily pond at Giverny fills the entire canvas — pale greens, lavenders and yellows with drifting pads and a few small pink blossoms, no bank or horizon to anchor the view. The mural-scale panel belongs to the Grandes Décorations, the cycle of monumental water-lily paintings that occupied Monet from about 1914 until his death in 1926. Museum of Modern Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-monet-water-lily-po: Water lilies float on the green-blue surface of the Giverny pond, the bank dissolved in a tapestry of brushstrokes that releases the picture from any horizon. Painted during Monet's late, near-abstract Nymphéas campaign and now installed in Tadao Ando's Chichu Art Museum on Naoshima, the canvas is housed in pure natural light.
collection-of-beauty-monet-waterlilies-p: A monumental canvas, two meters high and more than four meters wide, from the water-landscape decorations Claude Monet painted at Giverny between 1920 and 1926, in the orbit of the Grandes Decorations he ultimately gave to the French state. Known as Le Bassin aux nympheas, reflets verts (Waterlily Pond, Green Reflections), it stretches the pond's surface into a continuous field of deep green reflection scattered with lily pads. The painting belongs to the Foundation E. G. Buhrle Collection and is shown at the Kunsthaus Zurich.
collection-of-beauty-monet-wildenstein-1: Catalogued in Daniel Wildenstein's monumental Monet raisonné, this canvas belongs to the artist's late Normandy period, when he returned repeatedly to the cliffs near Pourville and Varengeville. Loose, broken brushwork dissolves form into atmospheric colour, the hallmark of his mature Impressionist practice.

From Monet's Giverny years, this work reflects his sustained meditation on water, reflection, and shifting light around the property he had transformed into a living motif. The palette favours violet-blues and greens applied in dense, woven strokes that flatten depth into surface.

An early Monet study from his formative years on the Channel coast, when he absorbed Boudin's plein-air practice and Jongkind's atmospheric handling of sky and sea. The brushwork is comparatively descriptive, anticipating the looser facture of the following decade.
collection-of-beauty-monet-yellow-irises: A late Giverny study of yellow flag irises, painted as Monet's eyesight clouded with cataracts and his palette grew correspondingly hot and saturated. The flowers swim in loose, near-abstract bands of green and gold, anticipating the decorative scale of the Grandes Décorations.
collection-of-beauty-monomakh-s-hunting: Grand Prince Vladimir Monomakh of Kievan Rus rests on the grass after a boar hunt, his retinue and dogs gathered around the kill. Painted in 1870 while Vasnetsov was still a student at the Imperial Academy, the picture anticipates his later turn toward medieval Russian history and bylina subjects.
collection-of-beauty-montagne-sainte-vic: The limestone ridge of Mont Sainte-Victoire rises beyond a patchwork of fields and trees east of Aix-en-Provence. Oil on canvas of 1904, one of the last in the long series Cézanne painted of the mountain. He built the foreground from overlapping facets of green, ochre and blue that blur the line between plain and sky.
collection-of-beauty-moonrise-by-george-: A pale moon rises over a level meadow fringed by dark trees, the sky banded in lavender and ochre. Painted in 1887 and held at the Yale University Art Gallery, the canvas belongs to Inness's late tonalist phase, when his readings of Swedenborg pushed him toward landscape as spiritual atmosphere rather than topographic record.
collection-of-beauty-moreno-garden-bordi: Painted on a winter trip to the Italian Riviera, the picture revels in the unfamiliar palette Monet found in Francesco Moreno's exotic garden, with its palms, citrus and Mediterranean blue. The artist wrote home that the light at Bordighera demanded tones of diamond and gemstone.
collection-of-beauty-morning-mist-in-taj: A color woodblock print by Hiroshi Yoshida of the Taj Mahal looming through early-morning mist, its marble silhouette dissolving in pale light above the reflecting garden. The design, Morning Mist in Taj Mahal No. 5, belongs to the India and Southeast Asia series Yoshida produced after travelling across the subcontinent in 1930-31, returning to the monument at different hours in companion prints. It was published in 1932.
collection-of-beauty-mortlake-terrace-a1: A Thames-side terrace bathed in the dissolving glare of low evening sun, with a small black dog famously cut out and pasted onto the foreground lawn. The picture is among Turner's most radical experiments in painting directly into the light source.
collection-of-beauty-moses-striking-the-: Moses lifts his rod over the desert rock as water gushes out for the kneeling Israelites who crowd forward with jars and children. Signed and dated 1624, the National Gallery of Art panel in Washington is one of Wtewael's late biblical pictures, executed on a small scale in the polished Mannerist manner he kept up long after the style had passed in Utrecht.
collection-of-beauty-mother-of-pearl-and: A standing female figure rendered in the pale, harmonised tones the title evokes, in keeping with Whistler's musical naming and his pursuit of arrangement over narrative. The subject becomes a vehicle for tonal close-keying rather than character study.
collection-of-beauty-mr-and-mrs-ralph-iz: The South Carolina planter Ralph Izard and his wife Alice DeLancey sit at a marble table in a Roman interior, a Greek vase between them and the Colosseum visible through the window. Copley painted the double portrait in 1775 during the couple's grand tour in Rome, his first European commission. The Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, holds it.
collection-of-beauty-mr-carlyle-deliveri: A wood-engraved illustration documenting Thomas Carlyle's rectorial address at Edinburgh, reproduced for a mass readership in the Illustrated London News. Such press engravings were the period's chief vehicle for circulating images of public events before photographic reproduction took over.
collection-of-beauty-mrs-thomas-lincoln-: Mary Groot Manson, a New York suffragist who would host votes-for-women meetings at her East Hampton home, sits in three-quarter length against a darkened ground, one gloved hand resting in her lap. Sargent painted the 1890 portrait as a gift to his hosts during a New York stay, and the canvas is now at the Honolulu Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-mu-ch-i-001: A section of the celebrated handscroll cycle Eight Views of the Xiao and Xiang Rivers, in which Muqi distils river, mist and distant peak into broad ink washes. The Chan-Buddhist economy of means deeply influenced later Japanese ink painting.
collection-of-beauty-mucha-apoteoza: The closing canvas of the Slav Epic, in which Mucha gathers the history of the Slavic peoples into an allegorical apotheosis culminating in a youthful figure of independence. The cycle of twenty monumental paintings was his self-declared life's work, given to the city of Prague.
collection-of-beauty-mucha-seasons-1897-: Spring from Mucha's second Four Seasons set, personified as a young woman tuning a lyre strung between blossoming branches. The decorative panel format, sinuous contour and floral framing typify the Art Nouveau idiom Mucha helped to define in Paris.
collection-of-beauty-munch-self-portrait: A late self-portrait in which Munch shows himself frontally before the easel, palette in hand, the face hollowed by age and frank scrutiny. Painting himself was a lifelong project for the artist, charting the shifts of his temperament as openly as any of his symbolic figures.
collection-of-beauty-murillo-descanso-en: The Holy Family pauses on its journey into Egypt, Mary cradling the sleeping Christ Child while Joseph watches over them and the donkey grazes nearby. Now in the Hermitage, the picture exemplifies Murillo's mature estilo vaporoso, in which figures emerge from a hazy, golden atmosphere with notably softened contours.
collection-of-beauty-musee-de-capodimont: The Croatian miniaturist Giulio Clovio holds open his illuminated Farnese Hours, gesturing toward a stormy landscape beyond a window. Painted around 1571-72 during El Greco's Roman years, the portrait now hangs in the Museo di Capodimonte, Naples, and records the friendship that helped the young Cretan secure Farnese patronage.
collection-of-beauty-musidora-and-her-tw: Three nude bathers from Thomson's poem The Seasons stand at a woodland pool while Damon watches unseen from the foliage. West first painted the subject in 1795 and retouched the canvas in 1806, working in the polished neoclassical idiom expected of the President of the Royal Academy.
collection-of-beauty-musizierender-einsi: A hermit plays an instrument outside his rocky cell in a sun-drenched mountain niche, a quintessentially Biedermeier vignette of contemplative solitude. Spitzweg specialised in such gently humorous, finely observed eccentrics set within picturesque German landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-nacimiento-de-san-j: An interior crowded with attendants tends to the newborn John the Baptist while Elizabeth rests nearby. Gentileschi treats the sacred subject as a domestic event, modelling figures in the warm tenebrist light typical of her Neapolitan period.
collection-of-beauty-nakahara-in-the-sag: From Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, the print situates the sacred peak behind travelers and scenery in the provinces. Hokusai's signature flat planes of color and bold contour line organize the landscape into the layered recession the series made famous.
collection-of-beauty-narcissus-caravaggi: The youth Narcissus leans over a dark pool, his lit shoulder mirrored by his reflected face. Caravaggio reduces the Ovidian myth to a single closed circle of body and image, with the harsh tenebrist contrast that defined early Baroque painting in Rome.
collection-of-beauty-nathaniel-hurd-by-j: The Boston silversmith and engraver Nathaniel Hurd leans on two folios, one labelled with the heraldic engraver's reference works that supplied his trade. Painted around 1765 and now in the Cleveland Museum of Art, the portrait shows Hurd in working dress, a rare colonial likeness of a craftsman rather than a merchant.
collection-of-beauty-natoire-adam-et-eve: Adam and Eve are driven from Eden by an admonishing angel in this Rococo treatment of Genesis. Natoire softens the moralizing subject with flowing draperies, pastel colour and graceful attitudes drawn from his work as director of the French Academy in Rome.
collection-of-beauty-natoire-sibylle: A French Rococo study of a sibyl, the prophetess of antique tradition shown in a moment of inspired contemplation. The drawing employs the fluid contours and idealized features that characterized academic figure work in mid-eighteenth-century Paris.
collection-of-beauty-nazari-old-man-in-a: A bearded sitter in a fur-trimmed coat and oriental headdress, painted in the half-length tronie format the Venetians adopted from Rembrandt and his Dutch followers. Bartolomeo Nazari worked mainly as a portraitist in Venice, where wealthy Grand Tourists prized such picturesque character studies as ornaments for the gallery wall.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-1301809-utag: A snow scene at Ueno from a nishiki-e album by Kunisada, the leading designer of the late ukiyo-e school. The print uses the muted palette and silent atmosphere appropriate to the bosetsu, or evening snow, theme inherited from classical Chinese poetry.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-1302763-tsuk: From Yoshitoshi's series Mirror of Warriors of Our Country, depicting the young Minamoto no Ushiwakamaru confronting the bandit Kumasaka Chōhan. The composition typifies the artist's dramatic late-Edo musha-e, with intricate armour patterning and a charged sense of action.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-04-k: The Kiyomizu Hall in Ueno Park seen across blossoming trees, from Hasui's Twenty Views of Tōkyō. The shin-hanga design preserves the planar colour fields of the woodblock tradition while introducing softened, plein-air light.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-10-k: Rain falls across Shinobazu Pond in Ueno, the lotus leaves and far shore softened to muted greys and greens. Hasui's mastery of bokashi gradation and overprinted rain-lines made him the foremost printmaker of weather in twentieth-century Japan.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-13-k: A sea cave on the Oga Peninsula renders blue-green water against weathered rock, from Hasui's third Souvenirs of Travel series. The artist toured rural Japan compulsively, and these prints document a coastline that motorised tourism was just beginning to reach.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-14-k: Karasu Marsh in Akita rendered as still water and reed beds under a quiet sky, from Hasui's third Souvenirs of Travel set. The reduced palette and emphasis on horizon embody the contemplative restraint that defines his shin-hanga landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-15-k: A view of Akita's vast Hachirōgata Lagoon from the shin-hanga series Souvenirs of Travel III. Hasui's quiet woodblock composition relies on flat washes of muted color and a low horizon to evoke the stillness of the inland water at dusk.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-18-k: From the shin-hanga series Souvenirs of Travel III, this nocturne shows the floating torii of Itsukushima beneath a star-pricked sky. Hasui pairs deep indigo bokashi gradations with sparse highlights to register the hush of Miyajima after dark.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-19-k: A scene of the towering Hōrai Rock rising from the Kiso River, drawn from Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III. The print balances the cliff's bulk against soft atmospheric washes, a hallmark of the shin-hanga revival of traditional landscape woodblock.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-20-k: A coastal view of the fishing port of Kamezaki in former Owari Province. Hasui frames boats and shoreline buildings under wide skies, using restrained palette and bokashi shading to render the still atmosphere of an Aichi inlet.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-22-k: Fukuoka's Nishi Park rendered in the shin-hanga manner, with figures threading through trees and lanterns. Hasui's design uses overlapping woodblock impressions to suggest dappled light and the casual pace of urban leisure in early Shōwa Japan.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-23-k: Morning rises over the hot-spring town of Beppu in Kyushu, with steam and hills pressed into a tight horizon. Hasui's bokashi gradations carry the cool light of dawn, a signature effect of his shin-hanga landscapes.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-25-k: From the series Twenty Views of Tōkyō, this print follows the Takinogawa River as it winds through suburban greenery. Hasui captures a quieter periphery of the modernizing capital, layering subtle woodblock washes for foliage and reflected water.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-26-k: Evening settles over the Beppu coast in this Souvenirs of Travel III sheet. Hasui anchors the composition with darkened silhouettes against a dusky sky, exploiting the shin-hanga technique of bokashi to dissolve land into water.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-31-k: Part of Twenty Views of Tōkyō, the print shows the moon hanging over the rural fringes of Magome. Hasui builds the night scene from layered indigo blocks and a single luminous disc, demonstrating shin-hanga's debt to classical Edo landscape traditions.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586549-40-k: A shin-hanga woodblock print by Kawase Hasui of Ryusen-ji, popularly known as the Meguro Fudo temple, in Tokyo. Seen from beside the vermilion main hall, a woman in kimono pauses at the entrance while blossoms show beyond the gate roofs and dappled light falls across the stone steps and lanterns of the precinct. The print was published in 1931; this impression is preserved in the National Diet Library, Tokyo.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586550-07-k: A view of the Ōmori coast on Tokyo Bay, drawn from Twenty Views of Tōkyō. Hasui registers the meeting of urban edge and water in soft, overcast tones, the shin-hanga answer to Hokusai and Hiroshige's earlier capital views.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586550-50-k: A colour woodblock print by Kawase Hasui from a print collection published by Watanabe Shōzaburō's print shop in 1935 (Shōwa 10). Hasui's shin-hanga landscapes pair traditional ukiyo-e craftsmanship with naturalistic light and atmosphere, and this sheet is preserved in the National Diet Library's digital collection.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586550-58-k: A colour woodblock print by Kawase Hasui, issued in 1935 (Shōwa 10) through the publisher Watanabe Shōzaburō as part of a collected print album. Like the rest of Hasui's shin-hanga output, it renders an atmospheric Japanese landscape with carved-block colour gradations; the copy digitised here belongs to the National Diet Library.
collection-of-beauty-ndl-dc-2586550-74-k: A colour woodblock print by Kawase Hasui from an album published by the Watanabe print shop in 1935 (Shōwa 10). Hasui, a central figure of the shin-hanga revival, supplied the watercolour design while Watanabe's carvers and printers produced the blocks; the impression shown is held by the National Diet Library.
collection-of-beauty-neapolitan-woman-18: A bust-length portrait of a young Neapolitan woman, painted during Repin's travels in southern Italy. The Russian realist favours direct observation over picturesque costume drama, registering complexion and gaze with a swift, loaded brush.
collection-of-beauty-negro-boy-by-l-baks: Costume study of a boy attendant, drawn in pencil, watercolour and silver paint on laid paper, 29 by 15.5 centimetres. The 1910 sheet is held by the MAGMA collection and belongs to Bakst's high Ballets Russes period, when his orientalist costume designs for Schéhérazade and Cléopâtre were reshaping European stage design.
collection-of-beauty-nesterov-florensky-: A double portrait of theologians Pavel Florensky and Sergei Bulgakov walking in conversation through a quiet wooded landscape. Nesterov's pared composition and contemplative palette frame the encounter as an icon of Russian religious philosophy on the eve of revolution.
collection-of-beauty-nesterovmv-narusi20: An expansive procession of Russian people - peasants, monks, soldiers and intelligentsia - moves across a northern landscape in search of spiritual truth. Nesterov treats his pre-revolutionary allegory in luminous, restrained colour, blending Symbolist mood with Orthodox iconographic gravity.
collection-of-beauty-newport-castle-by-j: The ruined keep of Newport Castle rises above the muddy banks of the river Usk, with figures and a small craft below. Turner painted the Welsh watercolour around 1796, the year of his first oil exhibition at the Royal Academy, drawing on sketches made during his 1795 South Wales tour.
collection-of-beauty-newton-williamblake: Blake's monoprint shows the natural philosopher hunched naked on a sea-floor rock, drawing geometric figures with a compass. The image reads as a critique of pure reason: Newton, absorbed in measurement, becomes blind to the imaginative cosmos beyond his diagram.
collection-of-beauty-niccolopaganini: A pencil portrait of the virtuoso violinist captured during Ingres's years in Rome. The drawing distils Paganini to crisp contour and minimal shading, exemplifying the precise linear style for which Ingres's portrait sketches of musicians and patrons remain prized.
collection-of-beauty-nichiren-bezweert-d: The Buddhist reformer Nichiren stands in a pitching boat off Kakuda, calming the waves with the Lotus Sutra during his exile to Sado. Kuniyoshi's woodblock print sets red robes against churning blue surf in the dramatic warrior-print idiom of late Edo Utagawa school design.
collection-of-beauty-nicholas-ii-of-russ: Tsar Nicholas II stands in the full dress uniform of the 2nd Dragoons, Royal Scots Greys, his bearskin tucked under one arm. Serov painted the portrait in 1902 for the regiment, of which the Emperor served as Colonel-in-Chief from 1894 until 1918, and it now hangs in the Royal Scots Dragoon Guards Museum in Edinburgh.
collection-of-beauty-nicolas-de-largilli: The First Painter to the King sits at his easel with palette and brushes, gesturing toward a canvas of his own equestrian compositions. Largilliere painted the homage between 1683 and 1686, late in Le Brun's life, recording the man who had directed the Academie royale and the Gobelins manufactory under Colbert.
collection-of-beauty-nicolas-poussin-fre: A serene Italianate landscape with shepherds, livestock and a distant fortified town beneath still water and clear sky. Poussin's late landscapes treat nature as a measured, almost stoic order, with each motif placed for compositional balance rather than picturesque incident.

Venus rises from the sea attended by tritons, nereids and putti in a Baroque treatment of the Anadyomene theme. Poussin organizes the marine cortege into a frieze-like rhythm, marrying Ovidian mythology with the cool classical structure he distilled from antique relief sculpture.
collection-of-beauty-nicolas-poussin-l-e: Roman soldiers seize Sabine women in a violent twist of bodies, framed by classicizing architecture. Poussin choreographs the abduction as a sculptural relief of opposing diagonals, applying his rigorous study of antique gesture to the legendary founding episode of Rome.
collection-of-beauty-nicolas-poussin-le-: Compressed to its essential cruelty, the painting isolates a single soldier pinning a mother and child as Herod's slaughter unfolds. Poussin condenses the biblical episode into a sculptural triangle of figures, prefiguring later modern responses to depictions of state violence.
collection-of-beauty-nicolas-poussin-sto: Storm clouds boil over a vast Italianate landscape as the Ovidian lovers meet their tragedy beside a reflective lake. Poussin uses meteorological drama to magnify human catastrophe, with sheet lightning, fleeing horses and bowed trees orchestrated into a single classical machine.
collection-of-beauty-nicolas-poussin-the: Mary is borne aloft on a tumbling cloud of putti, her arms outflung, while astonished apostles look up from her empty tomb. Painted in Rome around 1630, the canvas belongs to Poussin's early Italian years when he was absorbing Titian's colour and Roman Baroque altarpiece composition before settling into his sterner classicism.

Christ hands the keys of the Church to a kneeling Peter, with the apostles ranged in a measured Roman setting. From Poussin's second series of the Seven Sacraments, the painting translates the institutional moment into the artist's mature, archaeologically informed classicism.
collection-of-beauty-night-bivouac-of-gr: Soldiers of Napoleon's Grande Armée huddle around guttering fires in a frozen Russian field during the catastrophic 1812 retreat. Vereshchagin, a battle painter known for unsparing realism, treats the scene with documentary cold rather than heroic rhetoric.
collection-of-beauty-nighthawks-by-edwar: Edward Hopper's oil on canvas of 1942 shows a late-night diner on a deserted New York street corner, its three customers and white-jacketed counterman sealed behind curving plate glass under harsh electric light. The painting's air of urban solitude has made it the most famous image of Hopper's career and one of the most widely recognized works of American art. The Art Institute of Chicago bought it from the artist within months of its completion in 1942, and it remains there in the Friends of American Art Collection.
collection-of-beauty-nihon-fukei-senshu-: The cliffside Kannon Hall at Abuto, perched above the Inland Sea, drawn from Hasui's Selected Views of Japan. The shin-hanga print exploits a high horizon and bokashi water gradations to set the small temple against a wide expanse of tide.

A coastal view of Goryō on the Amakusa islands of Kyushu, from Hasui's Selected Views of Japan. The shin-hanga design pairs distant headlands with quiet anchorage, demonstrating the careful balance of woodblock colour and reserve that defined Hasui's travel sheets.

A woodblock print from Hasui's Selected Views of Japan, depicting Mount Onsengadake on the Shimabara Peninsula as seen across the water from Amakusa. Hasui captures the silhouetted volcano in the soft tonal washes that defined his shin-hanga landscapes.

Morning light over the hot-spring town of Beppu, rendered in the muted blues and greys typical of Hasui's shin-hanga manner. Part of the Selected Views of Japan series, the print balances atmospheric mist against the orderly geometry of harbor architecture.

A coastal view of Iwafune in the former Bingo Province, in which Hasui sets fishing vessels against weathered shoreline rocks. The print belongs to the Selected Views of Japan series and exemplifies his preference for unpeopled, contemplative landscape.

Cherry trees in bloom at Kakize in former Bungo Province, treated with the soft pinks and grey greens of early spring. Issued within the Selected Views of Japan series, it joins Hasui's broader survey of Japan's regional natural calendar.

A view of the seaside district of Hakozaki in former Chikuzen Province, near present-day Fukuoka. Hasui places the famous shrine precinct within a low coastal panorama, using flat color planes characteristic of his shin-hanga collaborations with publisher Watanabe Shozaburo.

Hasui depicts the Kayagafuchi rapids deep in Chomonkyo Gorge, a famous Yamaguchi ravine of sheer rock walls and clear water. The print belongs to Selected Views of Japan and shows his characteristic handling of river surfaces in graded blue.

A quiet hot-spring scene at Tochinoki in former Higo Province, set among Kumamoto's mountain forests. Hasui frames the bathhouse village with overhanging trees, employing the soft graded tones that became his signature within the shin-hanga movement.

An island view of Kabeshima off the Hizen coast in present-day Saga Prefecture, shown with low cliffs meeting still water. The print is part of Hasui's Selected Views of Japan, his sustained traveler's record of regional scenery.

A view of Kanahama on the Hizen coast, where Hasui balances rocky foreground shore against a broader open seascape. Issued in the Selected Views of Japan series, it reflects his interest in the quieter shorelines of Kyushu.

The fishing village of Kyodomari in former Hizen Province, set into a sheltered cove of the Kyushu coast. Hasui uses softly registered color blocks and a low horizon line, in keeping with the contemplative pace of the Selected Views of Japan series.

Dawn over the harbor of Mihogaseki in former Izumo Province on the Sea of Japan, rendered in cool grey-blues warming toward the horizon. From Selected Views of Japan, the print typifies Hasui's attention to specific times of day.

A view of Kiyomizu Temple at Yasugi in former Izumo Province, the wooden hall set among tall cedars. Within Selected Views of Japan, Hasui treats the shaded temple precinct with the carefully bokashi-graded skies of shin-hanga printmaking.

The Kotsuki River winding through Kagoshima city, with the volcanic outline of Sakurajima implied in the distance. Part of Selected Views of Japan, the print weighs urban riverbank against open water in Hasui's characteristic flat color planes.

A view of Sakurajima, the active volcano rising from the bay opposite Kagoshima, here seen across calm water. From Selected Views of Japan, Hasui simplifies the mountain into a tonal silhouette in the manner of the shin-hanga landscape.

A street scene at Kasuga-machi in Kumamoto, with low wooden buildings receding along a quiet thoroughfare. Issued in Selected Views of Japan, it shows Hasui turning from grand scenery to the modest texture of a provincial town.

Nezame-no-Toko, the celebrated stretch of pale, water-sculpted rock along the Kiso River in Nagano. Hasui treats the famous gorge with crisp green water and bleached stone, placing the site within his Selected Views of Japan.

A view of Suhara, a post-station village along the old Nakasendo highway in the Kiso valley. Within Selected Views of Japan, Hasui sets clustered roofs against the surrounding mountains in his customary flat planes of color.

Lake Ezu on the outskirts of Kumamoto, its still water spreading toward distant mountains. From Selected Views of Japan, the print exemplifies Hasui's preference for water surfaces graded in blue bokashi to suggest depth and weather.

Miyuki Bridge below the towering walls of Kumamoto Castle, with figures crossing in front of the fortress's distinctive curved stonework. The print belongs to Hasui's Selected Views of Japan and pairs civic architecture with everyday passage.

The vermilion Daigokuden, main hall of the Heian Shrine in Kyoto, modeled on the imperial palace of the ancient Heian capital. Hasui sets the bright lacquered architecture against open gravel courtyard and a soft sky in this Selected Views of Japan plate.

Evening along the Kamo River in Kyoto, with low riverside buildings silhouetted against a graded dusk sky. Part of Selected Views of Japan, the print pairs Hasui's interest in city water with the long twilight of a Kyoto summer.

Nonomiya Shrine in the bamboo groves of Sagano, west of Kyoto, traditionally the site where imperial princesses purified themselves before service at Ise. Hasui treats the dim grove and torii in greens and greys for Selected Views of Japan.

A view of Kanaya-machi, a hillside neighborhood overlooking the harbor of Nagasaki. Issued within Selected Views of Japan, the print sets stepped streets and tile roofs against the city's sheltered bay in Hasui's flat shin-hanga palette.

Sofuku-ji, an Obaku Zen temple in Nagasaki founded by Chinese merchants in the seventeenth century, recognizable by its red Ming-style gate. Hasui frames the precinct within Selected Views of Japan, marking Nagasaki's distinctive Sino-Japanese heritage.

A view of Okayama Castle, the sixteenth-century black-walled keep known as the Crow Castle, mirrored in the Asahi River. Hasui treats the silhouette in deep tonal blocks for his Selected Views of Japan.

The steep slope leading up to Senko-ji Temple in the port town of Onomichi, with rooftops descending toward the Inland Sea. From Selected Views of Japan, the print captures Onomichi's celebrated layered terrain.

A modest hot-spring village at Anraku in Osumi, southern Kyushu, set among low hills. The print is part of Hasui's Selected Views of Japan and reflects his persistent interest in regional bathing towns rendered in muted tones.

The volcanic Mount Mayuyama rising behind the harbor of Shimabara on Kyushu's Ariake coast. Within Selected Views of Japan, Hasui pairs working harbor and looming peak in a composition typical of his coastal landscapes.

Tsukumojima, the cluster of small islets scattered through the bay near Shimabara on Kyushu. From Selected Views of Japan, Hasui arranges the pine-tufted islands against still water in graded blue bokashi.

The Golden Pavilion of Kinkaku-ji in Kyoto under fresh snow, its gilded upper stories set against bare branches and a frozen pond. From Selected Views of Japan, this winter scene is among Hasui's most familiar treatments of a celebrated subject.
collection-of-beauty-nikko-kaido-hasui-k: A shin-hanga woodblock print depicting a quiet stretch of the Nikkō Kaidō, the historic highway leading to the Tokugawa mausoleum. Hasui captures the avenue's towering cryptomeria with the soft atmospheric tonality and precise gradation that define his landscape work.
collection-of-beauty-nikolaj-alexandrowi: Anna Chertkova, wife of Tolstoy's publisher Vladimir Chertkov, reclines on a Pompeian-painted terrace among potted shrubs, the southern sky bright behind her. Yaroshenko painted the picture on the terrace of his own house at Kislovodsk in 1890, after the Chertkovs had travelled south for Anna's recovery following the death of their young daughter.
collection-of-beauty-nikolay-ii-of-russi: A formal portrait of Tsar Nicholas II, the last emperor of Russia, painted shortly after his coronation. Repin balances state-portrait dignity with the loose, vigorous brushwork that distinguished him among the Peredvizhniki realists.
collection-of-beauty-niobe-jacqueslouisd: Apollo and Diana shoot down the children of Niobe from a cloud while their mother shields the youngest beneath her cloak. David painted the canvas in 1772 as his second unsuccessful entry for the Prix de Rome; the rejection prompted a suicide attempt before he finally won the prize in 1774. It now hangs at the Dallas Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-nishikawa-sukenobu-: A page from the Ehon Asakayama (Picture Book of Mount Asaka) of 1739, a woodblock-printed book by Nishikawa Sukenobu, the leading Kyoto designer of pictures of beautiful women. Printed in ink monochrome, this sheet shows a woman at her toilette, her kimono slipped to the waist as she binds up her hair before a lacquer cabinet and a folding mirror stand. The book's two dozen studies of women rank among Sukenobu's most important contributions to the bijin-ga genre.
collection-of-beauty-nitta-yoshisada-tsu: A historical woodblock print showing the medieval samurai Nitta Yoshisada at the Battle of Ikuta Forest, where his vassal Oyamada Takaie sacrificed himself in his lord's place. The composition follows the dramatic narrative conventions of late Meiji musha-e warrior prints.
collection-of-beauty-nmgrh-1455-adolf-lu: Adolf Ludvig Gustav Albert Couschi, a courtier of African descent brought to Sweden as a child and ennobled as Badin by Queen Lovisa Ulrika, sits in a powdered wig and embroidered coat. Lundberg drew the portrait in pastel in 1775; it belongs to the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm under inventory NMGrh 1455.
collection-of-beauty-nocturne-by-james-a: Part of Whistler's celebrated Nocturne series, in which the painter pared the Thames down to washes of dusky blue and pewter. The work treats landscape as a tonal arrangement, anticipating the abstract sensibilities Whistler championed in his Aesthetic writings.
collection-of-beauty-northeaster-by-wins: A lone outcrop of the Maine coast pummeled by a winter storm, rendered with the muscular realism Homer developed at Prout's Neck. The painting strips the marine subject to surf, rock, and spray, a meditation on raw natural force.
collection-of-beauty-notes-nocturne-lith: A single boatman crosses the Chelsea Reach of the Thames, with the Battersea factories and a church spire dissolved into atmospheric tusche washes. Whistler executed this second lithotint of 1878, the year of the Ruskin libel trial, working from memory on the stone in the Wellington Street printing offices rather than at the riverside.
collection-of-beauty-nuremberg-chronicle: A celebrated woodcut from Hartmann Schedel's Nuremberg Chronicle of 1493, showing capering skeletons in the late-medieval danse macabre tradition. Wolgemut's workshop produced one of the most ambitious printed-image programs of the incunabula period.
collection-of-beauty-nympheas-71293-3: One of the water-lily compositions Monet painted at his Giverny pond, dissolving the surface into floating pads, reflected sky, and submerged depths. The late series pushed Impressionism toward an immersive, near-abstract vision of light on water.
collection-of-beauty-o-soldado-esquecido: A monumental anti-war canvas by the Russian battle painter Vereshchagin, showing a fallen soldier abandoned on the battlefield as carrion birds gather. The work is part of the artist's unflinching cycle exposing the human cost of imperial conflict.
collection-of-beauty-ochanomizu-57588716: From Hasui's Twenty Views of Tokyo, this woodblock print shows wet snow muffling the rooftops along the Kanda River at Ochanomizu. The artist was renowned for his subtle differentiation of snowfall, here rendered as soft cotton-like accumulation.
collection-of-beauty-oeillets-et-clemati: A late still life painted in Manet's final months, when illness confined him to small flower pieces brought by visitors. Carnations and clematis are set in a faceted crystal vase, the brushwork economical yet luminous against a darkened ground.
collection-of-beauty-ohara-koson-gatto-e: A color woodcut of 1933 by Ohara Koson, the leading designer of bird-and-animal subjects in the shin-hanga print movement. A black-and-white cat wearing a red collar and bell crouches on the wooden floor, staring intently into a glass bowl in which orange goldfish circle, a small hand net lying beside it. An impression of the print is in the Cincinnati Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-on-the-beach-two-ar: A wood engraving after Winslow Homer published in Harper's Weekly, depicting a flirtation interrupted on a New England beach. Homer's Reconstruction-era illustrations chronicled American leisure with a wry observational eye.
collection-of-beauty-ono-shindon-in-the-: From Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, this print shows farmers tending paddy fields at Ōno in Suruga Province. The flattened planes of green rice terraces lead the eye toward Fuji's familiar silhouette in the distance.
collection-of-beauty-ornament-with-owl-m: An engraving by Martin Schongauer in which an owl with outstretched wings perches at the base of a dense thicket of curling foliage, harried by the small day birds that dart through the scrollwork above. The owl mocked by daytime birds was a familiar medieval emblem of folly attracting scorn, and Schongauer works the motif into an ornament design of the kind used as a model by goldsmiths and other craftsmen. The sheet bears his monogram and belongs to the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-p-1948-sc-276-scale: A landscape from Monet's mature Impressionist period, catalogued as Wildenstein 1192. The painter's broken touch and high-keyed palette translate atmosphere and shifting light into the building blocks of the picture.
collection-of-beauty-p1110627wallraf-mus: A young woman in a white dress cradles a fluffy Angora cat against her shoulder, the animal staring back at the viewer. Painted between 1783 and 1785 in collaboration with Marguerite Gerard, who had entered Fragonard's household as a pupil and sister-in-law, the panel hangs in the Wallraf-Richartz Museum in Cologne (inv. WRM 3652).
collection-of-beauty-painting-of-susanna: Susanna, surprised at her bath, twists away as two elders lean in over the garden wall — the apocryphal story from the Book of Daniel that let painters join a nude to a moral subject. Rubens painted this version in about 1606-07, during his years in Italy, and its compressed drama reflects his study of Italian models. Oil on canvas, Galleria Borghese, Rome.
collection-of-beauty-paisaje-con-san-jer: Patinir places the penitent Saint Jerome amid a sweeping panoramic landscape of crags, rivers, and distant towns. The Flemish painter is credited with elevating landscape to a primary subject in Western art, the figure dwarfed by the world he renounces.
collection-of-beauty-pallas-athena-by-re: A figure in gleaming helmet and gorget, traditionally identified as the goddess of wisdom and war. Rembrandt models the armour with thick, gilded impasto against deep shadow, a hallmark of his late chiaroscuro.
collection-of-beauty-pallasetlecentaure: Botticelli pairs the chaste, armoured Pallas with a subdued centaur in a tempera allegory of reason mastering brute instinct. The work was made for the Medici and is rich with humanist symbolism, including the entwined diamond rings of Lorenzo's emblem.
collection-of-beauty-pan-syrinx-rubens: Rubens stages the Ovidian myth of Pan pursuing the nymph Syrinx, who becomes a stand of reeds at the moment of capture. The figures and lush riverside vegetation were painted in collaboration with Jan Brueghel the Elder.
collection-of-beauty-panorama-vom-kreml-: The Ivan the Great bell tower rising above the cathedrals and crenellated walls of the Moscow Kremlin, seen across the slate roofs of Kitay-gorod. Gaertner painted the panorama in 1839 on commission from Friedrich Wilhelm III, working from Moscow during a tour of Russia that filled his late career with imperial sites.
collection-of-beauty-paolo-uccello-heili: Uccello's late panel of the chivalric saint lancing the dragon, with a tethered princess and a stylised storm gathering overhead. The artist's lifelong fascination with linear perspective is visible in the geometric grid of the cave and patterned ground.
collection-of-beauty-paolo-veronese-008: A reproduction documenting a painting by the Venetian master Paolo Veronese, photographed without its frame for archival study. Veronese's output spans grand religious cycles, mythologies, and ceiling allegories executed across sixteenth-century Venice.
collection-of-beauty-paolo-veronese-juno: A ceiling allegory painted for the Doge's Palace, in which Juno rains crowns, jewels, and ducal regalia onto a personified Venice. Veronese exploits the di sotto in sù viewpoint to send the goddess plunging through illusory clouds.
collection-of-beauty-paolo-veronese-lucr: Veronese's Lucretia presses the dagger to her breast in the Roman matron's act of self-destruction after her violation by Tarquin. The painter dresses the heroine in Venetian silks, fusing classical exemplum with sixteenth-century courtly elegance.
collection-of-beauty-paolo-veronese-the-: An early devotional canvas in which Christ raises the kneeling Magdalene from her former life. Veronese's Venetian instinct for sumptuous fabric, architectural staging, and silvery light is already evident in this youthful composition.
