collection-of-beauty-raphael-fire-in-the: A fresco in the Vatican's Stanza dell'Incendio del Borgo, depicting the miraculous extinguishing of a fire in Rome's Borgo district by Pope Leo IV. Heroic nudes and a fleeing Aeneas-like figure carrying his father give the scene a deliberately classical cast.
collection-of-beauty-raphael-saint-georg: George on a white horse drives his lance into the dragon's throat as the rescued princess flees at the right edge. Painted around 1506 for Guidobaldo da Montefeltro of Urbino as a diplomatic gift to Henry VII of England, the small oil panel is now in the National Gallery of Art in Washington.
collection-of-beauty-raphael-the-alba-ma: The Virgin sits on the ground in an open Italian landscape, steadying the Christ Child as he reaches across to take the slender cross held by the young Baptist. The tondo was painted around 1510 for the church of Monte Oliveto in Nocera dei Pagani and now hangs in the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
collection-of-beauty-raphael-the-miracul: A cartoon for the Sistine Chapel tapestry series commissioned by Pope Leo X, showing Christ blessing Peter and Andrew as their nets break under the weight of fish. The kneeling apostle and the cranes on the shore are among the most studied figures in Renaissance art.
collection-of-beauty-raphael-young-man-c: A red-chalk drawing of Aeneas carrying Anchises from burning Troy, made as a study for the figure group in the Fire in the Borgo fresco. The athletic torsion and confident hatching show Raphael's response to antique sculpture and to Michelangelo.
collection-of-beauty-reception-du-grand-: Louis XIV welcomes the Prince de Condé on the grand staircase at Versailles, the victorious general bowing as courtiers look on. Gérôme reconstructs the seventeenth-century scene with archaeological precision, marshalling marble, brocade and ceremonial hierarchy in the polished academic style he made famous.
collection-of-beauty-recoveredgleizes: A Cubist landscape of Meudon with a small figure threaded through faceted houses, trees, and a winding path. Gleizes exhibited Le Chemin (Paysage à Meudon) at the 1911 Salon des Indépendants, the show where the Salle 41 hang first announced Cubism as a public movement.
collection-of-beauty-red-cavalry-riding: Three lines of Red Army horsemen gallop across a horizon banded with twelve Suprematist stripes of earth colour. Painted between 1928 and 1932 and inscribed 'God 18' in the lower corner, the canvas was Malevich's one work accepted into the Soviet pantheon; it entered the State Russian Museum in Leningrad on the strength of its title and is the only abstract painting permitted into that lineage.
collection-of-beauty-red-fuji-southern-w: Better known as Red Fuji, this woodblock print captures the volcano flushed warm by dawn light during the late summer southerlies. Banded clouds and a near-abstract triangular silhouette make it a touchstone of the Thirty-six Views series.
collection-of-beauty-redoute-flowers01: A spray of cultivated flowers drawn life-size against an empty ground, each bloom and leaf described with botanical precision. A plate after Redouté, the botanist-painter attached to the Jardin des Plantes and to the Empress Joséphine's garden at Malmaison. Colour stipple engraving finished by hand, in the technique used throughout his folios.
collection-of-beauty-remaining-snow-at-i: A shin-hanga woodblock print of the wooded park at Inokashira in Tokyo, with patches of late snow lingering beside dark water. Hasui treats the season with the muted palette and atmospheric stillness that defined his landscape practice.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-abraham-e: An angel grasps Abraham's wrist at the instant the knife slips from his hand, while Isaac lies bound and bare-throated beneath him on the altar. Signed and dated 1635, the canvas in the Hermitage was painted for an Amsterdam patron and seizes the most violent split second of the binding, with the blade caught mid-fall.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-belsazar: The Babylonian king recoils as a glowing Hebrew inscription, MENE MENE TEKEL UPHARSIN, appears on the wall during his blasphemous feast. Rembrandt stages the moment with theatrical lighting, overturned vessels, and a sumptuous gold-embroidered cloak.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-christ-in: The disciples struggle with sail and rigging on a heaving boat as Christ is roused to calm the sea. Rembrandt's only known seascape, it was stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in 1990 and remains missing.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-christus-: An etching, in its later state, of Pilate presenting the bound Christ to a crowd that demands his crucifixion. Rembrandt scraped away the foreground onlookers and replaced them with shadowed arches, intensifying the confrontation between judge and viewer.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-de-poolse: A young horseman in Eastern European costume rides through a twilit landscape on a pale mount, bow and sabre at his side, a fortified hill rising behind him. Acquired by Henry Clay Frick in 1910 from the Polish Dzialynski family, the canvas remains one of Rembrandt's most debated late works, its identity oscillating between portrait, allegory and historical type.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-girl-in-a: A young woman leans out of a painted frame, her hands resting on the illusory ledge in a sly play on the picture's own boundary. The trompe l'oeil device reflects Rembrandt's interest in animating the threshold between image and viewer.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-harmensz-: The princess of Ethiopia stands chained to the rock, arms drawn back behind her head, awaiting the sea monster while Perseus is absent from the field. Painted on panel about 1630 and held by the Mauritshuis in The Hague, the canvas treats the Ovidian myth as an intimate nude study rather than a heroic action.

The philosopher Aristotle, in black robes and a gold chain bearing a portrait of Alexander, lays his hand on a marble bust of Homer. Commissioned in 1653 by the Sicilian collector Don Antonio Ruffo for 500 florins, the canvas was the first painting of a series the patron assembled around the philosopher and now hangs at the Metropolitan Museum.

Bathsheba sits naked after her bath, holding the letter from King David that summons her to him, her old servant drying her feet at the side. Signed and dated 1654, the canvas in the Louvre uses the body of Rembrandt's companion Hendrickje Stoffels for the biblical heroine caught between duty and complicity.
The evangelist pauses over his manuscript as an angel leans in to whisper at his ear. Rembrandt models both faces with a quiet warmth, treating divine inspiration as an intimate exchange.

Christ stands at the centre with the sick crowded to his right and parents pressing children toward him on the left, the dark archway opening onto Lazarus the leper. Known as the Hundred Guilder Print for the unprecedented price it fetched in Rembrandt's lifetime, the etching combines drypoint and engraving to compress several episodes from Matthew 19 into one nocturnal scene.

The apostle holds the knife of his martyrdom and turns aside in pensive reflection. Painted late in Rembrandt's career, the figure is built from rough, palpable strokes that give the saint the weathered weight of a real man.

Aged Jacob, propped on his deathbed, crosses his arms to lay his right hand on the younger Ephraim while Joseph tries to redirect it, his wife Asenath watching at the side. Signed and dated 1656, the canvas in Schloss Wilhelmshöhe at Kassel reframes the Genesis scene as a tender domestic gathering rather than a formal blessing.

The aged prophet leans on a sumptuous gold vessel, head in hand, while the city of Jerusalem smokes in the dim distance behind him. Signed and dated 1630, the panel in the Rijksmuseum is among Rembrandt's earliest narrative pictures to wed Caravaggesque chiaroscuro to a deeply introspective biblical subject.

Lucretia stands in a white shift stained with blood, a dagger in one hand and a bell pull in the other, her eyes lowered in the moment after the self-inflicted wound. Signed and dated 1666, the canvas at the Minneapolis Institute of Art was the second and more restrained of Rembrandt's two paintings of the Roman heroine.

Long known as The Jewish Bride, the painting shows a couple in tender embrace, often identified with Old Testament pairs such as Isaac and Rebecca. Built up with thickly trowelled pigment, the gold sleeve and ruby skirt are among Rembrandt's most celebrated passages of paint.

The ragged son kneels before his aged father, who lays trembling hands on the bowed shoulders while elder figures watch from the shadowed background. Painted in Rembrandt's final years around 1668, the canvas now hangs in the Hermitage, its thick impasto and warm umber light marking the late style of his last decade in Amsterdam.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-harmenszo: A black chalk study of a tame Asian elephant, the wrinkled hide built up with smudged and stumped strokes, trunk curled toward the ground. Signed and dated 1637, the sheet in the Albertina, Vienna, was drawn from Hansken, the celebrated travelling elephant who visited Amsterdam and reappears in Rembrandt's etching The Fall of Man.

Rembrandt presents himself at forty-six in a dark cloak and skullcap, hands folded in front of him, gazing out with composed gravity. Painted in 1652 and now in the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna, the canvas marks the moment his Amsterdam fortunes had begun to turn but before bankruptcy forced the inventory of 1656.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-lapidatio: Saul looks on from horseback as a knot of attackers raise stones above the kneeling deacon, who turns his face toward a beam of heavenly light. Signed and dated 1625, the canvas is Rembrandt's earliest documented painting, completed at nineteen in Leiden and now held by the Musée des Beaux-Arts de Lyon.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-portrait-: Hendrickje Stoffels, Rembrandt's common-law wife after Saskia's death, appears at half-length in dark warm browns, a fur-trimmed garment opening at the neck. Painted around 1656, the year of his bankruptcy, the picture in the Gemäldegalerie at Berlin is one of several intimate portraits Rembrandt made of the woman who managed the household with his son Titus.

A portrait of the artist's wife shortly after their marriage, dressed in fanciful pastoral costume with a feathered hat. Rembrandt's warm light glances across pearls, embroidery, and her unguarded expression.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-portret-v: A widow of seventy-three sits in profile in a black gown and starched ruff, prayer book closed on her lap, the face carved by quiet light. Signed and dated 1634, the panel in the Rijksmuseum is the pendant to a portrait of Dirck Pesser and belongs to the run of Amsterdam burgher commissions that established Rembrandt as the city's leading portraitist.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-scholar-a: A bearded scholar in fur-trimmed gown stands at a high lectern, quill poised over an open ledger, attention turned to the page. Signed and dated 1641, the canvas in the Royal Castle, Warsaw, is the pendant to A Girl in a Picture Frame and forms one of the few Rembrandt pairs to survive together since their commission.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-susanna-a: The chaste Susanna shrinks as the two elders intrude upon her bath, drawn from the Book of Daniel. Rembrandt focuses on her vulnerability and the elders' menace, modeling flesh and drapery with a soft, glowing chiaroscuro.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-the-abduc: Europa is borne away across the water on the back of Jupiter disguised as a white bull, while her companions react in alarm on the shore. The dark, wooded riverbank and tiny carriage on the bridge give the Ovidian subject the weight of a Dutch landscape.
Rembrandt reimagines the classical myth as a startled, urinating infant snatched skyward by Jupiter's eagle. The unsettling realism breaks sharply with the idealized Italian tradition of the subject.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-the-anato: A group portrait of the Amsterdam Surgeons' Guild gathered around the dissected forearm of an executed criminal. Tulp's demonstration of the flexor tendons and the differentiated reactions of his colleagues turn a guild commission into a study of attention.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-the-artis: A small early panel showing a painter, dwarfed by an enormous panel on his easel, contemplating his work from across a bare studio. The image foregrounds thought rather than craft, framing painting as a fundamentally mental activity.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-the-windm: An etching of a stoutly built post mill rising above the bastion of an old town wall. Rembrandt's careful drypoint touches give the brickwork, thatch, and surrounding figures a grainy luminosity prized by collectors of his prints.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-van-rijn-: Bust-length self-portrait of the painter facing right, wearing a gleaming steel gorget over a white collar and gazing back at the viewer. Long catalogued as a Rembrandt, the panel in the Germanisches Nationalmuseum, Nuremberg, was reassigned by the Rembrandt Research Project to a Leiden studio assistant copying a lost prototype of about 1629.

A bearded man in furred coat and a tall fur cap, a heavy gold chain across his chest, turning to meet the viewer's eye. Signed and dated 1637, the panel in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, belongs to Rembrandt's series of tronies of sitters in exotic and Eastern European costume rather than to commissioned portraiture.

An early tronie, or character study, of a bearded old man in a fur cap, painted in Leiden. Rembrandt explores the fall of light across creased skin and the shaggy textures of the cap as exercises in expressive description.

The painter at thirty-six gazes outward in a black flat cap and dark coat with embroidered gold trim, the face lit from the upper left against a neutral ground. RCIN 404120 in the Royal Collection at Windsor, the panel entered the British royal collection under George IV and is among the most sober of Rembrandt's mid-career self-portraits.

Rembrandt's son Titus, then about nineteen, is shown in the brown habit and rope girdle of a Franciscan friar, his face emerging from the cowl in golden light. Painted in 1660 and now at the Rijksmuseum, the picture casts the young man as a saint, probably Francis of Assisi, in the genre of the tronie rather than as an actual portrait of religious vocation.

A late self-portrait in which the painter sits with hands folded, dressed in a heavy gold-trimmed robe and dark cap. The frank, unflattering record of his own ageing has come to define how subsequent centuries imagine the artist.

A windmill stands silhouetted against a turbulent, luminous sky on a high earthen rampart above a quiet river. Long read as a brooding emblem of Dutch identity, the painting fuses topographical record with charged atmosphere.

An early Leiden self-portrait in which the young Rembrandt's face is half-lost in shadow beneath a tousled crown of hair. He scratches into the wet paint with the butt of the brush to suggest stray locks, an experimental touch typical of these years.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-winterlan: A rare winter landscape in oil, with skaters, a horse-drawn sledge, and low farm buildings beneath a wide pale sky. The thinly brushed surface and silvery palette stand apart from the artist's more familiar dark interiors.
collection-of-beauty-rembrandt-zelfportr: A self-portrait from the artist's later years, in which he sits frontally with a mahlstick and palette implied by his pose. Broad, loaded brushwork records a lined face that meets the viewer with sober self-knowledge.
collection-of-beauty-rembrant-self-portr: Rembrandt at fifty-four faces the viewer in a dark cap and brown jerkin, the face built up in thick, scraped layers of paint. Signed and dated 1660 and now in the Louvre, the canvas was painted the year he left his bankrupt house on the Jodenbreestraat for a smaller dwelling on the Rozengracht.
collection-of-beauty-remigius-van-leempu: Henry VIII stands four-square beside his father Henry VII, with Jane Seymour and Elizabeth of York behind, copying Holbein's lost dynastic mural for the Whitehall Privy Chamber. Remigius van Leemput painted the small oil in 1667 for Charles II, two decades after the original burned in the 1698 Whitehall fire; the canvas is now in the Royal Collection (RCIN 405750).
collection-of-beauty-renoir-a-box-at-the: Two women in a theatre box, one in black lace resting her arm on the red velvet rail, the younger in white holding pink roses. Renoir reworked an earlier portrait into this image of spectators in 1880, oil on canvas, now in the Clark Art Institute, Williamstown.
collection-of-beauty-renoir-by-bazille: A portrait of the painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir seated with his knees drawn up, in a dark jacket and blue cravat. Oil on canvas, 62 by 51 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée d'Orsay, Paris. Bazille and Renoir shared a studio that year and exchanged portraits.
collection-of-beauty-renoir-jeune-fille-: An intimate domestic scene of a young woman combing her hair, a recurring subject in Renoir's later years. The soft, feathery handling of flesh and fabric reflects his shift away from strict Impressionist plein-air practice toward a warmer, more classicizing manner influenced by Renaissance art.
collection-of-beauty-renoir-joseph-duran: Joseph Durand-Ruel, eldest son of Renoir's dealer Paul Durand-Ruel, shown as a young man against a leafy ground. Oil on canvas painted in 1882, the year Renoir also portrayed Joseph's younger brothers Charles and Georges. Joseph (1862 to 1928) went on to run the family gallery.
collection-of-beauty-renoir-pierre-augus: A bustling Sunday afternoon at a Montmartre dance garden, where dappled sunlight filters through the trees onto crowds of working-class Parisians. Renoir's loose, broken brushwork captures shifting light and lively conversation, treating modern leisure as a worthy subject for monumental painting.
collection-of-beauty-renoirgarden: A woman shaded by a parasol stands amid blossoming flowerbeds, her figure dissolving into the surrounding foliage. Renoir uses fragmented, comma-like brushstrokes and unmodulated touches of pure colour to fuse figure and garden into a single shimmering field of sunlight.
collection-of-beauty-repin-studying-exam: An early academic study from Repin's student years, depicting young men absorbed in their books before an examination. The careful tonal modelling and observed gestures already show the eye for everyday human drama that would shape his later realist canvases.
collection-of-beauty-repin-turf-bench: A relaxed open-air group portrait of Repin's wife, daughters, and in-laws gathered on a turf bench in the family garden. Painted during his summers in Krasnoye Selo, it shows him adapting Russian realism to a freer, sun-warmed plein-air idiom.
collection-of-beauty-reply-of-the-zaporo: A preparatory oil sketch for Repin's celebrated history painting, showing Cossacks erupting in raucous laughter as they dictate an obscene reply to the Ottoman sultan. The looser handling here preserves the immediacy and unbridled humour that the finished canvas would carry forward.
collection-of-beauty-reservist-of-the-fi: Cubo-Futurist fragments of a soldier's ear, moustache and cap collide with pasted printed paper, a postage stamp and a real thermometer affixed to the canvas. Malevich produced this assemblage in the autumn-winter of 1914 at 53.7 by 44.8 centimetres; it entered the Museum of Modern Art, New York, after the Berlin works left in Hugo Häring's care were acquired in 1935.
collection-of-beauty-retrato-de-juan-par: A portrait of Velázquez's enslaved assistant, an artist of Moorish descent whom the painter would soon free. Painted in Rome as a demonstration piece, it stunned contemporaries with its dignified presence, controlled silvery palette, and the assured economy of its brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-retrato-de-la-espos: Elsbeth Binzenstock, Holbein's wife, sits with their children Philipp and Katharina, her face worn and watchful. Painted shortly after Holbein's 1528 return to Basel from his first English sojourn, the picture is identified through the Amerbach inventory of 1587 and now hangs in the Kunstmuseum Basel.
collection-of-beauty-retrato-del-papa-in: A famously unflinching state portrait of the pope, whose shrewd, suspicious gaze emerges from a cascade of crimson and white. Velázquez orchestrates a near-monochrome of vermilions and rose tones, using fluid brushwork to render lace, silk and satin with startling immediacy.
collection-of-beauty-reunion-de-famille-: Ten of the painter's relatives gathered on a shaded terrace at the family estate of Méric near Montpellier, most of them looking out at the viewer. Oil on canvas, 152 by 230 cm, painted in 1867 and held by the Musée d'Orsay, Paris, under inventory RF 2749. Bazille reworked the canvas before showing it at the Salon of 1868.
collection-of-beauty-reverend-robert-wal: A Church of Scotland minister glides across a frozen Edinburgh loch in elegant profile, arms folded against the chill. The silhouetted black figure on pale ice and misty hills became an emblem of the Scottish Enlightenment and a touchstone of Scottish national painting.
collection-of-beauty-ritratto-della-fami: Carl Joseph Begas, his wife Wilhelmine and their young son grouped together in a domestic interior. The German Nazarene painter had recently returned from Rome under the patronage of Friedrich Wilhelm III when he made this family portrait in 1821.
collection-of-beauty-robert-delaunay-191: Faceted Parisian rooftops and the silhouette of the Eiffel Tower dissolve into a grid of prismatic colour. Painted across 1911-12 and now at the Guggenheim, Window on the City No. 3 belongs to Delaunay's Fenêtres series, the first sustained experiment in what Apollinaire would name Orphism.

A monumental synthesis combining the three Graces, the Seine and the Eiffel Tower into a single panorama of modern Paris. Delaunay fragments the city into faceted Cubist planes while introducing the prismatic colour rhythms that would define his Orphist style.

Cardiff rugby players leap for the ball beneath a Ferris wheel, an aeroplane, and a luminous advertising hoarding for Astra. Oil on canvas, 326 x 208 cm, the picture entered the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris as the largest of Delaunay's three Équipe de Cardiff variants from 1912-13.

A nude at her dressing table dissolves into wheeling discs of pure colour, the mirror and figure interpenetrating. Delaunay painted the 140 by 142 centimetre canvas in 1915 during his Iberian exile from the war; it is held by the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris and belongs to his Orphist series exploring simultaneous contrasts.
collection-of-beauty-robert-delaunay-193: Rotating discs and concentric arcs in saturated primaries fill a panel commissioned to decorate the sculpture hall of the 1938 Salon des Tuileries. Delaunay worked alongside Sonia Delaunay, Albert Gleizes, Jacques Villon and André Lhote on the cycle; the canvas was donated to the City of Paris in 1939 and remains in the collection of the Musée d'Art Moderne.
collection-of-beauty-robert-delaunay-aut: Delaunay portrays himself in a high-collared coat, the brushwork still indebted to the divisionist palette he was absorbing from Seurat and Signac. Painted between 1905 and 1906, before his shift toward Orphism and the Eiffel Tower series.
collection-of-beauty-robert-delaunay-der: An early treatment of the iron tower that would obsess Delaunay for decades, viewed from below and toppling against a turbulent sky. The fractured planes and sharp diagonals translate Cubist analysis into a celebration of modern engineering.
collection-of-beauty-robert-delaunay-eif: Painted at the height of Delaunay's Cubist phase, the tower lurches and splinters as if seen simultaneously from multiple vantage points. Surrounding buildings collapse inward, dramatising the giddy modern experience of urban scale.

A later, lyrical revisiting of the Eiffel Tower set against the green expanse of the Champ de Mars. By the 1920s Delaunay had softened his Cubist fragmentation into rhythmic curves and bright contrasting colour, integrating the tower into a holiday vision of Paris.
collection-of-beauty-robert-delaunay-jea: Jean Metzinger sits in profile in a blue hat against a stylised floral backdrop, a tulip pinned to his lapel. Also known as L'homme à la tulipe, the 1906 portrait was painted while Delaunay was working through Neo-Impressionist divisionism, before either sitter or artist turned to Cubism.
collection-of-beauty-robert-delaunay-l-h: A pre-Cubist portrait of fellow painter Jean Metzinger, holding a single tulip against a vivid mosaic of pure colour. The divisionist touch and saturated complementaries reveal Delaunay's debt to Neo-Impressionism on the eve of his turn to abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-robert-delaunay-nat: A green parrot perches above a table of fruit and crockery rendered in dense, saturated patches of orange and complementary hues. Painted in the first half of 1907, the canvas marks the high point of Delaunay's divisionist phase and his engagement with Chevreul's colour theories. A second, more mosaic-like version is in the Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum, Madrid.
collection-of-beauty-robert-delaunay-ryt: Interlocking discs of saturated red, blue and green rotate against a black field. Painted in 1934, the canvas belongs to the late Rythmes cycle that Delaunay developed from his earlier Simultaneous Disc paintings, and the work was shown in the Centre Pompidou's 'Rythmes sans fin' exhibition in 2014.
collection-of-beauty-robert-fulton-1806-: Steamboat engineer Robert Fulton, then thirty, leans against a draped table while sitting for his teacher Benjamin West in London, the year before the Clermont's first run up the Hudson. The 36 by 28 inch oil on canvas, gifted by Stephen C. Clark to the Fenimore Art Museum, dates from Fulton's final European stay as artist and inventor.
collection-of-beauty-rocks-at-mouthier-b: A close-up view of weathered limestone cliffs near the artist's native Franche-Comté, the river snaking through a narrow valley below. Courbet builds the rock face with palette-knife slabs of paint, asserting landscape as raw geological matter rather than picturesque scenery.
collection-of-beauty-rogier-van-der-weyd: A Netherlandish bust portrait of a young woman whose elaborate winged linen headdress frames a composed, downcast face. Rogier's precise contours, translucent skin and patient observation of folded cloth set the model for fifteenth-century Burgundian portraiture.

A stark devotional Crucifixion in which the swooning Virgin and grieving Saint John flank the cross against a flat red cloth and grey wall. Rogier strips the scene of landscape and narrative incident, concentrating the drama into sculptural silhouettes and restrained, almost monochrome colour.

A young woman in a starched linen headdress turns slightly to the left, her hands not yet finished in the drawing, the outline of one sketched at lower left. The silverpoint study, now in the British Museum, belongs to a small group of preparatory portrait drawings attributed to Rogier van der Weyden's Brussels workshop around 1440.

Christ on the Cross occupies the central panel, flanked by donor figures and saints in the wings, set against gilded and architectural backgrounds. The triptych shows the precise drapery, restrained gesture and devotional intensity characteristic of fifteenth-century Netherlandish panel painting.

The Virgin sits enthroned beneath a Gothic canopy, holding the Christ Child who turns the page of a small book. Painted in oil on panel, the work shows van der Weyden's command of finely modelled drapery and saturated red, set against a flat gold-tooled ground in the manner of Netherlandish devotional images.
collection-of-beauty-romaine-lacaux-by-p: A poised portrait of a Parisian ceramic-maker's young daughter, seated in a stiff white dress with a flower in her hand. Among Renoir's earliest signed works, it still carries the smooth finish of academic portraiture but already shows his sensitivity to reflected light on translucent fabric.
collection-of-beauty-roman-charity-piete: An interpretation of the antique tale of Pero, who secretly nurses her imprisoned father Cimon to keep him alive. Rubens treats the moralising subject with characteristic warmth of flesh, dramatic chiaroscuro and a tender, tightly compressed embrace.
collection-of-beauty-rome-from-mount-ave: A panoramic view of the Eternal City bathed in golden Mediterranean haze, with the Tiber winding past domes and ruins toward distant hills. Turner exhibited this canvas after his Italian travels, dissolving topographical detail into atmospheric light worthy of Claude Lorrain.
collection-of-beauty-roses-vincent-van-g: A dense bouquet of pale pink roses tumbling from a green vase, painted at the asylum of Saint-Rémy weeks before the artist left for Auvers. Van Gogh's swirling impasto and rhythmic brushstrokes turn a quiet still life into a study of vitality and renewal.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-and-snyders-: The Achaean general Philopoemen, mistaken for a servant, is recognized by his hosts while chopping wood, an exemplum of stoic humility from Plutarch. The lavish kitchen still life of game and produce is by Frans Snyders, a frequent collaborator, while Rubens supplied the figures.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-apostel-andr: From the Twelve Apostles series painted for the Duke of Lerma, Andrew is identified by the X-shaped saltire cross of his martyrdom. Rubens characterizes the fisherman-evangelist as a weather-beaten elder, modelled with the bold chiaroscuro he absorbed in Italy.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-apostel-paul: Paul appears as a forceful, balding philosopher gripping the sword of his beheading, in keeping with the Pauline iconography of the Counter-Reformation. The half-length panel belongs to the Apostolado painted in Spain for the Duke of Lerma's collection.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-apostel-simo: Simon the Zealot appears in profile, absorbed in a worn book, the long saw of his legendary martyrdom resting half-visible at the lower left against a dark ground. The panel belongs to the Twelve Apostles series Rubens painted around 1610-12 for the Duke of Lerma, preserved intact at the Museo del Prado.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-de-verenigin: An allegorical pairing of Cybele and Neptune, personifying earth and water joining hands in a fertile alliance. Painted during Rubens's diplomatic years, the picture has been read as a plea for free access to the sea for his blockaded native Antwerp.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-feast-of-sim: Christ reclines at the Pharisee's table while the kneeling Mary Magdalene bathes his feet, scandalising the assembled guests. Rubens orchestrates the Gospel scene as Baroque theatre, with surging diagonals, gleaming silver and vivid emotional reaction.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-landscape-wi: A panoramic Flemish countryside after a storm, peasants and cattle moving among glistening fields beneath a translucent rainbow. Painted on his country estate at Het Steen, it shows Rubens turning to landscape in his late years with broad atmospheric breadth.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-mars-et-rhea: The war god looms over the Vestal Rhea Silvia, the union that will produce Romulus and Remus and so found Rome. Rubens stages the encounter with cascading drapery, fluttering putti and the warm flesh-tones that mark his mythological inventions.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-medusa: The severed head of the Gorgon lies on a stony ledge, eyes still rolling and snakes writhing into a teeming brood of vipers, scorpions and lizards. Rubens collaborated with the animal specialist Frans Snyders on the reptilian still life, fusing Baroque horror with naturalist precision.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-painting-ada: An early treatment of the Fall of Man, with Eve offering the apple beneath the Tree of Knowledge as the serpent coils above. Painted in Antwerp before Rubens's Italian sojourn, the panel still shows the linear, Northern manner he would soon temper with Venetian color.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-peace-war: Painted in London for Charles I as a diplomatic gift, the allegory shows Minerva pushing back the war-god Mars while Pax nurses Plutus and children gather around the fruits of peace. The picture distilled Rubens's hopes for an Anglo-Spanish accord into a sumptuous tableau of bodies and abundance.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-peter-paul-m: A violent biblical tableau of soldiers wrenching infants from their mothers in a tangle of straining muscle and contorted limbs. Rubens compresses the figures into a writhing pyramid, drawing on his Italian study of Michelangelo, Caravaggio and antique sculpture.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-peter-paul-t: The mythological trio stand intertwined in a wooded glade, their pearly flesh set against deep green foliage. Rubens models the women on his second wife Helena Fourment, celebrating an unidealised, sensuous standard of female beauty.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-pieter-paul-: Part of the twenty-four-canvas Marie de' Medici cycle commissioned for the Luxembourg Palace, this scene stages the queen's 1610 coronation at Saint-Denis. Rubens orchestrates a vast crowd of dignitaries in a sweeping diagonal, mythologizing the event the day before Henri IV's assassination.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-portrait-of-: A bust-length portrait of a fair-haired sitter, her hair coiled into intricate braids above a richly trimmed bodice. The luminous skin, lively gaze and confident handling are typical of the workshop portraits Rubens produced for Antwerp's patrician class.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-rkdimages-27: An oil sketch of the Crucifixion, with Christ flanked by the two thieves on Calvary. Rubens uses dynamic diagonals and contorted, muscular bodies to charge the scene with Counter-Reformation pathos, the loose brushwork typical of his preparatory modelli.

A tronie-style head study of a youth in three-quarter profile, executed from life as workshop reference. The lively flesh tones and sketchy modeling show how Rubens accumulated a vocabulary of expressions and types for use in larger narrative compositions.
collection-of-beauty-rubens-saturn: The aged god Saturn devours one of his infant sons, biting into the flesh as the child writhes in his grip beneath the cold light of his eponymous planet. Painted for Philip IV's Torre de la Parada, Rubens fuses Ovidian myth with unflinching late-Baroque violence.
collection-of-beauty-rudolf-ernst-after-: Two men leave prayers through a magnificent horseshoe-arched doorway framed by carved stucco and blue-green tilework: an elderly worshipper in white robes and turban leans on his cane, steadied by a companion in an embroidered violet kaftan and red fez. The oil on panel, signed 'R. Ernst,' is typical of the Vienna-born Orientalist's polished studio compositions, which assembled Moorish architectural detail — much of it derived from the Alhambra — around quiet moments of daily ritual. Ernst spent most of his career in Paris painting such scenes for the Salon market.
collection-of-beauty-rue-neuve-notre-dam: A narrow medieval street on the Île de la Cité, with steep timbered houses leaning toward the square in front of Notre-Dame and shop signs hung from iron brackets. Gaertner travelled to Paris in 1825-26 to study perspective with François-Édouard Picot, and this oil of 1826 belongs to the Prussian Palaces and Gardens Foundation in Potsdam.
collection-of-beauty-russian-victory-vyb: Russian galleys and ships of the line break through the Swedish fleet trapped in Vyborg Bay in June 1790, smoke from broadside fire rolling across the Baltic. Aivazovsky painted the engagement in 1846 as part of a Naval Ministry commission documenting Russian victories at sea.
collection-of-beauty-russians-at-navarin: Russian, British, and French squadrons under Admiral Codrington pound the Ottoman-Egyptian fleet at anchor in Navarino Bay on 20 October 1827, masts toppling and gunsmoke piling against the cliffs. Aivazovsky returned to the subject several times for the Naval Ministry, dramatising a decisive engagement of the Greek War of Independence.
collection-of-beauty-sa-8422-de-klovenie: View of the Kloveniersdoelen on the Amstel, with the militia guildhall and the Swijgh Utrecht tower rising at the corner of the Kloveniersburgwal. Painted in 1775, the cityscape records a stretch of Amsterdam that the Dutch capital would substantially rebuild in the nineteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-sailing-boats-after: From the Inland Sea series of woodblock prints, this view shows fishing junks under afternoon light. Yoshida printed the same key block in successive variants from morning to night, a shin-hanga experiment in atmosphere achieved by altering only the inking and color blocks.
collection-of-beauty-sailing-boats-eveni: Junks ride a glassy sea under a low evening sun in this version of Yoshida's six-state Sailing Boats suite. The warm orange ground and silhouetted sails show how shin-hanga printers could transform a single composition through color alone.
collection-of-beauty-sailing-boats-mist-: Sailing junks drift in a pale, fog-bound sea, their masts dissolving into the haze. One of six time-of-day variants printed from a single key block, this state demonstrates Yoshida's command of bokashi gradations and his shin-hanga sensitivity to weather and air.
collection-of-beauty-sailing-boats-morni: Boats glide on still water under the cool tones of dawn, the mountains of the Seto Inland Sea faint on the horizon. Yoshida printed the work in six time-of-day variations, a virtuoso shin-hanga study in the chromatic rendering of light.
collection-of-beauty-sailing-boats-night: The darkest of Yoshida's six Sailing Boats variants, the scene is steeped in deep indigo with the silhouettes of junks just visible against a moonlit sea. The print shows shin-hanga craftsmen working color and gradation to evoke night without losing the woodblock's clarity.
collection-of-beauty-saint-christopher-f: A small copper engraving by Albrecht Dürer showing Saint Christopher wading through the river with the Christ Child on his shoulders, bracing himself on his staff as he strides to the left. Dürer engraved two versions of the subject in 1521, distinguished by the direction the saint faces. This impression, measuring only about twelve by seven centimeters, is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York, which received it in the bequest of Julie Parsons Redmond.
collection-of-beauty-saint-francis-of-as: The saint swoons in the arms of an angel after receiving the stigmata, his companions sleeping in the moonlit landscape behind. One of Caravaggio's earliest religious nocturnes, the picture introduces the raking light and tender naturalism that would shape his mature style.
collection-of-beauty-saint-jerome-writin: The aged Church Father bends over an open volume, his bald skull echoing the memento mori at his elbow. Painted in Rome for Cardinal Scipione Borghese, Caravaggio strips the scholar's cell to a few essentials so that flesh, parchment and shadow can do all the speaking.
collection-of-beauty-saint-john-on-patmo: Saint John the Evangelist sits on the rocky shore of Patmos with a book open on his lap, looking up at a radiant vision of the Virgin and Child in the sky; his eagle perches at his side and a small sailing boat crosses the sea behind him. Schongauer's engraving joins the saint's exile on the island to the apocalyptic vision he recorded there, and carries his monogram below. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-saint-sebastian-ten: After the Roman martyr's ordeal at the column, two angels withdraw the arrows and bind his wounds. Rubens treats Sebastian's nude body in the heroic manner of antique sculpture and Italian masters, softening the violence into a Baroque tableau of muscular grace.
collection-of-beauty-samovar-malevich-19: A Russian samovar dissected into cylindrical and conical facets of grey, ochre, and tin. Painted in 1913 and now at the Museum of Modern Art in New York, the still life sits between Malevich's Cubo-Futurist machine subjects and the radical abstraction he would unveil as Suprematism two years later.
collection-of-beauty-san-jeronimo-leyend: The Church Father is depicted half-length in a rocky grotto, bare-chested and absorbed in his book, a crucifix steadying his left hand. Murillo treats the penitent scholar with restrained naturalism, the warm Sevillian light modelling weathered skin and beard against a deep brown ground.
collection-of-beauty-san-romano-battle-p: From the three-panel cycle painted for the Bartolini Salimbeni and later Lorenzo de' Medici, this London panel shows Niccolo da Tolentino leading the Florentines against Siena. Uccello's foreshortened lances, fallen soldier and patterned ground are a famous early experiment in linear perspective.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-0: A late Lamentation showing the dead Christ across the Virgin's knees, ringed by mourners in a steeply compressed group. Botticelli's tightly knotted figures and stark grief reflect the religious severity that gripped Florence in the Savonarola years.

Saint Augustine sits in his study, deep in thought before book, inkwell and astronomical instruments. Botticelli's fresco for the Florentine church of Ognissanti casts the Church Father as a Renaissance scholar, painted as a pendant to Ghirlandaio's Saint Jerome.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-a: A late workshop Madonna in the Florentine devotional tradition, the Virgin tenderly cradling the Christ Child against a quiet ground. The flowing contours and elongated hands are characteristic of Botticelli's late manner, when his style turned more austere under Savonarolan influence.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-i: A profile bust of a young woman with elaborately plaited hair, long identified, however speculatively, with the Florentine beauty Simonetta Vespucci. Botticelli converts a Quattrocento portrait formula into a half-mythological nymph, the linear refinement balanced by jewels and serpentine ornament.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-l: Botticelli reconstructs a lost painting by the Greek master Apelles as described by Lucian: King Midas with ass's ears is approached by Slander, dragged forward by a sinister train of Envy, Deceit and Conspiracy, while naked Truth points to the heavens. The panel is a humanist defense of innocence against false accusation.

The newborn goddess arrives at Cyprus on a scallop shell, blown ashore by Zephyr while a Hora prepares to robe her. Painted on canvas for a Medici villa and indebted to the antique Venus Pudica, the image fuses Neoplatonic philosophy with Botticelli's hallmark linear grace.

The dead Christ is supported across the Virgin's lap as Mary Magdalene clasps his feet and saints crowd the dark mouth of the tomb. Botticelli's late Lamentations, painted in the wake of Savonarola's preaching, abandon courtly sweetness for compressed, anguished figures.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-m: The enthroned Virgin nurses the Child between Saint John the Baptist and Saint John the Evangelist, set within a vaulted niche dense with lilies, palms and myrtle. Painted for the Bardi chapel in Santo Spirito, Florence, the panel pairs Botticelli's linear elegance with an unusually botanical, symbol-laden setting.
collection-of-beauty-sandro-botticelli-r: The Hebrew heroine strides home with her maidservant after slaying Holofernes, the general's severed head balanced in a basket on the older woman's head. The small Uffizi panel pairs Old Testament tyrannicide with Botticelli's lyrical, wind-swept drapery.
collection-of-beauty-sans-culotte: A standing sans-culotte in the striped trousers, short carmagnole jacket and red cap of the Revolutionary Parisian, a pike at his side. Boilly recorded such figures and the street life of Paris through the 1790s. Oil on canvas, in the small finished format characteristic of the artist.
collection-of-beauty-sanson-matando-al-l: Samson grapples a roaring lion to the ground and tears its jaws apart, the biblical strongman rendered with anatomical force and twisting torso. Rubens reworked the subject several times, transposing the heroic male nude of antique sculpture into a violent Old Testament exemplum.
collection-of-beauty-sarah-goodridge-bea: A self-portrait restricted to the artist's bared breasts amid loose white linen, painted at miniature scale on a 6.6 by 8 centimetre ivory. Goodridge sent the case to the newly widowed senator Daniel Webster in 1828; he kept it among his papers until his death, and the Met acquired it in 2006.
collection-of-beauty-sarah-goodridge-eli: Elizabeth Greenleaf Parsons in lace cap and dark dress, painted in watercolor on ivory. Goodridge was the leading miniaturist of Federal-era Boston, trained partly by Gilbert Stuart; the portrait belongs to the Harvard Art Museums.
collection-of-beauty-sarah-goodridge-gil: A tightly framed miniature of the elderly portraitist Gilbert Stuart, his white hair and high white collar set against a softly stippled brown ground. Painted in watercolour on ivory in 1825, the work was made at Stuart's own request from life; he called it the only true likeness of him.
collection-of-beauty-sargent-group-with-: Four figures recline on a grassy slope beneath parasols, their forms half-dissolved in dappled shade. Sargent treats the bourgeois leisure scene with rapid, broken brushwork, prizing the play of filtered light over portrait specificity.
collection-of-beauty-sargent-life-study-: A standing nude rendered with academic precision during Sargent's travels in North Africa, the body modeled in warm earth tones against a neutral ground. The study reflects his sustained interest in the figure outside commissioned portraiture.
collection-of-beauty-sargent-madame-ramo: The Chilean diplomat's wife is shown seated at a piano in an interior of pale silvery tones, her loose white dress catching the light. The composition belongs to Sargent's early Parisian period and was admired at the 1881 Salon.
collection-of-beauty-sargent-monetpainti: Sargent depicts his friend Monet at work outdoors at Giverny, easel propped beside a thicket as a young woman reads nearby. The picture is a personal homage from one painter to another, executed with the very plein-air looseness it documents.
collection-of-beauty-sargent-robert-loui: Robert Louis Stevenson paces the floor of his Bournemouth drawing room mid-sentence, while his wife Fanny sits cross-legged in a gold Indian shawl at the far right edge. Sargent painted the canvas in 1885 during a visit while Stevenson was finishing Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde; the writer called the result excellent but too eccentric to exhibit.
collection-of-beauty-sarto-andrea-del-se: The Florentine painter regards the viewer with a sober, narrow-eyed gaze, his beard close-trimmed and his black cap drawn low. Painted in 1528 and now in the Uffizi, the panel belongs to the final years of Sarto's career, two years before his death from plague during the siege of Florence.
collection-of-beauty-scene-des-massacres: Greek civilians huddle in the foreground as Ottoman cavalry round up survivors after the 1822 massacre on the island of Chios, in which tens of thousands were killed or enslaved. Delacroix exhibited the canvas at the 1824 Salon alongside Constable's Hay Wain; the picture entered the Louvre directly from the state purchase.
collection-of-beauty-scene-from-the-last: Cora Munro kneels before the aged Delaware chief Tamenund among a crowd of warriors, with Magua looking on from the right, beneath a soaring mountain backdrop. Cole painted the picture in 1827, shortly after the runaway success of Cooper's novel, transposing the scene into White Mountain scenery now in the Wadsworth Atheneum.
collection-of-beauty-scheherazade-rimsky: A stage design for the Ballets Russes production of Scheherazade, set to Rimsky-Korsakov's symphonic suite, with billowing curtains and oriental cushions in saturated greens and oranges. Bakst's 1910 décor for Diaghilev established the scenographic vocabulary of jewel-toned exoticism that defined the company's early Paris seasons.
collection-of-beauty-schinkel1: A bust-length portrait of the Prussian architect Karl Friedrich Schinkel, painted by Begas in 1826, the year he was appointed professor at the Berlin Academy. The oil belongs to the Alte Nationalgalerie and shows the designer of the Altes Museum and Schauspielhaus in middle age, fixed against a plain dark ground.
collection-of-beauty-schinkel2: Schinkel's elevation of the terrace at Orianda, a country retreat for Tsarina Alexandra Feodorovna planned on a cliff above the Black Sea in the Crimea. The architect's 1838 design fused a caryatid portico with hanging gardens and museum rooms; the cost was prohibitive and the palace was never built, surviving only in lithographs.
collection-of-beauty-schinkel3: An imagined interior of the reception hall in Schinkel's projected royal palace for King Otto on the Athenian Acropolis, with polychrome painted walls and a coffered ceiling sheltering a colossal statue. Friedrich Wilhelm, Crown Prince of Prussia, suggested the commission in 1833; Schinkel submitted his drawings in 1834 and the scheme was never built.
collection-of-beauty-schongauer-anthony: An engraving in which the hermit saint is hoisted into the air and tormented by a swarm of bristling, scaled, and beaked demons. Schongauer's burin work, with its dense parallel hatching and inventive monstrous anatomy, exerted a famous influence on the young Dürer.
collection-of-beauty-scops-owl-cherry-bl: A small owl perches on a flowering cherry branch silhouetted against a full moon, in the kachō-e bird-and-flower tradition. Koson's woodblock combines soft tonal printing with a quiet, almost photographic stillness aimed at early-twentieth-century export markets.
collection-of-beauty-scorn-from-le-brun-: Head turned aside with brow raised and lip curled to illustrate the passion of scorn, drawn from Charles Le Brun's lecture on expression. Issued by Bowles around 1785 in red-brown ink as part of his English Passions of the Soul, the print belongs to the long afterlife of Le Brun's 1668 lecture to the French Academy.
collection-of-beauty-sebastiano-ricci-it: The huntress goddess pauses at rest, half-draped, with her hound pressed against her side and quiver beside her. Ricci handles the mythological subject with the airy palette and rococo grace that bridge late Venetian Baroque and the eighteenth century.
collection-of-beauty-sebastiano-ricci-ve: A reclining Venus, attended by putti, is approached by a leering satyr in a confection of soft pinks, blues, and silver greys. Ricci's eroticized mythology helped translate the Venetian tradition of Veronese into a lighter rococo idiom.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-1628-: The young painter turns from his easel, eyes shadowed beneath a tangle of frizzy hair, face half-lost in raking light. An oil on panel of about 22 by 19 cm in the Rijksmuseum, the picture experiments with highlights scratched into wet paint, a technique Rembrandt was developing in the Leiden workshop he shared with Jan Lievens.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-1769-: Copley shows himself at thirty-one in a soft cap and open collar, brush poised, eyes meeting the viewer's. Painted in Boston five years before he left North America for good, the small canvas records the painter's pre-European style, built on dense local colour and forensic observation.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-1908-: Malevich confronts the viewer in a heavy crimson coat, ringed by red-outlined female nudes in the background. The 27 by 27 cm gouache, dated to 1910,1911, marks his transition from the icon-derived figures of his early Symbolist works toward a more declarative, primitivist palette. It belongs to the State Tretyakov Gallery, Moscow.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-as-th: Gentileschi merges self-portrait and emblem, depicting herself as the personification of Painting from Ripa's Iconologia: brush raised, gold chain bearing a mask, sleeves pushed back over a working arm. The conceit could only be staged by a woman, since the allegory was female.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-by-ed: The young Degas, around twenty-nine, looks out from a dark ground in a black coat and high collar, his expression guarded and slightly aslant. Painted around 1863, the picture entered the collection of Calouste Gulbenkian and now hangs at the Gulbenkian Museum in Lisbon.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-by-ge: A half-length self-portrait in which Watts wears a dark slouch hat and black velvet coat against a plain ground. Oil on canvas, 64.8 by 52.1 cm, painted in 1864 and held by Tate Britain. Watts painted it during his years at Little Holland House in Kensington, drawing on Old Master portraiture such as Raphael's Castiglione.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-by-gi: A young man in armour faces the viewer with parted lips, holding the head of Goliath at the lower edge, the painter casting himself as the victorious David. The Braunschweig panel, now in the Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum, is a cut-down fragment of a larger self-portrait recorded by Vasari and engraved by Wenceslaus Hollar in 1650.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-by-pa: Gauguin shows himself half-length against the sloping beam of a Copenhagen attic, jacket lapels wrapped tight against the cold and the eyes set in shadow. Painted in 1885, the year he abandoned his Danish wife and five children to return to Paris as a full-time painter; infrared examination at the Kimbell Art Museum has revealed an earlier profile composition beneath the present face.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-by-sa: The Berlin painter regards the viewer directly in a sober, naturalistic likeness keyed to muted browns and ochres. Lepsius trained in Berlin and Paris and worked within the cultivated portraitist circles of late nineteenth-century Wilhelmine society.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-in-a-: The artist holds palette and brushes beneath a wide plumed straw hat, smiling outward in a pose adapted from Rubens's Chapeau de Paille. Vigée Le Brun cast herself as both fashionable subject and confident professional, a self-promotional image she repeated.

The artist holds palette and brushes beneath a wide plumed straw hat, smiling outward in a pose adapted from Rubens's Chapeau de Paille. Vigée Le Brun cast herself as both fashionable subject and confident professional, a self-promotional image she repeated.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-leani: The painter at thirty-three, in velvet cap and rich furred robe, leans his folded arm on a stone sill that runs across the picture. Signed and dated 1640, the canvas in the National Gallery, London, quotes the pose of Titian's so-called Portrait of Ariosto and Raphael's Castiglione, both then in Amsterdam collections Rembrandt had recently studied.
collection-of-beauty-self-portrait-with-: The painter is shown embracing her young daughter Julie in a Neoclassical interior, both wearing simple white chemise dresses. The intimate, sentimental staging was calculated to project natural maternal feeling for a Salon audience on the eve of revolution.
collection-of-beauty-selfportrait-rembra: A tiny self-image of the painter in dark cloak and beret, head turned three-quarters into a pool of light. Measuring just 15.5 by 12.2 cm on copper and held by the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm, the panel is among Rembrandt's smallest self-portraits, made for the same collectors' cabinets that prized his etched heads of the same year.
collection-of-beauty-seriziat: Pierre Sériziat, the painter's brother-in-law, sits on a grassy bank in riding dress with crop and gloves, a yellow straw hat held in one hand. David painted the portrait in 1795 after his release from prison, where his Jacobin politics had landed him following the fall of Robespierre.
collection-of-beauty-serov-devochka-s-pe: Vera Mamontova sits at a sunlit dining table in a pink blouse, a porcelain plate of peaches before her. Serov painted the eleven-year-old daughter of his patron Savva Mamontov over several weeks at Abramtsevo in 1887, the canvas now hanging in the Tretyakov Gallery as a founding work of Russian Impressionism.
collection-of-beauty-serovelizabethdepar: The boy emperor Peter II rides alongside the future empress Elizabeth Petrovna through autumn woods, hounds streaming beside their horses. Serov painted the small panel in tempera on cardboard in 1900 as part of a Romanov hunting series commissioned for the Grand Duke Mikhail Nikolaevich.
collection-of-beauty-sesshushuutoutou: A pair of seasonal landscapes in ink on paper by the Muromachi-period Zen monk-painter, with sheer rock faces, dwellings, and a solitary traveler picking his way through the cold. Sesshū's broken, axe-cut brushwork adapts Chinese Song models into a distinctly Japanese austerity.
collection-of-beauty-seven-sacraments-ro: A triptych setting the seven sacraments inside a vast Gothic church, with the Crucifixion at the center of the nave and the rites unfolding in the aisles. Van der Weyden orchestrates devotional precision, contemporary Netherlandish architecture, and an extraordinary system of inscribed banderoles.
collection-of-beauty-shah-alam-conveying: The Mughal emperor Shah Alam II hands a scroll to Robert Clive on a raised platform, transferring the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the East India Company. West reconstructed the 1765 Treaty of Allahabad fifty years after the event, recasting a profit-making contract as a regal ceremonial scene for the Company's London directors.
collection-of-beauty-sharaku-1794-ebisu: An ukiyo-e print issued during Sharaku's brief, intense ten-month career, depicting a kabuki actor in the role of the smiling fisherman-deity Ebisu. The mica-grounded portrait style condenses a stage character into bold contour and exaggerated expression.
collection-of-beauty-shipwreck-turner: A naval transport founders amid towering green-grey waves, lifeboats overloaded with survivors swept up the swells. Turner makes the wreck of HMS Minotaur an early demonstration of his lifelong subject of nature's indifferent force at sea.
collection-of-beauty-shironeko-by-takaha: A white cat is shown in profile against a plain ground, executed in the shin-hanga revival of woodblock printing. Shōtei's subtle gradations of grey in the fur and quiet, almost domestic mood typify the movement's blend of tradition and Western naturalism.
collection-of-beauty-show-booths-kustodi: Wooden show booths crowd a snow-trampled fair, with a brass band on a balcony and crowds in dark coats and bright scarves below the painted signs. Kustodiev returned to the Shrovetide balagany of provincial Russia repeatedly between 1916 and 1920, working from his Petrograd studio after spinal paralysis to reconstruct a folk world the Revolution was already dismantling.
collection-of-beauty-shurygin-levitan-18: A bust-length portrait of the landscape painter Isaac Levitan in dark coat and high collar, the brush handling kept tight and tonal. Shurygin painted the 1889 portrait during the years Levitan was establishing himself in Moscow with the Society for Travelling Art Exhibitions.
collection-of-beauty-siberische-blauwe-n: A small green Siberian blue robin perches on a snow-dusted reed shelter above a single pink peony, the composition set against a deep black ground. Ohara Koson worked closely with the Watanabe house to produce a long sequence of bird-and-flower designs for export.
collection-of-beauty-siernetel-in-bloemp: A potted coleus painted in Paris during Van Gogh's transition from the dark Dutch palette toward brighter, more broken color. The everyday flowerpot becomes an exercise in observing complementary reds and greens at close range.
collection-of-beauty-silk-merchants-indi: Indian silk merchants display bolts of cloth in a bazaar, their turbaned figures backlit by daylight through the shopfront. Printed in 1919 by the Watanabe workshop in Tokyo and held at the Honolulu Museum of Art, the design belongs to Bartlett's Indian shin-hanga series adapting Asian travel subjects to the Japanese woodblock medium.
collection-of-beauty-simple-bodily-pain-: Head contracted around tightened brow and grimacing mouth to illustrate simple bodily pain, after Charles Le Brun. The red-brown stipple engraving was issued by Bowles around 1785 in his English Passions of the Soul, one of many reprints that carried Le Brun's expression studies into eighteenth-century drawing manuals.
collection-of-beauty-sinite-parvulos-a-g: Christ, seated, gathers small children to him while apostles and mothers crowd around, taking up the gospel injunction "Suffer the little children to come unto me." Gentileschi treats the religious subject with naturalistic Caravaggesque lighting and grounded, individualized figures.
collection-of-beauty-sir-anthony-van-dyc: The Stuart king is presented in three-quarter length with elegant hauteur, a pose Van Dyck refined repeatedly to fix the image of Caroline kingship. The painter's silvered palette, fluid drapery, and aristocratic poise shaped English portraiture for a century.
collection-of-beauty-sir-david-wilkie-17: Wilkie commemorates the heroine Agustina de Aragón firing a cannon during the 1808 siege of Zaragoza, painted after his Spanish travels. The smoky, candlelit handling shows him reaching past genre toward the broader Romantic history mode of Géricault and Delacroix.

A crowded Scottish wedding feast unfolds in a low-beamed interior, fiddler at the front and dancers, drinkers, and gossips crammed across the canvas. Wilkie's careful Dutch-inspired genre painting helped popularize sentimental rural Scottishness for a Regency audience.
collection-of-beauty-sir-henry-raeburn-c: The Highland chieftain stands armed in full Glengarry tartan against a heroic landscape, every weapon and badge of clan pride on display. Raeburn's broad, direct brushwork supplies the swagger that Macdonell himself cultivated as a self-styled embodiment of clan tradition.
collection-of-beauty-sir-peter-paul-rube: Milkmaids tend cattle amid baskets of fruit and vegetables in a fertile Brabant landscape, a cornucopia of rural abundance. Rubens fuses pastoral genre and landscape with sweeping diagonal composition and an almost mythological sense of fertility.

Peasants, livestock, and farm tools fill a thatched Flemish barn lit by a cold doorway onto a snowy yard. Rubens's late-career rural scenes treat the working countryside around his estate at Het Steen with the same vigorous handling he gave to mythological subjects.
collection-of-beauty-sisley-bridge-at-vi: The cast-iron suspension bridge of 1844 across the Seine, looking toward Villeneuve-la-Garenne, with boats and figures along the bank. Oil on canvas, about 50 by 65 cm, painted in 1872 and acquired from the artist by Durand-Ruel that August; now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art (object 437680).
collection-of-beauty-slave-ship: A slaver flings the dead and dying from its hold as a typhoon rises over a blood-orange sea, painted in response to the Zong massacre and abolitionist debate. Turner dissolves moral horror into dazzling atmosphere, the figures and chains barely surfacing through churning paint.
collection-of-beauty-sleeping-beauty-by-: Costume study for a Countess in Act IV of Tchaikovsky's Sleeping Beauty, drawn in pencil and watercolour. Bakst designed roughly three hundred costumes and five scene changes for Diaghilev's 1921 London production at the Alhambra Theatre, his last collaboration with the Ballets Russes before his death in 1924.
collection-of-beauty-slovane-v-pravlasti: The opening canvas of Mucha's Slav Epic shows a couple cowering in a moonlit field while spectral horsemen ride overhead, embodying the early sufferings of the Slavic peoples. Mucha's tempera-and-oil technique on huge canvas gives the symbolist scene a pale, dreamlike pallor distinct from his Art Nouveau posters.
collection-of-beauty-smalllakewithboatmu: An early oil sketch on cardboard from Munch's teenage years, depicting a still pond with a moored rowboat. The plein-air naturalism, painted before his Symbolist breakthrough, shows him absorbing Norwegian landscape conventions in compact, atmospheric form.
collection-of-beauty-smiling-girl-holdin: A young woman grins broadly at the viewer while holding up a small framed picture of a couple in flagrante. Signed oil on canvas of 82 by 64 cm in the Saint Louis Art Museum, the painting belongs to the genre of Utrecht Caravaggesque half-figures in which Honthorst turned tavern wit into salon entertainment.
collection-of-beauty-snow-over-zojoji-te: Kawase Hasui's woodblock print of 1953 shows the great red gate of Zojo-ji temple in the Shiba district of Tokyo under heavily falling snow, kimono-clad figures sheltering beneath umbrellas at its base against a darkened sky. The print was commissioned by the Japanese cultural authorities to document the craft of polychrome woodblock printing, subsequently designated an intangible cultural property. It was published by Watanabe Shozaburo in the large oban format, carved by Sato Jurokichi and printed by Ono Gintaro.
collection-of-beauty-sokokura-by-hiroshi: A woodblock view of Sokokura, one of the seven hot springs of Hakone, with bathers and travelers gathered amid the steep wooded gorge. The print belongs to Hiroshige's series Hakone shichiyu zue, devoted to the spa villages prized by Edo-period travelers along the Tōkaidō.
collection-of-beauty-song-of-the-lark-wi: A young farmer pauses with his scythe at twilight, head tilted toward the unseen call of a lark. Painted shortly after the Civil War, the work distills Homer's interest in rural American labor and the silent intervals that punctuate it, rendered in a low-keyed palette of dusk.
collection-of-beauty-songhamaenghodo: A tiger crouches beneath a gnarled pine, eyes round and tail curled along its flank in the convention of Joseon tutelary beasts. Kim Hong-do painted Songhamaenghodo in colour on silk, the picture combining the apotropaic tiger with the longevity emblem of the pine in a single auspicious composition.
collection-of-beauty-sophia-alekseyevna-: Repin depicts the deposed regent Sofia Alekseyevna confined at Novodevichy Convent in 1698, her glare turned outward as a hanged Streltsy is glimpsed through the barred window. The picture compresses defeat, fury, and political claustrophobia into a single suffocating cell.
collection-of-beauty-sotatsu-dragons-and: Two dragons coil out of swirling ink clouds across a pair of folding screens by Tawaraya Sōtatsu, the early seventeenth-century founder of the Rinpa school. Working in ink alone, Sōtatsu pooled and blotted washes to make the beasts surface and dissolve in the mist. The screens are held by the National Museum of Asian Art in Washington, D.C.
collection-of-beauty-spring-blossoms-mon: A flowering tree fills the foreground of a small Montclair orchard, the white blossom muted against a grey-green field and overcast sky. Painted around 1891 near Inness's New Jersey studio and now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the picture works the late tonalist mode of softened edges and unified light.
collection-of-beauty-spring-flowers-by-c: Peonies, hydrangeas, and lilacs spill from basket and pot against a darkened ground, painted with an almost botanical attentiveness. An early still life, it shows the young Monet weighing studio precision against the looser, light-driven handling that would soon define his work.
collection-of-beauty-spring-kustodiev: A muddy thaw in a provincial Russian town, with melting snow, bare birches, and figures crossing a wooden footbridge between low painted houses. Kustodiev painted Spring around 1921 from his wheelchair, working entirely from memory of the Volga towns he had visited before his spinal illness ended his travels in 1916.
collection-of-beauty-st-martin-met-dp820: Saint Martin stands wrapped in a deep fur-lined cloak, drawing his sword to cut away a portion of it for the half-naked beggar kneeling at his feet. Schongauer presents the saint's famous act of charity as a standing figure rather than the more familiar scene on horseback, signing the plate below with his monogram. Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-st-michael-met-dp82: The archangel Michael, wings spread and robes swirling, drives a long-shafted lance into the dragon sprawled beneath his feet, its clawed wings and barbed tail thrashing across the lower margin. Schongauer's engraving renders feathers, drapery, and scaled hide with the disciplined burin work that made him the most influential Northern printmaker before Dürer. The plate carries his M†S monogram and dates from his Colmar workshop, around 1470-91.
collection-of-beauty-stadtschloss-schlue: The baroque inner courtyard of the Berlin Palace remodelled by Andreas Schlüter, populated with carriages, officials and curious onlookers on a cloudy summer day. Painted by Gaertner in 1830, the canvas chronicles a building that doubled as administrative quarters under Friedrich Wilhelm III; it now hangs at Schloss Charlottenburg.
collection-of-beauty-starry-night-over-t: Gaslamps along the Arles quay double in the dark water of the Rhône while the Great Bear hangs overhead. A small couple strolls in the foreground, anchoring Van Gogh's nocturne to the human scale of the river town.
collection-of-beauty-stenka-razin-by-vas: The Cossack chieftain Stepan Razin sits brooding in a fur-lined coat aboard a strug, his crew rowing out across the wide Volga. Surikov first sketched the subject in 1887 and only finished the 318 by 600 cm canvas for the 1906 exhibition, returning to repaint Razin's face around 1910. The painting hangs in the State Russian Museum, St Petersburg.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-alexandra-p: A Schönheitengalerie portrait of Princess Alexandra of Bavaria, daughter of Ludwig I, rendered in Stieler's characteristic porcelain finish. The sitter is shown with the soft idealization the Munich court demanded of its gallery of beauties.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-auguste-str: A half-length portrait of Auguste Strobl, later Auguste Hilber, painted for King Ludwig I of Bavaria's Gallery of Beauties at Nymphenburg. Stieler's polished oil technique, soft modelling and restrained palette typify the Biedermeier court portraiture commissioned for that celebrated cycle of Munich women.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-jane-digby: Painted for Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie, the portrait shows the English aristocrat at twenty-four, before the marriages and travels that would carry her from Munich to a Bedouin tent near Damascus. Stieler's smooth, neoclassical finish lends the sitter the air of court decorum she would soon scandalously discard.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-lola-montez: The Irish-born dancer who styled herself a Spanish noblewoman, painted at the height of her hold over Ludwig I of Bavaria. Her place in the Schönheitengalerie was itself a small political event, the affair contributing to the king's abdication the following year.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-marianna-ma: The Italian noblewoman, translator and longtime confidante of Ludwig I of Bavaria, shown with the soft idealisation reserved for the king's Gallery of Beauties in Munich. Stieler emphasises her dark eyes and intellectual composure, signalling her standing as a scholar rather than mere society sitter.
collection-of-beauty-stieler-portrait-of: Countess Caroline von Holnstein, a Munich society figure, painted for Ludwig I's Schönheitengalerie. Stieler frames her in dark drapery and pearls, the smooth modeling and steady gaze typical of the court's gallery of beauties.

A late entry in the Schönheitengalerie, depicting the Bavarian baroness with the soft chiaroscuro and idealized features Stieler used throughout the cycle. The portrait belongs to the long Munich project that gathered thirty-six women from across the social spectrum at Ludwig I's command.
collection-of-beauty-still-life-with-fru: The Antwerp specialist piles a Baroque larder with grapes, peaches, dead hare and game birds, animated by a thieving monkey, a wary cat and a darting squirrel. Snyders, Rubens's regular still-life collaborator, treats abundance as theatre, a moralising display of plenty under threat.
collection-of-beauty-stormy-sea-at-night: A three-masted ship rolls in heavy seas under a broken moon, its sails reefed against the swell, foam glowing pale where the waves crest. Aivazovsky painted dozens of nocturnal storm scenes throughout the 1840s, perfecting the thinly glazed translucent water that became his signature.
collection-of-beauty-stra-e-mit-kirche-i: A village street in the Black Foothills opens toward the parish church, the planes of road, façade, and sky reduced to firm coloured patches. Painted during Macke's Kandern period, the scene shows him absorbing Cézanne and the early Blaue Reiter palette before his shift to fully saturated colour.
collection-of-beauty-stuart-george-washi: Washington appears in a half-length variation of the Athenaeum head, his black coat picked out against a brown background. Stuart painted this 1797 version for William Constable of New York, one of dozens of replicas in which the artist adapted his unfinished 1796 prime to standing commissions.
collection-of-beauty-stuck-franz-von-sal: Franz von Stuck stages Salome in dark, lurid Symbolism: the dancer raised in ecstasy beneath jewelled veils while a servant hoists the Baptist's head into shadow. The picture distils the Munich Secession's fascination with the femme fatale.
collection-of-beauty-stuckelberg-sappho-: The Swiss painter imagines the Greek poet on a Lesbos cliff, lyre in hand, gazing seaward in the conventional pose of impending suicide. Stückelberg works in the late academic idiom, smoothing antique legend into a moralized salon image.
collection-of-beauty-sumida-river-the-wo: From One Hundred Famous Views of Edo, the print frames the Sumida River through the trees of the Suijin shrine grove at Masaki. Hiroshige uses the steep foreground branches and high horizon characteristic of the late series to fold the viewer into the riverside scene.
collection-of-beauty-sumo-wrestling-toad: Two toads grapple in a sumō ring while companions wait their turn, a gentle parody of the Edo wrestling print. Koson, working in the shin-hanga revival, brings naturalist observation to a comic subject with long roots in Japanese caricature.
collection-of-beauty-sunset-across-the-r: Plate twelve of the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji shows boatmen and stevedores along the Sumida embankment, the long span of Ryōgoku Bridge cutting the composition while Fuji rises faintly in the dusk. Hokusai keeps the celebrated peak modest in scale, ceding the foreground to working Edo.
collection-of-beauty-sunset-at-montmajou: Painted on the rocky outcrop near Arles, the work surveys the plain of La Crau through a foreground of scrub oak and limestone, the abbey ruins behind. Long doubted as authentic, it was reattributed in 2013 on the basis of letters, pigments, and the painter's own catalogue.
collection-of-beauty-suprematist-composi: Geometric planes of red, blue, yellow, and black float against a white field in dynamic, weightless arrangement. Painted in 1916 and held at the Stedelijk Museum in Amsterdam, the canvas belongs to Malevich's Suprematist phase, his project to reduce painting to pure feeling expressed through non-objective form.
collection-of-beauty-surikov-by-repin: Vasily Surikov, the future painter of the Boyarynya Morozova and the Streltsy, sits in dark coat and full beard against a neutral wash, painted by his older Itinerant colleague Ilya Repin. The portrait is a record of friendship between two of the central figures of the Peredvizhniki, made at the start of Surikov's career as a history painter.
collection-of-beauty-surikov-horseman2: An alternate version of the Bronze Horseman composition, with Falconet's equestrian Peter the Great rearing on the Senate Square pedestal beside the Neva. Surikov produced the study in 1870 during his Academy years in St Petersburg, before the Moscow history paintings that would make his reputation.
collection-of-beauty-surikov-pokoreniye-: Cossack atamans under Yermak Timofeyevich fire muskets from low boats at Khan Kuchum's mounted Tatar host on the Irtysh River in 1582. Surikov worked on Yermak's Conquest of Siberia for four years, exhibiting the canvas in 1895; Nicholas II bought it for the Russian Museum the same year.
collection-of-beauty-surikov-streltsi: Condemned streltsy in white death shirts hold lit candles in carts before the Kremlin wall, watched by their wailing families and by Peter the Great mounted at the right, as the gallows wait at Lobnoye Mesto. Surikov set his 1881 canvas on Red Square in the autumn of 1698, after the second streltsy revolt; Tretyakov bought it from the ninth Peredvizhniki exhibition almost as soon as it opened.
collection-of-beauty-surikovmenshikovber: The disgraced Prince Alexander Menshikov sits hunched in a low wooden izba with his three children in Siberian exile, the ceiling pressing down on his bulk. Surikov finished the canvas in 1883, not 1888, and Pavel Tretyakov bought it from the eleventh Peredvizhniki exhibition for the gallery in Moscow, where the brooding interior still hangs.
collection-of-beauty-surikovsnowfortress: Cossack riders charge a snow fortress while villagers in sheepskin coats throw snowballs and brandish brooms, the assault staged as part of the last day of Maslenitsa. Surikov painted the Shrovetide game from memory of his Siberian childhood, exhibiting the canvas at the 1891 Peredvizhniki show before it entered the Russian Museum.
collection-of-beauty-surprised-rousseau: A tiger crouches through whipping grasses as rain slashes a tropical thicket lit by lightning. Rousseau's first jungle picture, it stitched together motifs from botanical gardens and prints into the imagined wilderness that would occupy him for the rest of his life.
collection-of-beauty-susana-acusada-de-a: Susannah stands draped before the council of Israel while the two elders point in false accusation, the young Daniel rising to interrogate them. Coypel painted the Book of Daniel episode between 1695 and 1696, the smooth modelling and theatrical gesture already pointing toward the early Rococo.
collection-of-beauty-susanna-and-the-eld: A late treatment of the Book of Daniel episode, with the bathing Susanna recoiling from the two judges who threaten to denounce her. Gentileschi returned to the subject across her career, here in a more restrained, tenebrist key than her early Pommersfelden version.

Painted when the artist was seventeen, the canvas turns the usual erotic pretext on its head: Susanna twists from the leering elders in unmistakable distress. The closed marble parapet and tightly wound figures give the scene a claustrophobia rare in the subject's long history.
collection-of-beauty-susanna-i-badet-187: The Danish painter takes up the biblical bather in a polished academic idiom learned in Bonnat's Paris atelier. Susanna is set against a shadowed garden wall, the elders pressed close to a single edge of the canvas to sharpen the moment of intrusion.
