collection-of-beauty-suzanna-en-de-ouder: A Neoclassical treatment of the biblical episode in which the chaste Susanna, bathing in her garden, is spied upon by two elders concealed in foliage. The smooth handling of the nude and theatrical contrast of light and shadow reflect the Flemish painter's training in the academic tradition of David.
collection-of-beauty-suzanna-rembrandt-v: Rembrandt's small panel catches Susanna at the moment she steps from her robe, glancing back with sudden alarm as the elders emerge from the dark garden. The pearly nude and deep umber surroundings show the painter testing a Lastman-derived biblical mode in the year of Danaë.
collection-of-beauty-suzanne-et-les-viei: Susanna recoils in her bath as two white-bearded elders crowd in from the shadows, one gripping her arm as the other pulls back the drapery. Giambattista Pittoni painted the Old Testament subject in the 1720s in his Venetian Rococo manner, treating the apocryphal Book of Daniel episode with the pale flesh tones and sweeping silks typical of the city's settecento.
collection-of-beauty-suzuki-harunobu-c-1: From Harunobu's Eight Views of Ōmi, the print transposes the Chinese landscape topos onto Lake Biwa, here the returning sails at Yabase. Slender figures in a domestic interior stand in for the classical scenery, a witty mitate typical of his refined nishiki-e.
collection-of-beauty-suzuki-harunobu-wom: A young woman holds a paper lantern up to a flowering plum branch in the snow, the colour-printed surface tuned to soft greys and blacks. Harunobu was the first ukiyo-e artist to exploit the full nishiki-e palette, and the quiet nocturne is a showcase for it.
collection-of-beauty-svetlana-at-fortune: A young woman in a kokoshnik and sarafan sits with her back to the viewer, peering into a candlelit mirror to catch sight of her future husband. Bryullov painted Svetlana in Moscow while staying with Antony Pogorelsky, transcribing the heroine of Vasily Zhukovsky's 1812 ballad in his only canvas on a Russian folk subject; it hangs in the Nizhny Novgorod State Art Museum.
collection-of-beauty-swimming-hole: Six male figures, including Eakins himself swimming toward his dog at the right, bathe naked around a sandstone pier on Dove Lake outside Philadelphia. The 1885 oil was commissioned by Edward Hornor Coates of the Pennsylvania Academy and then returned as too indecent; it has hung in the Amon Carter Museum in Fort Worth since 1990.
collection-of-beauty-tab-v-fetus-with-um: An engraving from Tabulae VII uteri mulieris gravidae (Seven Tables of the Pregnant Uterus, 1748-51), the obstetric atlas of the Leiden anatomist Bernhard Siegfried Albinus. The fifth table shows a full-term fetus curled with its limbs drawn up, the umbilical cord running to the opened placenta, whose branching vessels are spread for display; an engraved Latin key fills the lower part of the plate. This impression is in the Wellcome Collection, London.
collection-of-beauty-tabi-miyage-dai-iss: An autumn road through the old Koshiji region, recorded in the first of Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel series. The shin-hanga print pairs sketchbook directness with Watanabe Shōzaburō's carefully graded colour blocks.

Iwai Beach on the Bōshū coast, fishing boats drawn up under a high cloud bank. Hasui's first travel album returns again and again to such quiet shorelines, the bokashi gradients standing in for shifting maritime weather.

Workmen load quarried stone onto a flat-bottomed boat in Awa Province, the labour rendered with the documentary clarity Hasui brought to early Taishō travel. The print belongs to Souvenirs of Travel I, the series that established his collaboration with publisher Watanabe.

The Asano River at Kanazawa, its banks lined by the dark eaves of the old castle town. Hasui treats the scene in muted dusk colour, balancing the traditional Edo-period view with a modern, photographically framed viewpoint.

A view of the Nagare pleasure quarter in Kanazawa, lanterns warming the wooden façades along a narrow lane. Hasui finds in the licensed district the same hushed melancholy he gave his rural and seaside views.

The Mishima River winding through Mutsu Province in northern Honshū, drawn from sketches Hasui made on his first long tour of the region. Issued by Watanabe in 1919, it stands among the earliest plates of the Souvenirs of Travel series.

A still woodblock view of Tsuta Marsh in the northern province of Mutsu, where reflected trees double the autumn forest on glassy water. The print belongs to Hasui's first Souvenirs of Travel series, in which the artist toured rural Japan recording the country's quieter corners.

A mountain temple outside Sendai is glimpsed through a screen of trees, the architecture half-absorbed into the hillside. Hasui's compact composition and softly graded skies belong to the shin-hanga revival, which reworked classical ukiyo-e idioms with modern atmospheric effects.

Autumn descends on the hot-spring village of Arayu in Shiobara, the slopes blazing with red maple above wooden bathhouses and a narrow river. The print captures the kind of seasonal regional travel that drove the early shin-hanga market.

Yuhi Falls drops between mossy cliffs at Shiobara, rendered with the layered greens and quietly observed water Hasui made his signature. Carved and printed in collaboration with publisher Watanabe Shozaburo, it is part of the first Souvenirs of Travel cycle.

The cliff face of Senjomaku rises from the still surface of Lake Towada, its scale exaggerated by Hasui's high horizon. Carved from successive woodblocks, the print exploits the bokashi gradient technique to soften water into mist.

Pine-fringed Kude Beach in Wakasa Province curves along the Sea of Japan, the foreground trees framing a low strip of water and sky. Hasui's clean geometry and reduced palette draw on Hiroshige's coastal landscapes while pushing toward modern simplification.

Lake Kugushi lies under a still, overcast sky, its shore traced by reeds and a scatter of fishing boats. The composition is typical of Hasui's first travel series, which favored the unspectacular waterways and country roads of provincial Japan.
collection-of-beauty-tabi-miyage-dai-nis: Rain falls in long diagonal strokes across the wooden stage of Kiyomizu-dera in Kyoto, its temple roofs darkened against a washed grey sky. Hasui treats the famed pilgrimage site not as a monument but as an atmospheric encounter with weather.

A quiet stretch of beach in Echigo Province frames moored boats and a low coastline under heavy cloud. Printed for Watanabe Shozaburo, the sheet exemplifies the shin-hanga preference for unremarkable rural views observed at a contemplative distance.

Kosho Temple at Himi nestles among trees on the Etchu coast, its tiled roof anchoring a composition of slope, sea and sky. Hasui's keyblock outlines are softened by carefully overlapping color blocks printed in registered succession.

Bare winter branches stand against the pale Hozu River at Arashiyama outside Kyoto, a district usually depicted in cherry blossom or maple. Hasui takes the inverse season, finding austere geometry where his predecessors found color.

Moonlight silvers the surface of Lake Kamo on Sado Island, the far shore reduced to a dark silhouette. The night scene relies on the bokashi technique, gradient printing across a single block to model the broad sky.

A rough beach hut at Himi sits low against the Etchu shoreline, its dark timbers contrasted with pale sand and water. Hasui's interest is in working coastal architecture rather than scenic landmarks, a recurring trait of the second Souvenirs cycle.

A street view in the Shimohonda neighborhood of Kanazawa shows a low row of merchant houses under a wide, flat sky. The print's restrained palette and elongated horizontal proportion are characteristic of Hasui's urban observation prints.

The Yanagawa district in Kai Province appears as a cluster of farmhouses and rice paddies set against distant mountains. Hasui sketched directly from life on his journeys, then reworked the studies for the carvers and printers of Watanabe's workshop.

Wooden irrigation troughs lift water across a Sado hillside, a practical landscape of rural infrastructure. The print's quiet subject reflects Hasui's commitment to ordinary working scenes over the picturesque set pieces of older ukiyo-e.

Stone lanterns flank the wooded approach to Kasuga Shrine in Nara, a route lined with thousands of votive lights to the Fujiwara tutelary deities. Hasui sets a single human figure within deep vertical trees to dramatize the scale of the precinct.

Nigatsu-do, the hall on the eastern slope of Todai-ji where the Omizutori water-drawing rite is held each spring, is shown perched above its veranda balustrade. Hasui's diagonal viewpoint compresses the wooden gallery into a strong horizontal band.

A woodblock print from the Souvenirs of Travel II series depicts the Asahi Bridge spanning the river at Ojiya. Hasui's shin-hanga style fuses Western perspective with traditional Japanese block-printing, building atmosphere through layered bokashi gradations.

Morning along Osaka's Dotonbori canal finds the famed entertainment district at its quietest, the theater district's lanterns unlit and its banks emptied of crowds. The composition trades nightlife spectacle for a city caught off-stage.

The mining town of Aikawa on Sado climbs a hillside in tightly packed wooden houses, each roof outlined by Hasui's keyblock. Once the seat of the Tokugawa silver and gold mines, the settlement appears here as a quiet provincial village.

The village of Kamo on Sado Island is laid out along the lake shore, low farmhouses set among rice fields. Hasui composes a near-empty middle ground that lets the water and ridge of the island do most of the visual work.

Mano Bay opens broadly on the western coast of Sado, its beach and headlands rendered in Hasui's typical low-saturation greens and blues. The print is part of an extended Sado suite within the second Souvenirs series.

A steep road climbs the Nishimikawa slope on Sado Island, its gradient cutting between dense pines. Hasui chooses an everyday traveler's vantage rather than a famous-place view, in keeping with the modest tone of the series.

The harbor of Ogi at the southern tip of Sado Island holds a cluster of fishing boats below sheltering hills. Hasui's composition layers sea, vessel and shore into clearly delimited bands of overlapping flat color.

Takamatsu Castle in Sanuki Province, one of the few sea-fed castles in Japan, is glimpsed across its tide-fed moat. Hasui's view registers the rebuilt keep and surrounding stone embankments under a softly graded shin-hanga sky.

A clear winter day at Miyajima sees fresh snow lining the rooftops of Itsukushima and the shore of the Inland Sea, the famous floating torii absent from this oblique view. Hasui exploits the contrast of warm vermilion architecture against cold white slopes.

The fishing town of Miyazu in Tango Province, near the spit of Amanohashidate, opens onto a calm bay edged by mountains. Hasui's restrained palette of slate blues and greens is tuned to the overcast light of the Sea of Japan coast.

Night rain falls heavily on the port of Teradomari, lantern light scattering across wet ground. Hasui was a master of nocturnes, and the sheet uses successive overprintings to build a saturated, almost lacquered darkness.

A partial view of the Phoenix Hall at Byodo-in in Uji, rendered as a shin-hanga woodblock print. Hasui isolates a fragment of the eleventh-century temple's tiled roofline, using flat colour fields and quiet tonal washes characteristic of the Souvenirs of Travel II series.

Dawn snow lies thick over the harbor at Ogi on Sado, with moored boats reduced to silhouettes against pale water. The print pairs a graded pink horizon with cold blue shadows, a daybreak chord Hasui returned to throughout his career.

Snow blankets the pine spit of Amanohashidate, the narrow sandbar in Tango Bay long counted among the Three Views of Japan. Hasui strips its familiar profile back to a quiet white horizontal between sea and sky.
collection-of-beauty-tabi-miyage-dai-san: A coastal view of Futomi in Awa Province from the Souvenirs of Travel III series. Hasui captures the meeting of village rooftops and sea through carefully calibrated woodblock gradations, a hallmark of the shin-hanga revival of landscape printing.

A panoramic alpine vista showing Asahi Peak as seen from Mt. Hakuba in the Northern Japanese Alps. Hasui's woodblock layers translate distant snow ridges and atmospheric haze into broad fields of muted colour, typical of his shin-hanga landscapes.

A traveller's view along the Nakayama-Shichiri road threading through the mountains of Hida Province. The print belongs to Hasui's Souvenirs of Travel III, in which woodblock bokashi gradations evoke the changing light of remote inland routes.

A nocturnal scene at the Arifuku hot springs in Iwami Province, with lantern-lit inns reflected on damp streets. Hasui exploits the deep, saturated indigos that became a signature of his nocturnes within the shin-hanga movement.

A coastal view of Hinomisaki on the Izumo peninsula, where pine-clad cliffs meet the Sea of Japan. Hasui's woodblock translates wind, wave and weather into a few decisive colour blocks, a characteristic of his Souvenirs of Travel III landscapes.

A hazy moon hangs over the canals of Matsue in Izumo Province, the city's wooden buildings dissolving into a violet dusk. Hasui's bokashi shading delivers the title's oborozuki — the misted moon of classical Japanese poetry.

Fishing boats and tile-roofed houses cluster along the harbour at Mihogaseki on the Shimane peninsula. The shin-hanga print balances closely observed coastal architecture against the broad calm of the bay.

An autumn rainbow arcs above rice fields at Hatta in Kaga Province. Hasui uses overlapping bokashi gradations to render the prismatic band — a meteorological subject that had become a quiet specialty of his shin-hanga landscapes.

The five timber arches of the Kintai Bridge in Suo Province span the Nishiki River, a famed seventeenth-century engineering feat. Hasui presents the structure in shin-hanga woodblock, foregrounding its rhythmic silhouette against riverbank pines.

A view of the Gozanoishi Shrine on the wooded shore of Lake Tazawa, Japan's deepest lake. The print uses Hasui's signature still-water reflections and bokashi-shaded skies to anchor the small red torii within an expansive landscape.
collection-of-beauty-taj-mahal-by-charle: Made during Bartlett's Asian travels and printed in Tokyo by the publisher Watanabe Shozaburo, the sheet fuses British watercolour atmosphere with Japanese shin-hanga woodblock craft. The marble mausoleum floats above its reflecting pool in flat, graded washes of dusk colour.
collection-of-beauty-takiyasha-the-witch: A nishiki-e triptych staging the sorceress Takiyasha as she summons a colossal skeleton against the warrior Mitsukuni in the ruined Soma palace. Kuniyoshi compresses three full sheets into one continuous, theatrically lit scene drawn from the gothic literature of late Edo.
collection-of-beauty-tamakatzura-tamator: The ama diver Tamatori clutches the Dragon King's pearl as sea creatures swarm in pursuit. Kuniyoshi treats the legendary recovery dive as a swirling, kinetic composition typical of his late ukiyo-e narrative prints.
collection-of-beauty-tamatori-being-purs: A second telling of the Tamatori legend, with the diver fleeing the underwater palace as a dragon and its attendants give chase. Kuniyoshi exploits the woodblock medium's capacity for sweeping diagonals and undulating tendrils of marine life.
collection-of-beauty-tempelskatten-peter: Despite the catalogue title, the panel records a bustling Flemish ferry crossing to Antwerp, packed with passengers, cargo and livestock. Jordaens animates the scene with the boisterous, low-life realism that anchored his early Antwerp output.
collection-of-beauty-tentaciones-de-cris: A fresco from the south wall of the Sistine Chapel staging all three temptations of Christ around a centrally placed temple based on Rome's Hospital of Santo Spirito. Botticelli folds the gospel narrative into a contemporary Roman setting alive with allegorical figures and Medici allusions.
collection-of-beauty-terror-antiquus-by-: Lightning splits a darkening sky over the Aegean as an archaic kore smiles enigmatically in the foreground, the Acropolis and the citadels of Mycenae and Tiryns flickering below. Bakst built the 250 by 270 cm canvas after a 1907 trip to Greece with Serov, aiming at an apocalyptic fable of ancient cataclysm. It won a gold medal at the 1910 Brussels Exposition Universelle and entered the State Russian Museum.
collection-of-beauty-terrour-or-fright-f: A head with eyes flung wide and mouth open in a scream, codifying Terrour or Fright in the system of facial passions. Engraved for Robert Sayer's 1765 English edition after Charles Le Brun's Paris academy lectures, the plate is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-the-abduction-of-th: Roman men seize struggling Sabine women in a tangle of figures, a classical history subject. Millet worked the canvas around 1844 to 1847, in the period before he settled at Barbizon and turned to peasant labour; the scene follows the Livy episode long favoured by academic painters.
collection-of-beauty-the-antiques-seller: A genre interior in oil on panel showing an antiques dealer surrounded by carpets, ceramics and weaponry from the Ottoman world. Weisse, a Czech-born painter active in Paris, specialised in such Orientalist bazaar scenes detailed with cabinet-picture precision.
collection-of-beauty-the-artist-s-garden: A corner of Monet's Argenteuil garden ablaze with dahlias, with the painter's house glimpsed beyond a wooden fence. The canvas — long associated with a similar work by Renoir painted alongside Monet — applies broken Impressionist touches to translate the heat of late summer.
collection-of-beauty-the-artist-s-wife: The painter's wife seated in his studio, surrounded by the props of his trade. Oil on canvas, 40.6 by 32.9 cm, at the Clark Art Institute and dated about 1795 to 1799. Boilly returned often to domestic interiors built around a single figure.
collection-of-beauty-the-arts-painting: Part of Mucha's four-panel allegorical suite The Arts, this lithograph personifies Painting as a young woman in profile contemplating a flower at twilight. The slender format, ornamented halo and arabesque border are classic vocabulary of Mucha's Paris-period Art Nouveau.
collection-of-beauty-the-attack-by-veres: A surging Russian infantry charge with fixed bayonets, drawn from Vereshchagin's late series on the 1812 Napoleonic invasion. The painter, a veteran himself, refused heroic abstraction, packing the canvas with the smoke, mud and panic of close-quarters assault.
collection-of-beauty-the-back-of-the-fuj: A woodblock view from the series Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, taken from the rear face of the mountain along the Minobu River. Hokusai contrasts the sinuous river bend and rocky banks with the broad, simplified silhouette of the peak, animated by tiny travelling figures.
collection-of-beauty-the-barber-institut: Turner's marine pairs working fishermen and beached fish with a low sun burning through coastal mist. Held by the Barber Institute, the picture exemplifies his early atmospheric naturalism, in which form is dissolved by light and humidity rather than drawn line.
collection-of-beauty-the-bathing-posts-b: A small panel of bathing markers driven into the Breton sand under a soft, overcast sky. Whistler reduces the seaside to a few horizontal bands of muted colour, in keeping with the tonal restraint and Aestheticist economy of his late oils.
collection-of-beauty-the-beach-at-etreta: Monet returned repeatedly to the Normandy coast at Étretat to paint its arched chalk cliffs and the Aiguille needle rising from the surf. Here the wet shingle catches a cold marine light, broken brushwork translating wind, spray and shifting weather into pure sensation.
collection-of-beauty-the-beach-at-trouvi: Painted on the Normandy coast during Monet's honeymoon summer, the canvas shows two seated women — likely Camille Monet and a companion — under parasols on the windswept sand. Grains of beach are embedded in the paint, a documentary trace of the open-air method.
collection-of-beauty-the-beautiful-serva: A young servant girl pauses with a basket, her white cap and rose-flushed cheeks set against a softly brushed interior. Jean-Honoré Fragonard worked the picture in his fluid, loaded manner inherited from Boucher; it entered the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm, where it carries the inventory number NM 22465.
collection-of-beauty-the-beheading-of-sa: Painted for the Oratory of San Giovanni in Valletta, where it remains the only canvas Caravaggio signed — in the spilled blood of the saint. The huge, half-lit composition stages the executioner mid-action with Caravaggio's signature tenebrist sobriety.
collection-of-beauty-the-blinding-of-sam: A violent rendering of Judges 16, with Philistine soldiers pinning Samson while a blade is driven into his eye and Delilah flees with the shorn hair. Rembrandt extracts maximal drama from a sudden shaft of daylight cutting into the cave-like darkness.
collection-of-beauty-the-blue-boy: A young man in a slashed blue satin suit of the Van Dyck period stands in a parkland landscape, plumed hat in hand. Painted around 1770 and shown at the Royal Academy in 1770, Gainsborough's portrait of the ironmonger's son Jonathan Buttall now hangs at the Huntington Library in San Marino.
collection-of-beauty-the-burning-of-the-: The 84-gun Ottoman flagship Mansur al-liwa explodes in red flame off the coast of Chios while Konstantinos Kanaris steers his fireship clear in the foreground. Aivazovsky painted the night attack of 6,7 June 1822, a Greek reprisal for the massacre of Chios during the War of Independence; the 162 by 223 cm canvas hangs in the National Gallery in Athens.
collection-of-beauty-the-card-sharp-on-t: A card game at a makeshift table on a sunlit Parisian boulevard, a sharper at work among a mixed crowd of players and onlookers. Oil on panel, 24 by 33 cm, in the National Gallery of Art, Washington. Boilly showed it in 1808 with a pendant of young Savoyards displaying their marmot, among his first street scenes of everyday Paris.
collection-of-beauty-the-christian-marty: A Roman arena scene in which kneeling Christians pray as lions are released and crucified figures burn against the stadium walls. Gerome combines archaeological detail of the Circus Maximus with the polished academic finish typical of his Salon machines.
collection-of-beauty-the-coast-of-seven-: A print from Hokusai's Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, in which a clearing of pruned, circular pines frames the distant volcano. The flattened decorative pattern of the foliage demonstrates the artist's command of Edo-period graphic abstraction.
collection-of-beauty-the-collector-of-pr: A bearded amateur sits in a tightly packed Parisian study, a bundle of unmounted prints on his knees and folios of engravings stacked against the walls. Degas exhibited the canvas at the 1867 Paris Salon; it is now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, an early example of his interest in the absorbed urban specialist.
collection-of-beauty-the-concert-a22894: Five figures around a draped table sing and play violin and lute by the light of a single candle, a music book turned toward the viewer. Signed and dated 1623, the National Gallery of Art canvas in Washington belongs to the Utrecht Caravaggist genre of merry companies that Honthorst painted after settling back in his home city.
collection-of-beauty-the-conspiracy-of-t: The surviving central fragment of Rembrandt's largest history painting, commissioned for Amsterdam's new Town Hall. Civilis raises a sword in a one-eyed oath-taking with his Batavian rebels — a coarsely lit, almost barbaric image that the city soon rejected.
collection-of-beauty-the-creation-of-ada: A fresco at the centre of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, in which God reaches across the void to a languid Adam. Michelangelo compresses the moment of ensoulment into the famously unmet gap between the two extended fingers.
collection-of-beauty-the-daughters-of-ed: Four sisters stand in the dim foyer of the Boit family's Paris apartment, the youngest seated on the rug, the eldest pair half-swallowed by shadow beside a pair of monumental Japanese vases. Sargent borrowed the deep recessive space and palette directly from Velazquez's Las Meninas, which he had copied in Madrid in 1879; the picture entered the MFA Boston in 1919.
collection-of-beauty-the-death-of-the-ea: William Pitt collapses among fifty-five identifiable peers beneath tapestries of the Spanish Armada's defeat, the moment of his fall in the House of Lords on 7 April 1778. Copley worked on the ten-foot canvas for two years and in 1781 installed it in a pavilion as a paying one-work show; it is now at Tate.
collection-of-beauty-the-descent-from-th: Nicodemus and John the Evangelist lower the body of Christ while the Virgin faints among the holy women. Painted by Charles Le Brun in the late 1640s, the 75 by 62 centimetre canvas dates from his first years back in Paris after study with Poussin in Rome, and was acquired by LACMA in 2004 with funds exchanged through the Joseph B. Gould Foundation.
collection-of-beauty-the-doorway-met-dp8: An ornate Renaissance doorway opens directly onto the water of a Venetian canal, its carved frame and latticed windows etched in dense detail that thins to almost nothing at the edges of the plate; a figure pauses on the shadowed steps within. The etching and drypoint belongs to the First Venice Set, the twelve plates the Fine Art Society commissioned from Whistler in 1879 after his bankruptcy. The doorway is that of Palazzo Gussoni on the Rio de la Fava; this impression is in the Metropolitan Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-the-emperor-commodu: An engraving from Goltzius's Roman Heroes series, depicting the megalomaniac emperor in the lion-skin and club of Hercules. The muscular low-angle figure and virtuoso swelling burin lines exemplify the technical bravura of Northern Mannerist printmaking.
collection-of-beauty-the-end-of-the-pose: A studio interior in which a model steps down from the dais at the close of a session, while the artist's marble in progress stands beside her. Gerome, both painter and sculptor, treats the academic ritual with cool, polished precision and an eye for telling props.
collection-of-beauty-the-entombment-of-c: Nicodemus crouches under the weight of the dead Christ while the Virgin and the Marys raise their arms in grief above the cold stone slab. Painted between 1600 and 1603 for the Vittrice chapel in Santa Maria in Vallicella in Rome, Caravaggio anchors the descending diagonal of bodies on a corner of bare rock pushed out toward the viewer.
collection-of-beauty-the-fall-of-man-161: Adam and Eve are shown beneath the Tree of Knowledge with the serpent coiled overhead, their elongated bodies posed in a Mannerist contrapposto. A late work by the Haarlem master, treating the Genesis subject with the smooth idealism of his post-Italian style.
collection-of-beauty-the-famous-scenes-o: A vertical ōban from the Famous Places in the Sixty-odd Provinces series, looking down on the swirling Naruto whirlpools that churn between Awa and Awaji. Hiroshige flattens the sea into concentric arcs of bokashi blue, framed by a steep cliff at left.
collection-of-beauty-the-farm-at-les-col: The farmhouse at Les Collettes seen through a screen of olive and orange trees, the foliage broken into flickering touches of green and rose. Renoir bought the estate at Cagnes near Nice in 1907 and moved there in 1908, painting the farm repeatedly between 1908 and 1914. Oil on canvas, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York.
collection-of-beauty-the-feast-in-the-ho: A vast Venetian banquet staged in a Palladian loggia of three Serlian arches, populated by guests, servants, dwarves, dogs and a parrot. Originally painted as a Last Supper, the work was retitled after the Inquisition objected to its profane figures.
collection-of-beauty-the-fighting-temera: The 98-gun veteran of Trafalgar is towed by a black steam tug along the Thames toward the breaker's yard, set against a smouldering sunset. Turner contrasts the pale, ghostly hulk with the squat industrial tug, mourning the passing of the age of sail.
collection-of-beauty-the-fountaine-famil: Conversation piece showing the Norfolk landowner Brigg Price Fountaine with his wife Mary and children Andrew and Elizabeth, a spaniel at their feet, set in the drawing room of Narford Hall. Painted in 1776 at the start of Copley's English career, the picture adapts the manner of Johann Zoffany and entered Tate Britain through Arts Council England's Cultural Gift Scheme.
collection-of-beauty-the-fuji-from-kanay: An additional view from the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, looking across the boulder-strewn Ōi River from the Kanaya post-station toward a snow-capped Fuji. Travellers and porters ford the shallows in the foreground, anchoring the landscape in everyday Tōkaidō life.
collection-of-beauty-the-gold-scab-erupt: Whistler's savage caricature of his former patron Frederick Leyland, painted in 1879 after the Peacock Room dispute and Whistler's bankruptcy, in which Leyland was a creditor. Leyland appears as a scaly, peacock-feathered demon seated on Whistler's White House while playing the piano — a jab at his amateur musicianship — with sacks of money at his feet. The painting is now in the de Young Museum, San Francisco.
collection-of-beauty-the-golden-age-oil-: Naked figures recline beneath fruiting trees in a paradisal grove drawn from the opening books of Ovid's Metamorphoses. Painted in oil on copper in 1605 and now at the Metropolitan Museum of Art, the small plate showcases Wtewael's Utrecht Mannerism at its most refined, the polished metal support intensifying the jewel-like colour.
collection-of-beauty-the-golden-pavilion: Yoshida Hiroshi's colour woodblock print of Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion in Kyoto, from his 1933 Kansai District series. The gilded temple rises over its reflecting pond in the layered, atmospheric colour that defined Yoshida's shin-hanga landscapes. This impression belongs to the San Diego Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-the-gorge-at-vareng: Painted on the Normandy coast near Dieppe, this canvas looks down through a wooded ravine toward a sliver of the Channel. Monet's broken touches of green, ochre and lilac translate the cliff vegetation into vibrating colour.
collection-of-beauty-the-grand-canal-of-: Painted on a Venetian visit alongside Monet, the canvas captures the Grand Canal in shimmering broken touches of blue, white and ochre. Striped mooring posts cut vertical accents through the rippling water, marking Manet's most overtly Impressionist experiment.
collection-of-beauty-the-grand-quay-at-h: A working harbour view of Monet's home port, painted the year of the first Impressionist exhibition. Masts, smokestacks and reflections dissolve into rapid, comma-like strokes, the artist treating modern dockside bustle with the same atmospheric urgency he had just brought to Impression, Sunrise.
collection-of-beauty-the-holy-family-wit: An intimate devotional panel showing the Madonna and Child with St Elizabeth, the infant Baptist and a hovering dove of the Holy Spirit. The warm flesh tones and tender exchange of glances reflect Rubens's recent return from Italy.
collection-of-beauty-the-hookah-lighter: An Orientalist genre scene of a turbaned attendant kindling the coals of a water pipe in a tiled interior. Gérôme's polished academic finish renders brass, silk and ceramic with photographic precision.
collection-of-beauty-the-house-on-the-ri: Painted during Monet's Dutch sojourn after the Franco-Prussian War, the canvas shows a row of green-shuttered houses reflected in the Zaan. Long horizontal brushstrokes mirror the calm of the Holland waterways that fascinated him.
collection-of-beauty-the-ill-matched-pai: A satirical Antwerp moral subject in which a young woman fingers the purse of an enamoured old man. Matsys updates a theme inherited from his father Quinten with sharper caricature and a cool grey-green palette.
collection-of-beauty-the-incredulity-of-: Christ guides the apostle's finger into the wound in his side as two other disciples crane forward to watch. Caravaggio collapses the moment into a tight, half-length composition lit from the upper left, the brows knit in shared concentration.
collection-of-beauty-the-intervention-of: Hersilia throws herself between the Roman king Romulus and her Sabine father Tatius, infants crawling at her feet as the two armies pause on the field. David painted the canvas in 1799 during and after his post-Thermidor imprisonment, intending the subject of reconciliation as a plea for an end to French factional bloodshed.
collection-of-beauty-the-judgement-of-pa: The Trojan prince hands the golden apple to Venus while Juno and Minerva turn away, with Cupid, Mercury, and a peacock crowded into a wooded clearing. Wtewael's National Gallery panel of 1615 packs the Olympian quarrel into a small copper plate, the polished metal support giving the figures their characteristic enamel sheen.
collection-of-beauty-the-junction-of-the: An estuary scene with merchantmen and a small boat tossed in choppy water where the two rivers meet. Turner builds the squally light from layered glazes, showing his early debt to Dutch marine painters.
collection-of-beauty-the-kitchen-maid-re: A young woman leans on a stone windowsill, her arms folded, gazing out at the viewer in warm reds, browns and ochres. Signed and dated 1651, the half-length is now in the Nationalmuseum in Stockholm and is thought to depict a member of Rembrandt's own household rather than a hired model.
collection-of-beauty-the-knife-grinder-p: A grinder pumps his treadle wheel on a tenement stair, his hands and the spinning blade multiplied into repeated facets to suggest motion. Malevich gave the canvas the subtitle Principle of Glittering and showed it in 1913 alongside the Russian Cubo-Futurists; it now belongs to the Yale University Art Gallery.
collection-of-beauty-the-lake-of-hakone-: From Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji, this print sets the still mirror of Lake Hakone in the foreground, with Fuji rising over wooded ridges beyond. Hokusai contrasts smooth bands of water with crisply outlined cedars and the modulated bokashi gradations of the sky.
collection-of-beauty-the-lawyer-possibly: A pile of legal books and document rolls draped in a fur-trimmed gown, the face assembled from plucked poultry and small fish, possibly satirising the humanist jurist Ulrich Zasius. Painted in 1566 and now in the Nationalmuseum, Stockholm, the panel reads as a sly Habsburg court joke at the expense of paper-bound learning.
collection-of-beauty-the-lion-and-the-mo: An Aesop subject likely painted in collaboration with Frans Snyders, who handled the animals while Rubens supplied the human figure. The freed lion crouches beside the sleeping man as the tiny mouse gnaws through the rope.
collection-of-beauty-the-luncheon-by-cla: An ambitious early figure piece showing Monet's companion Camille and their son Jean at a sunlit table, with a visitor lingering at the garden's edge. Submitted to and rejected by the 1870 Salon, it announces the everyday subjects that would define Impressionism.
collection-of-beauty-the-lute-player: A single seated figure tunes a long-necked lute in a dim Cairo interior, the strings catching a shaft of light. Gérôme uses the musician as a pretext for a study in muted tonality and meticulous costume detail.
collection-of-beauty-the-madonna-and-chi: The Virgin sits directly on the ground in the pose of the Madonna of Humility, her ample drapery pooling around her as she holds the Christ Child, whose head radiates spikes of light. Behind her a bare tree and the gate tower of a walled courtyard close off the scene — an enclosed garden alluding to Mary's purity. The engraving bears Schongauer's M†S monogram and was made in his Colmar workshop around 1470-91.
collection-of-beauty-the-mantree-bosch: A drawing of the hollow tree-bodied figure that recurs in the right wing of the Garden of Earthly Delights, his cracked eggshell torso supported on legs that end in tiny boats. Long attributed to Bosch's own hand, the sheet is among the few surviving drawings linked to him.
collection-of-beauty-the-massacre-of-the: Herod's soldiers, rendered as muscular nudes, seize infants from their screaming mothers in a paved square before a bridge, the violence choreographed across the sheet like a frieze. The engraving was cut by Marcantonio Raimondi around 1512-13 after a design Raphael made expressly for the print — the tablet at left reads 'RAPH URBI INVEN' — and their partnership became the chief channel through which Raphael's compositions spread across Europe. It ranks among the most celebrated engravings of the Italian Renaissance.

Herod's soldiers wrench infants from their mothers in a writhing knot of bodies before a palace portico, the women clawing and biting back at their attackers. This is Rubens's second, late treatment of the subject, painted around 1636-38 with the loose handling and theatrical energy of his final decade. The monumental canvas, over three metres wide, hangs in the Alte Pinakothek in Munich.
collection-of-beauty-the-milk-maid-by-wi: A young woman in a bonnet and apron carries a brimming pail through a sunlit pasture. Homer's loose, summery handling belongs to the Houghton Farm watercolours and oils that distilled American rural life in the post-Civil War decade.
collection-of-beauty-the-mocking-of-chri: Soldiers press the crown of thorns onto Christ's head and raise a reed sceptre in mockery, the bodies looming out of brown shadow around a hidden candle. Painted in Rome around 1617 and now at LACMA, Honthorst applies the tenebrism he learned from Caravaggio to a half-length devotional format favoured by the Giustiniani circle.
collection-of-beauty-the-moreno-garden-a: Painted during Monet's 1884 stay on the Italian Riviera, the canvas captures the orange-and-olive grove of the Moreno estate at Bordighera. Tangled trunks and a brilliant Mediterranean palette mark the artist's response to a southern light that he likened to fairyland.
collection-of-beauty-the-moscow-cathedra: A view across the thawing Moskva toward the bulbous domes of the Kremlin cathedrals. Vereshchagin, better known as a war painter, here records the Russian capital with the same documentary precision he brought to his battlefield reportage.
collection-of-beauty-the-muezzin-1865-je: A solitary cleric calls the faithful to prayer from a high minaret balcony, the city of Cairo spreading out far below. The vertiginous viewpoint and crisp morning light are typical of Gérôme's Egyptian travel subjects.
collection-of-beauty-the-muscles-of-the-: An anatomical engraving combining a flayed hand after Bernhard Siegfried Albinus with a foot after De Courcelles, the muscles, tendons and bones laid bare for study. Engraved by Robert Bénard for the late eighteenth-century editions of the Encyclopédie, the plate typifies the Enlightenment project of consolidating earlier anatomical illustration into a single compendium.
collection-of-beauty-the-old-adam-and-ev: A pen-and-ink illustration prepared for an edition of Carlyle's Sartor Resartus, picturing the first couple as worn, clothed elders rather than as youthful nudes. Sullivan's nervous cross-hatched line carries the late-Victorian taste for Symbolist book ornament.
collection-of-beauty-the-painter-s-daugh: Margaret and Mary Gainsborough, the painter's daughters, lean into one another while a cat curls into Margaret's arm, the picture left unfinished with the animal sketched only in outline. One of around a dozen portraits Gainsborough painted of the girls across their childhood, it now hangs in the National Gallery, London.
collection-of-beauty-the-petit-bras-of-t: A quiet backwater of the Seine fringed by bare poplars and reflected on a glassy surface. Painted in the first weeks of Monet's settlement at Argenteuil, the canvas balances delicate atmospheric grey-blues against incipient Impressionist touch.
collection-of-beauty-the-pond-at-benten-: A shin-hanga woodblock from Hasui's Tokyo Twenty Views, showing the red-railed bridge to the Benten shrine reflected in still water at twilight. Layered bokashi gradations and crisp keyblock lines exemplify the Watanabe workshop's revival of ukiyo-e technique.
collection-of-beauty-the-ragpicker-1869-: A life-size Spanish-inspired portrait of a Paris chiffonnier propped on his stick, set against a neutral grey ground. Manet borrows the format of Velázquez's philosopher portraits to dignify a marginal modern Parisian.
collection-of-beauty-the-rising-squall-h: An early oil view from the cliffs above the Avon Gorge as a sudden storm sweeps in over the Hot Wells spa. The seventeen-year-old Turner already orchestrates wind, rain and shifting light into a unified atmospheric event.
collection-of-beauty-the-river-le-fleuve: A male nude seated by water, the figure modelled in warm flesh tones against a loosely brushed bank. Dated 1885, the period when Renoir tightened his contours under the influence of Ingres and Raphael. The study is attributed to Renoir and reproduced from a monograph on the painter.
collection-of-beauty-the-school-of-athen: Ancient philosophers, mathematicians and scientists gather under coffered Roman barrel vaults, with Plato and Aristotle striding forward at the vanishing point. Painted between 1509 and 1511 for the Stanza della Segnatura in the Vatican, the fresco includes Raphael's own face beside Ptolemy in the lower right group.
collection-of-beauty-the-sea-at-le-havre: A grey Channel seascape painted from the harbour Monet had known since childhood, with sailing vessels riding a low swell beneath broken cloud. The high horizon and economical palette anticipate the marines of the following decade.
collection-of-beauty-the-secret-message-: A young woman in a satin gown leans on a stone parapet to read a folded billet, her companion looking on in the garden shade. Oil on canvas, 60 by 50.5 cm, signed and dated lower right FBoucher / 1767, now in the Herzog Anton Ulrich-Museum at Braunschweig.
collection-of-beauty-the-seine-at-bougiv: Painted from the riverbank at the village that drew Monet, Renoir and Pissarro alike, the scene catches a row of moored boats and the mirror of the Seine. Quick, comma-shaped strokes record passing reflections rather than fixed contours.
collection-of-beauty-the-siege-and-relie: Spanish and French floating batteries burn at anchor under the guns of Gibraltar on the night of 13 September 1782, the rock looming behind the rescued sailors in the foreground. Copley spent eight years on the vast canvas, commissioned by the Corporation of the City of London, which still hangs in the Guildhall.
collection-of-beauty-the-sleepers-by-gus: Two nude women lie entwined in dishevelled bedding, jewellery and a broken pearl strand scattered on the sheet. Commissioned by the Turkish diplomat Khalil-Bey, the canvas treats lesbian love with a frank realism that scandalised the Second Empire.
collection-of-beauty-the-soldier-and-the: A grinning soldier in a plumed hat offers a coin to a smiling girl who holds out her palm in the candlelight. Honthorst painted the half-length brothel scene around 1621 after returning from Italy to Utrecht, transposing Caravaggio's bordello subjects into the Dutch market for cabinet pictures.
collection-of-beauty-the-sorrows-of-love: A woman supported by a companion grieves while a servant returns her portrait and an unopened letter, signalling the end of an affair. Oil on canvas, 45 by 55 cm, in the Wallace Collection, London. The picture belongs to a set of eleven works on the stages of love that Boilly painted for the Avignon collector Calvet de Lapalun.
collection-of-beauty-the-sower-jean-fran: A peasant striding across a furrowed field, his arm flung out in the act of casting seed. Pastel and Conté crayon on beige paper, about 47 by 37.5 cm, made around 1865 and held by the Clark Art Institute in Williamstown. Millet returned to the sower motif across his career in oil, pastel and print.
collection-of-beauty-the-steadfast-philo: An elderly philosopher in a fur-trimmed gown ignores a young woman who tries to pull his book away, her exposed shoulder and laughing companion staging the temptation. Signed and dated 1623, the canvas survives in the Hohenbuchau collection at Schloss Schlangenbad and treats the Stoic ideal of constantia as a candlelit half-length.
collection-of-beauty-the-taking-of-chris: Judas presses forward to deliver his kiss as an armoured soldier seizes Christ's neck and a fleeing apostle howls behind. A self-portrait of the painter raising a lantern at the right edge introduces the artist into the violent nocturne.
collection-of-beauty-the-tea-plantation-: A woodblock print from the Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji series, framing the sacred peak through workers tending neat rows of tea bushes in Suruga Province. Hokusai integrates rural labor with landscape, the foreground figures pressing leaves into bundles while Fuji rises in cool, flat planes behind.
collection-of-beauty-the-tea-service-oil: An early domestic still life from Monet's Argenteuil years, when he briefly turned from landscape to tabletop subjects. A lacquered tray, porcelain cups and a polished kettle are arranged with Japoniste restraint, the gleaming surfaces reflecting his admiration for Manet and for Edo lacquerware.
collection-of-beauty-the-third-wise-virg: A young woman with loose waist-length hair and a wreath of foliage holds a burning oil lamp upright on her open palm — the mark of the wise virgins in Christ's parable of the ten bridesmaids (Matthew 25), who kept their lamps filled for the bridegroom's arrival. The sheet belongs to Schongauer's engraved series of the Wise and Foolish Virgins, each figure isolated on a small mound of ground. His M†S monogram appears below.
collection-of-beauty-the-toilet-of-venus: Venus is attended by three putti among rich silks, pearls, and roses, in a panel originally set into the carved boiseries of Madame de Pompadour's Château de Bellevue. Boucher referred back to her 1750 stage role in Pierre Laujon's ballet La Toilette de Vénus, and the Vanderbilts bequeathed the panel to the Metropolitan Museum in 1920.
collection-of-beauty-the-tribute-money: Christ holds the coin retrieved from the fish's mouth before the Pharisees, instructing his followers to render unto Caesar. Copley painted the religious composition in 1782 for the Royal Academy, where he was working to extend his reputation beyond portraiture in the wake of his successful Watson and the Shark.
collection-of-beauty-the-tribute-money-j: John Singleton Copley's oil on canvas depicts the Gospel episode of the tribute money, in which Christ, asked whether it is lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, points heavenward as a grey-bearded questioner indicates the coin lying in his open palm. The half-length figures press close around Christ, their faces picked out against a dark ground in a deliberately old-masterly manner. Copley gave the painting to the Royal Academy of Arts in London in 1782 as his Diploma Work following his election as a Royal Academician.
collection-of-beauty-the-triumph-of-bacc: An exuberant Rococo procession of the wine god, attended by satyrs, maenads and tumbling putti amid garlands and overturned vessels. Natoire animates the mythological subject with feathery brushwork and pearled flesh tones characteristic of the French eighteenth century court taste.
collection-of-beauty-the-triumph-of-chri: A vast allegorical canvas in which a cross-bearing Christ, ringed by sword-wielding angels, sweeps above the toppling deities of antiquity. Dore stages the contest as a vertiginous airborne procession, exploiting the canvas's monumental scale to push the pagan host into chaotic free-fall below.
collection-of-beauty-the-triumph-of-deat: Death triumphs over the world: a vast army of skeletons drives the living of every estate into a great coffin, the landscape behind reduced to ruin. Pieter Bruegel the Elder's panel of c. 1562 fuses the medieval danse macabre with the panoramic worldview that would carry into seventeenth-century Flemish painting.
collection-of-beauty-the-triumph-of-fred: An allegorical celebration of the Dutch stadtholder Frederick Henry, painted for the Oranjezaal at Huis ten Bosch. Jordaens orchestrates a swirling Baroque cavalcade of personifications, captives, and trophies in the Rubensian Antwerp manner, glorifying the prince's military and political triumphs.
collection-of-beauty-the-vision-of-the-v: An engraving from Dore's illustrated Bible, depicting Ezekiel's vision in which scattered bones reanimate as a vast army. The artist exploits dense crosshatching and dramatic chiaroscuro to give the desolate plain a haunted, otherworldly atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-the-wailing-wall-by: An Orientalist tableau of worshippers gathered in prayer at the Western Wall in Jerusalem. Bauernfeind, trained as an architect, renders the weathered ashlar masonry and embroidered prayer shawls with exacting documentary precision, capturing the devotional hush of the site.
collection-of-beauty-the-water-lily-pond: A view across the Japanese footbridge spanning the lily pond at Monet's Giverny garden, the green arch dissolving into shimmering reflections. The painting belongs to the celebrated bridge series in which Monet examined a single subject under shifting conditions of light.
collection-of-beauty-the-white-horse-by-: The first of Constable's six-foot Stour valley canvases, showing a workhorse ferried across the river on a flat-bottomed barge. Constable elevates everyday East Anglian labor to grand-manner scale, with broken impasto highlights and a damp, atmospheric sky.
collection-of-beauty-the-wounded-heron: A heron struck down in a hawking scene sprawls in the foreground, its wing spread on the ground. Watts, then about twenty, bought a dead heron from a poulterer to study the bird; the oil on canvas, 91.4 by 71.1 cm, was his Royal Academy debut in 1837 and now belongs to the Watts Gallery, Surrey.
collection-of-beauty-the-zuiderkerk-amst: A view up the Groenburgwal canal toward the spire of the Zuiderkerk, painted during Monet's brief Dutch sojourn. The canvas already carries the rapid, broken brushwork of nascent Impressionism, dissolving brick facades and water into vibrating coloured strokes.
collection-of-beauty-theknightatthecross: An armoured knight on a white horse halts before a moss-covered stone slab on the open steppe, ravens picking at scattered bones nearby. The stone's inscription warns that there is no return for the rider who goes straight ahead. Vasnetsov painted the nearly three-metre 1882 canvas, now in the State Russian Museum, as a free interpretation of the bylina of Ilya Muromets, sticking to ethnographically accurate armour and steppe terrain.
collection-of-beauty-theodore-gericault-: A Romantic landscape in the grand tradition, dwarfing fishermen beneath looming cliffs and gathering storm clouds. Gericault works the scene in dark earth tones, drawing on Poussin and Salvator Rosa to fuse classical composition with fervent natural drama.

One of Gericault's series of portraits depicting inmates of a Paris asylum, each suffering from a specific monomania. The unflinching, dignified treatment of the sitter and the somber palette mark a pioneering encounter between Romantic painting and clinical psychiatry.

An intimate study of two lovers locked in an embrace, modelled with the vigorous, sculptural brushwork that characterises Gericault's late work. The intense physicality and shadowed flesh tones reflect his sustained interest in bodily expression.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-carlyle-oil-: A bust portrait of the historian and essayist Thomas Carlyle, white-bearded and turned in three-quarter view. Painted by Watts in 1868 and given by the artist to the National Portrait Gallery, London, in 1895 (NPG 1002); Carlyle himself disliked the likeness.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-cole-a-view-: Morning mist lifts off the twin Catskill lakes as the white-pillared Catskill Mountain House perches on a cliff above. Cole lived in the village of Catskill from 1836 and painted this 1844 view of the famous hotel that had drawn tourists to the Hudson Valley since 1824.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-cole-archite: A bearded architect reclines on the capital of a fluted column, looking out over a fantastic harbour lined with Egyptian pyramids, Greek temples, Roman aqueducts and a Gothic cathedral at the back. Cole painted the canvas in five weeks for Ithiel Town in 1840, after the New York architect commissioned a view of Athens; Town rejected it as too architectural and the painting is now in the Toledo Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-cole-prometh: The Titan Prometheus is chained to a crag of the Caucasus at dawn, an eagle wheeling above to tear at his liver, the sun rising behind distant snow-capped peaks. Exhibited at the National Academy of Design in 1847, Cole's late mythological piece adapts Aeschylus to the vertical drama of the Hudson River sublime.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-cole-the-voy: An infant glides from a dark cavern in a gilded boat shaped like an hourglass, steered by a winged guardian angel through a lush spring landscape. First of four panels in the National Gallery's 1842 version of The Voyage of Life, a moral allegory of the soul's progress through earthly time.

The traveller, now grown, clasps his hands in prayer as his rudderless boat plunges through a torrent of black rocks under storm clouds, the guardian angel watching from above. Third panel in Cole's 1842 second version of The Voyage of Life, painted in his Catskill studio after the New York set was sold off.

The voyager, white-bearded, drifts on a glassy black sea while his angel gestures upward toward a host of celestial spirits breaking through the clouds. Fourth and final panel of the National Gallery's 1842 set, completing Cole's allegory of the Christian soul's passage from infancy to eternity.

The young traveller, now alone at the tiller, steers toward a shining cloud palace in the sky above a verdant river valley. Second panel in Cole's 1842 second version of The Voyage of Life series at the National Gallery of Art, painted after the original 1840 set passed into private hands.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-eakins-005: Amelia Van Buren, a former Eakins pupil at the Pennsylvania Academy, sits sideways in a carved armchair with one hand against her cheek, her gaze fixed past the viewer. Painted around 1891 and now at the Phillips Collection in Washington, the portrait is one of the unflinching psychological studies of Eakins's mature American Realism.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-eakins-ameri: A monumental scene of surgeon Samuel Gross presiding over an operation before his medical students at Jefferson College. Eakins records the bloodied hand, the chloroformed patient and the rapt amphitheatre with uncompromising realism, anchoring American painting in the lecture-hall light of modern science.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-eakins-the-b: Professional oarsmen John and Bernard Biglin pull in unison in their pair-oared shell during a five-mile race on the Schuylkill River, watched by crowds along the Philadelphia shore. Eakins, an avid rower himself, worked the picture up from drawings and precise perspective studies after attending the contest on 20 May 1872. Now at the National Gallery of Art.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-gage-john-si: General Thomas Gage stands in the scarlet coat of a British commander, his right hand resting on a cane, an encampment visible behind him. Copley's three-quarter-length canvas measures 127 by 101 cm and is inscribed at the lower right with Gage's name and death date of 1788; it belongs to the Paul Mellon Collection at the Yale Center for British Art.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-gainsborough: The actress Sarah Siddons sits in profile against a red curtain, wearing a striped silk dress and a wide black plumed hat. Gainsborough painted his rival to Reynolds's celebrated Tragic Muse in 1785, complaining of the difficulty of her nose; the canvas hangs in the National Gallery, London.

Augustus Hervey, third Earl of Bristol, stands in commodore's undress uniform with a coil of rope at his hand and his ship riding at anchor offshore. Painted by Gainsborough in 1767 for Hervey's seat at Ickworth, the portrait is now in the National Trust collection.

A flock of sheep clusters around a stone spring in a wooded valley, with a herdsman half-glimpsed beneath the dense trees. Gainsborough painted the rural fantasy in 1783 from clay and broccoli models arranged on his studio table, and presented it to the Royal Academy as his diploma work on his election.

A slim, elegantly dressed man identified as Mr Wood, said to have been a dancing master, stands in a quiet Suffolk landscape. The portrait dates from around 1757, near the end of Gainsborough's Ipswich years before he left for Bath in 1759, and is now in the Paul Mellon Collection at the Yale Center for British Art.

Richard St George Mansergh-St George stands in the red uniform of the 4th Regiment of Foot, hat in hand, with a ship at anchor in the distance. Gainsborough painted the full-length on commission in 1776 just before St George shipped for North America, where he was wounded at Germantown in October 1777.

A self-portrait painted around 1758-59, just as Gainsborough left Ipswich for the spa town of Bath. The small canvas, now NPG 4446 in the National Portrait Gallery, almost certainly hung in his studio as an advertisement of his skill; behind the loose, fluent brushwork the trees of a Suffolk landscape can still be made out.

A pastoral scene of cattle pausing at a wooded stream, painted with the feathery, scumbled foliage typical of Gainsborough's mature landscapes. The work belongs to his Suffolk-derived rural idylls, indebted to Dutch seventeenth-century models yet handled with English freshness.

The Welsh sitter Clayton Jones is shown half-length in a brown coat, with the soft rural foliage of a parkland background just visible behind. Gainsborough painted the portrait between 1744 and 1745, during his early London years before he moved his practice to Ipswich.

A late landscape in which a shepherd and flock cross a windswept shore beneath gathering clouds. Gainsborough loosens the topography into soft, tonal silhouettes, prefiguring the atmospheric coastal scenes that would influence British Romantic painters.

Anne Stanhope, wife of the 5th Earl of Chesterfield, sits in a blue and white satin gown with her left arm resting on a plinth, dense foliage behind her and her family's lands opening to the right. Gainsborough painted the 221 by 156 cm canvas in 1777-78, his loose, sweeping brushwork registering sky, drapery, and leaves with equal speed. It is now at the J. Paul Getty Museum.

Frances Browne, later Mrs John Douglas, stands full-length in a white satin gown with a wide black sash, leaning against a stone plinth in a wooded park. Gainsborough painted the portrait in 1783 to 1784 for the sitter's family; it now hangs at Waddesdon Manor, the National Trust Rothschild house in Buckinghamshire.

A wooded river landscape in the Dutch-influenced manner of Gainsborough's middle years, with travellers descending toward a rustic bridge. Feathered foliage and a silvery palette establish the gentle, picturesque mood that defined his Bath-period landscapes.

A wooded Suffolk lane opens onto pasture with grazing cattle and a distant church tower under heavy English cloud. Gainsborough painted the canvas between 1746 and 1750, during the early years he spent at Sudbury where the flat East Anglian countryside shaped his lifelong landscape vocabulary.

A wooded riverbank with a low weir, painted in Gainsborough's Suffolk period after his return from London to Sudbury and Ipswich. The canvas, now at the Yale Center for British Art, was acquired by the dealer Panton Betew and engraved in 1764, after which it was cut down on the left to its present near-square shape.

A young Frenchwoman in a powdered chignon and pale gauze gown sits half-length against an indistinct landscape. Gainsborough painted the sitter, identified as Madame Lebrun, in London in 1780 with the feathery brushwork and limited palette he favoured in his late portraiture.

Mary, Countess Howe, walks through a wooded landscape in a pink silk gown lifted to show a quilted petticoat, a black ribbon at her throat. Painted in 1764 at Bath and now at Kenwood House, the portrait is among Gainsborough's most admired full-lengths, the gown rendered in feathery strokes that animate the silk.

Mary Little, later Lady Carr, stands in a pale grey-blue gown with lace cuffs, set against a screen of foliage in the Bath manner. Painted around 1763, the portrait belongs to Gainsborough's mature Bath period and now hangs at Yale Center for British Art, gift of Paul Mellon.

A double portrait of a young Suffolk landowner and his bride seated at the edge of their estate, the rolling cornfields and oak deliberately presented as part of their identity. The crisp early style fuses French rococo elegance with topographical precision unusual in English portraiture.

A full-length portrait of the singer and society beauty Elizabeth Linley, wife of the playwright Sheridan, posed against a windswept landscape. Gainsborough merges sitter and setting through fluttering drapery and feathery foliage in his late, freely brushed manner.

A woman in a powdered coiffure and pale blue silk gown turns three-quarters toward the viewer, the cool palette set against a neutral ground. Gainsborough painted the sitter, sometimes identified as the Duchess of Beaufort, in the loose, late style associated with his Schomberg House years; the canvas now hangs in the Hermitage.

The young squire of Chadacre Hall sits on a grassy bank with his legs splayed and his dog beside him, the tower of All Saints, Lawshall just visible beyond the trees. Painted around 1752 during Gainsborough's Ipswich period and now National Gallery NG5984, the small canvas treats English landscape and portraiture as a single intimate field.

A rural landscape in which figures with laden horses return along a sunken track at the close of day. Gainsborough constructs the scene from imagined, idealised motifs, building a poetic vision of English country life in the Bath-period pastoral mode.

The Ipswich apothecary John Gravenor sits with his second wife Ann and their daughters Elizabeth and Ann at the edge of a cornfield, the daughters holding freshly picked flowers. Probably commissioned in 1754 to mark Gravenor's entry into local politics, the square canvas is now in the Paul Mellon Collection at the Yale Center for British Art.

Mary Cathcart, the seventeen-year-old Honourable Mrs Graham, stands in a feathered hat and dress of pink silk and lace, one hand resting on a stone pedestal. Gainsborough exhibited the full-length at the Royal Academy in 1777, two years after painting it; her widower hid the canvas after her early death and it entered the Scottish National Gallery in 1859.

Fashionable Londoners promenade in pairs and small groups under the avenue of trees in St James's Park, their pale dresses catching the filtered light. Gainsborough modelled the figures from a doll dressed in different gowns; the canvas of 1783 is held by the Frick Collection in New York.

The four Marsham children of Stratton Strawless play in a wooded landscape, the eldest girl gathering nuts while her brother reaches up to a sapling. Gainsborough painted the group portrait in 1787, the year before his death, combining the conversation-piece tradition with the feathery foliage and silvery palette of his late manner.
collection-of-beauty-thomas-howard-ruben: A state portrait of Thomas Howard, 14th Earl of Arundel, the great English collector of antiquities, painted during Rubens's diplomatic stay in London. The sitter is shown armoured and commanding, in the rich blacks and gleaming highlights of mature Flemish Baroque portraiture.
collection-of-beauty-three-friends-of-wi: An ink handscroll bringing together pine, bamboo and flowering plum, the classical scholarly emblems of resilience that endure through winter. Zhao Mengjian, a Song-dynasty literatus, brushes the trio in spare, calligraphic strokes that fuse poetry, painting and personal virtue.
collection-of-beauty-three-sisters-by-ya: A four-fold screen painted in ink and color on silk by the nihonga artist Yamakawa Shuho in 1936. Three young women in kimono are grouped around a white motor car: one leans against the front fender holding a handbag, another sits inside the open rear door, and the third looks out through the back window, a quietly modern image of well-to-do life in 1930s Japan rendered in the flat, elegant manner of traditional figure painting. The screen is in the Honolulu Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-and-lukr: A late Mannerist treatment of the Roman legend in which Tarquin's assault on Lucretia precipitates the founding of the Republic. Tintoretto stages the violence with twisting bodies, broken pearls and torn drapery, the diagonal composition lit by sharp Venetian chiaroscuro.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-depositi: A nocturnal Lamentation in which the slumped body of Christ is supported by mourning figures emerging from deep shadow. Tintoretto compresses the scene around a single shaft of light, using elongated forms and rapid brushwork characteristic of his late Venetian manner.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-jacopo-c: A Venetian rendering of the Gospel episode in which Christ appears to the disciples on a storm-tossed sea. The dramatic torsion of the figures, raking light and turbulent green-grey waves are characteristic of the Tintoretto workshop, though the attribution has been debated in favour of Lambert Sustris.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-prayer-i: A nocturnal Agony in the Garden, with Christ kneeling in radiant spotlight while the disciples slumber and torch-bearing soldiers approach through the olive grove. The picture exemplifies Tintoretto's preference for elongated figures, plunging diagonals and theatrical chiaroscuro.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-st-mary-: A solitary image of the penitent Magdalen withdrawn in a rocky wilderness with her book and ointment jar. Tintoretto isolates the saint against a brooding twilight landscape, animating the meditation with flickering, sketch-like brushwork.
collection-of-beauty-tintoretto-the-bapt: A Mannerist treatment of the Baptism in which crowds press toward the Jordan beneath a luminous descent of the Holy Spirit. Tintoretto orchestrates space through deep diagonals and silvery, restless light, characteristic of his late Venetian altarpieces.
collection-of-beauty-titian-self-portrai: A late self-portrait of the Venetian master, shown in three-quarter profile with brush in hand and the gold chain of imperial favor across his black robe. The looser handling and reserved gaze typify Titian's introspective final decade.
collection-of-beauty-titian-the-flaying-: Apollo punishes the satyr Marsyas for his musical hubris, suspending him upside down to be skinned alive. Painted in the artist's final years, the canvas is built from open, almost dissolving brushwork that anticipates later European painting.
collection-of-beauty-titian-venus-with-a: Venus sits draped in red velvet and white linen while two cupids hold up a looking-glass and a wreath above her, her hand drawn modestly across her breast. Painted around 1555 for Titian's own collection and kept by his family until his death, the canvas is now in the National Gallery of Art, Washington, the prime version of a composition he repeated for European princes.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-015-2: One of Titian's mythological poesie made for Philip II of Spain, depicting Diana's discovery of the pregnant nymph Callisto among her bathing companions. Diagonal drapery, a marbled fountain and richly varied flesh tones articulate the moment of accusation.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-080: A bearded Venetian patrician turns in three-quarter view against a dark ground, his black coat and white shirt rendered in broad, fluid strokes. Painted between about 1510 and 1515, the portrait belongs to the early group in which Titian sharpens Giorgione's mood into a more solid, sculpted likeness.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-085: A late poesia for Philip II showing the Phoenician princess carried across the sea on the back of Jupiter disguised as a bull. Loose, atmospheric handling and a glowing pink-gold sky transform the abduction into a turbulent seascape.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-091: Adam and Eve beneath the Tree of Knowledge, the serpent rendered as a child clutching the fatal fruit. Titian gives the Genesis subject a sculptural, classicizing weight, drawing on Northern prototypes filtered through Venetian colorism.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-danae-receiv: Danaë reclines nude on her bed as Jupiter descends as a shower of gold, while an old nursemaid stretches up an apron to catch the falling coins. Among Titian's poesie for the Spanish court, the scene contrasts youthful flesh and wizened greed in loose, atmospheric paint.
collection-of-beauty-tizian-portrait-of-: A court portrait of the Marquis (later Duke) of Mantua, shown in slashed silk and resting one hand on a small white dog as an emblem of fidelity. Titian sets the half-length figure against a neutral ground, balancing courtly polish with naturalistic detail.
collection-of-beauty-tokaido28-mitsuke: Mitsuke, the twenty-eighth station of the Tokaido road, depicting travelers crossing the Tenryu River by ferry. Hiroshige's woodblock design uses graded blue bokashi and a low horizon to evoke morning mist over the water.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-daiko: Daikon-gashi, the radish wharf along the Nihonbashi River, from the series Twelve Scenes of Tokyo. Hasui combines crisp architectural drawing with soft tonal washes typical of the shin-hanga revival of landscape woodblock printing.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-fukag: The Kaminohashi Bridge in Fukagawa, from the series Twelve Scenes of Tokyo. Hasui captures a quiet canal-side moment, using graded inks and reflective water in the shin-hanga tradition that updated ukiyo-e cityscape conventions.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-kiba-: Evening at the Kiba lumber yards, where stacked timber and floating logs catch the last light along the canal. From Twelve Scenes of Tokyo, the print exemplifies Hasui's shin-hanga blend of working-city subject and lyrical atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-samid: Early summer rain falls on the precincts of Hie (Sanno) Shrine, figures sheltering under umbrellas along the wet stone steps. Hasui's woodblock contrasts vertical rain lines against muted greens and greys in the shin-hanga manner.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-shina: A view of fishing boats anchored in the bay off Shinagawa, sails reflected on a tranquil sea. Part of Twelve Scenes of Tokyo, the design relies on flat planes of graded blue and economical silhouettes characteristic of shin-hanga.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-junidai-toyam: A winter moon rises over the bare expanse of the Toyama plain, with tiny figures crossing a darkened field. From Twelve Scenes of Tokyo, the print reduces the landscape to broad tonal bands of deep blue and silvered sky.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-niju-kei-kand: The grounds of the Kanda Myojin shrine, with worshippers passing beneath the vermilion gate. From Twenty Views of Tokyo, the design pairs precise carpentry detail with the soft snow effects that became a Hasui signature.
collection-of-beauty-tokyo-niju-kei-shin: The steel girders of the Shin Ohashi bridge over the Sumida River, rendered through slanting rain and a darkening sky. Hasui treats modern Tokyo infrastructure with the lyrical atmospherics of traditional landscape woodblock printing.
collection-of-beauty-torii-kotondo-kamis: A bijin-ga showing a young woman drawing a comb through her loosened black hair, her undergarment slipping from one shoulder. Kotondo revives the intimate vanity scenes of Edo-period printmaking within the early Showa shin-hanga movement.
collection-of-beauty-torii-kotondo-woman: A bijin-ga in which a woman in a patterned kimono adjusts her hair before a round mirror, the reflection partly visible at the print's edge. Kotondo balances flat decorative pattern against a quietly observed private moment.
collection-of-beauty-toshogu-shrine-5759: A colour woodblock print of the Tōshō-gū shrine at Nikkō, designed by Yoshida Hiroshi in 1937. Towering cryptomeria trunks frame the lantern-lined approach to the shrine, rendered with the soft gradations Yoshida carried from his watercolour training into woodblock. This impression belongs to the San Diego Museum of Art.
collection-of-beauty-transfiguration-rap: Christ rises in light between Moses and Elijah above the apostles on Mount Tabor, while in the lower zone the disciples fail to heal a possessed boy. Commissioned in 1516 by Cardinal Giulio de' Medici for Narbonne Cathedral, Raphael was still completing the panel when he died in 1520 and it now belongs to the Vatican Pinacoteca.
collection-of-beauty-transfiguration-rub: Christ rises in radiant white between Moses and Elijah while the apostles below shield their eyes, a subject drawn from Matthew 17. Rubens organizes the composition around a vertical axis of light, marrying Italian disegno with Flemish painterly warmth.
collection-of-beauty-treaty-of-paris-by-: John Jay, John Adams, Benjamin Franklin, Henry Laurens and William Temple Franklin sit together around a table in West's unfinished oil sketch for the planned Treaty of Paris group portrait. The British commissioners refused to sit, and West abandoned the canvas; the fragment is held at the Winterthur Museum in Delaware.
collection-of-beauty-trinidad-el-greco2: God the Father supports the dead body of Christ while the dove of the Holy Spirit hovers above, attended by mourning angels. Painted between 1577 and 1579 for the high altar of Santo Domingo el Antiguo in Toledo, the composition draws directly on a Dürer engraving but elongates the figures in El Greco's emerging Mannerist idiom.
collection-of-beauty-triumphant-cupid-am: Cupid sits in triumph atop instruments of art, science and war, a Baroque allegory of love's universal sway. Willeboirts Bosschaert painted the figures and de Vos the still-life trophies, reflecting the seventeenth-century Antwerp practice of collaborative specialization.
collection-of-beauty-triumphant-entry-of: Part of the Constantine cycle designed for tapestries woven for Louis XIII, showing the emperor's victorious procession through Rome after the Battle of the Milvian Bridge. Rubens stages the parade as a ceremonial relief, packed with banners, classical architecture and rearing horses.
collection-of-beauty-tsar-nikolai: Portrait of a Russian emperor named Nikolai, shown in formal pose. The image circulates without museum attribution or signed authorship, so the sitter could be either Nicholas I or Nicholas II of the Romanov dynasty.
collection-of-beauty-tsukioka-yoshitoshi: A pale full moon rises over the windswept grasses of Musashino, where a fox glances back through the autumn pampas. The plate from One Hundred Aspects of the Moon distills a literary motif into spare silhouette and graded sky.
collection-of-beauty-tsunami-by-hokusai-: The opening sheet of Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji shows a towering offshore wave (okinami) breaking over fishing boats while Fuji stands small on the horizon. Hokusai's use of imported Prussian blue and his geometric treatment of foam made the print a touchstone of Edo design.
collection-of-beauty-turner-antwerp-van-: An imagined homage in which the Dutch master Jan van Goyen sketches from a small boat in Antwerp harbor, surrounded by shipping under broken cloud. Turner pays tribute to the seventeenth-century landscape tradition while asserting his own atmospheric handling of sky and water.
collection-of-beauty-turner-cologne-the-: Cologne's quayside gilds in evening light as a packet boat draws in beneath the unfinished cathedral. The vast canvas, now in the Frick Collection, pushes Rhineland topography toward Venetian-style golden atmosphere.
collection-of-beauty-turner-deluge: An early biblical disaster scene depicting the universal flood, with massed bodies struggling against rising water beneath churning storm clouds. Turner builds the composition from a baroque diagonal of light, a precedent for his later sublime catastrophes.
collection-of-beauty-turner-fishermen-up: Fishermen struggle to bring a sailing vessel ashore as breaking surf and squall lines press against a steep coast. An early Royal Academy exhibit, the canvas sets Turner's lifelong concern with mariners' jeopardy in a darker, more Dutch-inflected idiom.
collection-of-beauty-turner-j-m-w-the-gr: A view down the Grand Canal toward the domes of Santa Maria della Salute, gondolas dispersed across luminous water. Turner dissolves the architecture of Venice into pale light and reflected color, characteristic of his late Romantic vedute.
collection-of-beauty-turner-joseph-mallo: Fishing boats work the swell off Hastings under a turbulent sky, the figures and rigging set against pale sea-light. Turner treats the everyday coastal labor with the atmospheric breadth of his mature marine paintings.
collection-of-beauty-turner-newark-abbey: The ruined Augustinian priory of Newark stands above the still waters of the Wey, framed by trees and scattered cattle. Turner adopts the picturesque vocabulary of the topographical watercolorists, softened by an early painterly attention to reflected light.
collection-of-beauty-turner-peace-burial: Commemorates the sea burial of the painter David Wilkie off Gibraltar, the steamer's silhouette and inky black sails set against a flaring sun. Exhibited as a pendant to Turner's fiery 'War,' the picture pairs cool nocturnal calm with the warmth of mourning.
collection-of-beauty-turner-port-rusdael: An invented harbour named in homage to the Dutch marine master Jacob van Ruisdael, with squat fishing craft straining against a grey-green swell. Turner adopts the seventeenth-century tonal vocabulary while loosening the brushwork toward atmospheric haze.
collection-of-beauty-turner-rain-steam-a: A Great Western Railway locomotive races across Maidenhead Bridge through curtains of rain, the iron viaduct dissolving into vapour and golden light. The picture is a defining statement of the modern industrial sublime, painted with palette knife and finger as much as brush.
collection-of-beauty-turner-ships-bearin: A squally Channel scene of merchantmen turning into the wind, indebted to the Dutch tradition of Willem van de Velde. Commissioned by the third Earl of Egremont, the canvas still hangs at Petworth House where Turner often painted.
collection-of-beauty-turner-the-banks-of: A French river view rendered in luminous gouache and watercolour on blue paper, part of Turner's projected 'Wanderings by the Loire' series. The chalky highlights catch a milky riverine light typical of his continental tour studies.
